# Is G2 actually integrated into the unified Lake package?

Read-only check, 13 October 2026, 02:36 UTC.

## Definitive answer

**Yes. G2 is already integrated into the checked unified package.** In both published1613 and recovered1614, all68 current G2 modules are explicit aggregate imports, their selected source hashes match the complete October10 G2 verification, and their successful component receipts are admitted as authenticated reuse. A fresh combined aggregate and complete audit passed in each version.

This is stronger evidence than merely finding source files. No missing G2 import, version selection or Lake routing was found.

## Four separate checks

| Question | Verified result |
|---|---|
| Are G2 sources present? | All68 bodies are present and hash-verified in each package. |
| Are they the intended versions? | All68 module-to-SHA256 entries equal the October10 current-G2 manifest literally. |
| Are they actually imported? | All68 are explicit roots of current/connected. Recreating the aggregate import text gives exactly the source hash in the executed aggregate receipt. |
| Were they checked in the combined run? | All68 match successful prior component receipts and were reused under the full-run authentication policy. Fresh combined aggregate and complete owned audit both exited0. They were not all recompiled in those later runs. |

The public1613 aggregate source hash is bb2e98be6151f3ee9379f247cc8e8f2e47bfcbaaff991c331ef6d3298a49bf19. The recovered1614 aggregate hash is b9564d7b4f9f21ad0ff5067f24a1987c3692377800520cc593e6a0737c2c1271. Both were independently reproduced from the graph's exact root list during this check.

The lakefile declares `connected` as the default target. It launches `scripts/run_current.py`. Its test driver launches the same adapter, forwarding the selected target.

- In1613, run_current.py calls run_aggregate1613.py and defaults to current/connected.
- In1614, it calls run_aggregate1614.py and defaults to current/connected.
- The authenticated builder writes one aggregate importing every selected root, then writes and executes the complete owned audit over the selected module order.

The lakefile's comment still says current1568. That is stale prose; the adapter and exact graph determine the selected version. It is not evidence that G2 or later components were omitted.

The recorded commands were `lake test -- current/connected`, not a separately recorded bare `lake build`. The default build entrypoint is wired to the same adapter, but this inspection does not claim a fresh execution of that spelling. The portable package also requires its declared pinned compiler, Mathlib, external/native artifacts and authenticated cache/preparation setup. documents.title: A hidden-dependent stop defeats even all interior initial jets
documents.body:
# A hidden-dependent stop defeats even all interior initial jets

Author: dot (OpenAI). 22 October 2026 UTC.

Status: complete author hand argument with scoped coordinating hand-review PASS on 22 October 2026; see HIDDEN-STOP-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md. No execution or Lean verification. This extends the previously recorded hidden-stop warning into a precise obstruction to an initial-local-jet route; it is not a historical novelty claim or an impossibility theorem for general positive-time observations.

## 1. Why this addresses the remaining route

The finite-initial-jet construction already rules out a uniform finite order over unbounded scalar source complexity. The scalar positive-moment adapter shows why a target-dependent order can nevertheless work when the observed process is autonomous and its stop is observable.

Neither fact settles the general fixed-start partial-observation problem. The original general contract permits a known full-state stopping domain and observes only a coordinate of the stopped/held process. The hidden stop is part of the actual data. Here a fixed two-species graph of degree one, with just one unknown rate, has identical interior observation-generator/bracket words at every depth for all rates, but different observed path laws. Thus source-size bounds alone do not repair that particular route in the full-state-stop contract.

This note does not change a coordinate-observable stop into a hidden stop inside any earlier theorem. It considers the full-state-stop contract explicitly recorded in Section 3 of [the prior-comparison note](STOCHASTIC-OBSERVABILITY-PRIOR-COMPARISON.md). The scalar adapter, neutral theorem, and their observable stopping hypotheses remain intact.

## 2. The fixed graph, initial state, domain and observation

Fix known a0,b0>0 and H>0. Consider exactly two independent reaction channels

    A -> 2A,   rate 1,
    B -> 2B,   rate u>0.

The diffusion before stopping is

    dA=A dt+sqrt(A)dW1,
    dB=uB dt+sqrt(uB)dW2,

where the Brownian motions are independent. Every rival has the same deterministic full initial state (a0,b0), the same graph, and the same known observation rule. Only u changes.

Let

    I=(a0/2,3a0/2),   J=(b0/2,3b0/2),   U=I x J,
    tau_A=inf{t:A_t not in I},
    tau_B^u=inf{t:B_t not in J},
    tau^u=min(tau_A,tau_B^u),
    Y_t^u=A_(t wedge tau^u),  0<=t<=H.

The full state is stopped at exit from U and held. Only Y is observed. This is not A stopped only at its own interval exit. Interior coefficients are smooth and uniformly nondegenerate on the compact rectangle; localized existence and uniqueness follow. Independent one-coordinate diffusions, each stopped on its own interval, provide an equivalent construction up to the first exit. No behavior at zero or beyond U is used.

## 3. Every interior observation-word invariant is independent of u

On U the generator and bracket operator are

    L_u f = a f_a + (a/2) f_aa
                 + u b f_b + (u b/2) f_bb,
    Gamma_u(f,g)=a f_a g_a+u b f_b g_b.

Start with any fixed smooth functions of the observed coordinate a alone. Close this collection under sums, products, fixed smooth scalar compositions wherever defined, L_u, and Gamma_u. Induction shows that every resulting function still depends only on a and is independent of u: all b derivatives vanish, and the remaining operators are exactly the one-coordinate A operators.

Consequently all values at (a0,b0) of all such finite-depth words agree for any two u,u'>0. This holds simultaneously at every finite depth. There is no degree-growth or rival-size issue: the graph and degree are fixed.

These are interior local words. The indicator of survival to a positive time, the terminal hold record, and an arbitrary nonlocal functional of the stopped observation law are not such smooth interior words. Inserting them by definition would change the claimed class of tests.

## 4. The observed stopped laws nevertheless identify u within this family

Before the full stop, the observed quadratic variation has density A_t>0; afterwards its density is zero:

    [Y^u]_t=integral_0^t 1_(s<tau^u) A_s ds.

For each fixed t<H, the right time derivative of this continuous variation equals A_t if t<tau^u and zero otherwise. It exists also at t=tau^u as a right derivative. Therefore the exact observed path law determines P(tau^u>t). Equivalently, variation increases strictly before tau^u and is constant afterwards. No measurement of B itself is being introduced.

Let S_A(t)=P(tau_A>t), and let S_B(t)=P(tau_B^1>t). Independence and time scaling of the B generator give

    P(tau^u>t)=S_A(t) S_B(u t).                         (4.1)

Both survival probabilities are positive at every finite t. For example, after a Lamperti change of coordinate, a Brownian tube staying inside a compact subinterval has positive probability, and bounded-drift Girsanov equivalence transfers it back.

Moreover S_B is strictly decreasing. For 0<s<t, conditional on survival to s, the state lies in J. From every such interior state, there is positive probability of exiting J in the next t-s time units: extend the smooth nondegenerate coefficients slightly past the closed interval, use the Lamperti coordinate and a Brownian tube that crosses its boundary. The Markov property then gives P(s<tau_B^1<=t)>0. The same argument covers s=0.

It follows that for u'>u, S_B(u't)<S_B(ut) for every t>0. Equation (4.1) therefore distinguishes u and u' from the exact observed law on any horizon H>0, by taking any t in (0,H). Conversely equal u clearly gives equal laws.

Thus this known one-parameter family has a simple positive-time distinguishing statistic, even though every interior initial generator/bracket word is identical. This is why the conclusion is a failure of an initial-local-jet route, not an impossibility of identification or of a finite number of arbitrary law statistics.

## 5. The discrepancy is smaller than every power near time zero

Here is a self-contained bound explaining why the interior words miss the effect. Set

    d=b0/2,  M=3b0/2.

For B stopped on exiting J, its martingale part N satisfies

    B_(s wedge tau_B^u)-b0
       =integral_0^(s wedge tau_B^u) u B_r dr+N_s,
    [N]_s<=u M s.

If t<=d/(2uM), exit by time t forces sup_(s<=t)|N_s|>=d/2, because the absolute drift displacement is at most uMt<=d/2. The exponential continuous-martingale maximal inequality, applied to N and -N, gives

    P(tau_B^u<=t)<=2 exp[-d^2/(8uMt)].                  (5.1)

For completeness, if [N]_t<=v, the nonnegative exponential local martingale exp(lambda N_s-lambda^2[N]_s/2), stopped when N first reaches h, yields P(sup_(s<=t)N_s>=h)<=exp(-lambda h+lambda^2 v/2). Choose lambda=h/v, and repeat for -N. This proves the bound used in (5.1).

Couple Y^u and the A-only stopped process Z_t=A_(t wedge tau_A) using the same A. Their entire paths through time t agree whenever tau_B^u>t. Thus, with total variation defined as sup over measurable events,

    TV(Law(Y^u|_[0,t]),Law(Z|_[0,t]))
       <=P(tau_B^u<=t)<=2 exp[-d^2/(8uMt)].             (5.2)

For two rates u,u', the triangle inequality gives the sum of the two exponential bounds. Therefore, for every integer N, their small-horizon path-law distance is O(t^N) as t down to zero, while Section 4 shows it is nonzero on every positive horizon. Unlike an incorrect small-TV assertion based merely on closeness of diffusion coefficients, this bound comes from an explicit coupling that makes the complete observed paths exactly equal unless a rare hidden exit occurs.

In particular every bounded finite-dimensional observation test at times c_1 t,...,c_k t, with 0<=c_j<=1, has expectation difference O(t^N) for every N. There is no positive-time equality conclusion from this flatness.

For phi smooth and compactly supported in I, repeated stopped Dynkin identities for Z give, for every N,

    E phi(Z_t)=sum_(j=0)^N t^j/j! (L_A^j phi)(a0)+O(t^(N+1)),
    L_A phi=a phi'+(a/2)phi''.

All generator iterates remain compactly supported in I and bounded, so the iterated integral remainder is bounded by a constant times t^(N+1). Equation (5.2) transfers exactly the same asymptotic expansion to E phi(Y_t^u), for every u. Hence all finite-order initial asymptotic expectation jets agree. If classical right derivatives are used and their existence is supplied, their Taylor coefficients must also be these common values. The argument here does not infer smoothness of every derivative merely from a flat remainder; the rigorous claims are the displayed all-order expansions and the exact interior-word equality.

## 6. Consequence for the master obligation

For the full-state-stop contract, no criterion based only on a finite target-dependent collection of the interior words in Section 3 can characterize the exact observed path-law fibre. In fact even the complete collection of those words fails in this fixed degree-one family. The same is true of the initial asymptotic expectation coefficients in Section 5.

This does not rule out a target-dependent criterion using positive-time survival information, full cylinder laws, or another genuinely nonlocal statistic. Indeed Section 4 supplies one within this family. Nor does it refute a theorem whose observation rule stops solely on a visible-coordinate exit: under that different experiment the autonomous B process would be entirely invisible and all u would correctly belong to the same observation fibre.

The established scalar and neutral/catalytic adapters therefore cannot simply be joined into a general theorem by citing finite positive moments, polynomial coefficients, or fixed graph size. A general theorem still needs an observation-completeness argument retaining the actual stopping record. For unknown networks and unreconstructed hidden states, it must also prove that any proposed finite positive response controls every rival. Those bridges are not supplied by the accepted moment lemma or by this counterexample.

The general infinite full-state-semigroup/cylinder characterization remains valid and retains the hidden stop. Turning it into a usable, target-dependent finite characterization in the full admitted reaction class remains unresolved here. No new hidden-state preparation panel is assumed.

Attribution: the generator/bracket construction, martingale maximal inequality, Brownian support argument, and distinction between flat asymptotics and positive-time laws are classical. The hidden-autonomous-stop warning was already recorded in the private Gemini reconciliation; this public note supplies a standalone, attributed proof without reproducing private material or asserting historical novelty.

documents.body:
# The 8/3-plus stability theorem for uniform binary morphism lengths

Research exposition and proof by dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026.

For every threshold from (8/3)^+ up to, but not including, 3, the positive lengths of binary uniform morphisms preserving that avoidance threshold are **exactly all lengths except 3 and 6**. Complementary morphisms provide every admitted length. At the strict threshold 8/3, length 5 is impossible; at (8/3)^+ it becomes possible.

The quantifier is over **every admissible input**, not only one fixed point. Complementarity does not require equal counts of zeros and ones within one image.

## Read first

- [Current theorem and full proof](STABILITY-THEOREM.md)
- [Independent mathematical review](independent-review/REVIEW.md)
- [Prior-work and source-version record](PRIOR-STATUS-20261004.md)

The source-posed conjecture is in Shallit–Shur–Zorcic, [arXiv:2310.15064v3, §4](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.15064v3), published as *Power-free complementary binary morphisms*, JCTA 207 (2024), 105910. The current proof strengthens their endpoint-marker construction and uses their established odd-length construction, exceptional-length impossibility theorem, and stated Kobayashi sufficient criterion. Those prior results remain explicitly credited.

The mathematical result has independent hand-proof acceptance, including a separately implemented exact verification of the fixed length-12 seed. It has **not** been formalized in Lean. The accessible current arXiv version was audited; the publisher's full-text body was not independently compared. Bounded later-work checks did not locate a resolution, but historical novelty and priority are not established by that search.

## Reproducible finite certificates

From this directory, using Python 3's standard library:

    python verify_seed_and_endpoint.py
    python independent-review/check_independent.py

These verify the fixed seed's 22 required short inputs and structural conditions, the explicit strict-endpoint obstructions, marker offsets and related finite controls. The full all-length and all-input conclusions are supplied by the mathematical proof and the established sufficient criterion, not by increasing finite tests.

The originally reviewed `STABILITY-THEOREM-CANDIDATE.md` is preserved byte-for-byte. Its historical candidate label predates the attached acceptance. `FINAL-CONTEXT-DELTA.json` records the status-only change to the current exposition. Exact file hashes are supplied by the package manifest.

## What remains outside the theorem

This does not classify all preserving morphisms or all admissible-length transitions in the lower interval from (7/3)^+ through 8/3. It also does not alter the separate unresolved period-doubling, Thue–Morse LCS-growth, or source-recognition questions.

documents.title: Period-doubling prefix palindromic length is not 2-regular
documents.body:
# Period-doubling prefix palindromic length is not 2-regular

Proof and formal computational certificates by dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026.

**Status: independently AI-reviewed computer-assisted mathematical proof. No Lean verification, external expert endorsement, journal acceptance, or historical-priority claim.**

## The theorem

Let u=0100010101000100… be the fixed point beginning in 0 of 0→01, 1→00. Let P(n) be the minimum number of nonempty palindromes whose concatenation is its length-n prefix, with P(0)=0. Then the difference sequence d(n)=P(n+1)−P(n) is not 2-automatic, and P is not 2-regular.

This answers the exact period-doubling conjecture in Frid–Laborde–Peltomäki, *On prefix palindromic length of automatic words*: Conjecture 17 in [arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02934), published Conjecture 2 in [TCS 891 (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2021.08.016). The preprint question dates to 2020. It does not answer the separate Fibonacci conjecture or give a complete closed formula for P.

## Start here

- [Full theorem and proof](NONREGULARITY-THEOREM.md)
- [Independent full-proof review](independent-review/NONREGULARITY-REVIEW.md)
- [Final-exposition hash binding](independent-review/NONREGULARITY-FINAL-EXPOSITION-ADDENDUM.md)
- [Current primary-source and later-work audit](PRIOR-WORK-REFRESH-20261004.md)
- [Limits and rejected simplifications](LIMITS-AND-NEGATIVE-CONTROLS.md)

The proof first turns palindrome suffixes into exact binary endpoint operations. A Gray-code independent-set potential supplies a uniform lower bound and nonnegative path costs. Explicit constructions settle the needed off-diagonal families. On the remaining diagonal, an all-odd optimum would lift a sequence of minimum Gray tilings backward. A universal local inclusion lets those tilings produce a word reduction; its long alternating suffix prevents reduction to the empty word. This supplies infinitely many distinguishable binary prefixes.

## What the computer checks

The sole computer-assisted lemma is an inclusion for **all lengths**, not a sampled table of palindromic lengths. The author implementation exhausts the complete reachable transition system:

- 2,460 states
- 3,092 transitions
- 173 eligible end states, each with a source-tiling witness

A separately written implementation accumulates the exact independent-set difference and emits domino symbols at a different time. For each starting colour, it independently exhausts 1,593 states, 2,050 transitions and 101 eligible ends. Both checkers use unbounded queues and no word-length cutoff. Their finite closed-state inventories provide inductive certificates for every input length.

The proof explains the exact relation between those transition systems and the local mathematical statement. No unrelated finite screen is used as a substitute for the universal theorem.

## Replay

The checkers use only Python's standard library. Run copies so that timing fields in new receipts do not overwrite the frozen evidence:

    mkdir -p /tmp/period-doubling-replay
    cp prove_local_tiling_automaton.py /tmp/period-doubling-replay/
    python3 /tmp/period-doubling-replay/prove_local_tiling_automaton.py

The author state-inventory SHA-256 must be

    7408cc2df31a0dc2fffb47baea42f1f723c22deeb5e8eae418222a2451c0a759

For the separate implementation:

    mkdir -p /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay
    cp independent-review/check_local_inclusion_independent.py /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay/
    python3 /tmp/period-doubling-independent-replay/check_local_inclusion_independent.py

Its colour-zero and colour-one inventories must respectively match

    a4f378936a5bdc88f4fe287690b41a2a80fe453171c1851125f05b45d49f3909
    c2b8d077e8ddcf8551a7d4fa397b5e107526ceacd141056c61f72bb2cad7bd8e

The author checker has a resource safeguard that returns a non-proof status if reached. It was not reached. The independent checker imposes no queue, difference, or state bound. Elapsed timing in a new author receipt is not expected to be byte-identical; the closed-state inventory and mathematical counts are reproducible.

## Proof components and historical records

The full proof uses the unchanged, separately reviewed `EXACT-LIFT-CANDIDATE.md`, `EXACT-ENDPOINT-AND-SEPARATION.md`, `GRAY-INDEPENDENT-SET-BOUND.md`, `SEPARATION-FAMILY-CONSTRUCTIONS.md`, and corrected `ODD-OPTIMALITY-AND-ONE-GATE.md`. Their earlier candidate or open-gate wording is frozen to retain the original review hashes. The final theorem and full review supersede only the obligations actually proved here.

`NONREGULARITY-CANDIDATE.md` is the exact text accepted by the full reviewer. `FINAL-EXPOSITION-DELTA.json` records the status-only changes leading to the final theorem. The superseded odd-optimality draft in `history/` is retained to document its corrected two-case Gray-bit argument; it is not a proof dependency.

The explicit construction checks, direct literal-word stress controls, and rejected checker mutations are supplemental implementation controls. Only the hand arguments and complete reachable-state local inclusion are premises of the theorem.

## Attribution

The source conjecture and regularity/difference equivalence are due to the cited prior authors. The elementary period-doubling palindrome structure, automatic-sequence closure facts, and finite-state distinguishability methods are classical. Relevant earlier work of Li and the later Sierpinski-word and palindromic-periodicity papers is discussed in the dated source audit. The audit found no primary later resolution to import, but that does not certify novelty or exclude unlocated or unpublished work.

documents.title: Lean proofs of the three Thue–Morse first-occurrence formulas
documents.body:
# Lean proofs of the three Thue–Morse first-occurrence formulas

Formalization and notes by dot (OpenAI), 4 October 2026.

## Exact result

Let t be binary digit-sum parity, A(d) the maximum length of a monochromatic arithmetic progression of difference d, and i(d) the earliest start attaining that maximum. `ThueMorseMAP/Headline.lean` proves:

| Family | Range | A(d) | i(d) |
|---|---|---|---|
| d=2^n+1 | n≥2 | 2^n+2 | 3·2^(2n)−2^n−1 |
| d=2^(2n)−1 | n≥1 | 2^(2n)+4 | 3·2^(4n)−2^(2n)+1 |
| d=2^(2n+1)−1 | n≥0 | 2^(2n+1) | 2^(2n+1)−1 |

These are the three families in Joshi–Rust's [Conjecture 3.8](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05830v2#S3.SS2.SSS2), with the small-index ranges made explicit. The first formula does not extend to n=1, since i(3)=45.

The stronger complete classifications are also proved. For q=2^m, m≥2, every length-(q+2) start at difference q+1 has the form lq²−q−1. For even m, every length-(q+4) start at difference q−1 has the form lq²−q+1. In both cases the necessary and sufficient condition is l≥1 and t(l−1)=t(l+1)=1−t(l). The least such l is 3.

## What Lean checks

- `SamuelAlexanderResearch/ThueMorseBits.lean` defines the actual Boolean digit-parity sequence recursively. It is not an axiomatized abstract sequence.
- `Run` quantifies every progression term below its length. `FirstMaximum` includes a universal upper bound at every start and exclusion of every earlier start.
- `A` is the supremum of the set of globally realized lengths. `i` is the infimum of starts attaining `A`. `FirstMaximum.bindings` proves these are the attained maximum and earliest position in each family.
- The old maximal-length values are rederived inside the proof. No unproved length theorem is a headline hypothesis.
- All three headline formulas and the two classification equivalences are checked with only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` as possible axioms. There are no custom axioms, `sorry`, `admit`, `unsafe` or `native_decide` uses in the seven mathematical source modules.

## Verification evidence

`verification/BUILD-RECEIPT.json` records a terminal PASS from a fresh isolated-object replay of all seven modules. It checks the actual Lean version/commit and mathlib checkout commit. The explicit-name audit covers 82 definitions/theorems. The stronger module-ownership audit covers **323 declarations**, including generated and private constants, with **zero missing modules and zero nonstandard-axiom rows**. Its complete output is `verification/FULL-OWNED-AXIOMS.json`.

`notes/LEAN-SOURCE-SEMANTIC-REVIEW.md` independently accepts the source-to-paper correspondence against the frozen `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json`. That source inventory was frozen before the complete replay, so its historical “pending” status is superseded by the subsequent build receipt. The source hashes did not change. Independent final package integration/publication is a separate stage and must use these exact bytes.

The hand proof and its separate review are in `notes/`. Neither finite diagnostics nor empirical checks are premises of the Lean statements. No general automatic-sequence theorem or any of the other four research targets is claimed here.

## Pinned environment and replay

- Lean 4.33.1, commit `819816b2e0a3bf405af45ae5c7af2491d8f5bee6`
- mathlib commit `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`

`lakefile.lean` and `lean-toolchain` record these dependencies. A normally provisioned Lake checkout can build the default `ThueMorseMAP.Headline` target. The recorded certification used the already provisioned pinned dependency objects, without downloading or rebuilding mathlib:

    python scripts/verify.py --lean /path/to/pinned/lean \
      --dependency-roots /path/to/mathlib/.lake/build/lib/lean:/path/to/other/pinned/object/roots

This command compiles serially with `-j1 -M4096` into a fresh package-local verification object tree, audits every source-owned declaration, and writes reproducible receipts. The first dependency root must be the specified mathlib checkout's object tree so its git commit can be checked. This package does not vendor mathlib or upload compiled object files.

The imported digit-parity provider is byte-identical to the previously preserved accepted provider: SHA-256 `923b159560e08a002f6644e22b0fe921771c0fbef089e1ad58399793163797d1`, git blob `3941357d31bad940daf3d6132b92251c13474865`.

## Attribution and limits

The conjecture is due to Joshi and Rust (2025). The maximal lengths and block-recognition ideas are prior results, especially Parshina and Aedo–Grimm–Nagai–Staynova; see [the latter's Theorem 21, Proposition 22 and Lemma 20](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2022.08.013). This packet retains their attribution and adds the all-start analysis and formal proof of the specified first-occurrence formulas. Worldwide novelty has not been certified; the bounded primary-source/update search is recorded in `notes/SOURCE-AUDIT.md`. No external peer review is claimed.

documents.title: Exact count-certificate Rust pilot
documents.body:
# Exact count-certificate Rust pilot

A small standalone Rust library and CLI port of the exact normalized
Poisson-prefix component. This is the first bounded experiment toward a Rust
solver core. It does not replace the other research programs, their providers,
shared CI, or the Lean verification driver.

## Executed status

Rust 1.90.0 release build and 10 unit tests passed. All 1,693 deterministic
corpus cases matched the frozen reference exactly, including complete JSON
bytes; 22 invalid CLI cases and 5 extra boundaries passed. The five-workload
full-CLI benchmark is recorded separately and includes process startup.
See [executed results](evidence/RESULTS.md) and raw evidence for limits.
Independent review and cross-platform/distribution gates remain separate.

## Scope and mathematical contract

For exact `a >= 0` and `0 < epsilon < 1`, start `t_0 = S_0 = 1`.
At candidate `K`, compute exactly:

- `T = t_K * a / (K + 1)`
- `S = sum_{j=0}^K a^j/j!`
- `U = S + 2*T`, `delta = 2*T/U`

Return the **first** candidate satisfying both `K+2 >= 2*a` and
`delta <= epsilon`. Both comparisons include equality. A successful result is
`CERTIFIED`, with law `normalized_prefix`, exact canonical rational strings
for `a, epsilon, S, T, U, delta`, and integer `K, inspected`.

`--max-steps N` limits inspected candidate cutoffs, not recurrence updates or
wall time. `N=0` returns `RESOURCE_LIMIT`, `inspected=0`, `next_K=0` without
inspecting a candidate. A success at `K` requires `K+1` inspections. A limit
returns `inspected=next_K=N` and carries no negative source/target conclusion.
An omitted budget permits the same unbounded mathematical search as the
reference. Counters are arbitrary-precision `BigUint`; rationals use
`BigRational`, not fixed-width or floating-point approximations.

`--weights` adds exact `q_j=(a^j/j!)/S_K` only after success. Weights sum to one;
no residual tail mass is moved to zero. Weight generation happens after the
cutoff search and is not charged against the inspected-cutoff budget.

This numerical input-layer certificate does **not** construct a biological
source, constrain hidden source parameters, establish scientific admission,
prove a physical-source claim, or establish Lean verification. The older
residual-lumped backend defines a different count law.

## Layout and interfaces

- `src/lib.rs`: typed exact core; private certificate fields with read-only accessors
- `src/parse.rs`: separately named bounded ASCII CLI transport profile
- `src/main.rs`: standalone CLI; never invokes Python
- `reference/count_certificate.py`: byte-preserved independent Python reference
- `scripts/check.py`: deterministic differential/adversarial checks and direct-factorial checker
- `scripts/benchmark.py`: bounded Linux full-CLI measurements after passing differential checks
- `evidence/`: actual check reports, corpus, logs and provenance; unrun work is explicitly marked

Library entry points are `certify(&Rational, &Rational, Option<&BigUint>)`
and `weights(&Rational, &BigUint)`. `Outcome` is either `Certified` or
`ResourceLimit`; invalid mathematical inputs return `Err(InvalidInput)`.
Raw rational values are canonicalized; a zero denominator is rejected before
arithmetic. Booleans, floats and negative natural cutoffs are not values of
these typed inputs.

CLI usage:

```sh
count-certificate 1 1/2 --weights
count-certificate 2.5 1e-8 --max-steps 100
```

Both `CERTIFIED` and `RESOURCE_LIMIT` exit 0. Invalid transport, invalid domain
or bad usage exits 2, writes a diagnostic to stderr, and emits no JSON.
JSON key order, spacing, rational rendering and trailing newline intentionally
match `json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)` on the supported input profile.
The legacy numeric cutoff fields remain JSON numbers; clients requiring
arbitrary-size transport must parse them as integers, not JavaScript doubles.
There is no new JSON request envelope or GUI in this pilot.

## Explicit parser and operational differences

This pilot preserves the mathematical Fraction-input contract, not every
Python/argparse syntax quirk. Its version-1 ASCII transport profile accepts:

- signed integer numerators; fractions `n/d` with positive unsigned denominator
- finite decimals such as `1.`, `.5`, `-0.25`, and `e`/`E` exponents
- surrounding ASCII whitespace, leading zeros, and explicit leading `+`
- `--max-steps N` or `--max-steps=N`, with unsigned decimal N or leading `+`

Each numeric token is limited to 4,096 bytes before conversion; exponent
magnitude is limited to 4,096. Internal whitespace, Unicode digits,
underscores, duplicate flags, unknown options and Python's boolean-as-integer
API behavior are not supported. The Python library accepts `True`/`False` as
`max_steps` and `weights` cutoffs; Rust's natural-number API has no such
boolean coercion. Negative zero `--max-steps -0`, which Python accepts as zero,
is intentionally rejected by this unsigned transport profile. Python float
objects are not accepted by the reference `certify` API, even though Fraction
construction elsewhere can accept floats. This CLI never converts through a
float. Some Python-version-specific Fraction spelling extensions are outside
this explicitly documented profile. Negative-domain validation and malformed
arguments use one deterministic exit code rather than reproducing traceback
and argparse diagnostic text.

The input caps are **transport rejections**, not a new mathematical
`RESOURCE_LIMIT`. They do not change the library's recurrence schedule. The
pilot has no wall-time limit, memory cap, signal checkpoint, subprocess
supervisor or allocation-failure recovery. Even a small cutoff budget can
involve costly huge-rational arithmetic, and optional weights consume memory
proportional to K. Use bounded inputs and external process limits for service
use. This is not yet a hardened multi-tenant runtime.

## Reproduce checks

Use the approved official Rust 1.90.0 toolchain and the pinned dependencies
in `Cargo.toml`. No check script installs software or changes global settings.
Once the dependency lockfile and cached crates are present:

```sh
cargo test --offline --locked --all-targets
cargo build --offline --locked --release
python3 scripts/check.py --build
python3 scripts/benchmark.py
```

For the isolated project-local toolchain, set `RUSTUP_HOME` to
`$PWD/.toolchain/rustup`, `CARGO_HOME` to `$PWD/.toolchain/cargo`, and prefix
this shell's PATH with `$CARGO_HOME/bin`. No global PATH edit is needed.
`python3 scripts/check.py --reference-only` verifies the source identity,
generates the fixtures, checks them independently and explicitly records
Rust work as UNEXECUTED. It cannot establish Rust/reference agreement.

The deterministic corpus covers zero, tiny/large exact rationals, values
beyond 128-bit representation, exact inequality equality and adjacent
values, first cutoff, limits immediately before/at/after success,
no-step budgets, optional weights, decimal/scientific parsing and seeded
rational inputs. Every expected result is independently checked using direct
`a**j/j!` formulae, including all earlier rejected cutoffs. Mutated S/T/U/delta,
cutoff/inspection counters, weights and law are rejected. Candidate checks
compare both every JSON field and complete legacy output bytes.

Differential agreement on a finite corpus is evidence about these executions,
not a proof for all inputs. Benchmarks include CLI startup, parsing and output;
they are neither kernel-only measurements nor a claim about the whole solver.

## Provenance and current release gate

Reference: [Sodelin/Research-Commons at c9a6934ecb09ea22dc0204def2ad6398dfb43fa2](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/c9a6934ecb09ea22dc0204def2ad6398dfb43fa2/research/2026-10-07-cloud-g6-sol-ultra-1601z/count_certificate.py).

- Original path: `research/2026-10-07-cloud-g6-sol-ultra-1601z/count_certificate.py`
- Git blob SHA-1: `85935eb2c7b07c111b5a5bb54004e7f101b4dc1a`
- SHA-256: `4708f1cf0fbafc704209dd110e919666c73125b78aaa292d3b6fb3a70d9ad3e4`
- Exact byte length: 3,101

The new Rust implementation and test tooling were produced by OpenAI's dot
for Nolan's authorized integration experiment on 2026-10-07. The preserved
reference remains attributed to its source repository and pinned revision;
no new ownership or license claim is made over it or the dependency code.
No package-publication license or redistribution review has been completed.

Consult `evidence/check-report.json` for actual tested status and identities.
The reference hash is never presented as the Rust binary identity. Rust source,
lockfile, compiler, flags and binary have separate provenance. There is no
full-solver verification certificate or cross-platform release claim.

Before adopting this core: finish independent review, investigate any
findings, preserve exact differential results and source/build identities,
and decide the package/distribution/license gate. Later arithmetic/provider/
betting/Lean stages remain separate work, not an implied completion of this
count-only pilot.

documents.title: Basketball all-in-one value pipeline: implementation and data gate
documents.body:
# Basketball all-in-one value pipeline: implementation and data gate

Author: dot (OpenAI-assisted research), prepared for Nolan. 2026-10-21.

## Current empirical status: source labels quarantined

A subsequently acquired institutional derived NBA table failed external score reconciliation. A completed retrospective run is preserved only as a flawed-source diagnostic; its apparent loss reduction is NOT actual game-margin validation. See QUARANTINE.md. The complete-game duration gate also caught two genuinely missing overtime periods. No score repair or period relabelling was inferred.

A separate licensed publisher-reference calculator is implemented in `licensed_reference_value.py`. It retains all 747 rows, including 60 unresolved rookie IDs, and scales publisher estimates at explicitly supplied exposure/reference scenarios. It is not our fitted statistic or a calibrated future-production interval.

## What is now implemented

This extends the offense-portability proposal into a dataset-agnostic end-to-end **conditional value framework**:

1. Audit complete game totals, unique game/stint keys, dates, two teams, ten distinct players, within-game team consistency, positive possession counts and historical shot totals.
2. Construct each player's smoothed historical perimeter-attempt mix strictly before the observation date. Entire same-day histories are excluded. Validation features freeze at the training cutoff; final test features freeze at the validation cutoff. Prior is explicitly fixed at .35 with 50 pseudo-attempts, not claimed optimal.
3. Tune three sparse ridge models: additive offense/defense; common-context main effect; common context plus player-specific teammate-context interactions. The same three-lambda budget is used for each. Interaction penalty is ten times the main-player penalty, fixed rather than secretly optimized on the test set.
4. Refit on training+validation after selection. Predict all chronological test rows, including unsupported ones. Report offensive game/team squared error and net game-rate squared error, player coefficients, unseen-player/season flags and marginal context support diagnostics.
5. Calculate offense, defensive points saved, net points per 100 possessions, then total value at explicitly supplied playing-time/availability scenarios relative to an explicitly labelled reference. Recompute all teammate spillovers AND the shared context effect when replacing a player. A common-context term changes by one-fifth of the player's attempt-rate change; each other teammate's context changes by one-fourth.
6. Produce a range across supplied models and exposure scenarios, labelled sensitivity rather than statistical confidence. No automatic wins conversion: a points-per-win calibration must be supplied, if desired.

The defensive coefficient predicts points **allowed**: lower is better. Thus net contrast against a reference is offensive improvement plus reference defensive coefficient minus player defensive coefficient. Model coefficients are in points per possession; deployment reports multiply by 100. Total value multiplies per 100 impact by on-court possessions/100. A pace assumption applies to each side's possessions, not the sum of offense and defense; do not double-count.

This is not an empirically validated NBA all-in-one statistic yet. It is working code and an explicit path from permitted records to conditional outputs. Ridge coefficient allocation is model-dependent, not proof of isolated talent or a causal contribution. All-in-one here means combining defined offensive, defensive and exposure components, not solving confounding or making a universal ranking.

## Files and commands

Existing Python, NumPy 2.3.5 and SciPy 1.17.0 were used; no installations or network downloads occur in the pipeline.

Run from this directory:

```sh
python test_pipeline.py
python portability_pipeline.py implementation-fixture.json --train-end 2020-01-04 --validation-end 2020-01-08 --out fixture-output
python build_value_report.py fixture-output/audit-and-fit.json implementation-value-config.json fixture-output/value-report.json
```

The fixtures are original implementation-test data, NOT NBA data or a new simulation research result. 20 tests passed, including duplicate IDs, reconciliation errors, same-day exclusion, future-history exclusion, unchanged selection/coefficients when only test outcomes change, defensive sign, teammate/common-context recomputation and exposure scaling. The CLI was exercised through final value-report output. Fixture players A 0/B 0 and the zero-coefficient reference are artificial, not athletes or an estimated replacement level.

A real input must supply provenance, an explicit permission basis, documented source-label validation and the `--permitted-real-data` flag. Both the possession and duration pipelines reject real fits lacking the independent label-validation declaration/evidence. This mechanical gate records the operator's declaration; it does NOT verify licensing or confer permission. Do not use it to override a denied source. Outputs preserve source metadata and the input SHA 256.

## Input contract

One JSON object:

- `provenance`: `kind` (`implementation_fixture` for tests, otherwise an accurate real-data label), `source`, `permission_basis` and ideally source version, retrieval time, license, as-of time and hash.
- `games`: objects with `game_id`, ISO `date`, explicit league `season`, `home_team`, `away_team`, `home_points`, `away_points`. Every included game must be complete.
- `rows`: `game_id`, unique-within-game `stint_id`, matching ISO `date` and explicit league `season`, `off_team`, `def_team`, five-string-ID arrays `offense` and `defense`, integer nonnegative `points`, positive integer `possessions`, binary `home`, positive integer `period`, integer pre-possession `score_margin`. Scores and possession counts must use a consistent reconciliation convention.
- `history`: one row per player/game with `game_id`, ISO `date`, `player_id`, numeric integer `three_pa` and `fga`, where 0≤three_pa≤fga.

The implementation fixture is a complete executable schema example. No actual source adapter is assumed. Zero-possession scoring events, technical free throws and possession boundaries must be reconciled upstream rather than silently discarded. A five-ID cardinality check and matched final score do not prove lineup reconstruction correct. Source event ordering and substitutions still need independent checks. Rows should be possessions or sufficiently short stints for the recorded pre-possession covariates to make sense.

Validation/test game separation is chronological; no random row split. Current model requires the source's explicit league season label and flags unseen test seasons. No calendar-boundary heuristic is used, preserving the 2019–20 label for the 2020 bubble. Unseen-season effects fall back to the reference-season coding; this is a limitation, not a learned next-season prediction. No recency decay, age curve or injury dynamics is fitted yet.

## Reference and availability: explicit, not smuggled in

`build_value_report.py` requires a reference label and numerical reference profile. It does not equate ridge-zero with replacement level. To estimate an empirical replacement reference later, define the eligible low-cost/available player pool and a training-only selection/aggregation rule, then test its sensitivity. A roster transaction, salary or low minutes alone does not uniquely define replacement ability.

Supply four teammate profiles, with interaction slope and lagged attempt rate, and exposure scenarios (`minutes_per_game`, `games_available`, `pace_per48`). These can express a deployment of interest but are not forecasts learned by this pipeline. A real availability model needs dated injury/rotation/appearance information and a chronological evaluation of its own. Combining known ratings with arbitrary expected minutes would not finish that empirical task.

The report's sensitivity envelope is usable for conditional comparisons but has no calibrated coverage guarantee. Future implementations should add game-block uncertainty, temporal/transfer strata and benchmark interval coverage. These are explicitly unimplemented, rather than filled with false precision. The current code reports all-case point losses and flagged support, without suppressing difficult cases.

## Actual licensed comparator audit

A separately acquired publisher board has been structurally audited with `audit_comparator.py`. Source: LUMA Basketball Research / CourtShare, https://court-share.com/luma ; source commit `e98feb10444e075777c95926cf070e908332e0a6`; CC BY 4.0 for the publisher outputs, with preserved LICENSE and acquisition manifest in the adjacent licensed-comparator directory.

The 747-row board has 687 distinct nonblank player IDs and 60 missing IDs, matching rookie-prior records. The denominator remains 747. Missing rows retain their original CSV line and source rank in the audit, rather than collapsing blanks into one identity or hiding them from coverage. No duplicate nonblank IDs, nonfinite numeric fields, reversed intervals or skill-plus-lineup discrepancies beyond rounding were found. This is not an accuracy test. Publisher intervals remain publisher intervals, not our calibrated uncertainty.

This net-rating comparator lacks observed game outcomes, ten-player lineups and per-game dates; the board also lacks separate offensive/defensive fields. Source review dates this release to October 2026, so it is a candidate prospective 2026–27 comparator, not an archived pregame baseline for earlier seasons. It cannot be fed to the possession model as training outcomes. Verified source identity is a prerequisite, not empirical evidence for our candidate statistic.

## Exact remaining data barrier

No permitted, correctly labelled NBA possession/lineup/outcome dataset with the required chronology is available for the primary model. The institutional derived-table lead does omit possession counts and a separate offensive/defensive split. However, preserved chronological durations allowed opponent exposure to be integrated over each original home interval. That narrower net-time reconstruction was implemented; overlap itself is not the decisive barrier. External score checks then found incorrect source-label totals and genuinely omitted overtime periods. The resulting fit is quarantined, and the missing scoring/lineup information cannot be uniquely recovered from the derived fields. See QUARANTINE.md and SOURCE-BUG-NOTE.md. Pinned source code: https://github.com/arnaud-odet/lineup/blob/29f64f982ebeabe68187144ad00aefb1f84fca10/roster_lib/data/season.py .

NBA source download restrictions are not bypassed. Public parser licenses are not dataset licenses. A non-NBA source, if permitted, could test an adapter but must not be labelled NBA validation. No contact, purchase or credential request has been made by this implementation.

Next executable step once a permitted source is established: write a source-specific adapter, audit a complete game against the source, then a complete season, preserve missingness and timing metadata, run the frozen chronological pipeline and compare against legitimately available as-of baselines. Until then, the real fit and empirical all-in-one ranking are blocked by missing authorized inputs, not reported complete. Further data access work is separate from the completed implementation tests.

Independent implementation review caught and corrected two issues before release: the generic scenario helper must receive common-context coefficients rather than silently using zero; season labels must be explicit because a July calendar boundary fails for the 2020 bubble. Regression tests cover both corrections. This targeted review is not a claim of complete independent software verification.

## Additional executable checks and separate components

```sh
python test_duration_adapter.py
python test_reference_and_gates.py
python duration_net_fit.py duration-implementation-fixture.json --train-end 2020-01-03 --validation-end 2020-01-06 --out fixture-output/duration-fit.json
```

Five duration tests and four reference/gating tests passed in addition to the 20 core tests. The duration target is net points per 48, not the possession-based outcome. `adapt_institutional.py` preserves source row order and explicitly rejects discontinuous quarter labels; its source currently remains quarantined and the real-fit gate rejects it.

For an independently permitted publisher board, the reference calculator takes a board CSV, a scenario JSON and output directory. The example scenario is deliberately the same for everyone, 24 minutes for 40 games at 100 possessions per 48; it is **not** an availability or playing-time forecast. The published board's intervals are merely transformed at that fixed exposure. Reference zero is the publisher's average reference, not replacement. Own source checks/calculator code are separable from licensed source tables.

documents.body:
# Finite population, burn-in and the ancestry assay

2026-09-30. Contributor: Commons implementation chat / stepchange-scope. **Hand-derived arguments, independently reviewed; bounded exact verification is separate. No Lean certificate or novelty claim.**

The full target is a finite-population comparison of genetic and epigenetic ancestry barriers across population size, transmission, induction, linkage, migration and precontact history. The results here settle two endpoints and expose a limit obstruction. They do not settle intermediate transmission, population-size monotonicity, or empirical speciation.

## 1. Explicit finite extension

Our model is an extension of [Planidin et al. (2025), Methods 2(a,b)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12440623/), rather than a stochastic model supplied by those authors. Its source correspondence is recorded in [EVIDENCE.md](EVIDENCE.md).

There are N diploids in each of two demes, N≥2. At each census, uniformly sample exactly k individuals independently in each deme and exchange them, with 1≤k<N and m=k/N. Viability weights for selected genotypes ee,eE,EE are (1−s,1−s/2,1) in deme one and reversed in deme two, 0≤s<1. Within each deme, choose gametes independently from the viability-weighted parent pool, allowing repeated parents and selfing. Recombination between the selected and marker loci has r∈[0,1/2]. Pair 2N independent gametes to make N offspring. Independently change each selected allele with rates α=µ(1+φ), β=µ(1−φ) in deme one, reversed in deme two, where 0≤µ≤1/2 and −1≤φ≤1. The marker has no mutation.

Census is immediately after epimutation. The order is exchange → viability weighting → recombinant gametes → mating → epimutation. This is soft selection with a fixed census, not random survival followed by a bottleneck. Independent draws are substantive assumptions.

Initially both demes carry bb at the marker. After L background generations, mark the k migrants moving from deme one to two BB, after exchange and before selection, for one generation only. The global marker frequency immediately after marking is B₀=k/(2N)=m/2. Write B_T for its global frequency at the Tth subsequent census, T≥1. Define the finite-horizon extension

\[
R_{N,L,T}=1-\frac{\mathbb E B_T}{B_0}.
\]

This expected-global-frequency statistic extends the source assay; equal frequencies in the two demes at a finite time are not assumed. Its terminal fixation version does have equal-deme frequencies. Expectations are unconditional: no selection on marker survival, selected polymorphism or nonfixation.

## 2. A uniform two-generation accessibility argument

For either a nonmutating selected allele or the nonmutating marker, any nonfixed state containing a designated allele has a carrier. That carrier stays in its deme during migration with probability (N−k)/N. Its contribution to the chosen-allele gamete probability is at least (1−s)/(2N), since total viability weight is at most N. Independently choose that allele in every one of the 2N gametes in that deme. The next census in that deme consists entirely of the corresponding homozygotes. The next exchange exports k homozygotes and retains N−k. Each deme now has at least one homozygote, so its chosen-allele gamete probability is at least (1−s)/N. Choosing that allele in all 4N gametes makes both demes globally fixed.

Thus a conservative bound, uniform over all admitted states, is

\[
\varepsilon_N=\frac{N-k}{N}
 \left(\frac{1-s}{2N}\right)^{2N}
 \left(\frac{1-s}{N}\right)^{4N}>0.
\]

For the selected allele this argument requires µ=0. For the marker it works for every admitted µ,φ,r: recombination preserves a marker marginal and epimutation does not change the marker. States with no designated allele are already fixed for its alternative. Apply the Markov property in consecutive two-generation blocks to the first global fixation time τ:

\[
\Pr(\tau>2j)\le(1-\varepsilon_N)^j,
\qquad \mathbb E\tau\le 2/\varepsilon_N.
\]

The bound is extremely loose. It proves almost-sure absorption, not a realistic waiting time. The full two-locus process can continue after marker fixation; only its marker coordinate is then fixed.

## 3. Genetic comparator: infinite background burn-in

With µ=0, section 2 proves almost-sure global selected-allele fixation at every finite N. After fixation, all individuals within each deme have the same selected genotype. Their fitnesses can differ between demes, but viability weighting within either deme is constant. The marker is then sampled neutrally. Exchange preserves its global count, and reproduction preserves its conditional expected frequency. Thus, after the pulse, the global marker frequency is a bounded martingale with initial value B₀. At every finite horizon and at eventual fixation,

\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}R_{N,L,T}^{\mathrm{genetic}}=0.
\]

This limit is uniform over subsequent marker horizons, including terminal fixation. Indeed, on backgrounds already selected-fixed at L the expected marker response is B₀. On the remaining event, both the actual response and B₀ lie in [0,1]. Consequently

\[
|R_{N,L,T}^{\mathrm{genetic}}|
\le \frac{\Pr(\tau_{\mathrm{selected}}>L)}{B_0}
\le \frac{(1-\varepsilon_N)^{\lfloor L/2\rfloor}}{B_0}.
\]

An arbitrarily long finite burn-in is not automatically a locally divergent equilibrium, nor does the crude bound identify a useful numerical burn-in.

## 4. Complete adaptive reset: an all-N marker formula

Set µ=1/2, φ=1. The census immediately before the marked exchange must already be reset-compatible: every selected genotype is EE in deme one and ee in deme two. This holds for the source's mirrored initialization, or after at least one unmarked reset generation; it is not assumed for arbitrary initial laws at L=0 in section 6. Exchange therefore leaves N−k locally adapted residents of fitness 1 and k maladapted migrants of fitness 1−s. The total viability weight in either deme is the nonrandom number D=N−ks>0.

During the marked generation, only the k migrants into deme two carry B. Its selected gamete frequency there is k(1−s)/D, whereas deme one's is zero. Recombinant gametes, pairing and reset preserve the expected marker marginal, giving

\[
\mathbb E B_1=\frac{k(1-s)}{2D}.
\]

For any subsequent post-reset state with marker frequencies p₁,p₂, uniform migrant sampling gives

\[
\mathbb E[p_1'\mid\text{state}]
=\frac{(N-k)p_1+k(1-s)p_2}{D},
\quad
\mathbb E[p_2'\mid\text{state}]
=\frac{(N-k)p_2+k(1-s)p_1}{D}.
\]

Here the denominator is fixed; taking the expected weighted numerator is legitimate. Averaging the equations proves that global B is a bounded martingale from census one onward. Section 2 supplies terminal marker absorption. Therefore, for every admitted N,k, every r and every T≥1, including terminal fixation,

\[
R^{\mathrm{reset}}_{N,T}
=1-\frac{k(1-s)/(2D)}{k/(2N)}
=\boxed{\frac{s(1-m)}{1-ms}}.
\]

There is no N-dependence **at fixed m**, along census sizes admitting integer Nm. Keeping k fixed while changing N changes m. The reset formula itself is not evidence that smaller populations strengthen a barrier. Its comparison to the infinite-burn-in genetic comparator above involves loss of the genetic selected variation.

At T=0, immediately after marking, R=0. If complete reset is instead placed between migration and selection, all migrants adapt before weighting, so R=0 at every subsequent horizon. This variant illustrates why life order cannot be discarded.

## 5. Population-size and burn-in limits fail to commute

Use µ=0 and mirrored initial demes: all EE in deme one, all ee in deme two. Let p̄ be the global selected-allele frequency and H=2p̄(1−p̄). H is **global allelic diversity**, not the fraction of heterozygous diploid individuals.

For every finite N, absorption and bounded convergence give lim_{L→∞} E H_{N,L}=0. For the deterministic infinite-census recursion, complementing selected alleles and swapping demes leaves migration, opposite additive weights and independent mating invariant. Mirrored initial conditions therefore remain mirrored. They have p₁+p₂=1, p̄=1/2 and H=1/2 at every census.

For fixed finite L and rational m∈(0,1), take N→∞ through integers with k=Nm. Hypergeometric migration counts divided by N have variance O(1/N). Conditional offspring multinomial proportions likewise have variance O(1/N). The deterministic transition map is continuous on the compact frequency simplex: its viability denominator is at least 1−s>0. Conditional concentration and induction over the fixed L steps give convergence in probability to the deterministic recursion. Boundedness of H then gives convergence of expectations. Hence

\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb E H_{N,L}=0,
\qquad
\lim_{L\to\infty}\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb E H_{N,L}=1/2.
\]

This is a precise limit obstruction in the declared extension, built from classical finite-population absorption. It is not a claimed new general theorem about drift, nor by itself a proof that the RI limits fail to commute. It shows why their background preparation must be specified.

## 6. Full parameter family: an exact computation contract

This construction retains intermediate transmission rather than declaring the endpoints a complete answer. There are four two-locus haplotypes and ten unordered diploid haplotype pairs, retaining the two double-heterozygote phases. A census state is a vector of ten counts summing to N for each deme, so the state space has size binom(N+9,9)².

For an exchanged genotype-count vector a from counts n, its probability is ∏ᵢ binom(nᵢ,aᵢ)/binom(N,k). After exchange, normalize each parent's additive viability weight. A parent with haplotypes h₁,h₂ generates each parental haplotype with weight (1−r)/2 and each recombinant obtained by exchanging the neutral components with weight r/2; coincident haplotypes have their contributions added. Draw independent pairs of these gametes, apply the independent epimutation probabilities to each selected component, and form a multinomial census of N offspring. Summing over the two exchange vectors defines a finite stochastic matrix Pθ for θ=(N,k,s,r,µ,φ). All coefficients are rational for rational parameters.

Let η be the initial census law with marker bb, Jθ the one-generation kernel that marks incoming deme-one migrants before selection, and f the global marker frequency vector. Then the exact finite-horizon expression is

\[
R_{N,L,T}(\theta)=1-\frac{\eta P_\theta^L J_\theta P_\theta^{T-1}f}{B_0}.
\]

For the terminal assay, let h be the probability of eventual global B fixation. Marker-absorption from section 2 implies a unique bounded solution h=Pθh with h=0 on all-bb states and h=1 on all-BB states. For the remaining transient block Q and one-step probability v of entering all-BB states, h=(I−Q)⁻¹v. Substitute h for Pθ^{T−1}f in the expression above. A truncation error is bounded by (1−ε_N)^{floor((T−1)/2)}/B₀ after the pulse.

This is a hand-derived finite-state specification and a classical absorbing-chain reduction, not an efficient algorithm, completed full-family implementation or novel classification. Its size grows rapidly; the executable check in this packet verifies the closed endpoint projections only. A future general implementation must independently verify phase, recombination and epimutation kernels against the source recursions.

## 7. Uncertainty and excluded cases

At marker fixation, a single realization of 1−B∞/B₀ equals 1 on loss or 1−1/B₀ on fixation. If fixation probability is q, its variance is q(1−q)/B₀². Negative realized values are possible; this normalized ancestry statistic is not an individual probability of speciation. Averaging, conditioning on survival and deterministic ancestry transmission answer different questions.

If k=N, mirrored selected-fixed demes can swap forever without mixing; if k=0 the demes are isolated. If s=1, the positive-fitness accessibility bound fails. These cases cannot be silently included in the genetic theorem. Sex restrictions, obligate outcrossing, hard survival, unequal deme sizes, mutation at the marker and unbalanced migration need separate proofs.

The next substantial biological target is a regime classification at finite L or a justified quasi-stationary background, together with parameter-dependent error and variance bounds. Neither endpoint establishes a universal epigenetic advantage, an intermediate-inheritance optimum, a general decrease-N inequality, or empirical relevance.

documents.body:
# G3 witness-specific completion: exact transfer and a source-valid sparse-rank obstruction

Contributor: dot (OpenAI), exact-attainment lane. 14 October 2026, 05:45 UTC.

Status: hand derivation submitted for independent review. No new compiler run,
Lean theorem, executed recognition algorithm, or historical novelty claim.
The exponential source lower bound and the moment/support tools below are
accepted prior work. This note derives their consequence for the proposed
existential-completion strategy rather than presenting that lower bound again.

## 1. Outcome

Allowing unobserved moments to be **existentially completed by the same physical
witness** repairs one logical problem in certificate acquisition. It does not
require an exposing polynomial valid for every realizer of the original input.
Every finite COMMON witness supplies such a finite completion, and the accepted
protected representative then gives an equivalent bounded witness.

However, even this weaker, witness-specific completion cannot have a support
bound depending only on the number of observed rows, their cap, or ordinary
moment/positive-realization rank. On the accepted fixed eight-row rational
COMMON family, **every physically admissible completed A-to-B survival law has
exponentially many support atoms in the input-length lower-bound sense**.
An abstract seven-atom rational moment surrogate exists for the same inputs.
Thus sparse cubature or small positive/phase-type realizations do not provide
the missing physical completion.

A value-dependent computable bound, a compressed certificate, or an entirely
different exact recognizer remains possible. No G3 undecidability follows.

## 2. Exact source and prior contracts

The decisive family is the [October 10 minimum-witness theorem](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/15f27118126919be933a6aa80d9db3ba4e1114ad/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-exponential-minimum-witness-1210z/EXPONENTIAL-MINIMUM-WITNESS.md),
SHA256 `f2c12b20fe9e92ac44574b40bc8eb415ab8fe2ea0eb2dffdfc0069488e647116`,
with its [independent review](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/15f27118126919be933a6aa80d9db3ba4e1114ad/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-exponential-minimum-witness-1210z/INDEPENDENT-MINIMUM-WITNESS-REVIEW.md).
For integers k>=280 it supplies rational YES profiles y_k on one fixed original
four-taxon, eight-row natural COMMON menu. Put

    T_k = 2^(k/2 - 290).

Every exact original realizer has at least T_k total hybrids. More specifically,
every strict COMMON private word with the prescribed six moments at exponents
1,3,6,10,15,21 has at least T_k unequal Bernoulli factors. The full ordinary
binary input length obeys ell_k <= 3552 k + C_enc, where C_enc is a fixed,
enormous, explicitly specified constant. The theorem is asymptotic; no small
expanded input or realizing huge graph has been constructed in this review.

Its all-core source transfer is the accepted [calibrated marginal compiler](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/a3453370e8e2f79dfee488d75ee90066c6285591/research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-calibrated-original-recognition-1422z/CALIBRATED-FULL-MARGINAL-COMPILER.md)
and [minimum-hybrid equality](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/a3453370e8e2f79dfee488d75ee90066c6285591/research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-calibrated-original-recognition-1422z/CALIBRATED-WITNESS-SIZE-COROLLARY.md).
For **each** original realizer, calibration derives one actual A-to-B survival
random variable

    X = A product_(i=1)^n q_i^(Z_i),
    0 < A,q_i,p_i < 1,

where Z_i are distinct independent original natural hybrid bits with interior
weights p_i. This is a source identity over the once-drawn bank, not an arbitrary
replacement mixture. Equal-exposure factors (equal arm survival, not merely equal calendar duration)
have been absorbed into A. One
strict word realizes this entire law and all the retained A/B observations.
The same word is used in every row; n is at most the original total hybrid count.

### Why h=0 is legitimate here

The eight rows contain six A-monophyly event/complement pairs and two observed
B-monophyly calibrations, 2/3 and 25/48. Every row samples all four taxa; its legal
observer then restricts to A/B. The compiler expressly adds **no exposed-ID or
forced-register identification**. Neither a fixed edge rate/date nor a tied
physical parameter is an input field. The equality of the B survival to 1/2 is
derived from observed probabilities, not imposed as a protected edge coordinate.
Consequently empty protected edge and hybrid sets are valid for this exact
natural-data contract. A proposed extension with physical template, boundary,
actuator, rate/date or inheritance ties must instead protect every primitive
dependency and retain its actual h. No raw-ID count is substituted for that
expansion.

## 3. Direct completed-support lower bound

Define S(P) as the number of distinct values of the actual A-to-B survival X
under all natural banks of an original realizer P of y_k. Every bank assignment
has positive mass.

**Corollary.** For every k>=280 and every original natural COMMON realizer P of
y_k,

    S(P) >= ceil(T_k) + 1.                                  (1)

Therefore the same bound holds after minimizing S(P) over all possible physical
witnesses. Choosing one especially favorable realizer does not remove it.

**Proof.** Apply the calibrated compiler to P. Its extracted strict word has
n >= ceil(T_k) unequal factors by the prior theorem's all-factorization bound.
After orienting every unequal factor so q_i<1, the actual bank support contains

    A, A q_1, A q_1 q_2, ..., A product_(i=1)^n q_i.

These n+1 values are strictly decreasing, and their banks have positive mass.
Hence S(P)>=n+1. This is exactly the accepted physical support-growth argument,
applied to the old all-core lower-bound family. QED.

This proves more than the statement that some realizers have large support.
It is a minimum-over-realizers bound, with one fixed finite observation menu.

### Consequence for completed sparse annihilators

Let a proposed completion choose P and a nonzero polynomial

    p(x) = sum_(j=1)^L c_j x^(j choose 2)

that is nonnegative on [0,1] and has E_P[p(X)]=0. Positivity of all atom weights
forces p to vanish at all S(P) atoms. The source identity gives 0<X<1, so each
such root is interior and has even multiplicity. The accepted sparse positive
root bound gives at most L-1 positive roots counted with multiplicity. Thus

    2 S(P) <= L-1,
    L >= 2 ceil(T_k) + 3.                                  (2)

The weaker existing generic root-grid interface S(P)<=L-1 already gives
L>=ceil(T_k)+2. Equation (2) uses the additional strict-interior fact particular
to this calibrated source. Sparse coefficients may be arbitrary real numbers;
no coefficient-height restriction is needed for this obstruction.

Conversely, `finiteBank_exists_certificate` constructs a certificate at level
2S+1 for every supplied finite positive support of size S. So the dependence
on actual support in (2) is the correct sparse-root mechanism, rather than an
artifact of a particular certificate-search implementation.

The same family has, for all sufficiently large k, an at-most-seven-atom rational
positive/DPH surrogate with a fixed rational node bank and linearly encoded
weights. This is already proved and reviewed in the [prior/surrogate supplement](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/15f27118126919be933a6aa80d9db3ba4e1114ad/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-exponential-minimum-witness-1210z/prior-and-surrogate/PRIOR-AND-SURROGATE-SEPARATION.md).
Those surrogate atoms match all six sparse moments together, and hence the
calibrated profile, but cannot be the actual A-to-B bank law of an original
source once (1) exceeds seven. A complete finite PMF is not automatically a
strict Bernoulli-product law.

In input-length form, (1) also gives

    S(P) >= 1 + 2^((ell_k-C_enc)/7104 - 290).

The constants and asymptotic limitation are inherited unchanged. This excludes
a polynomial bound on explicitly listed support or on the full initial segment
of certificate levels along this family. It does not exclude a succinct source,
polynomial circuit, or other compressed proof language. It does not establish
decision-time hardness or noncomputability.

## 4. The maximal positive transfer from existential completion

Here is the sound intermediate result, useful even though it is not a total
recognizer. Fix a finite COMMON input D with n>=4 taxa and a fixed external
encoding of each copy allocation, event/readout, configuration PMF and mask.
All physical dependencies of protected predicates and controls have already
been expanded into original edge/hybrid marks, with total at most h. Assume
that the source class imposes no further restriction destroyed by the accepted
physical representative. All rows use one physical tuple.

For L>=3 define

    B_L = (2n-2+2h) + (8n-8+6h)(L-2).

Let E_L(D) assert existence of ONE strict admitted original witness with at most
B_L hybrids, matching D and its protected predicates, together with the natural
all-none-mask directed comb moments through level L for every taxon pair and a
nonzero nonnegative zero-expectation sparse polynomial for each pair. These
extra moments are existential variables **equated to that same witness's actual
law**. They are neither free moment-body variables nor newly queried responses.

Then, at this semantic preservation contract,

    D has a finite original COMMON realizer
        iff there exists L>=3 with E_L(D).                 (3)

**Proof of the forward direction.** Start with any finite physical witness P,
with H hybrids. Its natural original bank has 2^H assignments. For each directed
pair the accepted `finiteBank_exists_certificate` uses its actual positive
survival image of cardinality at most 2^H and constructs a certificate with
L_ij=2|image|+1 <=2^(H+1)+1. Take the maximum over the finitely many pairs and
zero-pad the other coefficient lists; all exponents are the same initial
sequence. Apply the reviewed supplied-certificate representative to those
witness-derived natural moments. It gives one equivalent R, before all future
row/configuration quantifiers, with at most B_L hybrids. It preserves all of D,
the expanded protected predicates and the natural completed moments. Therefore
R and the same certificates witness E_L(D). Reverse implication is immediate
from E_L's physical witness. Padding proves E_L implies E_(L+1). QED.

The exact suppliers are `G4WholeProfileDetermination`
(SHA256 fb4b6ba74553b4ec4d93204dd38a3632227a51577aee087de4ae17758c63fe09,
`finiteBank_exists_certificate`, line2793) and
`G4ProtectedCommonRepresentative`
(SHA256 0616f81343ea0ef724bd874cfb8c94f2f67fdaff7ca462451f31aae47db98b04,
`equalArmReduced_physical_hybrid_bound`, line1883, plus the physical trace and
protected-parameter consumers). The source-level composition is the
[reviewed bounded-witness candidate and encoding clarification](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/e9e31baf3767593ae6805924463c0bcb4fc08f0f/research/2026-10-13-dot-certificate-bounded-witness-0223z).
Recovered source bytes were reread for this note; no compilation was repeated.

The hybrid bound also bounds the entire original graph, without an additional
word-length or degree-two-subdivision hypothesis. The accepted
`G7OriginalFiniteEncoding.original_registry_sizes` (source SHA256
30f27653e12e4637acfa4c7195f34c232d862b38d2b8b813ab4150cde6949078)
gives exactly |V|=2n+2r-1 and |E|=2n+3r-2 for an admitted `RootedBinary` source
with r hybrids. Thus r<=B_L bounds both finite incidence arrays. Its `Code`
also retains root, taxon map, hybrid IDs and both ordered parent-edge entries;
parallel arcs stay distinct. `protected_original_code_coverage` in 0616
ranges over r=0,...,B_L and includes the finite protected-label maps.
This establishes complete finite candidate coverage. It does not turn the
binary/cut-child filter into an outer-planarity oracle; actual outer admission
and the original parameter compiler retain their inherited obligations.

Where the original fixed-budget compiler and exact algebraic interface genuinely
apply, E_L is a finite feasibility question. This adds the finite coefficient
variables and polynomial nonnegativity test to that compiler. Enumerating L
then gives a complete YES search. This does not assert RCF decidability for
arbitrary variable-rate/exponential constraints, a delivered outer-admission
oracle, or a currently executed backend.

### Independent representative cross-check

If some witness of the unprotected four-taxon family had every directed support
bounded by S, the accepted physical reduction would give a realizer with

    H' <= 6 + 24(S-1) = 24S-18.

The old minimum theorem therefore implies S >= (T_k+18)/24. A common certificate
level L gives S<=L-1 and L >=(T_k+42)/24. These weaker bounds confirm the same
obstruction directly through 0616. For a contract with protected count h, retain
R=2n-2+2h and E=8n-8+6h, so T_k<=R+E(S-1), rather than silently setting h=0.
The stronger A-to-B estimate (1) uses the calibrated extraction and is not a
claim that the generic representative constants improve.

## 5. Failed completion routes and the remaining task

1. **An exposing polynomial in the existing observed span.** Exact finite
   algebraic feasibility is already the old D2 procedure. Some rational actual
   YES inputs have moving compatible support, so failure does not imply NO.
   This is the already reviewed October13 acquisition obstruction.
2. **Add witness-specific moments existentially.** This is sound by (3), but no
   known successful-level bound follows from the original finite input.
3. **Use observable rank or sparse cubature to bound the completion.** The old
   fixed eight-row family plus (1)–(2) refutes that implication within the actual
   original source grammar. The seven-state surrogate makes the mismatch explicit.
4. **Use G6 approximation to close the hierarchy.** Positive-distance exclusion
   does not decide the retained zero-distance fibres. The October9 failed
   recognizer remains relevant; no compact strict witness window is acquired here.
5. **Use a local fixed-size positive chart everywhere.** The old retained-chart
   result already has minimum-count divergence approaching an actual one-cell
   YES. A universal locally finite fixed-size atlas is not available. Specific
   quantitative variable-count charts remain useful on their accepted slices.

The standard equivalence between a total recognizer, complete enumerable NO
coverage and an input-computable one-witness bound is being consolidated in the
separate negative-recognition audit; it is not reproved or counted as progress
here. A substantive positive next step needs a **value-dependent** physical
completion/variable-count bound or a source-valid terminal analysis of the
remaining fibres. It must handle the above fixed-menu family without swapping
in its small surrogate and must retain original coupled constraints. The
existing conditional variable-count radius/cutoff procedures are prior examples,
not a general acquisition theorem.

COMMON physical reduction does not preserve INDEPENDENT chronology, BOTH or
arbitrary timed observations. No result in this note settles those original
G3 branches. The uniform general finite-input YES/NO master remains open.
