# Independent reciprocal exponents at fixed algebraic bases

Stable source key: G3-ARITH-INDEP-RECIP-EQ-01.

23 October 2026. Existing G3 owner. Status: PROVED BY HAND, not Lean
formalized. Independent review has not been performed; no solver, source
producer, numerical check, native build or new experiment was run.
This is a supporting arithmetic result, not original G3 closure or a new
full G3 attack. No historical novelty claim is made for its classical inputs.

## 1. Prior-solution comparison and precise increment

Original G3 still requires total exact recognition on every original finite
algebraic joint input, one actual strict source/ID map/physical bank on YES,
and termination excluding every unknown finite source on NO. Its original
COMMON/I/BOTH, menu, chronology and register contract is unchanged.

The following actual statements/proofs were compared before selecting this
extension. Commons below is8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6.

- The accepted predecessor is
  `handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-unreviewed-source-copy-001/INPUT-RADICAL-BOUND-AND-FULL-SOURCE-TEST-03.md`,
  25098B/SHA25697987236e5c6f5429d2f597ff1ebd5b34dac7078ff56515122483524a5ad968e,
  Gitblob09d171c9d252f7120cd8dc5f97b25f48c7fd3de7, with later scoped
  `research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-radical-review-0055z/REVIEW.md`,
  SHA179b0a86bdbc37816f971cf5fe072c0258071e47a5c205ae85c0852897468af4.
  Its common-denominator reciprocal-power obstruction, identity alternative
  and source counter-test are OLD/REUSE. Sections3--4 were reread for the
  exact exponent quantifier; the complete proof/review had already been read.
- The subsequent COMPLETE20193B source
  `handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-primitive-multiplicity-increment-005/ONE-TYPE-BOUNDEDNESS-AND-PRIMITIVE-MULTIPLICITIES-07.md`,
  SHA5c5cd7e670d670d528d0a8414ec39748e37db467e84c4d1b18f25b20056f9916,
  Gitblob67aaf47b31c221fd4749f8f547abb57fb96d61c3, was read. It supplies
  hand boundedness without an effective exceptional cutoff, and a fixed
  rational full source input with arbitrarily large independently chosen
  multiplicities whose physical types RETUNE. It expressly preserves the
  distinction between every presentation and one witness. Those completed
  hand arguments are reused, not reopened for missing Lean/review.
- The saturated positive S-unit coordinate construction in
  `G3-REPEATED-BLOCK-ALGEBRAIC-COUNT.md` is reused. Its earlier NEW attribution
  is corrected by `G3-RECIPROCAL-PRIOR-ATTRIBUTION-CORRECTION-20261023.md`.
  Saturation and classical radical independence are not new here.
- The COMPLETE6915B old `RATIONAL-REPETITION-COUNT-SCREEN.md` under
  `research/2026-10-08-codex-g3-g4-full-shot-1253z/g3-impossibility/nonlinear-counter-lifts/`,
  SHAa21c138332f51f5db48d58374d5745a83b4e896bf585da161729c90761322bd9,
  excludes a literal fixed rational Jordan-counter readout. No such readout
  or hardness simulation is assumed below.

The increment is an explicit terminating EQUALITY decision with independently
varying denominator integers and FIXED algebraic bases. It does not bound all
solutions. The retuned-head counterexample has moving bases and does not
contradict this statement. This bounded source comparison does not establish
historical priority or absence of the result from all literature.

## 2. Decision problem

Given finitely many positive effectively real-algebraic numbers beta_{sti},
effectively real-algebraic coefficients c_{st}, and positive integer lower
bounds nu_i, define, for independently chosen integers n_i>=nu_i,

    F_s(n) = sum_t c_{st} * product_{i=1}^k beta_{sti}^{1/n_i}.

Every root is the unique POSITIVE root. The same vector n serves every F_s.
Given a finite Boolean formula made from F_s(n)=0 and F_s(n)!=0, decide
whether any such n exists and return one vector when it does.

THEOREM. This problem has a total effective algorithm. In particular it
covers finite systems of polynomial equalities/disequalities in positive
algebraic reciprocal roots with separately varying denominator counts.
It does not assert a decision for arbitrary polynomial SIGN inequalities.

The proof consists of a finite radical-ratio partition and the following
elementary unit-fraction decision procedure.

## 3. Rational-linear constraints on unit fractions

LEMMA. Feasibility of a finite Boolean combination of rational affine
linear equalities and disequalities in u_i=1/n_i, n_i>=nu_i, is decidable,
with an integer witness on YES.

Expand the Boolean formula into finitely many conjunctions. Consider one
conjunction A u=b together with L_j(u)!=d_j. Use induction on the number m
of unassigned variables; after a choice, substitute its rational reciprocal
everywhere. With no variables, test rational constants exactly.

If some remaining equality has nonzero right-hand side, choose one,

    sum_i a_i/n_i=b,   b!=0.

If all a_i=0 the branch is impossible. Otherwise any solution satisfies

    |b| <= sum_i |a_i|/n_i.

Hence, for at least one i with a_i!=0,

    n_i <= floor(m*|a_i|/|b|).

Enumerate every such index and every integer in its finite permitted range,
substitute, and recurse. Every possible solution enters some branch. The
number of unassigned variables strictly decreases, so this part terminates.

It remains to handle a branch whose equalities are all HOMOGENEOUS, A u=0.
Solve the rational-linear feasibility problem

    A v=0,  v_i>0,  L_j(v)!=0 for every j with d_j=0.

This is a finite sign split of rational linear systems. A nonempty one has
a rational point v, obtainable effectively; rational points are dense in
its rational affine hull and the inequalities are strict. If no such v
exists, there is no unit-fraction solution either.

Write the selected positive v_i=a_i/b_i in lowest terms. Choose a positive
integer T divisible by every a_i, sufficiently large that

    T >= nu_i*v_i  for every i,
    |L_j(v)|/T < |d_j|  whenever d_j!=0.

There are finitely many rational bounds, so this choice is effective.
Then u=v/T has n_i=T*b_i/a_i in the required positive integer range.
Homogeneous equalities/disequalities are retained by positive scaling, and
the other disequalities hold by the strict displayed bound. This constructs
a solution. The construction also permits every remaining n_i to exceed any
additional supplied common lower bound. No limiting n_i=infinity is used.

Both directions and termination have now been proved for the conjunction;
the finite disjunction proves the lemma. Coefficient signs and cancellations
are allowed: the finite branching estimate used absolute values, not an
incorrect termwise positivity assumption.

## 4. Effective saturated algebraic coordinates

Take a real number field K containing every beta and coefficient, with its
specified real embedding. Let Gamma be the subgroup generated by all beta.
The positive saturation

    Gamma_sat = {g in K, g>0 : g^h in Gamma for some integer h>=1}

is effectively finitely generated and torsion-free. This is the OLD
S-unit/lattice construction: let S be the finite set of prime ideals
supporting the beta. Every saturation element is a positive S-unit. In a
basis of that group, take the rational span of the integer coordinate
columns of the beta and intersect it with the ambient integer lattice.
Smith normal form supplies a primitive lattice basis. Its positive S-units
g_1,...,g_r form a basis of Gamma_sat, with computable integer coordinates
for every beta. No unproved GRH/unit-group output or logarithmic zero test
is part of this input.

For clarity, effectiveness of the positive S-unit basis can be acquired by
the standard finite-index construction already given in the reused source.
The known rank permits enumeration until a full-rank logarithmic/valuation
tuple is certified by a NONZERO determinant enclosure. Reduction into its
parallelepiped bounds S-valuations and all Archimedean absolute values.
After multiplying by a fixed rational integer, a computable finite
integral-basis box contains all quotient representatives. Enumerating those
supplies generators for the full group. Exact algebraic product relations,
their known kernel rank, lattice saturation and Smith normal form extract
a basis. Positivity at the chosen embedding removes the only real torsion,
-1. This repeats the established acquisition argument, not a new algorithm
implementation or claimed backend execution.

For q in Q^r, the unique positive value g^q lies in K if and only if q is
integral. The forward direction follows because some power of g^q lies in
Gamma, so membership in K puts it in Gamma_sat; uniqueness of coordinates
in its free basis then gives q in Z^r. The reverse direction is immediate.
Uniqueness for rational coordinates follows by clearing denominators and
using multiplicative independence of the basis.

## 5. A finite radical-ratio partition

Take the union of the radical monomials in ALL F_s, assigning coefficient0
when one is absent from an F_s; combine duplicates if desired. Index this
finite set by t. Put u_i=1/n_i. In the saturated basis each monomial is

    M_t(u) = g^{v_t(u)},   v_t(u)=sum_i a_{ti}*u_i in Q^r,

where all coordinate vectors a_{ti} are known integers. Constants can be
included using the zero vector. Rank r=0 gives M_t=1 and is decided directly
by algebraic coefficient arithmetic.

For each coordinate h choose an integer bound

    B_h >= max_{t,t'} sum_i |a_{ti,h}-a_{t'i,h}|.

Because 0<u_i<=1, every integral vector v_t(u)-v_{t'}(u) is in the FIXED
finite box product_h[-B_h,B_h]. Thus every possible pair of K-proportional
monomials has one of finitely many rational-linear descriptions

    v_t(u)-v_{t'}(u)=z,  z in that box.

Enumerate partitions of the monomial index set into proposed proportionality
classes. In each class choose a representative t0 and enumerate the possible
integral differences z_t=v_t-v_t0, setting z_t0=0. Impose these equalities.
For indices in different classes, exclude EVERY integral vector in the box
as their difference. Each exclusion is a finite disjunction of rational
linear disequalities. Inconsistent choices are harmless and are rejected
by the unit-fraction lemma. Every actual n induces one enumerated choice.

In a fixed choice, the contribution of class C to F_s is

    M_t0(u) * A_{s,C},
    A_{s,C}=sum_{t in C} c_{st}*g^{z_t} in K,

where an absent coefficient is zero. Every A_{s,C} is an EXACT algebraic
constant, independent of the remaining integers.

Representatives of different classes are linearly independent over K.
Each has some positive integer power in K, and their pair ratios are
outside K by the constraints. Apply Carr--O'Sullivan, Theorem1.1 for REAL
field extensions, with the elementary one-element case included. Therefore

    F_s(n)=0 iff A_{s,C}=0 for EVERY class C.

This uses the classical pairwise-to-joint radical independence theorem,
not a new transcendence result. Its statement and Section2 proof were read
at https://arxiv.org/html/math/0703522v2 . No complex root choices or
root-of-unity substitutions are permitted.

Evaluate the requested Boolean formula using these decidable algebraic
class sums. Discard choices where it is false. For every remaining choice,
apply Section3 to its rational-linear constraints on the SAME u vector.
There are only finitely many choices, and each test terminates. A successful
one returns integers n_i and the corresponding exact algebraic roots.
If none succeeds, all integer vectors are excluded. This proves the theorem.

## 6. Consequences and exact G3 boundary

The procedure supplies a total one-witness bound for THIS root-equality
problem: on YES return the maximum count in its returned vector, on NO
return0. It does not bound every solution. For example,

    (2^(1/n_1))^2 = 2^(1/n_2)

has all n_1=2*n_2, with arbitrarily large solutions; the method can return
(2,1). This is a hand example, not a computational check.

The mechanism removes a common-denominator requirement when all algebraic
bases are supplied and the requested constraints are equalities/disequalities.
It does NOT decide:

- polynomial SIGN inequalities in the reciprocal roots;
- arbitrary real exponents;
- physical heads or hidden per-slot base vectors that vary with n;
- unknown original-source reconstruction, menus or the complete joint fibre;
- the several-log Phi=0 predicate on the original cone-promised inputs.

The16October successor's independent primitive multiplicities have types
retuning on one fixed complete source input. Those unknown type outputs
cannot be replaced by individually supplied fixed algebraic bases. Even a
necessary root equality is not sufficient physical source admission. Any
use as an original YES/NO engine must prove the exact source equivalence
and retain natural strictness, IDs, chronology, registers and one bank.
No such full-source supplier is acquired here.

Original G3 remains ACTIVE and unresolved. The next missing implication is
source-complete acquisition of the required fixed-base/equality description,
or a genuinely different all-input bound/NO mechanism; this theorem is not
that acquisition under a different name. There is no new cap/rank ladder,
source experiment, review obligation on completed work, owner transfer,
worker/chat, local Git action or held-job replay.

## 7. Source and evidence record

The companion SOURCE-STATUS.json preserves the separate mathematical, review,
formal and implementation axes. It is a source-status record for this one
claim, not a second master registry. Author completion is PROVED (not Lean
formalized); independent review and implementation were not performed.

Immutable prior sources actually compared:

- [Accepted common-denominator predecessor](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6/handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-unreviewed-source-copy-001/INPUT-RADICAL-BOUND-AND-FULL-SOURCE-TEST-03.md) and its [scoped hand review](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-radical-review-0055z/REVIEW.md).
- [Later retuned-type/primitive-multiplicity successor](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6/handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-primitive-multiplicity-increment-005/ONE-TYPE-BOUNDEDNESS-AND-PRIMITIVE-MULTIPLICITIES-07.md).
- [Classical real radical independence, Carr--O'Sullivan Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0703522v2). The classical theorem supplies radical independence; it is not claimed as a new result.

The exact increment is the finite class partition plus the terminating
unit-fraction recursion for independently chosen denominators. Historical
priority of that combination has not been established. No mathematical
experiment, implementation, compiler, QE instance or new model job was run.

# P1: a direct measurement bound from a Holevo increment

20 October 2026. dot (OpenAI), working with Nolan.

For every finite ensemble of quantum states, its actual n-copy pretty good measurement, reporting its candidate state, obeys

    expected squared Bures loss <= Q_n <= 2(1-exp(-delta_n)) <= 2 delta_n,
    expected squared full trace norm <= 4 Q_n <= 8 delta_n.

Here Q_n is the affinity/square-root loss and delta_n=chi_(n+1)-chi_n is the finite-prior Holevo increment. This includes noncommuting, interacting, coefficientwise-bounded Gibbs candidates and does not assume an eigenvalue lower bound. The proof uses a CPTP block-Gram channel and identity-reference Schatten interpolation. The proof's extra register does not query an additional unknown copy.

This repairs a direct Bures/affinity measurement gate. It does NOT equate the Holevo increment with Umegaki prediction risk after measurement; the previously identified information-loss term for that stronger loss remains valid. It is not a generic unrotated Petz-recovery fidelity theorem.

## What remains open

The original P1 class and full-copy accounting are unchanged. A uniform Gibbs estimate delta_n=O_(beta,k)(M/n), or a suitable dyadic estimate chi_(2n)-chi_n=O_(beta,k)(M), remains unproved. Here M=sum_(j=1)^k 3^j binom(N,j). The prior-independent/minimax two-source step must retain all original copies. No improved full P1 upper or lower bound is claimed; accepted upper13 and lower32 remain unchanged.

## Reading and evidence

2. [Unchanged producing-pass candidate](P1-PGM-AFFINITY-INCREMENT-CANDIDATE-20261020.md).

7. [Hash manifest](MANIFEST.json): exact included bytes.

The scientific status is a scoped mathematical hand proof and a separate assistant-context review, not external peer review, a novelty claim, a uniform Gibbs rate, a Lean-verified result, a laboratory experiment, or efficient circuit implementation. # Independent review of quadratic joint acquisition

Reviewer: dot (OpenAI), existing review lane. 2026-10-14 23:13 UTC.

## Verdict

**Scoped HAND PASS** for Theorem Q and the stated fixed-chart/fixed-residue comparison example in [comment6180481227](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/issues/1#issuecomment-6180481227), as read during this review. No blocking mathematical defect found. This is acceptance of a sufficient source-producing branch under the complete inherited receiver, not universal G3 acquisition, all-core recognition, a complete NO language, implementation or Lean verification. The expanded local manuscript/checker claimed by the contributor was not independently retrieved; the reviewed proof is the self-contained public comment. The attached saved comment records the reviewed version.

## 1. Algebraic acquisition and rank

For fixed rational residues and denominators, all moment coordinates A^lambda B^e and derivatives of the composed polynomial feasible chart F are algebraic-polynomial expressions. The finite rho disjunction, Jw=Jv_i=0, Wxi+c+H(w)=0 and rank conditions are finite RCF formulas. Algebraic sampling includes the curvature directions; no unknown physical witness supplies them. Rank W=rho and rank[W,B(w,v_i)]=k imply that any rho independent columns L_I spanning imW, together with the k-rho stated curvature columns, form an invertible square matrix.

L differs from W by nonzero column scalings, including computable b_s>0. Selection can therefore be made by exact algebraic minors of W; solving for z0 in L_I z0=-(c+H(w)) is computable and consistent. Logs are not placed in the RCF predicate. rho=k,w=0 recovers the existing branch. In corank one, scaling v by sqrt[-ell c/(ell H(v))] cancels the quotient residual and yields ell B(w,v)=2a0 ell H(v), nonzero. The sign is correct.

## 2. Orders, remainder and removable extension

The old cubic split is inherited, not a new identity. After t=s^2 the moment perturbations start at s^6, with their next possible order s^8. The feasible core motion is s^3(w+sum kappa_i v_i)+s^6 eta. Its linear s^3 term vanishes identically for all correction variables because J kills every displayed direction. Its order-six contribution is Jeta+H(w+sum kappa_i v_i). Core cubic and core-slot mixed terms begin at s^9; slot quadratic terms begin at s^12. Thus all derivatives of P-y below six vanish identically in the correction variables, not just at one root.

Taylor's integral remainder gives (P(s,x)-y)/s^6 = (1/5!) integral_0^1(1-tau)^5 partial_s^6 P(tau s,x)d tau. The coefficient is correct: integrating the weight and multiplying by1/5! gives1/6!. Log arguments remain positive on sufficiently small compact boxes, including s=0; this establishes analytic extension without dividing by a numerically tiny s. The selected x derivative at the limiting root is exactly [L_I,B(w,v_i)].

## 3. Effectiveness, strict certificates and common N

The acquired algebraic point and positive algebraic A,B yield computable logs, finite computable z0 and inverse Jacobian. Polynomial/log/exp compositions and their derivatives have effective compact-box bounds once strict denominator margins are certified. Uniform bounds can be refined by rational subdivision; the known open semialgebraic U can be handled using an interior rational box around u0 and exact algebraic comparisons. An arbitrary membership oracle for U is neither needed nor admitted.

Dovetailing rational centres, invertible rational preconditioners, positive radii/s0 and finite enclosure precision is essential: a failed or equality-boundary candidate must not block the search. The limiting exact root/invertible derivative ensures some strictly certified candidate exists. The first1/3 derivative and eps/6 centre bounds leave genuine slack. At fixed positive s0, the residual replacement has a jointly analytic delta=0 extension through the stated log integral. Uniform C1 convergence on the computed compact cube yields a positive rational E with the1/2 and eps/4 bounds. These searches use finite derivative certificates and known strict existence, not a transcendental equality decision.

Use the residual weight b_s(s0^2), uniformly over the whole correction cube, in the additional E*b_s<1 condition; this is the same notation/convention as the inherited regular construction. It is not enough to check only the unperturbed centre b_s. With this interpretation, N with1/N<=E gives every primary probability strictly between0and1. The preconditioned map sends the closed eps cube into its3eps/4 subcube and contracts. R invertible turns its fixed point into an exact zero. The same chosen N is valid for every slot. No practical bound on N or conditioning is claimed.

## 4. Source legality and final algebraic extraction

The final equations use the finite shape with N+2 factors per eligible slot, the original polynomial chart/equalities and every target row. They do not impose the analytic path or logarithmic constants as algebraic constraints. The analytic solution proves nonempty real feasibility; an algebraic point can then be sampled. Numerically equal parameters on repeated factors do not identify their distinct natural bits. All slots and retained coordinates are solved together. Hence the count bound H_core+q(N+2) is valid under the inherited fresh unexposed COMMON, entering-cap<=7, legal insertion, polynomial survival-coordinate and complete-joint-kernel contract.

The example uses two retained pendant COMMON bigons, not two invented abstract kernels. Equal branch survivals make the first bit's complete population kernel independent of p. The second contributes z^lambda[1-g(1-r^(3lambda))]; all fixed ordinary factors collect into rho0^lambda. Its supplied finite polynomial relation g=g0-(p-1/2)^2 and |u|<d0 give an actual open feasible curve with p,g interior. The relation is allowed for this constructed input; it is not imposed on arbitrary input or on unbounded fresh positions. The extra protected bigons are included in H_core. Calendar/graph insertion legality and complete forest reconstruction remain the accepted receiver's providers, rather than new runtime checks.

The cited original A/B compiler applies to the stipulated natural unranked A/B-restricted rows with all four taxa sampled and fixed B calibration. It does not promote the example to arbitrary full four-taxon, exposed-register, timed or INDEPENDENT data. Within that menu, the actual pendant construction preserves the full joint word and supplied ties. Additional protected side information does not require importing the compiler's converse for every possible alternative constrained core; this is a constructive YES example.

## 5. Fixed-family separation and exact controls

The Descartes argument is valid: a nonzero polynomial with at most seven monomials cannot have seven positive roots counted with multiplicity; annihilation of Lambda,D(r),D'(r),D(r^2),D'(r^2),D(r^3) would force doubles at1,r,r^2 and a simple root at r^3. Hence the sixth direction is independent. For g<=g0<1/8, denominators1-gd exceed1/2 and |B0(g)-a|<=2gC<a/4, so B0 is strictly positive.

In the equality of two weak centres, applying nu cancels both logA and logB directions. Strict positivity of B0 on (g0/2,g0] forces g=g0 and u=0. Independence of Lambda,D(r) then fixes A,B. Thus the old full-rank test fails at every centre of this fixed template/chart/residue family, whereas Q succeeds. EXACT-CONTROLS.json SHA256 ad4e3d2cd80d1cb1b4002cfd77687365cbe781a419a5b2af0701a5420bbf46b1. These are small exact arithmetic controls, not executed QE, radius selection, source synthesis or the paused compiler workload.

## 6. Prior work and remaining obligations

Directly reread: [regular proof/review](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/80cb48d0301f8a7097e7a841de93ed3863bda80d/research/2026-10-14-dot-g3-regular-acquisition-handoff-0906z/regular), original polynomial criterion at eb284f41 (EXACT-CRITERION.md blob c66168d611800e32b986d243f9fba8fd9840ca05), and the [full A/B compiler](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/d47787d8f4f9a91a4d66dbc5769a4358d0383c0d/research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-calibrated-original-recognition-1422z/CALIBRATED-FULL-MARGINAL-COMPILER.md), blob063a5ffe4dc9e9890d71d895a7f6d6f15a36fa28. The public regular proof already supplies algebraic acquisition, the cubic split, effective double contraction, common integer replacement and final fixed-shape RCF extraction. The present addition is the algebraic feasible-curvature predicate and its s^3/s^6 reduced construction, with fixed-family separation example. Those inherited steps must not be claimed anew.

[Shi's author-hosted notes](https://jxshix.people.wm.edu/2013-taiwan/taiyuan-notes2011.pdf), Section1, give the classical contraction/implicit-function method, including the1/2 and3/4 cube argument. This is method background, not a theorem supplying the project's biological receiver or effective acquisition completeness. No historical novelty is certified.

Successful Q still ends in an invertible finite-source contraction. Perturbing full output changes the fixed reduced equation by -Delta/s0^6, so sufficiently small changes admit the same finite N. # General G3 and G4: directed remaining-obligation audit

Contributor: dot (OpenAI). 16 October 2026, 19:29 UTC. Coordinating source/status review approved 16 October 2026, 19:30 UTC. Original master quantifiers retained. No new proof, execution, undecidability or historical novelty claim.

## 0. Executive answer

Substantial parts are already resolved: exact fixed-source compilation and feasibility, protected finite core reduction, positive physical approximation, certificate-bounded COMMON slices, several exact local acquisition branches, finite natural BOTH determination, and entire-INDEPENDENT to entire-COMMON transfer. They must not be presented as absent.

Two master implications remain unproved in the inspected sources: G3 requires total input-effective exact source acquisition or complete negative recognition; G4 requires one finite legal INDEPENDENT panel at each fixed target that forces its finite COMMON certificate across every unknown-size finite rival. Positive physical jets and a uniform clock budget are requirements of a particular proposed negative route, not additional independent master axioms. Their failure would not settle the positive alternative.

This audit covers the named obligations in current scope/reductions and the preserved supplier ledger, rather than claiming every historical file or every theorem in mathematics was searched.

## 1. Canonical sources and coverage

- Earlier targeted ledger covers principal statements and scoped independent receipts from October 6–15; its explicit partial-read boundaries remain. The present audit does not replay all their long proofs.

Original IDs, independently varying literal occurrences, original source admission, positive finite populations, chronology, and ONE shared physical tuple are retained wherever required by the original menu. A source normalization theorem for COMMON alone is not a general BOTH/INDEPENDENT normalization theorem.

## 2. G3 obligations and dispositions

### G3.1 Effective fixed-template exact feasibility — RESOLVED at the original polynomial contract

The original reduction's Sections 1–4 protect all finite named/tied sites, enumerate finitely many admissible retained templates, and compile each finite append word into a finite semialgebraic system. RCF decides each fixed-size case; enumerating sizes recognizes YES. This preserves full forest/register interfaces internally without granting hidden observations. Calendar/exponential extensions outside that polynomial contract require their own compiler, and are not silently added.

Missing: termination when no finite word exists. Fixed state dimension and finite action types do not bound append count.

### G3.2 Total input-only one-witness bound — STILL MISSING

A total computable H(d), defined also on NO inputs, with YES(d) implying a witness of size <=H(d), suffices. Conversely, a total G3 decider plus bounded-size search computes such an H. A minimum at each YES fibre, or minimizing a supplied source, does not meet this total-input obligation.

The [supplied certificate bound](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/7cdbb35da93dc82ce5b8ddc8db91140537838774/research/2026-10-13-dot-certificate-bounded-witness-0223z/CERTIFICATE-DERIVED-BOUNDED-WITNESS-CANDIDATE.md) was freshly read. Its COMMON exposing-polynomial premise yields

    B=(2n-2+2h)+(8n-8+6h)(S-1).

It preserves the specified protected registry and uniformly later permitted COMMON laws. Its assembly header is historical candidate status; accepted underlying providers and later scoped status must be distinguished from a new independent re-audit here. No certificate is promised for every original input. Missing certificate is not NO.

The [reviewed bounded-anchor/high-minimum composition](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/c92d959d9ef2444b70f31ac43cefc25dcfec3425/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G3-ANCHOR-BUDGET-HIGH-MINIMUM.md) rules out locally bounded budget-only completion; it does not refute encoding-sensitive H(d).

### G3.3 Exact source acquisition from compactification — NARROWER BRANCHES RESOLVED; GLOBAL COVER MISSING

The ledger's accepted fixed-normal floor, finite real-critical census, finite-residue lift, regular joint acquisition, quadratic fixed-fibre acquisition and local positive-killing recognizer genuinely produce effective bounds or exact sources under their stated premises. None proves every input enters one of these branches. Infinite retained lists force interior in the accepted normal-form setting, but the unknown remaining finite list does not acquire a global bound automatically.

[Source09 exact-fibre deletion](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8181505bd8ebb976ae4f128f088a20f93f1f8da5/handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-joint-fibre-source-09/EXACT-JOINT-FIBRE-DELETION-AND-DEGREE-COVERAGE-CORRECTION-09.md) is a supplied-shape conditional test, not an eventual-deletion theorem. Derivative kernels need not integrate to head deletion. A smaller source on another component remains possible.

Missing: an input-effective all-component/all-architecture comparison or complete exact acquisition cover. Moving-normal transverse floors require acquired separation from the exceptional set; thinness alone does not acquire it.

### G3.4 Complete NO certificate language — STILL MISSING; A PARTICULAR CLASS CONDITIONALLY OBSTRUCTED

Reduction Section 5 gives sound semialgebraic inductive certificates and decidable checking at fixed formula shape. Completeness is not established. The [all-core conditional certificate obstruction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-07-dot-g3-calibrated-certificate-classes-0253z/conditional/WORKING-PROOF-R2.md) says a promised pure algebraic rank-five input would defeat that all-state semialgebraic certificate class, even with the stated finite lifts. Missing: complete exclusion of exact nonattained boundary inputs in an actually adequate certificate language, or another total decision method.

### G3.5 Arithmetic equality on the inherited promised subproblem — PARTLY RESOLVED; RANK-FIVE VALUE TEST MISSING

[Three-log purity reduction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-three-log-purity-1210z/THREE-LOG-PURITY-REDUCTION.md) retains a five-coordinate cone promise and tests one fixed degree-eight polynomial of three algebraic logarithms. Multiplicatively dependent/rational-node branches have accepted arithmetic suppliers. The possible rank-five pure branch is neither exhibited nor excluded. Effective isolation of the logarithms is available; their nonlinear polynomial zero test is the missing operation. A computable positive lower gap conditional on nonzero value would decide this promised branch.

The [decision reassessment](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8ede964c050a23972dd7de620357f9bac7e0fc05/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G3-DECISION-THEOREM-REASSESSMENT-0900.md) already checked real-exponential model completeness, generic-power decidability and effective Schanuel-style gaps. Baker linear relations do not decide arbitrary nonlinear logarithmic equality; the generic-power nondefinability premise fails for the actual definable residue. No fresh assertion that full Schanuel is necessary is made. Even a solver for this slice would not automatically solve all append reachability.

### G3.6 Positive physical approximation/closure-distance effectivity — RESOLVED AT DECLARED G6 SCOPE; NOT EXACT ATTAINMENT

See Section 4 below. This is useful existing infrastructure, not a missing theorem. Exact membership on zero-distance boundaries remains G3's separate task.

## 3. G4 obligations and dispositions

### G4.1 Legal observer/source alignment — RESOLVED FOR THE CITED ORIGINAL NATURAL MENU

The exact bridge uses legal completed-topology rows, padding/pruning through accepted adapters, one source and tuple, and all taxa as required. Entire-law extraction and full-forest internal compilation have accepted uses. Additional interventions, hidden readouts and changed observation contracts are not supplied by these adapters.

### G4.2 Entire-I implies entire-C; finite BOTH forcing — RESOLVED

The current [entire-law acceptance](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-13-codex-g4-renewed/critical-review/ROOT-GENERAL-ALL-LAW-COMMONIZATION-ACCEPTANCE.md) and [finite BOTH acceptance](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-13-codex-g4-renewed/critical-review/ROOT-GENERAL-NATURAL-BOTH-FINITE-FORCING-ACCEPTANCE.md) supersede older gaps at those scopes. They do not permit querying COMMON rows in an I-only experiment.

### G4.3 Finite I-only exposure of C_T — STILL MISSING, EXACT POSITIVE MASTER GATE

For each fixed strict T, find a finite J_T, independent of rival architecture, such that I(N)|J_T=I(T)|J_T forces C(N)|C_T=C(T)|C_T for ALL finite unknown-size N. Existing fixed-chart Noetherianity, entire-law extraction and ambient linear span do not supply architecture-uniform J_T.

The finite-bridge predicate M_A(p)^u e_C(A,p)^v <= B_A(p)e_J(A,p), with positive M_A on strict tuples, is a sufficient guard. Fixed-architecture semialgebraic inequalities presuppose the requisite zero implication; they do not establish it uniformly over architectures. The accepted endpoint-decodable occupation restriction and unbounded-rank legal Gram examples block particular shortcuts only. No global non-finite-generation result was proved.

### G4.4 Exact finite-prefix rivals at one fixed target — STILL MISSING, ALTERNATIVE NEGATIVE MASTER GATE

For one fixed admitted T and EVERY finite legal I panel, an actual finite strict rival must match exactly and differ later. ### G4.5 High-order physical jets / exact constrained endpoint return — CONDITIONAL CORRECTION RESOLVED; PHYSICAL EXISTENCE MISSING

[Oct14 jet theorem](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/6309c491674435a06455011a0e5db791f0521078/research/2026-10-14-g4-independent-algebraic-jets-0621z/ALGEBRAIC-JET-THEOREM.md) and [independent review](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9eab89b70e9cb15340a0d047b8059f5126903c8b/research/2026-10-14-codex-g4-algebraic-jet-review-0706z/INDEPENDENT-MATHEMATICAL-REVIEW.md) provide q>R max(r,s), with R=d(6d-3)^(N-1), for a fixed full polynomial physical chart. The [Oct8 positive-cofinality attempt](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-08-dot-g4-ordinary-cofinality-1402z/ATTEMPT-A4-ORDINARY-COFINALITY-AND-EXTENSION-GAP.md) already isolates exact positive return on the lower fibre before adding each new diagonal/forest layer. ### G4.7 I-only compactification/resource budgets — NARROWER OR CORRECTED; NOT A GENERAL SIZE BOUND

### G4.8 Observation-only effective stopping and arbitrary controlled menus — SEPARATE, NOT AUTOMATIC

The semantic finite certificate question does not itself give a recognizable stopping criterion from unknown-target data. Existing declared controlled-menu/compiler contracts and G6 robust-fibre stopping apply only at their stated scope. Neither a full G3 decider nor finite natural BOTH forcing automatically resolves these extra quantifiers. They should not be used to obscure the precise natural-I master gate above.

## 4. Requested physical-approximation comparison

The answer is YES, accepted physical approximation exists. [G6 Lemma 1 and Appendix A](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-01-g6-effective-certification/PROOF.md) give actual positive bounded-length representatives at each cap and tolerance, simultaneous over entering forests, with source-faithful calendar realization. ## 5. Directed search coverage and established-method outcomes

The coordinator separately screened primary abstracts on [matrix-exponential membership](https://people.mpi-sws.org/~joel/publications/matrix-exponential17abs.html) (commuting versus unrestricted), [rational Heisenberg semigroup membership](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09597), and [Nonnegativity Problems for Matrix Semigroups](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06241). Those screens were not full-proof inspections. No exact physical-source embedding, fixed finite generator set or required commutativity was supplied. Generic undecidability cannot be transferred to G3. These external searches were not duplicated here.

The coordinator additionally read [Basu–Mohammad-Nezhad, Improved effective Łojasiewicz inequality and applications](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-sigma/article/improved-effective-lojasiewicz-inequality-and-applications/022BF859F5714FDA8050F6DC1992E48B), Theorem 2.11 and Remarks 2.12–2.13. The reported basic-closed/nonempty and bounded-set hypotheses give a d^O(n²) exponent independent of the number of constraints, with a stated zero-dimensional bound. This potentially useful modern estimate still depends on dimension and an error-bound constant; no growing-architecture strict-margin/distinction or all-cap clock guarantee was supplied. It has not been substituted automatically for the existing equality-map exponent or claimed uniformly stronger in the present charts. This entry is attributed to the coordinator's primary-source review, not an independent reread by this contributor.

## 6. Disposition

No newly identified supplier closes either original master. The audit recovers significant already resolved premises and narrows the actual missing comparisons. The most concrete requested bridge is the physical approximation-to-exact-correction inequality above, with all-cap uniform clock control where required. A bounded local or arithmetic supplier should be used when its premise is available; its failure to apply is UNKNOWN, not NO.

Keep this as one auditable obligation map rather than counting each failed route as a new result. Coordinating review approved this source/status audit, with the matrix-semigroup title corrected. This is not a new mathematical proof acceptance; no scope rewrite is proposed.

documents.title: A nonlocal realization attack on the fixed-start hidden reaction-network fibre
documents.body:
# A nonlocal realization attack on the fixed-start hidden reaction-network fibre

Author: dot (OpenAI). 23 October 2026 UTC.

Status: source-led applicability audit and complete author hand argument for the rank diagnostic in Section 4. Scoped coordinating hand-review PASS for that diagnostic and the separately identified source checks; see NONLOCAL-REALIZATION-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md. Other source checks remain author-inspected. No runtime, compilation, Lean verification, or historical novelty claim.

## 1. Question and unchanged experiment

The remaining target is the exact observation-law fibre among all admitted finite mass-action diffusion sources, not merely parameter uniqueness in a preselected graph. Each comparison retains the original fixed full initial-state preparation, observed projection, finite horizon H>0, and actual full-state exit followed by holding. Where rivals share a species space, they share the prescribed initial state and stopping region. No all-start preparation panel, upper bound on hidden species or reactions, projected-Markov assumption, or restriction excluding hidden-only reactions is introduced here. Any originally admitted initial-state nuisance retains its original quantifier.

The earlier interior-jet obstruction makes a nonlocal route necessary for that proposed method, but does not rule out a different finite signature. This audit instead asks whether primary exact-behaviour or stochastic-realization results complete the existing full-stopped-state semigroup-cylinder criterion. The prior comparison note was checked first; the sources below are additional, rather than another presentation of van Handel's initial-measure observability or the moment/bracket methods already audited.

The observable is the projected held path, not an automatically enlarged record containing the hidden exit time or full exit state. A single cemetery state can discard the observed concentration at exit. Consequently a killed-process representation is legitimate only when its relation to the actual held observation is proved. Finite-horizon data must likewise not be replaced by equality on an unknown future beyond H.

## 2. Exact behavioural equivalence: a useful language, but a stronger structural relation

Chen, Clerc and Panangaden's Theorem 30 gives bisimulation => temporal => trace equivalence (Definitions 23/26/29); Proposition 46 disproves the reverse implication generally. Section 3.1 assumes locally compact, countably based Feller-Dynkin states and measurable countable-proposition labels with open/closed truth partitions. Definition 21 additionally requires measurability of a trajectory-event's image under integer-time observation; the label sigma-algebra is described as discrete. Definition 53 requires continuous, open, surjective, all-state path-law-preserving homomorphisms; Proposition 54 supplies bisimulation. Section 6 permits disjoint-union comparison. [Primary journal HTML, indicated definitions and results inspected](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-structures-in-computer-science/article/behavioural-equivalences-for-continuoustime-markov-processes/FC41538B74A131C13C212A2EC8B757D3).

**Applicability finding.** Rational coordinate cuts verify individual open/closed partitions, not the complete observation/event measurability contract. Actual stopped-state regularity and a faithful finite-horizon encoding also need proof. Even granting those bridges, the theorem does not make a structural bisimulation witness necessary for our one-start coordinate-law equality. The fork is not a mass-action example. Thus neither exact identification of their trace relation with our fibre nor strictness inside the chemical class is asserted. Different hidden dimensions are not themselves excluded by disjoint union.

The newer trajectory-metric work assumes an honest Feller-Dynkin process with continuous paths, weak continuity of the initial-state-to-path-law map, and a continuous observation into [0,1] (Definitions 2.10 and 2.15; Section 2.3). Theorems 4.9 and 4.11 identify an iterated path-transport fixed point; Theorem 5.7 identifies its logical pseudometric. Section 8 discusses exact-computation difficulties. [Primary preprint arXiv2511.21621v1, 26 November 2025, selected definitions, results and discussion inspected](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21621v1).

**Applicability finding.** Honest boundary holding can be preferable to loss of mass, but the regularity assumptions still need verification for the actual source and stopping region. These structural metrics do not furnish a finite closure of our one-start observed-cylinder algebra or a classification of every finite chemical realization. No claim is made here that their zero set has been proved equal to our finite-horizon trace fibre.

## 3. Predictive Markovization and nonlinear realization

Meyer's 1976 exposition of Knight's prediction theory starts with a measurable process in a separable metric space. Its prediction state is probability-law-valued (printed pp. 88–89). Theorem 3, p. 100, gives a homogeneous strong Markov process with transition mechanism independent of the original law. Section IV/Lemma 8, pp. 101–102, relates it back to the pseudo-path; Section V, p. 103, discusses cadlag Polish paths. [Primary exposition, indicated sections inspected](https://www.numdam.org/item/SPS_1976__10__86_0.pdf). Knight's original article was not available for a comparable full-text inspection here.

**Applicability finding.** This is a genuine nonlocal representation route: the full observed held-path law, including its stopping effects, can be encoded predictively without declaring the projected concentration Markov. Continuous paths are determined by their almost-everywhere time values. For a finite observed horizon one may extend the observed path constantly after H as a data encoding, not as an assertion about the physical process's unobserved future. However, the predictive state is a probability law on a path space. The cited theorem supplies neither finite-dimensional mass-action coordinates nor all finite chemical realizations of that law. Minimizing predictive information would still not enumerate nonminimal hidden extensions or identify hidden-only reactions. Markovization alone therefore does not close the requested fibre.

Lindquist, Mitter and Picci's nonlinear realization paper assumes, in Section 2, a centered, mean-square-continuous, purely nondeterministic stationary process on the whole real time axis, together with a Wiener innovation representation. Theorem 1 addresses minimal states within its chaos/splitting-space framework. Section 8 explicitly treats the development as structural rather than algorithmic and notes the nontrivial innovation-representation requirement. [Official primary PDF](https://mitter.lids.mit.edu/publications/32_toward_a_theory_LNCIS.pdf); [author-uploaded primary text used to inspect Sections 2 and 8 and Theorem 1](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/37592599_Toward_a_theory_of_nonlinear_stochastic_realization).

**Failed hypotheses.** A deterministic fixed start followed by a nondegenerate diffusion law is not stationary. Passing to equilibrium or a two-sided stationary version changes the experiment. No Wiener-innovation representation satisfying that theorem's assumptions has been established for the admitted general stopped projection. Thus this specific realization theorem cannot be imported unchanged. The official PDF was retrieved but its scan was not visually inspected; the section check used the identified author-upload text. A later Taylor–Pavon realization paper was accessible only at abstract level and supplies no theorem-level negative conclusion in this audit.

## 4. Finite observable-operator rank: a concrete failed hypothesis

Wu and Noe's OOM definition, equation (1), factors word probabilities through an m-dimensional linear state. Equation (6) is the past/future feature matrix C_12. Section 3.2, Assumption 2, explicitly assumes an m-dimensional OOM and an asymptotic stationarity condition; Assumptions 1 and 3 impose data-limit and rank conditions. Theorem 1 is conditional on all three. The continuous-observation Theorem 3 retains them, adding a closed Euclidean observation space and bounded features. [Primary 2016 conference paper, Sections 2.2–4.2 inspected](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2016/file/296472c9542ad4d4788d543508116cbc-Paper.pdf).

The relevant rank is linear predictive/Hankel rank, not number of chemical species. The following exact test uses the same adjacent-observation feature block as equation (6), with feature length L=1. It does not replace the continuous diffusion by a finite-state jump chain or coarse-grain the observation.

### Proposition: a one-reaction stopped diffusion has infinite observable two-time rank

Take the single reaction A -> 2A with rate 1. Fix x0>0 and I=(l,r) with 0<l<x0<r<infinity. Let

    dX_t = X_t dt + sqrt(X_t) dW_t,
    tau = first exit from I,
    Z_t = X_(t wedge tau).

The record is held at the reached endpoint. Fix any Delta>0 with 2 Delta<=H. For f,g in C_c^infinity(I), extended by zero to the endpoints, define the observed bilinear form

    B_Delta(f,g) = E_x0[f(Z_Delta) g(Z_(2 Delta))].

For every integer N>=1 there exist f_1,...,f_N and g_1,...,g_N of this class such that the N by N matrix [B_Delta(f_i,g_j)] is nonsingular. Consequently no exact finite-dimensional OOM representation of the sampled observed law can factor all these feature matrices.

**Proof.** All coefficients are smooth and uniformly elliptic on the closed interval. Write K_t for the Dirichlet killed semigroup on I, and k_t(x,y) for its interior density. The standard regular-interval killed-diffusion facts used in the previously reviewed two-time proof give continuity and strict positivity of k_t for t>0 and x,y in I. The generator is

    Lf = x f' + (x/2) f''.

For a direct specification of its self-adjoint realization, put

    m(x) = 2 exp(2x)/x,          p(x) = exp(2x).

Then Lf = m^(-1)(p f')'. The Dirichlet form

    E(f,g) = integral_I p(x) f'(x) g'(x) dx,
    domain(E) = H_0^1(I)

on L^2(I,m dx) is closed; m and p are bounded above and below by positive constants. Its nonpositive self-adjoint generator has domain H^2(I) intersect H_0^1(I) and the displayed expression. Its semigroup is K_t by uniqueness of the regular Dirichlet problem. In particular K_Delta is injective: if K_Delta g=0, the spectral theorem gives

    0 = ||K_Delta g||^2 = integral_(-infinity,0] exp(2 Delta lambda) dmu_g(lambda).

The integrand is strictly positive at every finite lambda, so mu_g=0 and g=0. Zero as a possible spectral accumulation point of K_Delta creates no kernel.

Let h(x)=k_Delta(x0,x)>0. The full stopped Markov property gives

    B_Delta(f,g) = integral_I h(x) f(x) (K_Delta g)(x) dx.       (A)

This is not survival-conditioned data. If absorption has occurred by the first time, f vanishes; if it occurs between the two times, g vanishes. Equation (A) is therefore an observable cylinder expectation of the actual held record, with exactly the required killing restriction and no extra exit indicator supplied as data.

Choose any N linearly independent g_j in C_c^infinity(I). Suppose a linear combination of the functionals f -> B_Delta(f,g_j) vanishes for every f in that test space. Equation (A) and distributional testing imply

    h K_Delta(sum_j c_j g_j) = 0  almost everywhere on I.

Since h>0, injectivity implies sum_j c_j g_j=0; independence gives every c_j=0. Thus the N functionals are linearly independent. The evaluation map f -> (B_Delta(f,g_1),...,B_Delta(f,g_N)) has range R^N: otherwise a nonzero linear functional annihilating its proper range would give the dependence just excluded. Choose f_i whose image vectors are the standard basis. The pairing matrix is then the identity. QED.

The density and regular Dirichlet operator providers are the same ones specified in [the reviewed two-time manuscript, Sections 3–5](TWO-TIME-SAMPLED-EXTENSION.md). The source history remains classical scalar diffusion theory, including [Kent's Theorem 8.1 and interval boundary framework](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~sschmid/Courses/Stat376/Papers/Langevin/KentAdvAppProb1978.pdf). The proposition is an author hand diagnostic, not a new general spectral theorem.

### Exact connection to the cited observable feature matrix

Set the first two sampled observations to Z_Delta and Z_(2 Delta), and take phi_1=(f_i) and phi_2=(g_j). Their feature matrix C_12 is precisely the matrix in the proposition. If an m-dimensional OOM represented this law, integrating its word factorization against f_i and g_j would yield

    C_12(i,j) = [omega Xi(f_i)] [Xi(g_j) sigma],

and therefore rank(C_12)<=m for every feature choice. Taking N=m+1 contradicts the proposition. Boundary atoms cause no escape: the features vanish there; even granting an operator-valued-measure extension accommodating the mixed boundary/interior law, this finite-dimensional factorization has the same rank bound. Thus the failure is tied to the actual feature block, not to an unrelated operator on hidden states.

This one-species example is a legitimate subclass diagnostic: finite species and a finite reaction list do not imply the finite predictive rank required by this method. It is **not** a negative result about a finite-dimensional nonlinear state, finite parameterization, or a target-dependent finite identifying signature. This very process has a one-dimensional chemical realization, and the separate scalar adapter proves finite identifying signatures within its declared source class. Approximate low-rank models and coarsened observations are not excluded; they answer different questions from exact observational equivalence.

## 5. What the attack establishes, and the exact remaining bridge

Three tempting replacements for the missing theorem have now been checked rather than assumed:

1. A structural bisimulation/homomorphism gives a sufficient comparison, but the inspected theorem does not make it necessary for the fixed-start trace law of our admitted chemical class.
2. Predictive Markovization retains nonlocal path information, but does not identify every finite mass-action realization of the predictive law.
3. Exact finite-linear-rank realization cannot cover the whole admitted source class merely because each source is finite. The proposition disproves that particular hypothesis transfer without disproving nonlinear or finite-signature approaches.

The still-needed result is a stop-faithful, fixed-start, all-rival completeness theorem connecting observed path laws to the entire admitted physical reaction-network fibre, with its unavoidable full-generator equivalences. It must either justify a complete nonlocal signature or classify all compatible finite mass-action realizations without presupposing their hidden size. Hidden-only reactions cannot be removed merely because they have zero instantaneous projected covariance weight: they can affect later hidden coupling or the full-state exit clock.

No inspected provider supplies that bridge. This is a bounded conclusion about the named sources and their exact hypotheses, not a universal absence theorem and not a proof that the master problem is impossible. No further initial-jet component, stronger preparation experiment, changed stopping rule, or new runtime evidence is substituted for it.

# Literal opened drawings and source-cycle curves

Attributed formalization and checks: dot (OpenAI), 5 October 2026.

Six independently reviewed modules derive geometric preparation from actual edge curves. They preserve all 47 preceding owned sources and 41 providers.

## Actual opened drawing

Each new hybrid-parent tip is the midpoint of its original incoming edge arc. Its new pendant edge follows the first half of that arc. Skeleton vertices and edges retain their original drawing. Original point/arc injectivity and incidence conditions derive the full crossing-free drawing of the literal opened graph, preserving parallel edge occurrences. Its drawing is a subset of the original drawing. No rotation, cyclic order or desired adjacency certificate is an input.

## Actual source-cycle parameterization

Undirected occurrence walks traverse original edges forwards or backwards. Their vertex sets, edge sets and simplicity predicates are combinatorial. The physical trace is exactly the union of the traversed original arcs and the initial vertex; injectivity of a nonempty vertex-simple walk is derived from original incidence conditions.

Two nonempty simple occurrence walks with the same endpoints, disjoint edge sets and no shared internal vertices therefore give a continuous injective map from AddCircle(1) onto their physical union. This supplies an actual circle map for an edge-indexed source cycle, including parallel-edge bigons. Desired topological cycle separation is not assumed.

documents.body:
# A fixed-start scalar derivative adapter to the prior positive-moment certificate

Author: dot (OpenAI). 22 October 2026 UTC.

Status: complete author hand argument with scoped coordinating hand-review PASS on 22 October 2026; see the separate SCALAR-ADAPTER-COORDINATING-REVIEW.md receipt. No execution, Lean verification, or historical novelty claim. The positive atomic moment theorem is inherited; the experiment-specific work below is the stopped scalar law-to-derivative adapter and the return to the correct reaction-law target.

## 1. Precise scope and target

Fix x0>0, a bounded open interval I containing x0 with closure contained in (0,infinity), and H>0. Admit any nonempty finite scalar mass-action reaction list

    n A -> (n+v) A,   n>=0, v an integer, v!=0, n+v>=0,

with positive active rates kappa_(n,v). Repeated identical edges, if allowed, are aggregated. The target and every rival use the same x0, I and H. There is no source-degree bound, no rival-size bound, no change of preparation, and no extra species. Null reactions are excluded because they are invisible to the diffusion.

Write

    b(x)=sum_n beta_n x^n,   beta_n=sum_v v*kappa_(n,v),
    a(x)=sum_n alpha_n x^n,  alpha_n=sum_v v^2*kappa_(n,v).

The variance coefficients alpha_n are nonnegative, with finite nonempty support S. Moreover beta_n=0 whenever alpha_n=0. Let r=|S| for the target. This counts active reactant degrees, not reaction edges or total polynomial degree.

The observation is the exact law on C([0,H],R) of the scalar diffusion

    dX=b(X)dt+sqrt(a(X))dW,

stopped at tau=inf{t: X_t not in I} and held afterwards. Since a>0 on the positive axis, all coefficients are smooth and uniformly nondegenerate on the closure of I; the localized law is unique. The stop is observable from X. This is the autonomous scalar class used in the finite-initial-jet obstruction, enlarged from unit births to general admitted scalar jumps. It is not the general unreconstructed-hidden-species class.

The primary target is the diffusion-law equivalence class, namely all reaction lists with the same alpha_n and beta_n. General reaction edges and individual rates cannot be recovered from these two sums without an additional admitted-family uniqueness statement.

## 2. Law-to-derivative adapter at the one fixed start

**Lemma 1.** The exact stopped law determines every finite collection of numbers

    a^(j)(x0), b^(j)(x0),  j>=0.

This is a statement about deterministic invariants of a probability law, not a consistent finite-sample estimator or differentiation of the drift of a single noisy path.

**Proof.** Work in the completed natural filtration of the canonical stopped process. It has the unique continuous semimartingale decomposition

    X_t=x0+D_t+M_t,
    D_t=integral_0^t 1_(s<tau) b(X_s) ds,
    [X]_t=integral_0^t 1_(s<tau) a(X_s) ds.

Bounded coefficients on the stopped compact interval justify the martingale identities in the natural filtration by conditioning. Uniqueness follows because a continuous local martingale of finite variation is constant. Quadratic variation is likewise unique. Thus the law determines D and [X], up to the usual indistinguishability of canonical versions.

Before tau, take the time densities U0=a(X) and V0=b(X). At zero use right limits. At tau use the continuous left limit, then hold this value, rather than replacing it by the post-exit zero density. These are continuous semimartingales because they equal the smooth functions a(X^stop) and b(X^stop). The density construction is possible for each finite collection using common almost-sure subsequences for quadratic-variation approximations and continuity. No claim that a fixed universal subsequence works simultaneously for every possible source is needed for the identification implication.

If Uj=a^(j)(X^stop), Ito's cross-variation formula gives

    d[X,Uj]_t/dt = 1_(t<tau) a(X_t) a^(j+1)(X_t).

Divide by the strictly positive U0 before the stop, then extend continuously to the stop and hold. This recovers U_(j+1). The same recursion with Vj=b^(j)(X^stop) recovers V_(j+1):

    U_(j+1) = (d[X,Uj]/dt)/U0,
    V_(j+1) = (d[X,Vj]/dt)/U0,                 t<tau.

The initial values are the claimed derivatives. Since tau>0 almost surely, every finite recursion is defined on an initial positive time interval. Values after tau are never mistaken for the physical coefficient. Alternatively, equality of two laws gives common canonical D and [X], then the same finite recursion under that common law proves equality of all these deterministic initial values. QED.

The variance side is path-functional quadratic-variation extraction. The drift side uses the exact law's canonical drift, not a pathwise drift estimator. This distinction matters when counting physical information.

## 3. Exact supplying theorem and normalization

Let E be the shifted Euler operator

    (E f)(x)=f(x)+x f'(x).

It satisfies E^k(x^n)=(n+1)^k x^n. Define the law invariants

    M_k=(E^k a)(x0)=sum_n alpha_n x0^n (n+1)^k,
    B_k=(E^k b)(x0)=sum_n beta_n x0^n (n+1)^k.

For each k these require derivatives only through order k, so Lemma 1 supplies them without changing the initial state. In particular M_0=a(x0)>0. The actual normalized positive atomic law is

    mu=sum_(n in S) [alpha_n x0^n / M_0] delta_(n+1).

Its r nodes are distinct and strictly positive, including when the zero-order reactant n=0 is admitted. Its weights are strictly positive and sum to one. Its ordinary moments are M_k/M_0. A rival produces the same kind of finite positive law, with no bound on its support size or maximum node.

The relevant previously checked project declaration is

    Astra.CommonMoment.support_card_le_of_equal_sparse_moments

from CMSeparation.lean, reproduced with exact source and verification scope in the [CM-T02 component certificate](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/514648b697aeed8f46582109cfeefcd7707cd738/research/2026-10-15-common-moment-checked-component/CM-T02-CERTIFICATE-001.json). It assumes two finite strictly positive probability laws on distinct strictly positive real nodes and 2*target.card+1 distinct natural-number exponents with equal moments. Its conclusion is rival.card<=target.card. The direction is important. It does not by its stated conclusion alone identify the nodes, original reaction list, or physical observation adapter.

Here ordinary exponents 0,...,2r allow the classical stronger support certificate directly: for the target nodes z_1,...,z_r, put

    Q(z)=product_(i=1)^r (z-z_i)^2.

This degree-2r polynomial is nonnegative everywhere and zero exactly at the target nodes. Equal moments through 2r imply integral Q dnu=integral Q dmu=0. Positive rival weights force every rival node into the target set. The first r moment equations then identify the weights by the ordinary Vandermonde matrix. Thus nu=mu.

This annihilating-square proof is classical and is the ordinary-moment specialization of the existing positive-support mechanism. Neither it nor its 2r+1 count is a new contribution of this note. The source-normalization step, node shift, and physical derivative adapter are stated explicitly to prevent importing the supplier without its hypotheses. The old abstract component's Lean evidence does not verify this new stochastic adapter.

## 4. All-rival finite signature for the scalar law fibre

**Theorem 2.** Fix any target in Section 1 with r active reactant degrees. For every admitted finite rival, regardless of its degree or edge count, the following are equivalent:

1. The exact stopped path laws from the common x0 on [0,H] are equal.
2. Their finite signatures agree:

       M_k,  k=0,...,2r;     B_k,  k=0,...,r-1.

3. All variance and drift coefficients agree: alpha_n=alpha'_n and beta_n=beta'_n for every n.

This uses 3r+1 scalar law invariants, not 3r+1 trajectories, sampling times, preparations, or finite-sample measurements.

**Proof.** (1) implies (2) by Lemma 1. Suppose (2). The equality of M_0 supplies the same positive normalization. Section 3's positive-moment certificate gives equality of the normalized measures, hence identical supports S and identical alpha_n x0^n. Since x0>0, alpha_n=alpha'_n. In particular the rival has no hidden additional reactant degree: positivity of its variance coefficients is essential to this conclusion.

The supports of both drift polynomials lie in the now-common S. The r equations for B_k give

    sum_(n in S) (beta_n-beta'_n) x0^n (n+1)^k=0,
                                                    k=0,...,r-1.

The Vandermonde matrix at distinct nodes n+1 is invertible; beta_n=beta'_n for every n. This proves (3). Finally (3) gives the same scalar coefficients and the same observable stop, so localized uniqueness gives (1). QED.

**Unit-birth specialization.** If the source class consists only of nA->(n+1)A, then b=a. The signature M_0,...,M_(2r) alone is sufficient. Every coefficient is an individual aggregated reaction rate, so this identifies the exact graph and rates against all finite unit-birth rivals. This is the same source class and observable-stop experiment as the preceding finite-initial-jet obstruction. There is no contradiction: that obstruction lets r grow with the prescribed jet order, whereas this count depends on the fixed target's r.

**Unit forward/reverse specialization.** If only v=+1 and v=-1 are allowed, with v=-1 excluded when n=0, the identified coefficients recover the rates as kappa_(n,+1)=(alpha_n+beta_n)/2 and kappa_(n,-1)=(alpha_n-beta_n)/2. Admission already guarantees these rates are nonnegative and the excluded n=0 reverse rate is zero.

**General jumps.** Network/rate uniqueness is false without such restrictions. At reactant degree n=1, allow jumps v=1,2,3. Positive rate vectors (1,4,1) and (4,1,2) both give beta_1=12 and alpha_1=26. They therefore have exactly the same observed diffusion law under the theorem, although the individual rates differ. This is the familiar generator-level ambiguity, not a new nonidentification mechanism.

## 5. What is and is not resolved

The exact result combines an experiment-specific fixed-start derivative adapter with the existing positive-moment supplier. It does not rename a full-state coefficient/cone criterion as a new theorem. Faul, Hoessly and Xia's [generator and reaction-vector analysis](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0956792526100382) remains the prior structural background; the coefficient sums above are its scalar specialization.

The result needs an autonomous scalar observed diffusion and an observable interval exit. For a general projected hidden diffusion, the observed drift is a conditional characteristic rather than the unconditioned polynomial b(X), and the variation density can depend on hidden state. The recursion then follows full-state covariance directions, not ordinary derivatives in the observed coordinate. No positive atomic degree response follows automatically. The finite-family neutral and catalytic reconstructions supply special closures, not a uniform closure for all finite hidden reaction networks.

If r is unknown, the theorem is target-dependent existence of a finite signature. It does not by itself supply a finite-precision stopping rule or an effective representation of exact law access. An adaptive Hankel/positive-support decision procedure would need an explicitly admitted exact-arithmetic response oracle. There is no stability, statistical sample-complexity, noisy-data, discrete-time, or arbitrary hidden-stop conclusion.

In particular, a finite list of law-determined real invariants is not automatically an effective legal finite-experiment or response interface. The proof supplies no implementation of exact canonical-drift extraction or exact derivative queries from an external representation of a law.

Historical novelty of the fixed-start adapter or its combined scalar statement is not established. All bracket, canonical semimartingale, positive-moment and Vandermonde ingredients are classical; only the displayed experiment-specific join is being recorded here as an author-checked specialization. General fixed-start partial-observation closure and a full formal stochastic proof remain open.
