documents.body:
# Normalization effects: exact experiment minima and their biological boundary

Contributor/publisher: Codex Work, NORMALIZATION-EFFECTS-20260930. Contributions and internal challenges: network_lower_bound, menu_combinatorics, log_optimal_design, common_inheritance_bridge, decoder_integration and normalization_tests. Their actual written receipts or delivered arguments are distinguished below. Governing contract: MASTER-CLOSURE-STANDARD-20260930 accepted. This continues Nolan's r and g reduction question; it preserves the biological normal-form and exact-enumeration owners.

## 0. Executive decision brief

**The experiment count can be reduced beyond logarithmic growth to an exact worst-case constant when a valid structural control map is supplied: three environments for occurrence at least g, four for occurrence one.** The information assumption is decisive. The earlier 2r-2 and logarithmic minima remain correct when only identified parental control coordinates are supplied.

Scope: every finite binary semi-directed LSA-rootable, outer-labeled planar galled network in the pinned source class, arbitrary levels and blob counts; nonempty taxon ports; binary hybrids with independent natural parental probabilities in [g,1-g], 0<g<=1/2. Controls force parental choices and leave the other laws unchanged. Protocols are fixed before observation and are parameter-oblivious. The structural graph/embedding or a certified sufficient interaction map is additional information. Biological confidence transfer below is for NMSCcom, one sample per taxon, positive switched-quartet length floor tau, and IID loci.

| Finding | Precise effect | Evidence band |
|---|---|---|
| Graph-informed partial controls | Worst-case minimum 3 environments | Conditional hand proof, independent internal upper review, admitted exact lower witness and exhaustive row checks |
| Graph-informed certain occurrence | Worst-case minimum 4 environments | Conditional upper proof; admitted signed-pair lower and independent 8-taxon counting witness |
| Topology control erasure | Collapse <=3-port blobs; retain s<=floor(3n/2)-2 original IDs | Switching-wise proof and sharp graph-count constructions; internal review |
| Actuation budget | Three-row protocol uses <=n-2 controls in any row and <=2n-4 forced assignments in total | Exact degree/color count; not an optimal actuator-cost theorem |
| Passive CF normalization count | After genuine two-port replacement, r<=2n-3, improving the candidate 3n-6 | Sharp conditional graph count; NMSCind simultaneous replacement still owned and open |

These evidence bands concern mathematical proof premises and execution, not clinical GRADE ratings. No Lean or biological experiment is claimed. Prior contraction and covering-array mathematics are attributed; historical novelty is unresolved.

Next actions: preserve the completed experiment theorem; return the sharper bounds and control-law distinction to the biological owner; let the accepted Astra enumeration owner finish publication/replay and Q*(8) optimization. Do not repeat its expensive census here. Before practical use, specify accessible interventions and verify their observation laws, the source premises and the intended statistical promise.

## 1. Abstract

We separate topology normalization, stochastic normalization and experiment optimization. A switching-wise quotient erases controls in blobs with at most three ports, while an exact coordinate-dependence test can erase further neutral controls. A facial interaction graph is outerplanar; its three-coloring yields three partial-control environments covering every two-choice split witness. A nine-taxon source graph realizes all signed pairs of a triangle and proves that two environments cannot suffice under the same universal parameter contract. Four binary color rows give certain occurrence, with matching admitted lower bounds. Effective edge responses characterize control-aware two-port CF reduction under common inheritance. Passive equivalence does not preserve all interventions; a three-port common-inheritance example even prevents general passive reduction to a fixed tree star.

## 2. Introduction and the shared end question

The end task is to recover the complete displayed nontrivial split union and a compatible circular order from declared observations. There are two different optimizations: how many exact quartet queries a recovery algorithm needs, and how many experimental environments provide reliable quartet support. A small query minimum is not automatically a small experiment minimum.

The initial source read was Commons eec5b7c2c15adf621b2ff99a8938626a32140e1a. A later read at 9ec0d3c515c3b7642343b6cb072910ce3537930d found the accepted ASTRA-ENUMERATION-20260930-1430Z lane and its reported Q*(6)=8, Q*(7)=11 certificate replays and 6,955,830-target eight-taxon census. Q*(8) was explicitly not optimized or certified. This note uses that actual status, not a live-presence inference or an independent replay of its large certificates.

The biological normal-form lane is BIO-NORMALFORM-DIRECT-20260930T1223Z, preserving ASTRA-OBS authorship. Its inspected artifact is an acceptance, not a completed probability-preserving proof. The later exact-query normalization is a separate topology-only result: bounded source representatives preserving Q/S, not CF laws.

## 3. Methods, prior and exact contract

Inherited source facts are pinned to Samuel e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7, ALL-LEVEL-PROOF.md Sections 1,2,7,8 and its audits: capped galled blobs have a plane tree opening; each hybrid becomes an adjacent duplicated port; bounded faces correspond to hybrids; local switches extend independently; every displayed split has a sufficient certificate using at most two controls and localizes in a branching capped blob.

A row c belongs to {0,*,1}^r. The star preserves the natural choice; the other entries force a parent. For every admitted graph, parameter vector and displayed target, some row must give target occurrence >=g. Rows may differ by target. The graph-informed protocol may depend on the graph and original ID map, but not on the unknown probabilities. A probability-one protocol uses the stronger conclusion. Adaptive learned interventions and actuator-budget optima are separate contracts.

Prior was checked first. Holtgrefe et al. (2025), DOI 10.1007/s11538-025-01549-4, explicitly note that 2/3-blob contraction does not change displayed topologies. Ané et al. (2024), DOI 10.1007/s00285-024-02050-7, Theorem 4 supplies quartet-CF edge replacement for 2-sub-blobs, with potentially negative lengths in its broader correlated setting. Meagher and Stevens' covering arrays on graphs and Meagher's thesis supply the established graph-coloring/homomorphism design framework. Gunawan, DasGupta and Zhang's earlier galled-network bound 2n-2 has a different simple-DAG convention; the Commons multigraph allowance must remain explicit. None of these prior findings establishes historical priority for this precise controlled >=g transfer.

## 4. Findings and proofs

### 4.1 Switching-wise support normalization and exact coordinate erasure

Take an actual admitted source and its tree of blobs. Each cut has a nonempty taxon set on both sides. In any global switching, the pruned local tree joining two ports is a path; joining three ports gives the unique unrooted tripod. Replacing <=3-port blobs by those pieces preserves EACH switching's unrooted tree topology, hence all quartet and split outputs. The original outside incidences and embedding persist. A nonroot tripod is oriented from its unique entry; a root in a replaced piece can be put on a replacement edge with two taxon-bearing sides. No new cycles are introduced. This inherits the same path, capping and rooting premises audited in the existing actual-source normalization.

Retain the original IDs in blobs with >=4 ports, numbering them s. All erased switches may remain naturally random. If a sufficient old certificate contains erased literals, delete them: complete them to the old values, apply sufficiency, then use switching-wise independence from erased coordinates. Thus a menu on retained coordinates lifts by forcing those SAME original IDs; no passive hidden-network selector is used.

Further exact erasure is available for the declared coordinate-projection task. A hybrid is necessary iff some two global switchings differing only at that hybrid have different unrooted tree outputs. To test this without enumerating 2^r global switches, inspect each four-port set in its capped blob. Only the sampled ports' own hybrid choices matter after tree restriction, so at most four bits need enumeration. For every hybrid h, enumerate the other three ports and their at most eight choices; compare the two h choices. A changed local quartet lifts by choosing one taxon in each nonempty port component. Conversely every changed global quartet either is resolved by a fixed cut or occupies four ports of one central blob. Therefore this test detects exactly every coordinate dependency.

Iteratively flipping individually irrelevant bits proves factorization through the relevant coordinate set. If a removed bit has a dependency witness, any coordinate projection deleting it identifies two states with different required outputs. Hence this is a necessary-and-sufficient, computable minimum subset for COORDINATE ERASURE. It is not the minimum network realization or every possible nonlinear encoding. Tree-quartet preprocessing makes the number of local tests O(sum_B h_B p_B^3), with a fixed factor at most eight; graph reading and embedding/ID acquisition still have their own cost.

### 4.2 Sharp counts and a stronger finite enumeration cap

Each hybrid in a capped blob has a distinct outgoing child port. A nonroot p-port blob has an ordinary rootward entry, so h<=p-1; at most one root-containing blob can have h=p. If t counts ordinary trivalent attachment vertices, the blob tree identity is sum_B(p_B-2)+t=n-2.

After two-port deletion all p>=3, giving r<=2n-3. After <=3-port deletion all retained p>=4, giving s<=n-1+floor((n-2)/2)=floor(3n/2)-2. If no retained blob contains the root, each bound improves by one. The independent count argument and exterior-cycle attaining constructions are in normalization_count_argument.md. Thirty-four finite extremizers, n=4,...,20, passed degree, DAG, root-LSA dominator, bridge, port and count checks. Sharpness is for the specified port compression, not minimum equivalent stochastic realization.

For a rooted binary network, V=2n+2s-1 and E=2n+3s-2. Thus this topology quotient supplies an actual source representative with at most 5n-5 rooted vertices and 5n-6 after root suppression (one smaller for odd n). This strengthens the existing 8n-14 unrooted bound for discrete profile enumeration. It changes neither the profile set nor a certified Q*(n); it only narrows a safe actual-graph census cap. The faster root-aware paired-tip census may already avoid that naive graph search, so a wall-clock improvement is not presumed.

### 4.3 Three environments are sufficient

For every retained capped blob let D be its simple weak dual: vertices are bounded faces/hybrids, and adjacent faces give an edge. A duplicated hybrid pair straddles a skeleton edge exactly when its bounded-face tree path contains that edge. Two straddlers are therefore the two incident bounded faces and form an edge of D. A two-choice certificate can consequently be chosen on an edge of D. Singleton and zero-choice certificates need no edge.

Each bounded face has its hybrid boundary edge incident to the exterior face. Deleting the exterior vertex in the plane dual puts every remaining vertex on one face. Simplifying loops/parallel edges gives an outerplanar D, which is three-colorable. Reuse colors between blobs. Permute each blob's colors so its largest class C3 is passive.

| Environment | C1 | C2 | C3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | force 0 | force 0 | natural |
| 2 | force 1 | natural | natural |
| 3 | natural | force 1 | natural |

Every two distinct colors cover all four signed assignments with no conflict and at least one correct force. A certificate edge has distinct colors, so its occurrence is >=g in one row. A singleton in the passive class still occurs naturally with probability >=g; the other singleton colors have compatible rows. A zero-choice target is certain. Global splits localize in one blob; a displayed quartet can inherit a witness from a full split realizing it. This proves the whole-class upper bound.

The maximum controls in a row are <=floor(2s/3)<=n-2. Total forced assignments across the rows are <=2floor(2s/3)<=2n-4. These are upper bounds, not matching actuator-cost optima. An edgeless D allows a passive baseline; a bipartite D allows two rows, forcing both values on one color class.

### 4.4 An admitted graph proves three necessary

The lower fixture is a plane binary copy tree

    (((11,0),(1,6)),(((7,2),(3,8)),((9,4),(5,10)))).

Its contour is 11,0,1,6,7,2,3,8,9,4,5,10. Taxa 0,...,5 are ordinary. Pair copies (6,7), (8,9), (10,11) become hybrids H0,H1,H2 and taxa 6,7,8. Join each adjacent pair in its disjoint exterior wedge; all taxa remain exterior and every hybrid has a pendant cut child edge. Orient the remaining tree from a binary root inserted at taxon0's edge. That direct taxon branch makes the root the LSA; the graph is binary, acyclic and galled. Positive coalescent lengths and interior parent probabilities can be assigned freely.

There are three branch stems, each containing a different anchored ordinary pair {0,1}, {2,3}, {4,5}. Each has exactly two boundary hybrids. Its four distinct target splits correspond EXACTLY to the four assignments of those two choices. No other edge can realize that same bipartition: an edge within a branch separates its anchored ordinary pair, while an edge in another branch includes/excludes another ordinary pair. The three stem pairs are the three edges of a hybrid triangle. Thus twelve actual target events are the twelve signed pair cylinders, not artificial coverage demands.

For any missing signed-pair coverage, choose both required parent probabilities equal to g. Every conflicting row gives zero, and any nonconflicting row fixing neither gives g^2<g. Hence a fixed parameter-oblivious menu must cover all twelve assignments by at least one correct force. A row can cover at most two assignments of a given pair, and does so only when exactly one pair coordinate is fixed. Two rows covering all four patterns would each have to fix exactly one coordinate of EVERY triangle edge. This is impossible: for three fixation indicators x_i in {0,1}, the three equations x_i+x_j=1 sum to 2 sum_i x_i=3. Therefore at least three rows are necessary for any 0<g<=1/2 under this contract.

three_environment_lower.py independently constructs the actual graph, checks degree/DAG/LSA, recomputes eight switched split sets, verifies all twelve exact cylinder events, and examines ALL 378 two-row menus from the 27 possible partial rows at the fair state g=1/2. None succeeds. The three-row construction passes 432 actual probability comparisons at declared corner parameters. Thus the worst-case graph-informed partial-control minimum is exactly THREE. This is not a claim every individual network needs three, nor a parameter-aware minimum for every fixed small g.

### 4.5 Four environments give certain occurrence and are optimal in the worst case

On the three colors use rows 000, 011, 101, 110. Every color pair realizes all four assignments with both coordinates fixed. Force only retained original IDs; leave erased IDs natural. Every full split certificate then holds surely in one row, and topology-neutral randomness does not change it. A singleton also sees both choices. Thus four environments suffice for occurrence one, with <=s simultaneous controls each.

The same lower fixture contains four distinct exact signed-pair targets on one actual pair. Under positive natural probabilities, a target has probability one in a row only when BOTH pair coordinates are fixed correctly. One row certifies at most one of its four assignments, so at least four rows are necessary. The exact script also checks every three-row partial menu. Independently, the Halin receipt contains an eight-taxon graph with sixteen supported nontrivial splits. Each selected tree has n-3=5, so three arbitrary environmental distributions can have at most fifteen distinct probability-one split targets; this rules out three even beyond product partial rows.

## 5. Conclusion and transfer to the recovery master

The graph-informed fixed experiment counts are characterized: three for >=g, four for certainty, with actual admitted lower witnesses. The earlier IDs-only optimum remains m_g(r)=min{m:2r-1<=[z^m](1+z+z^2)^m}; one forced choice per row remains 2r-2. Constant counts become possible because the graph tells us which pairs matter. Passive probabilities alone do not supply that original-ID map.

Use the original network's NMSCcom laws, not a substituted unsupported metric model. The inherited contrast provider gives Delta=g(1-exp(-tau)) for the three-row design and Delta_1=1-exp(-tau) for the four-row certain-support design. For a deterministic total exact-support learner capped at B queries, N>=ceil(8 Delta^-2 log(6mB/delta)) IID loci per environment suffice by the already proved fixed-ideal-transcript argument. Invalid answers, excess queries or a guarded computation failure return failure. This replaces m by 3 or 4; it does not change the recovery algorithm's exact query minimum. Keep gene-readout, locus, actuation and wall-clock costs distinct.

## 6. Deconstructive analysis: what is allowed to disappear?

| Reduction | Preserves | Does not automatically preserve |
|---|---|---|
| <=3-port topology quotient | Each switched unrooted tree, Q/S and compatible-circle space | Quartet CFs, metric/rooted/full joint laws |
| Exact neutral-coordinate erasure | Complete switching response through remaining IDs | Original probability response of deleted controls |
| Two-port fixed passive edge | Declared passive CFs; restricted used-row laws under independence | Interventions inside the eliminated component |
| Three-color design | Target occurrence and original-law support contrasts | Hidden graph reconstruction or physical accessibility |
| Exact query catalogue | Complete support profiles and required split targets | Original control-response functions or probabilities |

## 7. Reconstructive analysis: common-inheritance response edges

Consider a genuine two-port blob with all sampled attachments outside it. For local switching s, let L(s)>=0 be its pruned unrooted species-tree path length between ports, including exactly the chosen component region. For partial local row c under NMSCcom define

    phi(c)=E_c[exp(-L(S))],    t(c)=-log(phi(c)).

A quartet exposing the cut as 2|2 has internal length a_q(outside)+L(S). Its tree-MSC CF is linear in exp(-internal length); independence of local and outside switches therefore permits replacing the blob by an edge t(c). Other allocations place the local path on a pendant quartet part, so it has no CF contribution. Unroot tree species switchings first to include a root-containing two-port blob; tree quartet CF root invariance gives the same proof. This argument is common inheritance only.

If erased IDs remain natural in every used row, phi is constant, and one fixed edge preserves all quartet CFs under arbitrary controls on the retained IDs. If original controls inside the deleted blob are allowed, an exposed cut admits one fixed edge for all those controls iff phi(c) is constant. With every local switching fully forceable, this is iff every L(s) agrees. A terminal one-taxon side does not expose a 2|2 quartet and is a separate unobservable case.

The executed serial-bigon fixture uses route lengths log2 and log4. Passive contraction and all nine retained rows preserve all five quartet CFs. Forcing the removed bit changes the required effective survival from 3/32 to 1/8 or 1/16, disproving one fixed all-control normal form. Read normalization-effects-checks.json for exact vectors. This is not a substitute for the biological owner's independent-lineage root/interface theorem.

## 8. Middle-out synthesis: the boundary at three ports

Topology-only three-port erasure is safe; a fixed stochastic tree-star replacement is not generally safe even under common inheritance. An explicit triangle has U->V, U->H, V->H; V leads to a two-taxon clade A, H to a single taxon B, and the rootward side to a two-taxon clade C. All switches display the same unrooted five-taxon topology. With natural inheritance 1/2 and every original edge length log2, put a=x=log2 and c=2log2 (the two root-side edges). Its two local switched arm pairs are (L_A,L_C)=(a+x,c) or (a,c+x).

Then E exp(-L_A)=3/8 and E exp(-L_C)=3/16, but E exp(-(L_A+L_C))=1/16, rather than their product 9/128. Quartets 2A|B|C and 2C|A|B pin those two effective arm survivals. Quartet 2A|2C requires their product to be 1/16, an impossibility for a fixed metric star. All original lengths are positive, and rootability/galled/exterior admission hold. three_port_cf_check.py evaluates both actual switched trees with exact Fraction arithmetic and verifies this discrepancy. This is a hand-derived and exact-tested counterexample, not a stochastic simulation. It shows why the universal stochastic operation cannot be extended from two to three ports by topology reasoning alone.

This does not prove the globally minimum CF-equivalent reticulation count or rule out other retained-network models. The full passive CF-fiber classification, NMSCind simultaneous normalization, unknown-control-map recovery and practical intervention remain open.

## 9. Glossary

- r: original identified hybrid count; s: retained count under the stated topology quotient.
- g: lower bound on each natural parental probability, not a complexity parameter.
- Port: a cut-edge taxon component attached to a capped blob.
- Environment: one fixed intervention row, with many IID loci sampled within it.
- Q*(n): minimum deterministic adaptive quartet-query count for the exact support oracle.
- Coordinate quotient: erase input bits while preserving the complete switched output function.
- CF: probability of an unrooted gene quartet under a declared coalescent mechanism.
- Weak dual: adjacency graph of bounded faces of a plane blob.

## 10. Bibliography and pinned research evidence

Primary prerequisites: Holtgrefe et al. (2025), DOI 10.1007/s11538-025-01549-4; Ané, Fogg, Allman, Baños and Rhodes (2024), DOI 10.1007/s00285-024-02050-7; Meagher and Stevens (2005), Covering arrays on graphs; Meagher (2007), arXiv:math/0701553; Gunawan, DasGupta and Zhang (2017), DOI 10.1016/j.ic.2016.11.001. The count subnote records exact convention and prior limitations. Source-to-tree premises are Samuel e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7. Existing controls and confidence composition are Commons eec5b7c2c15adf621b2ff99a8938626a32140e1a. Exact enumeration status is Commons 9ec0d3c515c3b7642343b6cb072910ce3537930d, SEVEN-TAXON-CHECKPOINT.md. Bibliography.bib supplies imports; notes distinguish foundational prior from new derived transfer claims.

## 11. Process-integrity assessment

Verdict: auditable mathematical component with explicit upstream dependencies. Source definitions, multigraph/root conventions and prior contraction were checked before promoting results. Separate internal reviewers challenged count, face adjacency and control-law transfer. Root independently constructed and executed the actual-source lower witness and replayed the count and CF-discriminator scripts. The Halin program separately compares tree-edge witnesses to graph-switching cuts at its declared sizes. Exact query-owner checkpoint claims were READ, not independently rerun here. Literature search was targeted rather than a systematic exhaustive historical review; no AMSTAR-2 score or trial RoB score is applicable. Fixes before external promotion: source-critical proof review, practical law correspondence, and exact control-map verification. Finite tests corroborate, not replace, universal proofs.

## 12. Robustness and counterfactuals

Verdict: exact within the fixed parameter-oblivious, ideal graph-informed contract. Three and four have matching actual-source lower bounds; confidence bounds remain conditional. Changing to IDs-only information restores the logarithmic lower bound; one actuator restores 2r-2. Knowing probabilities, learning controls adaptively, altering the target or allowing non-product interventions changes the optimization problem. Support-neutral controls can change CFs, as executed counterexamples show. A source-admitted two-environment menu covering the lower graph for every allowed parameter vector would refute the three minimum; a failure of face incidence or source localization would invalidate the universal upper proof. Clinical meta-analysis statistics such as I² are inapplicable to these exact combinatorial claims. Physical validity and NMSCind require separate evidence.

## 13. Zotero integration

Import bibliography.bib into Zotero. Tag the primary papers phylogenetics, coalescent, graph-normalization and covering-arrays as appropriate. Attach this Markdown report as a research note and link its prior entries: source definitions -> admitted representation; CF replacement -> stochastic boundary; graph arrays -> color design. Link the Commons exact-enumeration checkpoint separately under exact-query, not as experimental evidence. New own results should remain tagged hand-proof, internal-review and exact-checks until promotion. This packet does not modify the user's Zotero database or a retired notebook.

## 14. Appendix and reproduction

Run three_environment_lower.py, normalization_count_audit.py, normalization_effects_check.py, three_port_cf_check.py and halin_normalization_checks.py. The CF discriminator imports two unchanged helpers from the earlier committed 2026-09-30-control-menu-continuation packet; keep that sibling directory. The Halin test covers 196 plane skeleton fixtures through eight ports, 40,264 switched trees, 9,408 signed adjacent-pair checks, 32,712 target-probability comparisons and 784 deterministic row checks. Root's replay matched every parsed field except the output pathname. Its two-row search is only a fair-parameter test; the separate nine-taxon proof supplies universal necessity. Normalization_count_receipt.json records 34 extremizers with an all-field-equal root replay. ROOT-VERIFICATION.json records the remaining exact checks and exclusions. The complete original decoder integration of 420 fixtures remains in the earlier packet; it was not rerun merely because this design changed. No new large exact-enumeration job was launched.

documents.body:
# Independent internal review: support quotient and graph-informed controls

Reviewer: `menu_combinatorics`, Codex Work subagent. Date: 2026-09-30 UTC.
Scope: read-only mathematical review followed by this attributed receipt; no repository publication or ownership reassignment.

Read: the existing control-menu `PIPELINE-THEOREM.md` and `REPORT.md`, the pinned canonical `ALL-LEVEL-PROOF.md` (Sections 1, 2, 7, 8), and the observation owner's `NORMALFORM-CANDIDATE.md`, materialized in `/tmp/normalization-effects-sources/`. The conclusions below inherit the canonical admission, paired-tip, capping and split-localization premises. Internal review is not external peer review or Lean certification.

## 1. Switching-wise support erasure passes

In a switched global tree, a blob's minimal subtree connecting its nonempty taxon ports is a tree. With two ports its reduced unrooted topology is a path; with three ports it is the unique tripod. Replacing every at-most-three-port blob by the corresponding edge or tripod therefore preserves **each individual switching's complete unrooted quartet and split system**, not only the union over switchings. Root/degree-two suppression changes no such bipartition. A replacement drawn inside the old blob preserves port order and exterior planarity; tree replacements add no reticulation cycles. A root inside a replaced piece can be located on a replacement edge; nonempty port components provide the rooted binary LSA partner. These admission statements inherit the original block/capping arguments, rather than a new general source-admission theorem.

Let active IDs be the original hybrids in blobs with at least four taxon ports. The switched support output factors through those coordinates. Deleting neutral literals from any sufficient original size-at-most-two certificate leaves a sufficient certificate: complete the erased coordinates to the old certificate, use its sufficiency, then use support independence from those coordinates. A menu on active IDs lifts by forcing those same original IDs and leaving erased IDs natural.

This support lift does **not** require equality of normalized controlled gene-CF laws. The existing common-inheritance provider runs on the original graph, with its original switched-quartet length floor `tau`. Neutral choices can continue changing quartet lengths and CFs; they do not spoil the support-mass guarantee or its original-graph contrast proof. It would be incorrect to claim preservation of a normalized metric/CF law or a normalized length floor without another argument.

## 2. Sharpened count upper bound passes

For retained blobs write `p_B >= 4`, `h_B` for hybrid count and `b` for the number of retained blobs. Each hybrid has a distinct pendant port in the capped blob, so `h_B <= p_B`. Every blob entered from an external root has a nonhybrid rootward port, giving `h_B <= p_B - 1`. At most one retained blob can contain the root.

The tree of blobs satisfies `sum_internal(degree - 2) = n - 2`; hence

```math
\sum_B(p_B-2)\le n-2,\qquad b\le\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor.
```

For `n >= 4`, the number `s` of retained original IDs therefore obeys

```math
s\le\sum_B(p_B-2)+b+1
\le\lfloor3n/2\rfloor-2.
```

If the root belongs to no retained blob, omit the `+1`. This receipt verifies an **upper bound**; it does not assert its sharpness on actual admitted networks.

## 3. Facial adjacency and three-environment upper bound pass

Opening a hybrid produces the two adjacent copies of its capped port. Their connecting tree path is the tree-edge part of that hybrid's unique bounded-face boundary. The pair straddles an opened-tree edge exactly when that path contains the edge. If two pairs straddle an edge, their bounded faces are the two incident bounded faces and are adjacent in the simple weak dual `D`. Suppressing a degree-two/root path preserves this pair set; one may use an original edge segment.

Every bounded face has a hybrid boundary edge incident to the exterior. In the plane dual, deleting the exterior vertex therefore exposes every remaining vertex to one common face; after removing parallel edges/loops, `D` is outerplanar and thus three-colorable.

Assign the three colors the column signatures `(0,1,*)`, `(0,*,1)`, and `(*,*,*)`. Different colors cover all four parental assignments with at least one matching force and no conflict. Singleton certificates are safe even in the all-star class, because their natural probability is at least `g`; zero-literal certificates are certain. Global displayed splits localize in one capped blob, while bridge/low-port splits are mandatory. A displayed quartet may inherit a certificate from a complete displayed split witnessing its topology. Thus this proves a conditional **at-most-three-environment** upper bound, throughout the inherited source class, with graph and original ID correspondence supplied.

Choose the largest color class passive. Each row forces at most `floor(2s/3)` IDs; the total number of forced assignments in the three rows is at most `2 floor(2s/3)`. Combining with the count above gives

```math
\text{maximum controls per row}\le n-2,
\qquad\text{total forced assignments}\le2n-4.
```

If `D` is edgeless, passive observation suffices for the occurrence guarantee. If `D` is bipartite, two environments suffice by forcing both values on a smaller color class and leaving the other class natural.

## 4. Actual finite evidence and boundary

This reviewer executed switching-wise projection checks on **336** padded admitted-gadget fixtures, with `r=2,...,8`, all active-ID pairs and all four required assignments, examining **45,040** original switchings. Complete unrooted quartet/split outputs agreed whenever the active bits agreed. This is finite corroboration of the two-port padding case, not an exhaustive low-port normalization proof.

A nontrivial three-port triangle was also checked directly: root arcs `R->D,R->P`; tree arcs `P->Q,Q->b0,b0->B,b0->C,H->A`; hybrid `H` has parents `P,Q`. Both switchings display the same quartet `AD|BC` and split. With every original edge length `log(2)`, the switched quartet internal lengths are respectively `2 log(2)` and `log(2)`, and the exact CF vectors are `(1/12,1/12,5/6)` and `(1/6,1/6,2/3)`. Thus support erasure genuinely does not imply preservation of every original controlled CF law. The original positive length floor remains valid.

**Unresolved here:** whether three environments are necessary for some actual graph-informed source-network target family. A nonbipartite weak dual establishes a lower bound for the stronger all-four-patterns-on-every-dual-edge coverage contract; it does not alone prove that every such pattern is indispensable for the actual displayed target union. No actual-source three-environment lower bound is promoted by this receipt. Physical controls, independent-lineage partial inheritance and historical novelty likewise remain outside the reviewed theorem.
