# Direct maximal-root-blob replacement with the original cut matrices fixed

Author: dot (OpenAI), 23 October 2026.
Record: PHY-MAXIMAL-DIRECT-PORT-v1.
Status: complete author-checked hand proof with scoped coordinating-assistant
hand-review PASS on 23 October 2026. See the separate
[review receipt](RETAINED-PORT-DIRECT-REVIEW.md). No Lean elaboration, runtime,
independent-human review or historical novelty certification is claimed.

## 1. Exact improvement, source relation and target

This note adds a direct adapter for a genuine maximal binary root 2-blob.
Its two boundary attachment vertices need not both be internal sinks. It
replaces the blob interior by a fresh rooted fork on those SAME attachment
vertices, keeping BOTH original cut-edge matrices, and every other exterior
parameter, exactly fixed. The earlier subdivision adapter remains valid; it
does not prove this stronger fixed-cut statement because it may change the
cut matrices.

The target is the retained-port rooted fork, not an unrestricted single
semidirected edge. Its two retained ports have indegree one and outdegree
one in the full network. This intermediate graph is a permitted rooted DAG,
not silently a binary phylogenetic network without degree-two vertices.
This note does not assert that arbitrary zero-entry edge parameters may be
split when these degree-two ports or the root are suppressed.

Primary setting: [Sullivant, Section 5, Propositions 5.6–5.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.23056v2#S5)
defines a retained-port replacement and asks for exact image equality after
establishing inclusion and a limiting converse. His proposition explicitly
uses two sinks. The present graph argument also covers the nonterminal-port
maximal binary case, using the source binary conventions of
[Brits et al., Definition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12919v3#S2.SS1).
It is not a solution of the broader literal nonmaximal 2-sub-blob contract
in [Brits et al., Section 5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.12919v3#S5.SS1).
The separately recorded definition/operation and rooting-lift blocker is
unchanged.

The algebra reuses [PROOF.md, Sections 3–4](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/f8da22c7305d18bf4e9cc3b56d3c82d1aa1da2ad/research/2026-10-22-dot-phylogeny-root-blob/PROOF.md),
[OPEN-EQUIVARIANT-PROOF.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/808c5f2931878a70dc08faed26e764c43b4a4e37/research/2026-10-22-dot-phylogeny-root-blob/OPEN-EQUIVARIANT-PROOF.md),
and [CONTINUOUS-TIME-BOUNDARY.md, Section 2](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/befa68f0095139f5ff747b3b671d8a82e96ac4fc/research/2026-10-22-dot-phylogeny-root-blob/CONTINUOUS-TIME-BOUNDARY.md).
The new obligation is their direct composition with a possibly nonterminal
original boundary port, rather than an assertion that the old two-sink
hypothesis held automatically. The two-sink proof-source package and later
maximal subdivision source package remain entirely unelaborated and do not
formally verify this new argument.

## 2. Graph contract and the terminal-port lemma

Let G be a finite simple binary rooted directed acyclic network. Its unique
root has indegree zero and outdegree two. Every other nonleaf vertex has
degrees (indegree,outdegree)=(1,2) or (2,1), and leaves have indegree one and
outdegree zero. Only labelled leaves are observed. If the original source
class requires the root to be the last stable ancestor of the leaves, keep
that hypothesis; the argument below does not remove it.

Let B be a nontrivial maximal connected bridgeless vertex-induced region
containing the actual root. Assume exactly two edge occurrences cross from
B to its complement in the underlying graph. All references to maximality
and bridges are undirected; all ancestry and path references are directed.

The reviewed graph argument supplies the following facts, repeated here
to expose the exact dependency.

1. Every vertex of G is root-reachable: following incoming edges backwards
   in a finite DAG terminates at the unique source.
2. Each boundary edge of B is a global bridge. Otherwise an undirected cycle
   containing that edge has connected bridgeless union with B, enlarging B
   and contradicting maximality.
3. Each boundary bridge is directed out of B, since a root path must cross
   it to reach its outside endpoint. In particular B is ancestral.
4. Every vertex of the nontrivial connected bridgeless B has internal
   undirected degree at least two. Thus B has no global leaf; its root has
   no boundary edge; each nonroot vertex, of total degree three, has at most
   one boundary edge. The two edges have distinct nonroot sources a and b.
5. Every internal sink of B is one of these two sources: a different sink
   would be a global leaf inside B. Finite acyclicity gives at least one
   internal sink. Label such a sink b and the other boundary source a.

Since b has no internal child and exactly one boundary edge, it has total
outdegree one. Therefore it is a reticulation with indegree two. Both its
parents are in B by ancestry, and they are distinct because G has no
parallel edges. At least one of these parents is not a. Vertex a is not a
descendant of b inside B; no assertion that a is itself a sink is needed.

For reference, the prior scoped graph receipt is
[ROOT-BLOB-GRAPH-REVIEW.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/7671217d457440a0fae8b435015f772ea0302845/research/2026-10-22-dot-phylogeny-root-blob/ROOT-BLOB-GRAPH-REVIEW.md).
Its earlier fixed-cut exclusion remains an accurate description of that
earlier proof. This note is a separate proposed strengthening.

## 3. Resolutions, path lengths and one common assignment

Fix once and for all a strictly positive normalized parent-choice vector
at each nonroot vertex of B. The choices at different vertices are
independent. Indegree-one vertices have their unique choice with weight
one. These original vectors are not adjusted during any realization below.

For a complete selector sigma, retain its chosen incoming edge at every
nonroot vertex. Following selected parents terminates at the root, so the
retained graph is a rooted tree on the original vertices of B. Write w_sigma
for the product of its prescribed choice weights. Every w_sigma is positive
and their finite sum is one.

Let L_sigma be the number of edges on its undirected a-to-b path. Since a
and b are distinct, L_sigma>=1. Since b is a sink, that path contains
exactly one selected edge entering b and no other edge entering b.

Choose at b a parent different from a, and make any choices elsewhere.
In that resolution a and b are not adjacent: its sole edge incident to b
connects b to that other parent. Consequently at least one selector sigma_0
has L_sigma_0>=2 and w_sigma_0>0. Other selectors may have L_sigma=1; they
must not be discarded or assumed absent.

Put the SAME matrix A on every original edge entering b, and the SAME reset
matrix E(t) on every other internal edge, with 0<t<1. This is one assignment
on the original edge occurrences. No matrix depends on the selector.
For each path the number of reset edges is L_sigma-1, possibly zero. Define

    c(t) = sum_sigma w_sigma t^(L_sigma-1).

Then 0<c(t)<1: every summand lies in (0,1], and the sigma_0 summand is
strictly below one. Finiteness gives c(t)->1 as t increases to 1. Thus every
strict threshold c(t)>eta with eta<1 can be met at a finite t<1. If desired,
Lmax=max_sigma L_sigma and Bernoulli's inequality give
c(1-1/n)>=1-(Lmax-1)/n for integers n>1.

## 4. Literal Fourier JC/K2P/K3P domain, including zero edge entries

Let K be the Klein four group. A stochastic group-based matrix has the form
M_p(x,y)=p(y-x), for a probability distribution p on K. Let T_3 consist of
those matrices for which all three nontrivial Fourier eigenvalues lie in
(0,1). T_2 imposes the designated equality of two eigenvalues, and T_J
requires all three equal. Entries are NONNEGATIVE, not assumed positive.
Let T_*^+ denote the strictly positive-entry subfamily. The root is uniform.

### 4.1 Forward image: why even K3P becomes strictly positive

For every admitted p, inversion at zero gives

    p(0)=(1+lambda_1+lambda_2+lambda_3)/4>0.

If its support had at most two elements, it would be contained in {0,h}
for a nonzero h, or consist only of 0. A nontrivial character equal to 1 on
h is then equal to 1 on all of the support. Its eigenvalue would be 1,
contrary to admission. Hence the support has at least three elements.
This argument applies separately to the entire T_3 class, not merely T_2.

For two such probability distributions p,q and any g, the subsets
supp(p) and g-supp(q) of the four-element group intersect. At an element
h in their intersection, p(h)q(g-h)>0. Hence every entry of their convolution
is positive. Additional probability factors preserve positivity.

In each resolved tree, ordinary marginalization of unused branches and
uniform-root reversibility give the ordered pair table

    P_sigma(X_a=i,X_b=j) = (1/4) (K_sigma)_{ij},
    K_sigma = product of M_e over the a-to-b path.

All matrices are symmetric and commute, so path orientation makes no
difference. Every path product has nontrivial eigenvalues in (0,1), is
stochastic, and preserves the designated JC/K2P equalities. Products with
L_sigma>=2 are strictly positive by the support argument. Since sigma_0
has positive weight, their mixture

    K_B = sum_sigma w_sigma K_sigma

is strictly positive in every entry, including when some one-edge terms
have zeros. Its Fourier eigenvalues are convex combinations of numbers in
(0,1), and the same equality constraints persist. Therefore K_B is in T_*^+.

### 4.2 Reverse image: exact finite realization

Take any target M in T_*^+. Let U have all entries 1/4 and put
J(t)=tI+(1-t)U. Use Section 3's common assignment with E(t)=J(t).
For every selector,

    K_sigma = A J(t^(L_sigma-1)).

This identity includes a one-edge path, for which the reset factor is
algebraically J(1)=I; no actual original edge is assigned an identity.
The affine dependence of J on its scalar gives

    K_B = A J(c(t)).

Let m=min_ij M_ij>0 and lambda_max=max_i lambda_i(M)<1. Choose a finite
t<1 with c=c(t)>max{0,lambda_max,1-4m}, and set

    A=U+(M-U)/c.

Its entries [M_ij-(1-c)/4]/c are positive, its rows sum to one, and its
nontrivial eigenvalues lambda_i(M)/c lie in (0,1) with the same required
equalities. Thus A and every J(t) lie in the SAME original T_* class,
indeed in T_*^+. Direct multiplication gives K_B=M exactly.

**Theorem F.** For the maximal root-blob graph contract of Section 2 and
every fixed strictly positive original inheritance assignment, the exact
ordered (a,b) pair image is {(1/4)M : M in T_*^+}, separately for
*=J,2,3, even when the allowed original edge class is the literal T_*.

The two-edge rooted fork has exactly the same image. Necessity is the
two-factor support argument. For sufficiency, the same compensation with
any c in (max{0,lambda_max,1-4m},1) gives M=A J(c), with both fork matrices
in T_*^+. Thus the theorem compares the original full domains, not only
an approximation or their closures.

## 5. Full open H-equivariant class, with the D_mu convention

Let S be a finite state set of size at least two, and H any group of state
permutations. Allow ALL strictly positive row-stochastic matrices M with
M(hi,hj)=M(i,j), and freely varying H-invariant root distributions.
The root distribution may have zero entries. There is no embeddability,
fixed-root, shared-generator, reversibility or spectral restriction.

Let P_H^+ be the strictly positive probability tables J on S x S satisfying
J(hi,hj)=J(i,j). Rows are indexed by the state at a and columns by the state
at b. Diagonal matrices D_mu always use this row-marginal convention here.

### 5.1 Forward image, including root distributions with zeros

Fix any admitted parameters. Both a and b are distinct nonroot vertices.
For any requested pair of states i,j, choose a root state of positive root
probability and arbitrary states for the other hidden vertices, with a=i
and b=j. In any resolved tree all its transition factors are strictly
positive. This assignment contributes positively to the requested pair
probability. Thus every resolved table and their mixture are strictly
positive. Applying h to all assigned states preserves the root and edge
factors; summing preserves simultaneous H-invariance. Hence the resulting
table lies in P_H^+. No marginal-zero or terminal-independence assumption
is hidden in this argument.

### 5.2 Reverse image without commuting A past a reset

Fix J in P_H^+. Set

    mu_i = sum_j J_ij,
    M_ij = J_ij/mu_i,
    nu = mu M.

Then mu and nu are strictly positive invariant probability rows, M is
positive stochastic and equivariant, and J=D_mu M. Put

    E_mu(t)=tI+(1-t)1mu.

Use root mu, put A on every incoming-b edge, and E_mu(t) on all other
internal edges. The common reset satisfies

    mu E_mu(t)=mu,
    E_mu(s)E_mu(t)=E_mu(st),
    E_mu(t)^T D_mu = D_mu E_mu(t).

Since b is an internal sink, no A edge can be ancestral to a or to the
resolved lowest common ancestor of a,b. Thus that ancestor has law mu.
If its path to a has k reset edges and its path to the parent of b has
ell reset edges, then k+ell=L_sigma-1. Ordinary rooted-tree conditioning
gives the ordered table

    (E_mu(t)^k)^T D_mu E_mu(t)^ell A
      = D_mu E_mu(t)^(k+ell) A
      = D_mu E_mu(t^(L_sigma-1)) A.

This also handles a being the common ancestor (k=0), and the possible
one-edge a-to-b path (k=ell=0). Averaging gives

    J_B = D_mu E_mu(c(t)) A.                         (H1)

There has been no assertion that A commutes with E_mu(t). Only reversibility
and mutual multiplication of the reset factors were used.

Let alpha=min_ij M_ij/nu_j>0. Choose finite t<1 with 1-c(t)<alpha, and put

    A = [M-(1-c)1nu]/c,     c=c(t).                  (H2)

Every entry of A is positive. Its row sums are [1-(1-c)]/c=1, and it is
equivariant because M is equivariant and nu is invariant. Moreover

    mu A=[nu-(1-c)nu]/c=nu,
    E_mu(c)A=cA+(1-c)1(mu A)=M.

Equations (H1)–(H2) give J_B=D_mu M=J exactly, with the original inheritance
unchanged. Every edge remains in the original full open equivariant class.

**Theorem H.** Under the Section 2 graph contract, the exact ordered pair
image is P_H^+ for every fixed strictly positive original inheritance
assignment. The retained-port rooted fork has the same image: its necessity
is the same positive-assignment argument, and its sufficiency is this
construction with L=2 and c=t. Root parameters may change to mu; this is
not a fixed-root theorem except in the separate uniform-root group-based
cases already proved in Section 4.

## 6. Strictly positive-rate CT-K2P, not the rate boundary or CT-K3P

For completeness the same direct-port proof also composes the previously
reviewed CT-K2P-positive theorem without subdividing any cut edge. Its edge
class C2> has integrated rates a,b>0, uniform root, and eigenvalues x,x,y
with x=exp[-2(a+b)], y=exp[-4b]. Equivalently 0<x,y<1 and y>x^2.

On each resolved nonempty a-to-b path, products X_sigma,Y_sigma satisfy
Y_sigma>X_sigma^2. Hence the mixed eigenvalues satisfy

    y=sum w_sigma Y_sigma
      >sum w_sigma X_sigma^2
      >=(sum w_sigma X_sigma)^2=x^2.

This inclusion requires only L_sigma>=1, so one-edge paths cause no gap.
For a target (x,x,y) in C2>, use the same A/J(t) assignment and choose
c(t)>max{x,y,x^2/y}. The compensating A has eigenvalues x/c,x/c,y/c and
strictly positive integrated rates

    a_A=log(c y/x^2)/4,     b_A=-log(y/c)/4.

Every reset J(t) also has both integrated rates -log(t)/4>0. Thus the target
is attained in the same original C2> class. The rooted fork has exact image
C2> because these commuting generators add and each positive rate pair
splits into two positive halves. This proves both local image directions.

No zero rate is included. The earlier positive-entry/zero-rate K2P failure
and positive-rate K3P mixture obstruction remain unchanged. In particular
the latter does not satisfy the convex-path inclusion just used for K2P.

## 7. Complete observed-law equality with fixed original cut matrices

Write the two original cut edges as a->c_a and b->c_b. Define F with vertex
set (V(G) minus B) union {a,b,rho}, where rho is fresh. Remove EVERY original
edge with both endpoints in B, including a->b if present, and add precisely
rho->a and rho->b. Keep all original edges whose target lies outside B,
their original occurrences, and the exterior observations. In particular
both cut-edge occurrences a->c_a and b->c_b remain unchanged. The
rooted fork's two new incoming weights are 1, since each port now has just
one parent. Deleted interior edge IDs and weights are not asserted to
survive as new fork edge IDs.

Fix any allowed exterior parameter assignment theta_ext, including BOTH
cut matrices, all other exterior matrices, and all parent-choice vectors
at exterior vertices. Fix any allowed positive normalized original
inheritance assignment W_B inside B. Its choices are independent of the
exterior choices. There is no incoming boundary edge and no observation
inside B. Thus the unchanged exterior defines one stochastic kernel

    Q_theta_ext(z | i,j)

from the ordered port states to the full labelled observation z. This
kernel can be obtained by the finite product of exterior conditional
factors followed by summation over all exterior hidden states. Its
dependence on internal B states is only through a,b. External reconvergence
or additional parent terms do not license replacing a joint table by its
marginals, and no such replacement is used.

For both networks the full observed probability is exactly

    p(z)=sum_ij P_ab(i,j) Q_theta_ext(z | i,j).

For each of the domains in Theorems F and H and Section 6:

* Starting from any original G parameter point, its port table belongs to
  the classified pair image. The rooted fork realizes that same table.
  Leave theta_ext unchanged. The complete observed law is identical.
* Starting from any fork F parameter point, its port table belongs to that
  same image. The construction in the ORIGINAL blob realizes it with the
  originally prescribed W_B, not new or limiting inheritance. Leave
  theta_ext unchanged. Again the complete observed law is identical.

Consequently the two observed-law images are equal for EVERY fixed common
theta_ext and EVERY fixed allowed W_B. In Theorem F the fixed exterior
Fourier matrices may themselves contain zero entries. In Theorem H they
are strictly positive, as required by that original domain. In Section 6
they have strictly positive K2P rates. The construction does not alter any
of them. Interior edge matrices remain freely and independently variable;
constraints coupling them to protected exterior matrices are not covered.

## 8. Precise exclusions and remaining trust dependencies

This is a stronger retained-port hand theorem, not a retraction of the
previous free-cut subdivision theorem. In particular:

* It does not turn a zero-entry K2P/K3P matrix into a product of two literal
  domain matrices. The support argument proves that such a product is
  impossible. No individual zero-entry cut factorization is used here.
* It does not assert equality with an unrestricted single semidirected
  replacement edge or with all possible root placements. The published
  quartet boundary counterexample still has exactly its earlier force.
* It does not preserve a prescribed open-equivariant root parameter or
  fixed original interior matrices. For Fourier and CT-K2P the root remains
  uniform throughout, as specified by those domains.
* It does not cover arbitrary smaller equivariant families, shared edge
  matrices/generators, fixed branch lengths, zero-rate CT-K2P or CT-K3P
  model-image equality.
* It does not justify the literal broader root-trapping 2-sub-blob operation
  or its universal semidirected larger-blob root lift. The maximal actual
  root-containing graph contract remains explicit.

The whole hand claim depends on the graph facts in Section 2, the actual
shared-selector path marginalization in Section 3, the domain-specific
forward and reverse proofs in Sections 4–6, and the joint-context identity
in Section 7. None is replaced by a conditional algebra lemma alone.
The prior two-sink and maximal-subdivision source proposals remain
UNELABORATED; this note adds no Lean code or execution. The new direct-port
argument has not been formalized. Historical priority remains bounded by
the existing primary-source review, not certified worldwide novelty.

documents.title: Contiguous multicopy extension: independent scoped hand review
documents.body:
# Contiguous multicopy extension: independent scoped hand review

Date: 23 October 2026. Reviewer: dot, coordinating assistant.

**Verdict: PASS at the stated abstract plane-tree scope.** This independently reviews an already author-complete theorem. It is not a new theorem, a retroactive authorship gate, external human peer review, a fresh computational run, or a Lean certificate.

## Proof identity

Reviewed the complete [CONTIGUOUS-MULTICOPY-EXTENSION.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/CONTIGUOUS-MULTICOPY-EXTENSION.md), at commit `e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7`, Git blob `c788025d2d7821a884bb1ea10fc1389a8e7024ce`.

The source theorem assumes a finite unrooted plane binary tree, at least four taxon labels, one nonempty contiguous cyclic occurrence block per label, and independent choice of one occurrence of each label. The retained occurrences are the two endpoints of each block, or its sole occurrence. Restriction means the minimal connecting subtree followed by degree-two suppression. Block endpoints are defined by the block's boundaries in the cyclic order, not by an arbitrary linear cut through its interior.

## Checks of the full extension

1. **One-block replacement.** The three components at the median of three fixed other-label tips have disjoint interval leaf sets in the plane contour. An occurrence block avoiding those three tips lies inside one of the three complementary open arcs. Such an arc meets only the two adjacent median components, with at most one transition between them. Consequently any component met by the block contains an endpoint of that block. Replacing a selected occurrence by that endpoint preserves the quartet split because the quartet depends only on its median component.

2. **All quartet sets.** The one-block argument may be applied successively to each of four distinct labels while holding the other selected tips fixed. Every resulting witness uses retained endpoints. Associativity of minimal-subtree restriction identifies its quartet in the reduced tree. Reverse inclusion follows because retained tips were original tips. This proves equality of the complete indexed system of distinct quartet sets, not joint realization of all quartet witnesses by one selection.

3. **Circular order and split union.** Endpoint deletion preserves the collapsed taxon order. Every selected tree has that order. For a nontrivial circular split, take its adjacent boundary pairs (a,b) and (c,d). A displayed (bc| ad) quartet extends to a full selected tree by independent choices for the other labels. An edge of its central path separates those pairs; circularity and the two prescribed boundary gaps force its full split to be the specified split. Thus equality of quartet sets gives equality of split unions. Trivial splits are present throughout. This does not assume equality of full displayed-tree families.

4. **Distance, anchors and parameter transfer.** The original distance averages over distinct quartet topologies and retains the same number of taxon labels. Its entries, the anchor matrices, and fixed taxon-mass-weighted sums are therefore unchanged. The reduction lands in the adjacent singleton/doubleton representation class with at most (2|X|) physical tips. Conversely that class is already a subclass of contiguous blocks. Hence any score formula using only the indexed quartet sets, common order and taxon-level masses has the same universal parameter domain on the two classes. This is a transfer, not a new numerical parameter-domain calculation.

5. **Full-tree exclusion.** Direct hand inspection of the seven-tip caterpillar confirms the three displayed five-label split sets:
   - (x_0): (ax| bcd), (acx| bd);
   - (x_1): (ac| bdx), (acx| bd);
   - (x_2): (ac| bdx), (acd| bx).

   The middle tree is distinct from both extreme trees and disappears after deletion, while each of its splits remains. On the five four-label subsets, the quartet triples in order (x_0,x_1,x_2) are:
   - (abcd): (ac| bd, ac| bd, ac| bd);
   - (abcx): (ax| bc, ac| bx, ac| bx);
   - (abdx): (ax| bd, ax| bd, ad| bx);
   - (acdx): (ax| cd, ac| dx, ac| dx);
   - (bcdx): (cx| bd, cx| bd, cd| bx).

   Removing the middle column preserves each row's set, not its multiplicities. For example, uniform occurrence choice gives probability (1/3) to (ax| bc) on (abcx), versus (1/2) after endpoint reduction. Thus the exclusions of full-tree equality and occurrence-weighted distribution equality are substantive and correct.

## Supplier scope inspected

All links below use the same immutable commit.

- [ALL-LEVEL-STRUCTURAL-AUDIT.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/ALL-LEVEL-STRUCTURAL-AUDIT.md), blob `c655b69c1180fbe0e284a5e27218dace3c686bfb`: minimal-subtree repair, arbitrary-size restriction and the abstract adjacent-copy representation domain.
- [ALL-LEVEL-SUPPORT-STRUCTURAL-AUDIT.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/ALL-LEVEL-SUPPORT-STRUCTURAL-AUDIT.md), blob `42e6fef0d4a7f7f24f91d59c4b210747a5195f99`: boundary-quartet criterion and positive-weight exact-support transfer.
- [ALL-LEVEL-PROOF.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/ALL-LEVEL-PROOF.md), blob `313f0aff82eabf1a08b4551ed7e31501b137cebd`: Sections 3–6 and 8 specify the anchor convention, representation-wide coefficient reduction and exact support ingredients.
- [ALL-LEVEL-FINITE-AUDIT.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/ALL-LEVEL-FINITE-AUDIT.md), blob `0722de104b5d2006fe5a0b02c3ca0d4c46f4118b`, and [ALL-LEVEL-SUPPORT-FINITE-AUDIT.md](https://github.com/Sodelin/Work-on-Samuel-Alexander-Research-/blob/e2502c82ab9a77c00543932f775a71e5374221f7/research/nanuq-all-level-2026-09-29/ALL-LEVEL-SUPPORT-FINITE-AUDIT.md), blob `15b85cc6475a6b8bf3b64f79722231b42127b383`: their recorded assertions cover all enumerated adjacent-copy systems, not only representations known to come from biological networks.

These supplier documents were read. Their domain and use in the extension match. The downstream circularity/exact-support transfer inherits the previously accepted computer-assisted ingredients; this review neither reran them nor independently audited every verifier implementation or re-established the external network-representation literature.

## Limits and records consequence

No mathematical repair was identified within the stated theorem. The proof does not cover interleaved occurrence blocks, nonbinary trees, constrained cross-label choices, infinite trees, or automatically admit higher-indegree biological networks. Biological use still requires the separate source-to-contiguous-block representation theorem. No historical novelty or formal-verification upgrade is made.

For card **CB-NANUQ-004**, preserve complete authorship and add this separately scoped assistant hand-review receipt. Replace only the historical claim that no separately located whole-extension review was available. No execution or public repository mutation was performed for this review.

# Fail-closed BPP inference release screen and application roadmap

Author: dot (OpenAI), 5 October 2026.

The current result is **inference not yet numerically reliable**. This tested interface authenticates the frozen reviewed evidence and deliberately withholds ranked-history recommendations. It makes the unresolved inference state a machine-readable outcome rather than allowing successful execution or selected high ESS values to masquerade as a scientific result.

## Implemented behavior

`release_screen.py` accepts two exact profile names: `frog-a01` and `matched-synthetic-a00`. It checks a source-pinned evidence manifest and authenticates all referenced artifacts before interpreting their schema/profile. Both current profiles return:

- `status: WITHHELD_NUMERICAL_RELIABILITY`
- `ranking_released: false`
- `ranked_histories: null` and `recommended_history: null`
- target assumptions, gate states, supporting evidence hashes and required next evidence
- process exit code 2, so a caller does not mistake withholding for a successful ranking

Unknown profiles return `NOT_ADMITTED`. Missing, changed or malformed evidence returns structured `EVIDENCE_INVALID`. The screen neither launches BPP nor fits new data. It contains no approved success/ranking-release path. Future successful release requires a separately implemented and reviewed path; callers cannot force it by supplying a boolean flag.

The frog profile retains exploratory candidate frequencies in their authenticated original artifact without presenting a selected tree as a reliable recommendation. The synthetic A00 profile explicitly records that fixed-topology analysis did not perform topology ranking. A valid synthetic fixture cannot override unresolved frog diagnostics. Prior-only chains and a same-seed recovery are not counted as independent posterior replicates.

Ten tests cover both current decisions, unknown inputs, changed/missing evidence, semantic/schema failures, candidate withholding, fixed-topology scope, prior-chain separation and the CLI exit contract. Both saved decisions independently reproduce exactly. The implementation is a **withholding-only release screen over frozen research profiles**, not generic biological admission, a full diagnostic package or a completed DNA-to-histories application.

## Evidence and use

The original source layout supports:

`python bpp-fail-closed-release-20261005-0816z/release_screen.py frog-a01`

`python bpp-fail-closed-release-20261005-0816z/release_screen.py matched-synthetic-a00`

    G30(FG)=k12(F)*G30(G)+G30(F)*k9(G),             (4)

with their actual no-merger diagonals k_r. No hidden two-insertion term

We need the uniform source consequence

    |G30(C)-F(C)|<=C*s, |d12-1|<=C*r.              (5)

r_j=g^j+(1-g)^j. Hence for every n>=4,

    [u^2]A_n=3(r2^2-r3)=-3v*beta.

## 4. The third filter, with both real source transports

Let s_r=b_r(S(t)) and define the known reference number

The denominator is90h+O(h^2). The fair source in(3) has

Since I<=H, equations(9)--(10),(14) prove the first bound in(1).

# Explicit finite-barrier nanowire certificate

This addendum gives two fully specified rational 60-site devices in the [previously declared fixed-lead model](../README.md). Both use the same external leads, a 1 eV end onsite barrier, zero internal dissipation, and the same common applied-field settings.

- Their reflection determinants at B = 2 meV have certified opposite margins: −0.203 < TV_minus < −0.202 and 0.996 < TV_plus < 0.997.
- Their lowest nonnegative closed-wire energies differ by at most **0.09999 μeV at every common field**. On any common 512-setting menu, one midpoint report lies within **0.049995 μeV** of both.
- This is one explicit finite pair at t = 25.08215 meV, not a uniform finite certificate over the earlier hopping interval. It makes a previously existential construction concrete; it does not assert equality of noiseless spectra or a measured classifier failure frequency.

## Read the result

1. [Exact statement, model, rational parameters and proof](FINITE-PAIR-CERTIFICATE-02.md)

The 13 arithmetic controls and direct verifier both passed. This is a hand-checked proof plus independently replayed exact-arithmetic certificate, **not a formal Lean proof**.

The 1 eV end onsite is a mathematical example; physical feasibility and the effective model's validity at that barrier are unestablished. The model class permits unrestricted scalar potentials and has zero internal dissipation. Its exact lead/disorder implementation has not been authenticated as Taylor's original executable model. The 0.6 μm length is excluded from Taylor Appendix II's modified energy-plus-length unsupervised variant. MEDA studies a different target.

## Contract and conclusion

Unknown admitted finite binary rooted LSA outer-labeled planar cut-child source, n≥4, arbitrary finite level/blob count, complete r ORIGINAL binary hybrid IDs with parental labels, positive finite edge lengths/interior natural inheritance. Known independent inheritance or unknown common/independent mode is allowed. Observe exact unrooted one-copy gene-quartet laws, or the vector of these marginals. Controls reset, force all live lineages at original IDs and preserve other source parameters.

Natural (*) and partial/full forcing rows are allowed; programmes may retain the selected-row label. Configuration cost is positive support union along a programme trajectory, sites are union of forced original IDs, and programmes are executed exact-law calls. No cap smaller than r is imposed on simultaneous actuation. Policies are deterministic total identifying policies; row randomization is part of a programme.

**Theorem.** For r≥1 the jointly attainable sharp worst-case vector is

sites r; distinct configurations 2; labelled programmes1.

With positive support cap L, programme minimum is ceil(2/L). The upper works for every finite n≥4/all levels; lower necessity is already witnessed on four taxa. For known common inheritance only, the already accepted passive branch has sites0/configuration1/programme1; the two-row policy remains valid but is not optimal.

This sharp branch does not require binary covering-array many full rows: allowing a NATURAL row supplies a different observation. The [C(r) theorem](FULL-FORCING-NUMERICAL-OPTIMUM.md) remains correct under its stricter FULL-forcing-only contract.

## 1. Only two original-source shape lemmas are needed

Source: [ASTRA-OBS PROOFS Sections1–3](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/eeb1cc98ed2c829dbb55eb5748be5e33256420f7/research/2026-09-30-astra-alllevel-observation-1034z/PROOFS.md). Structural quartet/cut-edge localization and at-most-two displayed topologies are inherited source premises. No compressed/synthetic actuator IDs are introduced.

**Singleton shape:** if original Q={t}, its two absent CFs are equal. Localize an original 2|2 cut edge. A merger within its descendant two-tip component fixes t. Otherwise the two unresolved roots meet at the SAME original population interface at its fixed source time. Subsequent Kingman/routing is invariant under swapping those roots; this exchanges the other two unrooted quartet topologies. Earlier asymmetry can contribute only to t, not break absent equality. Root histories/other lineages and per-event inheritance coins remain in the original source. No lower bound1/6 or singleton attainability classification is used.

**Two-support shape:** if Q={t,u}, its absent topology v is strictly below both natural CFs p_t,p_u. In the central four-port blob, each hybrid-child bridge contains only one selected taxon. Until first merger, each pendant hybrid receives at most one entering lineage, so common/independent routing agree there. First merger fixes the unrooted quartet. Above the rootward interface, surviving three ingroup roots are permutation-exchangeable under either mechanism, producing the same uniform residual contribution. When root is inside the blob, the corresponding four-root ancestral contribution is exchangeable. Thus the quartet law has the displayed-tree mixture shape; every displayed switching and its positive internal path contributes strict excess above the absent minimum.

These statements retain original structural localization, same-interface/exchangeability, positive parameters and mode semantics as premises. They do not assert independent inheritance equals common inheritance for singleton sources. Parent/root has independently challenged these exact shapes, including rootward symmetry and original-interface timing; final theorem acceptance remains separate below.

## 2. Explicit decoder, without arbitrary-law recognition

Programme chooses natural row and the single all-zero full-forcing row each with probability1/2; retain row label. Exact joint law exposes both conditional vectors p and f, by dividing label masses by1/2. They use one graph/parameter assignment and actual original IDs.

Full forcing yields a positive tree MSC law. Its unique maximum t0 is a displayed quartet of the ORIGINAL source. It is a known support member, not one sampled gene topology.

Compute candidate supports from p:

- singleton {t} is a candidate when the OTHER two p entries are equal
- pair {t,u} is a candidate when BOTH exceed the remaining entry

Retain candidates containing t0. Exactly one remains:

1. Uniform p: only singleton candidates; marker picks {t0}
2. Unique maximum/equal lower entries: singleton maximum
3. Three distinct entries: pair of entries above the unique minimum
4. Unique minimum/equal higher entries: singleton minimum or complementary pair; marker membership selects exactly one

This also resolves independent-inheritance anomalous singleton laws and equality/uniform strata. An arbitrary supplied p need not be source-realizable; the promise is the admitted source, and no G3 membership solver is assumed. The checker rejects inconsistent marker/input patterns rather than silently inventing a source.

Do this for every taxon quartet and use the inherited original Q→S/order decoder. Whole-gene quartet correlations do not matter to population-law identification; no independence of quartets within a locus is asserted.

The policy costs two rows, r sites and one labelled programme. For L=1, query the two rows separately in two programmes.

## 3. Matched configuration lower bound

A procedure with worst-case at most one distinct configuration must choose its first row before obtaining source observations. Repeats of that exact row add no information; choosing another row/support violates the proposed one-configuration budget.

- If any original ID is left natural, place the admitted triangle/diamond natural equal-law collision at that ID, with every other ID in single-lineage neutral pendant padding. All forced/natural settings at the remaining IDs are irrelevant. Both sources return (59/200,141/400,141/400), while Q/S differ
- If every ID is forced, use the one-hybrid forced-row collision: a selected switched diamond tree and a matching singleton tree with neutral hybrid have the same entire gene-quartet law, but different original Q/S. Pad the remaining IDs neutrally and name/reverse parental labels to match the chosen full row

Each witness pair has one fixed shared-source assignment across every repetition, same complete named registry, admissible root/cut-child/embedding, positive lengths and interior natural inheritance. This is numerical-law equality, not missed-occurrence inference. Thus at least two configurations are necessary. Since support union≤KL, K≥ceil(2/L); the policy attains it.

This one-row argument also covers an adaptive deterministic total policy with a worst-case configuration budget1: the first colliding response remains the same forever, and a second row would violate that budget. No general adaptive configuration frontier is inferred.

## 4. Distinct-site lower bound, including the transcript consistency step

For any fixed design omitting ID h, the same padded natural triangle/diamond collision at h defeats every programme weighting/label. This proves static sites≥r.

For a total deterministic adaptive strategy claiming worst-case sites≤r−1, use the following actual-source adversary. Answer each programme with its exact law built from the constant three-vector p=(59/200,141/400,141/400): labelled output is (w_c p)_c, pooled output is p. At each finite prefix, any still untouched ID h realizes the entire transcript with BOTH padded competitors whose active hybrid is h.

The strategy cannot next force all remaining IDs: that would violate its claimed r−1 bound on those currently consistent actual sources. Hence the union of ever-touched sites along this virtual history remains≤r−1. If it runs forever, choose an ID outside that final union; one FIXED admitted source then realizes the entire infinite path, contradicting totality. If it stops, that same untouched-ID pair gives different targets at the identical terminal transcript. This contradicts correctness.

Therefore worst-case distinct-site cost≥r; the policy attains it. The proof does not silently change the active source after terminal output or substitute a fixed-design lower bound for an adaptive one.

Zero programmes cannot distinguish possible targets. One labelled programme is thus sharp, but its one programme contains TWO underlying environments; this is not one locus or a free physical assay.

## 5. Exact executed checks

[natural_marker_decoder.py](natural_marker_decoder.py), exact pinned compiler/census byte checks, Python3.12.14/SymPy1.14/NetworkX3.5: PASS.

- all546 parent-labelled admitted four-taxon one-hybrid graphs
-1,092 decoder checks across independent/common mechanisms
-1,674 exact law compilations
-18 padded critical source fixtures through r=6
- natural patterns:756 unique-max/equal-minors;336 three-distinct;12 unique-min/equal-majors;6 exact-uniform
- the original anomalous triangle and complementary diamond return identical natural laws but are correctly separated by the marker
- the uniform triangle uses positive survival16/45, not a zero-edge limit

[Exact output](natural-marker-results.json). These finite controls support code; all-r/all-level validity comes from Sections1–4 and the stated source dependencies.

## 6. Correctness versus significance and remaining endpoint

This is a cheap classical decision step once the source-specific CF-shape theorems and a genuine displayed-tree marker are available. The nontrivial project content is their admitted-source assembly and matched resource bound. It does not invent functional identifiability or prove historical novelty.

It improves exact configuration count from the full-forcing C(r) benchmark to2 under a relaxed natural-plus-labelled-marker menu. Programme count1 is partly packaging two labelled environments; physical actuator/locus expense remains separate. An observed gene tree is NOT a displayed-tree marker because ILS gives absent gene outcomes positive probability.

Exact equality/strict-order tests cannot be applied as zero-error empirical comparisons. A rare alternative with the marker on its dominant route can make natural laws arbitrarily close to a singleton source while changing Q. Thus this exact-law optimum is not an honest finite-data support-certification optimum. G6/CG2/BIO-1's uncertainty/observation bridge remains essential.

Still unresolved here: simultaneous-control cap b<r; erased-label pooled programmes at reduced support; joint partial/continuous adaptive resource Pareto frontiers; actual general backend/policy extraction; richer readouts; unbounded expected constants; DNA calibration and Lean. These are the named residual contracts, not added gates or a paper draft.

documents.body:
# E8 finite-grid traceback-to-observable Lean bridge

Attribution: dot (OpenAI), research assistance for Nolan.
Conversation checkpoint: 2026-10-02 05:17 UTC. Execution-host clocks in raw receipts differ; source hashes and immutable attempt identities determine the compiled versions.

## Result and scope

Seven new proof modules and one aggregate import audit passed Lean 4.33.1 (commit `819816b2e0a3bf405af45ae5c7af2491d8f5bee6`) with mathlib `0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474`. Two previously compiled strict-prefix/uniform-law prerequisites are included unchanged. The seven new modules print 29 theorem axiom audits, all limited to `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`; the aggregate independently imports the composed model and prints nine selected endpoints.

**This is a checked finite mathematical model bridge, not end-to-end PRISM executable correctness, not biological validation, not a new general sampling principle, and not an efficient arbitrary-class aggregation algorithm.**

Actual composition now checked:

1. Strict prefix selection has exact interval fibers and continuous-uniform branch probability `weight/total`.
2. A fixed arbitrary observable aggregates every branch in its fiber, including repeated labels.
3. Under uniform counting on the `N` exact midpoint grid points, a branch count is the difference of two ceiling cutoffs. Each branch error is at most `1/N`; branch-table total variation is at most `(b-1)/(2N)`.
4. Exact production contributions `factor × childPartition` induce the same continuous law, and their grid-selector fiber counts form a normalized finite branch table.
5. Finite-depth conditional products telescope to normalized derivation weights. A literal bijection from derivations to structures removes multiplicity and yields the weighted structure/class law.
6. Nonnegative normalized local kernels with local TV at most `epsilon` have depth-`d` trace TV and arbitrary observable-event error at most `d × epsilon`.
7. These components are composed, giving class-law bias at most `d × (b-1)/(2N)` for exact-real midpoint traceback within the explicit finite grammar model. At `N=2^52` this is `d × (b-1)/2^53`.

The last formula assumes uniform independent conditional grid draws, exact arithmetic, a common state/continuation graph, the given finite depth and production bound, exact contribution matching, and a literal source bijection/weight agreement. It does not independently establish those assumptions for the executable.

## Per-module prior-work and integration contracts

| Module | Established closest contract | What this implementation checks | Named source integration obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| E8StrictPrefixSelector | Classical inverse-CDF sampling and finite cumulative weights; PRISM §2.1 stochastic traceback | Least **strict** crossing, nonzero selected weight, exact interval fiber | Match every executed categorical scan's term order and boundary convention |
| E8UniformPrefixLaw | Continuous-uniform inverse-CDF interval-length law; mathlib Lebesgue measure | Actual `volume.restrict [0,1)` branch probability | The executable has finite-grid input, so this is the ideal local law only |
| E8ObservablePrefixLaw | Standard measurable pushforward and finite disjoint-fiber summation | Measurability and class probability as the sum of all matching branch weights | Match the frozen executable observable, including label collisions |
| E8MidpointGridLaw | Elementary uniform-grid counting and floor/ceiling arithmetic, using mathlib's checked ceiling facts | Exact midpoint count formula and `1/N` branch error | Match `uniform_open52`'s exact-real idealization; admit/verify uniform engine words and floating calculations separately |
| E8MidpointGridTV | Classical finite total variation and cumulative-boundary accounting | `(b-1)/(2N)` local TV, including strict ties and zero weights | Establish the maximum executed production count and separate numerical local-kernel bias |
| E8FiniteTracebackLaw | PRISM §2.1/Ding–Lawrence partition-weight cancellation; CParty unambiguous weighted decomposition | Partitions are defined from productions; finite path products telescope; explicit source bijection yields class law | Encode actual reachable continuation stacks, prove exhaustive disjoint productions and exact Boltzmann factors |
| E8TracebackErrorComposition | Standard stochastic-kernel perturbation/data-processing argument | Local TV accumulates by finite depth; every arbitrary event gets the same error bound | Prove independent conditional inputs, common reachable states, and a genuine depth bound; certify numerical local errors |
| E8MidpointProductionKernel | Composition of the inverse-CDF and weighted-production contracts | Actual selector fibers give normalized production kernels with the grid TV bound | Identify each C++ production contribution with `factor × childPartition` |
| E8GridTracebackBridge | Composition of the preceding established contracts | Complete finite-model grid-to-weighted-class error theorem | Discharge the actual PRISM carrier, weights, classifier, numerical and RNG assumptions |
| E8SamplerBridgeAudit | Standard exact-source import/axiom audit | Nine composed endpoints import and print only standard axioms | This is an integration audit, not another domain theorem |

No exhaustive historical novelty search is implied by this table. Elementary arithmetic and generic pushforward/weighted grammar machinery are expressly treated as established. The value added here is exact compiler-checkable contracts and their composition for the source-specific implementation obligations.

## Primary sources

- [PRISM, WABI 2026 article 30](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.WABI.2026.30), §2.1: partition-contribution stochastic traceback and cancellation; §5: adaptive confidence and selected-class mass directions.
- [Ding and Lawrence, 2003](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkg938): established RNA partition-function sampling architecture.
- [CParty, 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11709253/): fixed-scaffold hierarchical density-2 partition function with ambiguity removal. Duplicate derivations cannot silently count as distinct structures when summing mass.
- [Voß, Giegerich and Rehmsmeier, 2006](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1479382/): existing exact shape-class mass machinery. The arbitrary observable aggregation theorem here does not establish the compositional inverse-image language needed by a fast selected-class grammar.
- [RapidShapes, 2010](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2828121/): established selected-shape matcher and residual-mass architecture. This batch supplies an upstream sampler/error model, not a new residual-mass principle or a density-2/L6 matcher implementation.
- [Pinned mathlib natural ceiling facts](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean) and [Lebesgue interval measure](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/Basic.lean).

## Concrete implementation boundary

The checked PRISM source version motivating this work is commit `87a88715282d279fc361eb56de27153a321359be`. A separate local research adapter uses explicit seed handling, midpoint grid input, strict positive selection and a numerical recurrence-sum guard. **No private adapter code is included in this public batch.**

Next actual-source proof obligations:

- Model reachable `Sample_*` calls and their pending continuations. Nested grammar subcalls are represented by a continuation stack, not by pretending each C++ call is a one-child production.
- Prove termination/depth and production-count bounds on that carrier, including band states and all boundary cases.
- Prove emitted pairs/structures are exactly the fixed-sequence, fixed-scaffold admissible ensemble, with one derivation per structure and matching source energy/scaling conventions.
- Prove every forward contribution equals its corresponding traceback contribution; a tolerance guard passing is not that theorem.
- Prove the frozen L5/L6 classifier matches the mathematical observable. No automatic classifier-compositionality premise is adopted.
- Admit or independently justify the conditional random input law. A fixed pseudorandom seed is deterministic and does not itself give independent uniform draws.
- Bound floating normalization, exponentiation, subtraction and scanning errors. The exact midpoint theorem alone does not cover IEEE/long-double behavior.
- Combine the resulting law-error bound with an actually proved/admitted concentration event and certified confidence numerics. The downstream deterministic top-k/residual lemmas alone do not establish coverage.

## Replaying and auditing

`SOURCE-AND-COMPILE-MANIFEST.json` contains complete successful receipt records and exact SHA256 pins. Each `.lean`, `.log`, and `-receipt.json` triple is copied from its successful immutable attempt. The seven new sources plus both prerequisites form the replay set; compile them in the order listed above with their objects in `LEAN_PATH`, the pinned mathlib/dependency objects available, and `lean -j1 -M4096`. Then compile `E8SamplerBridgeAudit.lean`. No broad `import Mathlib` or costly certificate replay is needed.

The raw compiler receipts include the exact commands, bounded budgets, compile times, source/log/object hashes, direct project-import object hashes and stable-dependency checks. Receipt PASS statements apply to the precise source bytes, not arbitrary future edits.

# E8 originality audit: what remains to solve

Author: dot. Checked 2026-10-02. This is a bounded claim-by-claim technical/prior-art audit, not an exhaustive novelty search. New implementation/proof expansion was paused for this audit. The privately delivered runnable checkpoint is preserved.

## Verdict

**No new generic weighted-grammar, shape-class probability, residual-mass, adaptive-confidence or stochastic-traceback theorem has been established here.** Those ideas have close, often explicit, prior. The currently justified output is an application-specific integration and verification project, with reproduced source evidence and newly written proof artifacts for stated component contracts.

The original PRISM authors' first two future directions still give useful **PRISM-specific software targets**. Their general mathematical ingredients are already known. An exact existing drop-in for the pinned conditional density-2 ensemble, actual current classifiers, executable sampling law and adaptive certificates has not been verified. That does not imply novelty or nonexistence.

## Claims checked individually

| Proposed/current claim | Exact closest prior or existing implementation | Verdict and source-specific difference |
|---|---|---|
| One grammar/provider with exchangeable inside, energy, best derivation and observation modes | ADP/classified DP; MCF-ADP2016; Ponty–Saule2011 RNA weighted hypergraphs; the **actual public SCFG2 README** already explicitly describes a single provider/schedule/local-weight backbone with SumProduct/MaxProduct and observers | Established architecture, already implemented for CParty. Our private wrapper is integration/validation, not invention of a common engine. |
| Sum all members of an observable/shape class | Classified DP and finite measure pushforward; RNAshapes2006; RapidShapes2010 Theorem1; actual pKiss shape×PF algebra product | General theory and substantial software prior. Current PRISM's σ5/σ6 inverse-image restriction on Γ(S,G) still needs implementation/binding to the same local weights and Z; the SCFG2 fixed-target evaluator currently maximizes one derivation. |
| Selected exact class masses plus residual stopping | RapidShapes Theorem1 and threshold/residual strategy; an actual `tdmwrapper` compiles/runs one selected shape's PF | Classical method. Its nested-RNA recognizer/energy grammar is not automatically the PRISM crossing classifier. The classical theorem does not certify our C++ source. |
| Adaptive pair/shape uncertainty and mode/top-k certification | Existing confidence-sequence/e-process methods; Lindon–Malek2022, Ryu–Wornell2024; CITE2026 preprint for fixed targets/sets in unknown countable support | Reuse established statistical machinery. Actual stopping software, class discovery/selection handling, and a justified sampling/bias admission are still missing. Fixed seeded counts are not this interface. |
| Weighted grammar correctness and traceback Boltzmann law | **CParty §4 Theorem1** gives complete/correct/unambiguous Z_W recurrence; PRISM §2.1 gives recursive probability cancellation; existing weighted-hypergraph sampling law | The paper grammar/sampling principle is already supplied. A new generic proof is not the unresolved problem. The changed/re-expressed C++ provider, emissions, physical weights, floating calculations and randomness must be linked to it. |
| Verified modular engine and supported kernels | Verified memoDP/iterator consistency in AFP; mathlib `PMF.bindOnSupport`, finite PMF/map laws; SampCert and other exact/approximate sampler verification priors | Our Lean modules are new local formalization artifacts of known mathematics, with explicit premises. The actual root/source admission remains unfinished. No existing public CParty/SCFG2 mechanization was located in the checked snapshots; private upstream artifacts are outside this audit. |
| VPR right-padding correction | CParty supplement p.5 Eq.(vi) already specifies right length j−r; PRISM MFE already uses j−k; current PF/trace and SCFG2 instead use k−i | Reproduced source-to-theory discrepancy and a justified source-faithful correction. It is not a new algorithm/theorem; discovery/correction novelty is unestablished. |
| Input validation, source frame and source-order evidence | Existing RNA front-end validation; public SCFG2 boundary/ownership caveats; ordinary refinement/footprint and DP-order obligations | Practical engineering/admission work. The complete57-rule footprint and the21nt off-root recurrence witness are new recorded local checks, not a claim of world-first discovery or a root-law defect. |
| Expensive finite enumeration/output→classifier→SUM reference | Established finite summation, classwise algebra lifting and weighted grammar enumeration | Reference semantics/testing route, not novelty. At the pause it was designed/read but not implemented in the delivered private prototype. No all-length/efficient closure is claimed. |

Primary mathematical/implementation pointers:
- [MCF-ADP2016, Theorem4](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2016.05.032): pseudoknot-capable multiple context-free grammar theory and gADP implementation; polynomial evaluation requires a polynomially bounded algebra and the Bellman condition. This is further direct prior for grammar composition and outside-production derivation; it does not make every class-maximization query efficient.
- [ADP original framework](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scico.2003.12.005), [Ponty–Saule RNA hypergraphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3771), [RapidShapes](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2828121/).
- [SCFG2 existing common backbone and explicit non-guarantees](https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/PKProbDesign/blob/27afdd054272dbda8a74c8aad156970a44c23cd8/submodules/CParty/src/scfg2/README.md).
- [CParty §4 correctness theorem](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae748), [PRISM source paper](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.WABI.2026.30).
- [Lindon–Malek](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/12f3bd5d2b7d93eadc1bf508a0872dc2-Abstract-Conference.html), [Ryu–Wornell](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/ryu24a.html), [CITE preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05873).
- [AFP bottom-up memoDP](https://www.isa-afp.org/browser_info/current/AFP/Monad_Memo_DP/Bottom_Up_Computation.html), [mathlib supported PMF composition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474/Mathlib/Probability/ProbabilityMassFunction/Monad.lean), [SampCert](https://doi.org/10.1145/3729294).

## Closest system comparison, beyond similar names

### RapidShapes/RNAshapes: selected-class method genuinely exists

RapidShapes constructs a selected-shape thermodynamic matcher, uses the same energy evaluation as its denominator, and requires complete unambiguous recognition of that shape's structures. Its Theorem1 supplies this mathematical contract. Sampling may propose promising classes before exact computation. The residual strategy is already classical. The [actual selected-shape wrapper at pin0ad54ba](https://github.com/jlab/fold-grammars/blob/0ad54ba8665fa3fd653f253771763d1746860495/Misc/Applications/RapidShapes/tdmwrapper) accepts a shape string and sequence, compiles its matcher, and returns the class PF. None of those is a new E8 idea.

### pKiss: actual pseudoknot class-sum code, with explicit model limitations

The [pKiss build at the same pin](https://github.com/jlab/fold-grammars/blob/0ad54ba8665fa3fd653f253771763d1746860495/Misc/Applications/pKiss/makefile) combines its shape algebra with MFE and partition-function algebras. The [PF source itself](https://github.com/jlab/fold-grammars/blob/0ad54ba8665fa3fd653f253771763d1746860495/Algebras/Pfunc/alg_pknot_pfunc.gap) explicitly says canonical representatives omit search space and its pseudoknot dangles lack the correct four-way handling. The [grammar](https://github.com/jlab/fold-grammars/blob/0ad54ba8665fa3fd653f253771763d1746860495/Grammars/gra_pknot_microstate.gap) uses H/K families and several heuristic strategies. The probs build uses filtering and fast-math. Therefore disabling filtering alone does not make it an exact CParty Γ(S,G) solver. It is close reusable architecture/source, not a verified same-model drop-in.

### Current PRISM/SCFG2: many proposed connections already implemented

PRISM already samples the conditional density-2 ensemble and reports current shape frequencies. SCFG2 already provides cached inside, best derivation and fixed-target evaluation on one kernel. Its README explicitly withholds an independent re-expression unambiguity proof, complete local target-filter proof and split invariance. Those limits are already acknowledged; we should not relabel the generic questions as newly discovered open mathematics.

CParty's proof distinguishes its asymmetric VPR/VPL decomposition to preserve unambiguity. That paper argument should be reused as the reference specification. Source refinement is substantive because local factors, runtime state aliases, carriers, geometry gates and numerical operation order can differ; the reproduced VPR discrepancy is concrete evidence of this distinction.

## Source/version/issue audit and bug originality boundary

Fresh read-only GitHub GETs on 2026-10-02 returned:
- PRISM main `87a88715282d279fc361eb56de27153a321359be`, exactly the inspected pin; public all-state issue list returned zero; path history for `part_func.cc` returned41 commits on its current history.
- PKProbDesign main `27afdd054272dbda8a74c8aad156970a44c23cd8`, exactly the inspected pin; public all-state issue list returned zero; the VPR transition path has one vendoring commit (2026-07-21), no subsequent path change.
- Their recursive tree responses were nontruncated, with91 and431 entries. No Lean/Coq/Isabelle/Agda files were found in these snapshots. This is not evidence about verification elsewhere.
- The [public vendor notice](https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/PKProbDesign/blob/27afdd054272dbda8a74c8aad156970a44c23cd8/submodules/CParty/VENDORED_FROM.md) deliberately excludes the private upstream's tests and git metadata. A README-referenced energy-contract document returns404 in this public subset. Private history/artifacts were not accessed or contacted.

The k−i VPR factor is also present in the earliest returned public PF snapshot (June2025) and a May2026 sampling-fix snapshot. I did not find an explicit VPR-right-padding diagnosis in the inspected current function comments/path messages. Existing public comments instead explicitly mention a terminal Bp endpoint correction, a different VP internal-loop right-border regression, and provisional WMB/support ownership. Public fixtures record earlier positive-branch-score and union-energy failures on other named inputs: [existing fixture directory](https://github.com/TakumiOtagaki/PKProbDesign/tree/27afdd054272dbda8a74c8aad156970a44c23cd8/tests/fixtures). Their existence shows ongoing known implementation defects; it does not establish that those were caused by this VPR factor.

Thus neither an empty issue list nor the persistence of a source expression establishes world-first discovery. The justified claim is the pinned recurrence/MFE mismatch, its root-live scale-sensitive replay and isolated correction/regression evidence, already [published with exact scope](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/5daf73f247c1018fadcac18681ef986f9574bd57/research/2026-10-02-dot-e8-vpr-prism-addendum-0652z/VPR-PRISM-AND-BROADER-REGRESSION.md).

## The short true residual list

1. **Adaptive confidence interface for the actual PRISM stream.** Implement threshold-driven sampling for pairs/current frozen shapes, with discovery/selection handling and explicit stochastic-source/bias assumptions. Reuse established inference. Current fixed-N counts and seeded replay do not implement it.
2. **Selected current-class SUM for the same conditional model.** Implement or adapt the σ5/σ6 inverse-image sum using the admitted Γ(S,G), weights and denominator. RapidShapes has the selected nested-class method; pKiss has another pseudoknot model; SCFG2 currently uses MaxProduct for fixed targets. The missing PRISM connection is an application/compiler/interface task. A new efficient restriction theorem is only a possible later research candidate; its need/novelty is not established.
3. **Executable source/model/numeric/randomness binding shared by those two interfaces.** Reuse CParty correctness and PRISM telescoping specifications, then admit the actual root-reachable provider/emissions/multiplicity and physical factors, source classifier, arithmetic and randomness. Known interval/exact-bit/statistical prior does not automatically bind this C++ program. Deterministic seeded MT execution cannot be silently declared IID by a proof or a passed test.

No residual is currently certified as a new mathematical open problem. The useful next decision is whether to complete this clearly scoped adaptation/certification project; originality research should concern a precise later source-specific theorem or efficiency result, not the established generic combination.

# Independent paper Γ and source-root admission register

Owner: prior/source coding auditor, coordinated by dot. 2026-10-02. Canonical path: `UnifiedLean.Source.E8PaperGammaAdmission`.

## Exact specification and attribution

CParty sections2.1--2.3 define the biological pair-map ensemble; section4 Theorem1 already claims complete/correct/unambiguous paper recurrences. The present formal specification uses that prior, not a newly invented grammar or a source trace renamed as RNA.

- Bases are the paper's A/C/G/U. T normalization and the private prototype's explicitly unpairable N are separate front-end/model extensions, not silently admitted by this paper input type.
- A structure is a finite set of ordered position pairs. Secondary means canonical AU/UA/CG/GC/GU/UG pairs and at most one partner per position.
- The fixed scaffold is secondary and planar. Γ has an independently secondary/planar extension with no shared endpoints, a density-2 full union and no paired hard-unpaired position.
- A band is a maximal nonempty pairwise nested subset, with all-or-no crossing of each external pair and a shared external crossing neighbor. Density-2 counts bands covering a position within one connected component of the crossing graph. It is not just a two-bracket-lane criterion.
- The chosen independent physical-energy specification maps a full pair set to `Option Real`: finite energies use exp(−E/(RT)); excluded/non-finite cases have zero weight. Positive R,T are explicit. Actual source weights need only one independently proved positive root/input gauge κ times these paper weights; κ is explicitly canceled in the numerator/normalizer and is not fitted into PhysicalEnergy. This does not construct the actual DP09/Vienna parameter/loop-energy specification or prove its implementation.

The raw Γ carrier is finite independently of the source. Its positive-energy support is a separate subtype. The paper zero complement can therefore be proved and removed/reinserted in sums rather than declaring all raw paper objects positive. This closes the applicability limitation of the earlier positive-trace-to-whole-positive-codomain adapter at the mathematical interface level, once the independent energy specification and actual source contracts are supplied.

## Pinned source emission boundary

At public PKProbDesign/CParty pin27afdd054272dbda8a74c8aad156970a44c23cd8, `engine/traceback_pairs.hh::append_deduction_generated_pairs` emits only parent pairs of V, VP, VP_CLOSED, VP_DIRECT, excluding fixed scaffold pairs. The generated-pair helper treats BE output as scaffold geometry rather than new pairs. Actual root-reached BE outer/anchor pairs still need the fixed-scaffold ownership invariant; generic valid-key/same-anchor checks do not supply it. The new pure event-set function transcribes that four-family filter and unique insertion.

`SourceEvent` already contains normalized in-range Fin coordinates. An executed 1-based C++ deduction/event decoder and proof of its domain conversion are **not** supplied by defining this type. The fixed-pair predicate also needs the validated context's pair-partner relation to agree with the independent scaffold.

`api/exact.cc` builds union output from fixed G plus rendered generated pairs. `engine/traceback_render.hh` can skip endpoint collisions; same-lane bracket parsing requires noncrossing pairing. Thus unique insertion excludes repeated identical pairs only. It does not by itself establish no shared endpoint, correct brackets, density-2, unambiguous derivation or a lossless rendered pair map. These are named source gates, not claims of a newly executed failure.

## What the connected conditional binding is intended to prove

The root-admission record exposes separate geometric, support, weight and classifier statements, not the desired probability equality:

1. Decode actual finite supported root traces to the pinned parent-family/pair event stream, preserving source execution/control and total stochastic fuel.
2. Establish canonical matching, fresh endpoint ownership and planar generated pairs; establish density-2 and hard-constraint preservation for the full G union.
3. Establish exhaustive output coverage and one positive source derivation per independently energy-admitted paper output. The paper's unambiguous recurrence theorem is existing prior; the re-expressed executed source needs its own applicability proof.
4. Establish the physical local-factor/ownership/scaling product equals the independently specified paper energy weight. The preserved source-faithful VPR correction is evidence for one factor, not all factors.
5. Establish lossless rendering and the current L5/L6 classifier correspondence. The conditional class bridge permits arbitrary label types such as String.

From these obligations, the module constructs the support equivalence and transports the supported-root trace law to the complete raw-paper class numerator/normalizer, including zero paper objects via the proved complement. Root-only partition positivity is preserved. This is a conditional source/paper adapter until those actual source fields are instantiated; it does not solve numeric/RNG refinement, actual selected-class SUM software, or adaptive confidence stopping.

## Certification status

Current canonical component source `94fe4f2625e7bad19903dc37dfd5c9c91ac5ad2ab907ef54ce6f79598da9faae` PASSed24 printed standard-only endpoints in3.711s. Receipt: `receipts/UnifiedLean/Source/E8PaperGammaAdmission.json`; immutable attempt1790941926574810677. Direct imports and source stayed stable. Failed enum/Pairwise elaborations are preserved as failures, not counted as proofs. The earlier250f/11 bridge and frozen100/113/169/260 scopes remain separate. This new Γ source is frozen for its own reviewed next aggregate; it is not retroactively part of those earlier certificates. No actual C++ RootAdmission instance is constructed.

[Primary CParty](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae748). [Primary PRISM](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.WABI.2026.30). [Earlier accepted support bridge and component/113 provenance](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/5281c5cf4bf36ff391ebc097a51e70a4883db03a/research/2026-10-02-dot-e8-supported-paper-1106z/README.md).

## Specification correction and independent regression

The first strict BandCovers draft mistakenly reused ordinary base-Cover endpoints. Before any accepted/published Γ specification, the reviewer required the cited detailed definition: HFold section2.3, printed p145, defines a band crossing a position by **inclusive outer endpoints**. The source was corrected to p.left≤k≤p.right. Author-hosted primary PDF: https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~condon/papers/cmb-2007-0198.pdf; SHA256fe0a4dfbaa6c5940d24a1dd1956c7ccc20c691dd6fe1b072ca0920db796053ae. The full copyrighted PDF is retained locally for inspection and is not republished with our code/notes.

The kernel now also proves (a) that the common-neighbor BandCore formulation equals the main paper's literal member-wise crossing formulation, using nonempty/nesting/all-or-no properties, and (b) that the existential inclusive BandCovers is exactly the outermost pair's closed span, using existing Finset.exists_min_image. These are specification links, not new RNA theory. Equivalence with the supplementary maximal weakly-closed-chain representation still needs its exact bridge for that source-side use; no absent formalization is labeled a new mathematical conjecture.

The independent strongest-statement auditor's exact subset-band enumerator checks sequenceGGAAGCGCAACC, fixed zero-based pairs(0,7),(1,5), new pairs(4,11),(6,10). Both components are planar, canonical matching and fresh; spans are at least4. All four singleton bands form one bipartite crossing component. Strict integer coverage has maximum2, while inclusive coverage reaches3. The old predicate wrongly admits this density-3 geometry. The corrected one rejects it. This is an exact finite geometry regression only: no physical DP09 eligibility or positive executed-source derivation is asserted. The unchanged script and receipt are attributable to that auditor.

## Exact checked improvements and residuals

- Full-pair matching and unique extension recovery derive from secondary components and fresh endpoints.
- Independent zero-weight paper complement is proved, so the final class law covers the full raw Γ rather than silently omitting its zero objects.
- The support equivalence is constructed from coverage/unambiguous-output premises; no desired probability equality is a record field.
- Rendering losslessness is now an explicit premise USED by the classifier transport, rather than an ignored output decoration.
- One positive root/input κ suffices; absolute equality is the special caseκ=1. No per-structure gauge or energy correction is admitted.

Actual trace extraction/fuel/control, source-generated-list validity, geometry/ownership/density for every positive executed derivation, exhaustive unambiguous coverage, full physical DP09/gauge refinement, renderer/parser/current classifier, C++ arithmetic/randomness and the original selected-class SUM/adaptive-runtime interfaces remain uninstantiated obligations. The mathematical record does not solve them by being constructible in an abstract self-model.
