# Explicit two-atom relation for the repeated-bigon count bound

23 October 2026 UTC. Existing G3 owner. HAND/self-audited mathematical
supplement; UNREVIEWED and UNCOMPILED. No source, arithmetic, QE, compiler,
model, native or old-suite execution supplies acceptance for this proof.
The original all-input G3 goal remains ACTIVE/OPEN.

This makes one step of [the repeated-block count theorem](G3-REPEATED-BLOCK-ALGEBRAIC-COUNT.md)
explicit. That frozen predecessor is 13443B/SHA256
69ae2c128c73cff02cfed6e9876aa8877dad997c4418c20306afd7c4d4dcfcf1.
The use-site is four multiplicatively independent ALG target coordinates
of an unknown number of identical fresh COMMON bigons. It is not an
all-word size bound or an extension of the observation language.

## Prior and successor comparison

Complete relevant bodies were read, not merely their headings. These four
paths are at immutable Commons8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6:

- `research/2026-10-01-codex-g3-finite-recognition/COMMON-CAP-FOUR.md`,
  15058B/SHA256a0fda6976d285ede96bb0f67b0193405663758d3b0f87b00c5c24611b061aa1f,
  blob85fd78cd5de9300e20c4cfa9b0a43eca5f6fa2e0. Exact two-node compression
  for the THREE nonconstant moments at exponents1,3,6, and its bounded
  original COMMON cap-four recognizer, are OLD/REUSE.
- Its arbitrary-cap successor
  `research/2026-10-01-codex-g3-finite-recognition/ARBITRARY-CAP-BOUNDARY.md`,
  11325B/SHA256e718b8013324eb56a372639dbe0f3408741001209a6ed6e18adc43167073892c,
  blob5de3f810eed5825e1111c63694b22a7a0abe6b45, already detects an exposed
  sparse-moment boundary, uniquely recovers its atom law and bounds binary
  factors by support size minus one. Those algorithms are not reopened.
- `research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-one-retained-effective-nonattainment-1034z/ONE-BERNOULLI-QUALITATIVE-LOCALIZATION.md`,
  7777B/SHA25602fe3641345ed9d7d816947f03019157c672020ce00253d881c084e75c07cb39,
  blobfc44ee5f5375c971ed0c6ed8f37df670bdb6adb5, already uses the four
  moments1,3,6,10 to identify a two-point limit and localize one persistent
  Bernoulli factor. It explicitly supplies no effective all-word rate.
- `research/2026-10-08-codex-g3-g4-coordinated-1000z/g3-singular/PROOF-R2.md`,
  18565B/SHA25601824ddd515ea7d8d26f479eaad745689d9cba564b32f8c93904eeba5ec155f0,
  blobeeb96521e12c0bb8a465e1419a42ccad6a1732d0, supplies low-response-rank
  coupled compression using the OLD strict two-atom realization, with its
  declared whole-fibre COMMON hypotheses. It does not bound a repeated
  cell from multiplicative arithmetic of the four target moments.

The local [six-moment exposed-factorisation proof](G3-COMMON-SIX-MOMENT-EXPOSED-FACTORISATION.md)
is also reused. Its nonnegative polynomial is in the SUPPORT variable and
forces a representing measure onto finitely many roots. The polynomial
below is instead a universal relation in FOUR MOMENT COORDINATES of one
cell. It need not expose the target moment vector, and the final target of
N repeated cells need not itself have two atoms. Confusing these two
polynomials would duplicate the boundary result and invalidate this use.

Classification: explicit integration of classical moment recurrences,
resultants and the preceding radical theorem. The inspected predecessors
do not state the explicit relation/count interface below. This bounded
comparison makes no exhaustive absence or mathematical priority claim.

## One fixed polynomial, with a nonzero certificate

Let a,b be positive real supports and0<=p<=1. Put

    m_j=p*a^j+(1-p)*b^j, m_0=1,
    t=m_1, z=m_3, u=m_6, v=m_10,
    sigma=a+b, pi=a*b.

The ordinary two-atom recurrence is

    m_(j+2)=sigma*m_(j+1)-pi*m_j.

Eliminating m_2 from the j=0,1 equations gives

    z=sigma^2*t-(sigma+t)*pi.

For physical positive data sigma+t>0. In the polynomial ring
Q[sigma,t,z], define

    D=sigma+t, A=sigma^2*t-z,
    B_0=1, B_1=t,
    B_(j+2)=sigma*D*B_(j+1)-A*B_j       if j is even,
    B_(j+2)=sigma*B_(j+1)-A*B_j         if j is odd.

Substitution of pi=A/D in the moment recurrence proves, by induction,

    B_j=D^floor(j/2)*m_j.

In particular B_2=sigma*t^2+z and B_3=z*D. Define

    F_6=B_6-u*D^3,
    F_10=B_10-v*D^5,
    Q(t,z,u,v)=Res_sigma(F_6,F_10).

This is a completely specified rational polynomial: use the ordinary
18-by-18 Sylvester determinant, with degrees6 and12 in sigma. Indeed
B_4 has degree3 and B_5 degree4, each with leading coefficient z-t^3.
Induction in the displayed recurrence gives, for every j>=4,

    deg_sigma B_j=j+floor(j/2)-3,
    leading coefficient=z-t^3.

The other terms in F_6 and F_10 have sigma degrees3 and5, respectively.
Thus their generic degrees are exactly6 and12. Padding a determinant to
unnecessarily larger degrees would not be this definition.

For every positive two-atom moment tuple, its actual sigma is a common
root of F_6 and F_10. Therefore Q(t,z,u,v)=0. This remains necessary for
coincident supports and degenerate weights; no division by a-b or p is
used. Degenerate weights are not admitted as natural source permissions.

To prove Q is NONZERO, specialize the formal coefficient variables to

    (t,z,u,v)=(0,1,0,0).

This is an algebraic coefficient check, not a physical source. The same
recurrence gives

    F_6=sigma^6+3*sigma^3+1,
    F_10=sigma^12+7*sigma^9+15*sigma^6+10*sigma^3+1,
    F_10=(sigma^6+4*sigma^3+2)*F_6-1.

The specialized polynomials retain degrees6 and12 and are monic. At
each root of F_6 the second is -1. Consequently

    Q(0,1,0,0)=(-1)^6=1.

This hand identity proves nonzeroness without expanding the determinant
or running a polynomial-identity search. No assertion that Q alone
characterizes physical two-atom laws is needed or made.

A convenient loose total-degree bound is198. Assign weights1 to sigma,t,
weight3 to z,6 to u and10 to v. B_j is weighted homogeneous of weight
j+floor(j/2); F_6 and F_10 have weights9 and15. Every coefficient of
F_6 has ordinary total degree at most9, and every coefficient of F_10
at most15. Every Sylvester term takes twelve coefficients from F_6 and
six from F_10, so

    deg Q<=12*9+6*15=198.                         (1)

The bound is deliberately loose; constant sharpening is not a new queue.

## Explicit repetition bound

Supply FOUR exact positive real-algebraic numbers

    beta=(beta_1,beta_3,beta_6,beta_10)

which are multiplicatively independent over Z. The natural application
also has each beta_j in(0,1). The question here is whether there are ANY
positive real a,b and interior p, and ANY integer N>=1, with

    [p*a^j+(1-p)*b^j]^N=beta_j, j=1,3,6,10.       (2)

Both supports must be in(0,1) for the physical application.
The bound below remains necessary even before those extra inequalities.

Reuse, without reopening, the unconditional positive S-unit and primitive
lattice construction in the preceding count theorem. It returns positive
algebraic C_1,...,C_4 in one real number field K and an integer4-by-4
matrix E of rank4 such that

    beta_j=product_i C_i^E_(i,j).

The underlying S-unit coordinate lattice of the C_i is primitive. Put

    M=max_(i,j) |E_(i,j)|, H=396*M.               (3)

M>=1. This is a total computable integer from the supplied algebraic
target, including on a NO instance satisfying the rank-four premise.
No successful source search or transcendental zero oracle is assumed.

For a putative witness of count N set x_i=C_i^(1/N), choosing the positive
real roots. Then its one-cell tuple is

    (beta_j^(1/N))_j=(product_i x_i^E_(i,j))_j,

and Q vanishes there. Because E has rank4, distinct exponent vectors
alpha of Q remain distinct under alpha -> E*alpha. Thus the formal
Laurent polynomial

    Q(product_i X_i^E_(i,1),...,product_i X_i^E_(i,4))

is nonzero. By (1), every resulting exponent lies in[-198*M,198*M]
in each coordinate, so each exponent width is at most396*M. Remove a
common Laurent monomial. If N>H, all remaining exponents are in
{0,...,N-1} in every variable. The primitive-lattice radical independence
lemma of the preceding proof, applying Mordell's real-radical theorem,
says that these distinct monomials in x_1,...,x_4 are K-linearly
independent. They cannot give the nonzero Q relation. Contradiction.
Therefore EVERY witness of (2) satisfies

    N<=396*max_(i,j)|E_(i,j)|.                   (4)

The old proof provides the full elementary number-field/S-unit acquisition
and the exact source of the radical theorem. This supplement does not
rely on an uncertified class-group computation or a new PARI execution.
The primary theorem is Mordell, *On the linear independence of algebraic
numbers*, Pacific Journal of Mathematics3(1953), pp625--630:
https://msp.org/pjm/1953/3-3/pjm-v3-n3-p10-s.pdf .

The strict two-atom construction and complete fixed-N polynomial source
feasibility are OLD/REUSE. Enumerating N=1,...,H and those exact fixed-N
formulas gives terminating recognition of this supplied repeated family.
Additional original rows are tested together at the same N and ONE
physical tuple. A failed four-coordinate test rejects this family only.
If the four-coordinate rank premise fails, this supplier returns
OUT-OF-SCOPE, not NO. The more general count theorem is unchanged.

## Literal original-source interface and limits

For k current roots let lambda=binom(k,2). One fresh natural COMMON bigon
with first/parent0 probability p, original native gamma=1-p, arm survivals
x,y and an ordinary survival factor s has diagonal

    s^lambda*(p*x^lambda+(1-p)*y^lambda).

Its four k=2,3,4,5 coordinates are exactly the two-atom moments above,
with supports a=s*x,b=s*y. N repetitions use DISTINCT original private
IDs and independent cell bits; assigning the same numeric p does not
reuse one exposed register. Routing acts on current opaque roots, not
their old leaves. The four algebraic target values must be actually
supplied or licensed-decoded by the original caller. Choosing one latent
kernel from an unconstrained joint-response fibre does not qualify.

If otherwise identical cells have different ordinary connector factors,
their total product A can be absorbed for this DIAGONAL calculation as
supports a=A^(1/N)*x,b=A^(1/N)*y. This neither reorders the full forest
program nor freezes the exterior; fixed-N feasibility must retain its
actual chronology, connectors, parent order, register and all rows.
An unknown additional stochastic head/correction cannot be absorbed as
an ordinary factor and invalidates equation(2) for the whole target.

The COMMON coordinates can bound a supplied BOTH family too, but do not
independently fit its I parameters. A pure I input without a licensed
COMMON diagonal does not meet this supplier. Rank>=5 in an arbitrary
six-coordinate signature does NOT ensure rank4 of this particular
four-coordinate subtuple. The original general theorem remains available
where its actual rank/dimension hypotheses are acquired.

Nonvacuity is OLD arithmetic from the preceding proof, not a new run:
p=x=s=1/2,y=1/3 gives moments

    C_lambda=(3^lambda+2^lambda)/(2^(2*lambda+1)*3^lambda).

At lambda1,3,6,10 the numerator primes introduce, in order,5,7,13 and
a prime divisor of4621 (60073=13*4621). None of the latter primes occurs
earlier. These four rational numbers are multiplicatively independent;
every positive power preserves that property. This does not prove that
the displayed repetition count is a minimum among all source types.

No unbounded synchronization constraint is added to the original input
language. Repeated numeric cells are a restricted mathematical source
family; original arbitrary words may use different parameters at every
fresh position. No count bound for those heterogeneous words, no
whole-fibre choice, no Phi-zero decision, no all-core NO certificate and
no master H(D) follows. Those are the exact remaining original G3 gates.

## Verification boundary

The recurrence, generic degrees, specialized Euclidean identity and
degree/count inequalities were checked by hand in this derivation.
There was no determinant expansion, numerical test, fresh source tuple,
RCF/number-field run, old control replay or proof-assistant pass.
Read/hash custody is separate from mathematical acceptance. The four
inspected predecessor/successor statements are reused at their original
scope; no absent grep match is used as proof of prior absence.

# The entire homogeneous five-log matrix-rank route is already compatible

Existing G3 owner,22October2026UTC. HAND/UNREVIEWED/UNCOMPILED.
This is a uniform proof-method screen, not an arithmetic zero test or original
G3 completion. It uses an existing operator-scaling theorem. Historical
novelty is unassessed. No physical source, native build or model job is used.

## Actual predecessor and later-source comparison

The exact question is whether ANY finite rational-linear homogeneous pencil
in the original FIVE logarithms can contradict the proved strict
Waldschmidt--Masser rectangle conclusion on the putative transcendental-node
pure branch. Matrix sizes and ranks are unrestricted.

The COMPLETE7October RANK-FIVE-RECTANGLE-SCREEN.md and its complete independent
review were read at Commons9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1,
research/2026-10-07-dot-g3-singular-route-screen-2340z. The proof's SHA256 is
e244ce30090b428731e4d344948fbc11fe7f08600cde97c06a06744faddcb41d.
It already supplies the distinct pair sums and the direct rank-one screen.
Those are REUSED, not newly discovered.

The later COMPLETE METHOD-ADMISSION-UNREVIEWED.md was reread at Commons

research/2026-10-22-dot-g3-transcendence-admission-0557z,
SHA2566eaf35d5af52cf7b86b0e24d02c32bd3d999a6c24d2080f091ca42f37bddee13,
Gitblobc8955fb76337bc8e9783464aa0f28499e0306f7e. It explicitly leaves
all-five higher-rank pencils open. Its last requested simultaneous-block
certificate is stronger than excluding rational blocks.

The existing local rank-three screen3192d7a8... and Roy three-coordinate
all-size application73d09ac2... do not settle this whole-five-coordinate,
all-rank claim. The single-coefficient cutoff207b6381... addresses a different,
weaker conclusion. The precise additional implication below removes the
remaining homogeneous higher-rank pencil search all at once. A bounded
source search found no operator-scaling argument in the selected retained
G3 Markdown scope; this is not an exhaustive absence or novelty certificate.

A follow-up primary-source comparison also read Lakhani--Mukhopadhyay,
[Approximating commutative rank of matrix spaces in NC](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/185/download/),
15September2026, Theorem3.2 and COMPLETE Lemma3.3/Claim3.4 proof on
printedpages11--13, together with its introductory interface. Operator
scaling plus fourth-moment rank extraction is therefore explicitly REUSED
methodology. Their selected statement uses sign families in square matrix
spaces; it does not state this fixed polynomial-curve degeneration, its
rectangular bound or this G3 conclusion. The comparison was made after the
initial candidate, before freezing this record. No general method novelty
or review of their entire29-page algorithm is claimed.

## A general polynomial-pencil statement

Let f_1,...,f_k be nonzero complex polynomials with nonzero leading
coefficients c_i and distinct nonnegative degrees d_i. Suppose their
UNORDERED pair sums, including repeated indices, are all distinct:

    d_i+d_j=d_h+d_l implies {i,j}={h,l}.                 (S)

For arbitrary complex m-by-n matrices A_i, put

    B(t)=sum_i f_i(t) A_i,
    r=rank over C(t) of B(t), q=min(m,n).

Assume there are NO complex subspaces U subset C^m and V subset C^n,
with dimensions a,b, annihilating every coefficient matrix and satisfying

    u^T A_i v=0 for every i,u in U,v in V,
    a/m+b/n>1.                                         (Z)

Then

    r >= mn/[m+n-max(m,n)/k] > mn/(m+n).                (R)

In particular, every pencil of rank <=mn/(m+n) on this polynomial curve
already has a simultaneous complex block (Z). If the A_i are rational,
such a block can be chosen rational; the descent is proved below.

## The reused rectangular scaling supplier

Use Cole Franks, [Operator Scaling with Specified Marginals](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~wcf17/images/site_OSWSM_arxiv_ver3.pdf),
Definition3.11 and Theorem3.8, printedpages10--12 in the inspected85-page
author-hosted version. Definitions3.1--3.3, scalar flags and the theorem's
normalization were also read. This imports approximate rectangular scaling,
not its algorithm, runtime or an executed scaling.

Applied to T(X)=sum_i A_i X A_i^*, with target marginals

    Q=I_m, P=(m/n)I_n,

its subspace condition is exactly

    dim(sum_i A_i V) >= (m/n) dim V for all V subset C^n. (H)

Indeed a maximal annihilating row space has dimension
m-dim(sum_i A_i V), so failure of(H) is precisely(Z).
Both target operators are scalar, their flags have only the zero/full
subspaces, and the permitted scaling groups are the full general-linear
groups. Hence Theorem3.8 gives, for every eta>0, invertible L,R such that

    sum_i (L A_i R)(L A_i R)^* is eta-close to I_m,
    sum_i (L A_i R)^*(L A_i R) is eta-close to (m/n)I_n. (B)

Multiplying the individual A_i by ANY nonzero scalars leaves every image
sum and every simultaneous zero block unchanged. Thus(H), and the same
approximate-scaling conclusion, hold after those individual multiplications.

## Passing to the leading monomials without losing the rank bound

Let N tend to infinity through positive integers. Apply(B) to the tuple
c_i N^(d_i) A_i, with accuracy eta_N tending to zero. Choose the resulting
invertible L_N,R_N and set

    C_i,N=c_i N^(d_i) L_N A_i R_N.

The first balance in(B) bounds every C_i,N in Frobenius norm. A subsequence
therefore converges simultaneously to matrices C_i. Both marginal limits are

    sum_i C_i C_i^*=I_m,
    sum_i C_i^* C_i=(m/n)I_n.                            (L)

For |z|=1,

    L_N B(Nz) R_N
        =sum_i [f_i(Nz)/(c_i N^(d_i))] C_i,N
        -> C(z):=sum_i z^(d_i) C_i

uniformly. The bracket tends uniformly to z^(d_i). Importantly, no bound on
L_N or R_N is assumed: the bounded C_i,N absorb their possible growth.
For constant f_i the bracket is exactly1. All(r+1)-minors of B vanish as
polynomial identities, so each matrix on the left has rank<=r. Closedness
of that rank condition gives rank C(z)<=r for every point on the unit circle.

This is an algebraic proof on complex t, not a physical extension of an
original calendar or of the promised real node interval.

## Exact trace calculation and the uniform rank bound

Average over the unit circle and let

    s(z)=Tr C(z)C(z)^*,
    w(z)=Tr[(C(z)C(z)^*)^2],
    D=sum_i Tr[(C_i C_i^*)^2].

Distinct degrees and(L) give E s=m. In the expansion of E w, a term survives
exactly when d_i+d_h=d_j+d_l. By(S), only the two pairings survive; their
intersection, where all four indices agree, must be subtracted once. Thus

    E w=Tr[(sum_i C_i C_i^*)^2]
         +Tr[(sum_i C_i^* C_i)^2]-D
       =m+m^2/n-D.                                     (T)

There is no assumption that the ORIGINAL f_i(t) already have these phase
moments. The preceding balanced degeneration is necessary.

Every C_i has rank<=q. With t_i=Tr C_i C_i^*, Cauchy--Schwarz twice gives

    D >= (1/q)sum_i t_i^2 >= m^2/(kq),

since sum_i t_i=m. Pointwise positivity and rank C(z)<=r give s(z)^2<=r w(z).
Integrating and using E s^2>=(E s)^2 yields

    m^2 <= r[m+m^2/n-D]
        <= r[m+m^2/n-m^2/(kq)].

The latter denominator is positive in the nonzero balanced setting. Rearranging
is(R), because mn/q=max(m,n). Its strict comparison with mn/(m+n) follows
from max(m,n)/k>0. For square size s and k=5, this even gives r>=5s/9.
No matrix-size search, determinant enumeration or source-length cutoff occurs.

## Rational descent of the whole weighted block

Now suppose all A_i have rational entries. A complex violating subspace V
in(H) exists if and only if an algebraic one exists: after fixing dim V and
dim(sum_i A_i V), full-rank basis/minor conditions are a constructible
nonempty system over Q. Existence over C implies existence over Qbar.

For Qbar-subspaces V put

    F(V)=m dim V-n dim(sum_i A_i V),
    delta=max_V F(V).

If a violating subspace exists, delta>0. This integer maximum exists since
the dimensions are bounded. The function F is supermodular:

    F(V+W)+F(V intersect W) >= F(V)+F(W).

Here image sums commute with V+W, and the image of an intersection is
contained in the intersection of the images. Consequently the sum AND
intersection of two delta-maximizers are delta-maximizers. There is a unique
maximizer V_* of largest dimension: otherwise their sum would be larger.

Every automorphism of Qbar over Q preserves this maximization problem,
so fixes V_*. Its unique reduced-row-echelon basis is then fixed entrywise,
and all its algebraic entries belong to Q. Thus V_* is defined over Q.
Its image sum is rational too. Choose its rational annihilator as U.
Then, with b=dim V_* and a=m-dim(sum_i A_i V_*),

    a/m+b/n-1=delta/(mn)>0.

This is the required rational simultaneous rectangle. Extending rational
bases produces invertible rational row/column changes. The argument descends
the FULL weighted block; it does not mistakenly infer rational vectors from
an arbitrary nonempty projective variety.

## Application to the actual five-log arithmetic route

Reuse

    f_i=T_i, i=3,6,10,15,21,
    T_i(t)=sum_(h=0)^(i-2) (i-1-h)t^h.

They are monic, with degrees1,4,8,13,19. The retained fifteen unordered sums
are2,5,9,14,20,8,12,17,23,16,21,27,26,32,38, all distinct. Therefore(S) holds.

For ANY rational coefficient pencil M(X)=sum_i X_i A_i, let
M_T(t)=sum_i T_i(t)A_i. If r_0 is transcendental, evaluation preserves ranks
of rational polynomial matrices. On the putative pure branch
ell_i=a T_i(r_0), a!=0, the actual logarithm matrix is a M_T(r_0).

Whenever its rank satisfies the strict Waldschmidt--Masser threshold, the
proof above ALREADY supplies that theorem's rational simultaneous zero block
in the coefficient pencil. No logarithm or arithmetic theorem was needed to
produce it. It is therefore impossible to contradict the pure branch using
ANY homogeneous rational-linear five-log pencil at ANY size/rank in this way.
In particular, the three-condition simultaneous certificate requested by the
later source cannot exist, even with its stronger real-block exclusion.

## Changed frontier and verification scope

Remove the ENTIRE homogeneous five-log strict-rectangle construction from the
queue, including all ranks>=4. This supersedes the partial rank/size screens
at this receiver without invalidating their proofs or finite evidence.
There is no further quartic/quintic/higher-degree producer to run for it.

The general operator-scaling result, circle orthogonality and trace inequality
are reused mathematics. This source-specific synthesis is a new HAND argument
in this workspace, not independently reviewed, formally checked or attributed
historical novelty. A finite transcription control, if run, checks the trace
bookkeeping only; it cannot accept the universal degeneration/descent proof.

This result does NOT exclude the rank-five algebraic-input pure branch. It
shows why this entire admitted matrix method is consistent with that branch.
Affine constants, additional separately justified logarithms and nonlinear
entries are outside its contract. No conjectural Matrix Coefficient or
Structural Rank statement is used. Original G3 still needs a total one-witness
bound or complete unrestricted NO mechanism, preserving every original mode,
source/menu/ID/calendar/register/readout. That endpoint remains OPEN.

## Actual bounded transcription control

check_five_log_all_rank_trace.py, unchanged SHA256
0c2b6b0bbaa250d4554a737ee1c13b90cdbb1cb714b3399f5891f0702b523815,
actually PASSED once, exit0. It checks all625 four-index phase monomials,
the45 surviving terms and their COMPLETE noncommuting cyclic-trace
coefficients against(T), plus an independent scalar Laurent integral5071.
The non-Sidon degree list0,1,2,3,4 correctly FAILS that two-pairing identity.
All9 polynomial2-by-2 minors of its3-by-3 Hankel matrix t^(i+j) vanish,
while its t^2 coefficient is invertible with determinant-1. Thus rank1
and no shrinking subspace coexist in that negative example; dropping(S)
would make the claimed general statement false.

Complete result and both source hashes were encrypted before first

That record binds the proof BEFORE this attribution/evidence addition,

# Finite format cutoff for the five-log Matrix Coefficient route

Existing G3 owner,22October2026UTC. HAND/UNREVIEWED/UNCOMPILED.
This is a uniform screen of one arithmetic proof method, using retained
independence and classical linear/projective algebra. It is not a G3
recognizer, a physical word-length bound or a new transcendence theorem.

## Prior comparison and scope

The closest retained boundary is G3-LOG-MATRIX-RANK-BOUNDARY.md,
SHA25615d070bb81f52d3e6951fa0f011e911dabdc219c71c251d351dc3ac08d7b647a.
Its actual theorem/field clauses and low-rank proof were reread. It already
distinguishes Matrix Coefficient conjectures from the proved strict
Waldschmidt--Masser rectangle theorem. G3-SPARSE-LOG-ROUTE.md,
SHA2566c6378ce83e0116a424c825cae82ac436e17f1ff1147f325805efea959bb7d9b,
already supplies independence of homogeneous degrees1,2,3; no old finite
producer is rerun. The rank-three successor3192d7a8698d0623ba72c78beabadfe0d3dd0f16519128ae73393976e63bbc4a
screens the stronger RECTANGLE receiver at that rank, not the claim below.

The later Commons8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6 source
research/2026-10-22-dot-g3-transcendence-admission-0557z/METHOD-ADMISSION-UNREVIEWED.md,
SHA2566eaf35d5af52cf7b86b0e24d02c32bd3d999a6c24d2080f091ca42f37bddee13,
still requests an all-five-log contradictory pencil for the PROVED
rectangle theorem. This note does not answer or supersede that request.

The primary [Dasgupta--Kakde2024v1 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08178v1),
Conjectures1.2/2.3, Theorem2.2 and sections4--7 were actually inspected.
Its single-coefficient implication is conjectural; its proposed proof
retains an explicitly open auxiliary-polynomial step. We do not invoke
either conjecture as a theorem. Theorem2.2 is an unconditional linear
algebra supplier: a singular matrix subspace over an infinite field
has a common nonzero left/right pair annihilating every member.

The precise additional claim here is: arbitrary matrix order is unnecessary
for trying to CONTRADICT those single-coefficient conclusions using only
homogeneous recombinations of the original five logs. This is a stronger
uniform method screen, not a newly solved original G3 subproblem.

## Contract

Put k=Qbar. On the putative pure transcendental-node branch write

    ell_i=a*T_i(r), a!=0, r transcendental,
    i in {3,6,10,15,21},
    T_i(t)=sum_(h=0)^(i-2) (i-1-h)*t^h.

For an arbitrary matrix order s>=1 take rational s-by-s coefficient
matrices A_i and set

    M(X)=sum_i X_i*A_i,   M(ell)=a*M(T(r)),
    E_F=span_F(A_i), for F=Q or k.

The Matrix Coefficient conclusions seek nonzero u,v in F^s with
u^T*M(ell)*v=0. Because the T_i(r) are k-linearly independent, this
condition is equivalent to the coefficient-wise relations

    u^T*A_i*v=0 for EVERY i.                            (Z)

Thus an already present pair (Z) satisfies the proposed conclusion
identically, before substituting the logarithms. Zero/dependent coefficient
matrices only reduce dim E_F, which is at most5.

## Orders at most three

Suppose s<=3 and det M(ell)=0. Dividing by a^s gives
det M(T(r))=0. The determinant is a homogeneous polynomial of degree s
in five variables. The RETAINED degree-s independence forces

    det M(X)=0 identically.

Every member of E_Q is therefore singular. Apply the unconditional
Theorem2.2 over Q to obtain nonzero rational u,v satisfying (Z).
The zero-space/order-one cases are included. No conjecture or search
for a transcendental input is needed.

## Every order at least six: rational conclusion is automatic

Fix any nonzero rational v, for instance the first coordinate vector.
The at most five vectors A_i*v span a rational subspace of dimension<=5.
For s>=6 its orthogonal complement contains a nonzero rational u.
This is exactly (Z). This argument applies even when M(ell) is invertible.

Consequently a contradictory homogeneous RATIONAL Matrix Coefficient
construction can only have matrix order4 or5. There is no larger-order
ladder to run for this conclusion.

This is a finite FORMAT cutoff, not a finite enumeration of rational
coefficient choices or a decidability result for the two remaining orders.
No contradictory order4/5 pencil is constructed or asserted to exist;
the arithmetic conjecture itself remains unproved.

## Algebraic-coefficient conclusion: every remaining order is automatic

For s>=4, consider the Segre variety of rank-one matrices

    Sigma=P^(s-1)(k) times P^(s-1)(k)
           embedded in P^(s*s-1)(k).

Its dimension is2s-2. The equations u^T*A_i*v=0 are at most five
hyperplane sections in this embedding. The projective dimension theorem
over algebraically closed k implies their common intersection with Sigma
has dimension at least

    2s-2-dim(E_k) >= 2s-7 >=1.

In particular it is nonempty. A k-point of Sigma is a nonzero rank-one
outer product, giving nonzero algebraic vectors u,v satisfying (Z).
Again, no singularity of M(ell) is used in this range.

Together with the s<=3 argument, this proves that the entire algebraic-
coefficient Matrix Coefficient conclusion is ALREADY satisfied by every
singular homogeneous five-log pencil on this branch, of every order.
It cannot deliver the required contradiction in this class.

This dimension argument supplies ALGEBRAIC vectors. It does not turn them
into rational vectors at orders4/5. A nonempty projective variety defined
over Q need not have a rational point. Confusing these fields would erase
the exact remaining distinction.

## Changed frontier

Remove all orders>=6 from the rational single-coefficient route, and remove
the entire algebraic single-coefficient route in this homogeneous five-log
class. No new size search, old checker replay or solver execution is needed.

The PROVED Waldschmidt--Masser theorem demands a MUCH LARGER zero rectangle.
One pair (Z) does not supply that rectangle. Therefore this note does not
exclude all-five-log higher-rank attempts at that different receiver.
Affine constants, additional justified logarithms and nonlinear entries
are also outside the present contract.

The matrix order s is not a root cap, Taylor order, source word length,
unknown graph size, or input-derived H(p). The original exact equality,
all-mode source coverage and all-input terminating NO remain OPEN. No
formal acceptance, arithmetic decision, original source instance or master
completion is inferred from this hand screen.

# A fixed-source quintet observation decodes the full paired cap-three tuple

Authored2026-10-22UTC by the existing G3 owner. New HAND source/readout
specialization with exact rational interpolation and captured-source controls.
It is not an existing Lean declaration, a checked marked-current-root map or
an original all-source G3 NO. No original Source/compiler/native/model suite
was rerun for this recovery.

## The exact original source fibre and authorized observations

Use the five-taxon original caterpillar

    R->e, R->D, D->d, D->C, C->c, C->B, B->a, B->b.

All finite edges OUTSIDE D->C have survival1/2. There are no original hybrid
actuators. Sample ONE copy from each taxon, numbered0=a,1=b,2=c,3=d,4=e by
the retained compiler. Replace ONLY the eligible three-descendant bridge
D->C by an arbitrary finite fresh natural private word with strict arms,
positive ordinary bookends/connectors and free rates. Keep outside original
IDs/rates/calendar and original taxon labels fixed. One shared physical word
supplies COMMON and INDEPENDENT. Fresh bits are unexposed, distinct per site
and retained correctly within their own original registers.

The observation is the FULL unrooted five-copy topology, or its following
two event probabilities. It is not five separate quartet marginals. Define

    a = probability of the quintet with cherries {0,1} and {3,4},
    b = probability of the quintet with cherries {0,1} and {2,4}.

Equivalently each event can be specified by the simultaneous five quartet
splits of the SAME original genealogy. The coordinate order of the quadruples
is0123,0124,0134,0234,1234. Event a has signatures

    01|23, 01|24, 01|34, 02|34, 12|34,

and event b has signatures

    01|23, 01|24, 01|34, 03|24, 13|24.

computed merely from the individual quartet marginals. No new original

has no other hybrid and every outside program/readout is the same. Thus
two declared quintet events per mode recover (C,D,Q,R), without observing
the private forest, knowing the original private count or granting a hidden
statistic as an input. The original distinction between marginal and joint

## Why the response is affine for every private length

The lower fixed original program supplies an entering forest with at most

An affine map on these three coordinates is fixed by three linearly

# Removing the word-length quantifier for one-copy four-taxon quartet rows

Authored2026-10-22UTC. HAND conditional corollary using the inherited complete

This is an original-observation fragment, not the full G3 endpoint. No native

## Exact observation restriction

There are exactly four sampled taxa, one copy of each in every relevant row.
Each row observes the unrooted quartet of one original genealogy, or a finite
declared coarsening of it. Rows may use COMMON/INDEPENDENT mechanisms and finite

implies that each bridge's descendant side is proper, so it contains at most

## Three-descendant words are invisible to this precise readout

Let the descendant side be `a,b,c`, with only `d` outside. Condition on the
actual prefix forest and every retained original register value. If one or

register fixed; the private bits are fresh/unobserved. Inside pair or full
mergers also select the three possible inside cherries symmetrically. Thus

# G3: exact boundary of a broader logarithm-matrix route

Authored22October2026UTC in the existing G3 workspace. HAND proofs below;
the finite quartic calculation has its own actual verification. No original
G3 completion, theorem-of-absence, new model run or Lean acceptance is claimed.
No local Git action occurred.

## The controlling original implication

The complete inherited [three-log purity reduction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-three-log-purity-1210z/THREE-LOG-PURITY-REDUCTION.md)
was reread, not inferred from its title. Its Git blob is
6f6c389d223e5056738a6c3c8399ecaa62eebdac. Under its FULL five-coordinate
cone promise, purity is the original all-source COMMON **NO** branch and
nonpurity is the finite-source YES branch. Thus algebraicity of a parameter
in a fixed finite physical YES chart does not prove that a pure node must
be algebraic: that argument would put a physical witness in the NO branch.

Write n in {3,6,10,15,21}, ell_n=log(b_n), with the stated positive algebraic
inputs and promise. The surviving putative pure branch has

    ell_n=a*T_n(r), a>0,
    T_n(t)=sum[k=0..n-2] (n-1-k)*t^k,

where r is in the promised compact interval. The inherited exact polynomial
in three logarithms vanishes precisely on the promised pure branch. Positive
distance can be semidecided by approximations; an exact-zero procedure has
not been supplied. The transcendental-r, five-independent-log branch remains
unexhibited and unexcluded here.

This note concerns that arithmetic gate. It does not replace actual source
reflection, all-input attainment or unrestricted NO coverage by a log-curve
membership declaration.

## What the broader theorem actually requires

For an m-by-n matrix of logarithms of algebraic numbers, the
Waldschmidt–Masser theorem in [Dasgupta, Theorem1.6 and Section5.1](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~dasgupta/papers/Baker.pdf)
uses the strict bound rank(M)<mn/(m+n). Its conclusion is a zero rectangle
after invertible RATIONAL row and column operations, with dimensions m',n'
satisfying m'/m+n'/n>1. A singular square matrix need not meet that bound.
The same source's structural-rank statement is a conjecture; its arbitrary
affine determinantal representation lemma does not make it a proved rank
comparison. Only the named introduction/Sections4.3/5.1 were reviewed,
not the entire45-page paper.

The [Dasgupta–Kakde2024v1 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.08178v1)
distinguishes its Matrix Coefficient Conjecture from proved implications;
its two-by-two case includes the four-exponentials conjecture. This review
does not promote the stronger rank criterion or an unfinished implication
in that version into a G3 proof, or claim a complete2026 literature survey.

The matrices screened below have entries in the RATIONAL linear span of
the five ell_n. Such entries are again real logarithms of positive algebraic
numbers. No additional auxiliary logarithm or constant1 is introduced.

## New lemma: every rank-at-most-two attempt already has the rectangle

Let X=(X_1,...,X_5), let L(X) be any m-by-n matrix of homogeneous rational
linear forms, and suppose r is transcendental. Set T=(T_3,...,T_21).
The earlier finite certificate (owner-retained reference: `check_log_curve.py`) proves that homogeneous
monomials of degrees1,2,3 in T are independent over Qbar. It is reused here;
those degrees were not recomputed.

**Claim.** If s=rank L(T(r))<=2, then the generic rank of L(X) is s.

Every (s+1)-minor vanishes at T(r). Transcendence first makes its substitution
in T(t) a polynomial identity; degree-(s+1) independence then makes that
minor the zero polynomial in X. Conversely, an s-minor nonzero after
substitution is nonzero before substitution. This proves the claim, including
the zero-rank case.

Choose x0 in Q^5 with rank L(x0)=s; such a point exists because a nonzero
rational minor cannot vanish on all Q^5. Rational row/column operations put
L(x0) in rank normal form diag(I_s,0). For every y in Q^5, every (s+1)-minor
of L(x0)+h*L(y) is identically zero. The minor on the first s pivot rows/
columns and one additional row/column has linear h-coefficient equal to the
corresponding entry of L(y)'s bottom-right block. Hence that entire
(m-s)-by-(n-s) block is identically zero for every y, and therefore for L(X).

If the strict Waldschmidt–Masser bound holds, this rectangle has

    (m-s)/m+(n-s)/n = 2-s*(1/m+1/n)>1.

It already exists in the rational coefficient pencil. Applying the theorem
to a*L(T(r)) therefore returns a relation which is true identically before
any logarithm is inserted. It supplies no contradiction to this putative
pure branch. This screens ALL homogeneous rational-linear matrix sizes of
rank0,1,2, not just the previously screened rank-one two-by-three shape.
It does not screen higher rank, affine constants or auxiliary logarithms.

## New width bound and the entire four-row rank-three case

Let V be any k-dimensional rational subspace of Q(t), and let B(t) be an
m-by-n matrix with entries in V and rank<m. Suppose

    n>(k-1)*(m-1).                                      (1)

Then B already has a rationally transformed zero rectangle of the strict
Waldschmidt–Masser size. This assertion is elementary and does not use a
transcendence theorem.

Choose a nonzero left null vector f in Q(t)^m and let d be the dimension of
the rational span of its components. A constant rational row change puts
this null relation in the first d rows, with independent coefficients
f_1,...,f_d and zero coefficients on the remaining rows. Let F be their
span. The projection of each column onto these d rows lies in the kernel of

    V^d -> Q(t), (v_i) -> sum_i f_i*v_i.

The image is F*V and has dimension at least d+k-1. To see this without a
product-space theorem, clear denominators and choose bases of F,V with
distinct polynomial degrees. Their product degrees contain the sum of the
two degree sets, which has at least d+k-1 distinct integers. Corresponding
products are independent. Thus this kernel has dimension at most
(k-1)*(d-1).

A rational column change therefore kills the first d rows on at least
n-(k-1)*(d-1) columns. The resulting rectangle satisfies

    d/m + [n-(k-1)*(d-1)]/n > 1,

because (1) implies n>(k-1)*m*(d-1)/d for every1<=d<=m. All these are
identically zero rational functions, so specialization at transcendental r
and multiplication by the same nonzero a preserve them.

For our k=5, a genuinely new matrix route must therefore have both

    n<=4*(m-1), m<=4*(n-1).                            (2)

For m=4 and rank3, the strict arithmetic threshold requires n>12, whereas
(2) requires n<=12. Thus **every four-row rank-three attempt** is also
already explained by an identically zero rational rectangle. The transpose
is included. The first shapes not screened by these lemmas include5-by-8
and6-by-7 of rank3; the first square is7-by-7. This is a narrowed next target,
not a constructed matrix, a proof that one exists, or an exclusion of all
higher-rank constructions.

## Exact new quartic calculation

The70 homogeneous quartic monomials in T give a77-by-70 integer coefficient
matrix. Unlike degrees1–3, its exact rank is61 and its kernel dimension is9.
The earlier modular deficiencies alone did not establish this.

check_log_curve_quartics.py (owner-retained reference: `check_log_curve_quartics.py`) reuses the original
polynomial constructor and computes an integer kernel by fraction-free
elimination and rational back-substitution. It verifies all9 vectors against
the ORIGINAL matrix. Distinct nonzero free coordinates prove their
independence. A61-by-61 minor has determinant956015 modulo the previously
certified prime1000003, giving the complementary rank lower bound. These
certificates prove the exact rank and remain valid over Qbar.

Actual phone execution passed in under a second. Complete basis, row/column
indices, source/dependency hashes and result are encrypted at

    [owner-local path omitted]
    ciphertext SHA256 4dca0fc393a48a560740854f43f436d4f2142ca3df3bd0d485428197608adf67.

A separate Wolfram exact-kernel calculation returned the same rank/nullity
and zero products. Its formatted long basis was elided by that interface;
it is not advertised as a complete exported basis. The complete phone
certificate is the reproducible record above. The first phone revision
failed when an empty sum became a float; Fraction(0) fixes that denominator
collection. The failed source/reproduced traceback and received Wolfram
response are retained, encrypted:

    [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]
    ciphertext SHA256 1a2cef609f000ef5a59374ccbc43da6f7fd549764208d1f15c1039cf6a9dd52e.

The degree4–6 modular lower-bound exploration is retained separately as
[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]/ciphertext
6cef55ad643ae77bb58f87b3318788ffd3df6d994a920096c4e00a9a623db405.
No exact degree5/6 rank or complete defining ideal is claimed. In particular,
the9 quartics do not themselves construct a rank-three matrix satisfying
the strict theorem, or justify algebraic independence of the logarithms.

## Remaining implication and bounded next action

The exact promised zero test is still missing. A broader matrix attack would
now need an ACTUAL rational-linear matrix of rank at least3, satisfying the
strict bound and violating its rational-zero-rectangle conclusion; the
smallest eligible shapes above would need new quartic-level structure.
The two lemmas remove large families of futile candidates. They do not
turn the stronger structural-rank conjecture into an available theorem.

Keep this arithmetic branch separate from the useful original-source work:
actual whole unused-bank/prefix independence, full current-root grafting and
finite fixed-fibre consumers do not decide this global COMMON gate. General
G3 remains ACTIVE and OPEN; the next work must supply a real arithmetic or
all-input source/NO mechanism rather than repeat a failed rank-one screen.

Primary-source review/source packets were encrypted before persistence in
records19888/19892/19903, exact basenames and ciphertext hashes in the current
continuation index. No private record was uploaded. All source/native-writer,
held/consumed-job, no-subagent and no-local-Git boundaries remain.

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# Rational-power preprocessing and the polylogarithm height condition

22 October 2026. Authored HAND deduction, self-audited, UNREVIEWED/UNCOMPILED.
No mathematical program, source producer, solver or proof assistant was run.
Historical novelty is unassessed. Original all-input G3 remains OPEN.

The candidate use is arithmetic: preserve a homogeneous polynomial equality
in actual logarithms while raising the supplied algebraic numbers to rational
powers. For the old degree-eight Phi, common q!=0 gives Phi(qL)=q^8 Phi(L).
This does not require a physical source power/root construction.

## Provider and precise delta from the prior screen

Use Kawashima, *Linear independence of periods related to polylogarithms*,
[arXiv2605.17756v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17756v1), Section2, normalized
places/heights and equation(1), Theorem2.2 and Corollary2.3. These are the
already inspected primary results. The old G3 admission screen correctly
leaves V_v(alpha,beta)>0 unacquired and warns that roots change fields/heights.
It supplies no universal root or power normalization.

The added statement here is an explicit failure theorem for ALL nonzero
rational-power choices on prime-power logarithms, allowing ANY containing
number field, common denominator and matching Archimedean place. This is a
criterion-applicability result, not a zero test or a negative source verdict.
The separate physical integer-power/root-descent notes retain their own scope.

The closest retained admission is G3-PRIOR-SOLUTION-AUDIT-HISTORY-20261022-R4.md,
23137B/SHA256aeb691e42268b95fa22fb4996b3b6bc77a56d1271fbcc8adada4a65a95b09116,
and its current successor G3-PRIOR-SOLUTION-AUDIT.md. The relevant actual
admission passages and the primary definitions were read. A bounded search
of the own notes and selected Commons research/handoff Markdown found no
stronger supplied preprocessing result; that search is not absence/novelty
evidence. No old provider is rederived as a new result.

## 1. A bound independent of denominator choices

Use positive integers m,R and write

    M=(m+1)^R-1,
    C=M log2 + R(R+1)log(m+1)/2 + R + RM.

In the provider's notation put

    b=h_v(beta), a=h_v(alpha),
    rho=max_i |alpha_i/beta|_v,  0<rho<1.

Its exact height quantity is

    V=(M+1)b-a-M[h(beta)+mean_i h(alpha_i)+h(alpha)]-C.

All global heights are nonnegative, h(beta)>=b and h(alpha)>=a. Hence

    V <= b-(M+1)a-C <= b-a-C <= -log(rho)-C.          (1)

For the last inequality let t=log|beta|_v and u=log(rho)<0. The local-height
definitions give b=max(0,t) and a=max(0,t+u), so b-a<=-u. This also handles
|beta|_v<=1; no extra magnitude assumption was inserted.

Thus representing the same ratios by another common denominator or larger
field cannot evade the necessary upper bound (1).

## 2. Normalized local degree for a rational prime power

Let p>=2 be a rational prime, q=A/B!=0 in lowest terms, B>=1, and let the
chosen Archimedean embedding identify t=p^q with its POSITIVE real value.
Suppose t belongs to a number field K of degree d. Put kappa=d_v/d.

Then

    kappa <= 1/B.                                   (2)

Indeed Bezout gives integers u,w with uA+wB=1, so t^u p^w=p^(1/B).
Consequently Q(t)=Q(p^(1/B)), whose degree is B by Eisenstein for X^B-p.
At a real place d_v=1 and d>=B. At a complex place the chosen embedded K
contains this real degree-B field but is not contained in R. Its extension
over that field has degree at least two, so d>=2B and d_v=2 gives (2) again.
This covers additional algebraic parameters and nonreal denominator choices.

## 3. Real closeness is offset by (2)

For every integer B>=1,

    1-2^(-1/B) >= 2^(-B).                           (3)

To prove this, 2^B>=2B and Bernoulli give
(1-2^(-B))^B>=1-B*2^(-B)>=1/2. Take the positive B-th root.

If A<0, 0<t<=2^(-1/B), so |1-t|>=2^(-B) by (3).
If A>0, t>=2^(1/B)>=1/(1-2^(-B)), hence again |1-t|>=2^(-B).

For any admissible ratio z=1-t with |z|<1, (2) therefore implies

    -log|z|_v = -kappa log|1-t| <= kappa B log2 <= log2.       (4)

When |z|>=1 the required series/convergence inequality already fails.

## 4. Failure theorem for the exact log interface

Suppose even ONE of the supplied log arguments has the form t=p^q above,
and it is represented at the matching place as

    alpha_j/beta = 1-t,
    Li_1(alpha_j/beta) = -log(t).

Keep every prerequisite of the provider. Then rho>=|1-t|_v; (1) and (4)
give

    V_v(alpha,beta) <= log2-C < 0.                   (5)

The strict last inequality holds for ALL positive m,R, since M>=1 and all
the other terms in C are positive. Thus Theorem2.2/Corollary2.3 cannot be
admitted at this real-log use-site. This conclusion allows arbitrary
common-denominator scaling, additional containing number fields and arbitrary
nonzero rational powers; these choices do not supply V>0.

In particular, if B_i=p_i^(q_i) with q_i nonzero rational and p_i prime,
then B_i^s remains of that form for every nonzero rational s. Fractional
powers can make the real arguments close to one, but the associated degree
must be included in the normalized place. Treating that degree as fixed is
the erroneous step this theorem prevents. Consistent individual rational
rescalings of polynomial variables have the same criterion obstruction.

## 5. This occurs on a nonempty full-promised rank-five G3 domain

Use the ORIGINAL full promise, lambda in {3,6,10,15,21},

    V_lambda(r)=lambda-sum_(h=0)^(lambda-1)r^h,
    ell=log B in cone{V(r):r in J_6}, ell!=0,
    J_6=[1/6,5/6].

There are effectively selectable distinct rational r_1,...,r_5 in J_6
whose column matrix A=(V(r_1),...,V(r_5)) is invertible. The five polynomial

linearly independent on the interval. Their value vectors therefore span

This is an effective existence construction, not an executed tuple or new

documents.title: G3: all homogeneous rank-three logarithm matrices already have the rectangle
documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# G3: all homogeneous rank-three logarithm matrices already have the rectangle

Existing G3 owner,22October2026UTC. NEW **HAND/UNCOMPILED** argument plus a
separate actually executed exact finite algebra certificate. No arithmetic
zero procedure, original source recognition or G3 endpoint is claimed.
No subagent, model, compiler/native job or local Git action occurred.

## Precise result

Keep the inherited purity branch and notation

    ell_n=a*T_n(r), a>0, n in {3,6,10,15,21},
    T_n(t)=sum[k=0..n-2](n-1-k)*t^k.

Assume r is transcendental. Let L(X) be ANY m-by-n matrix of homogeneous
RATIONAL linear forms in five variables, with rank L(T(r))=3 and

    3 < mn/(m+n).                                     (1)

Then L(X) already has an identically zero rectangle after invertible
rational row/column operations, whose dimensions m',n' satisfy

    m'/m+n'/n>1.                                     (2)

Consequently the proved Waldschmidt--Masser theorem cannot contradict this
putative pure branch by ANY such rank-three matrix: its rectangle conclusion
already holds before any logarithm is substituted. Together with the prior
rank<=2 argument, this screens all homogeneous rational-linear rank<=3
matrix sizes. It does NOT screen rank>=4, affine constants or auxiliary logs.

The proved arithmetic theorem/strict bound and its primary-source scope
are retained in G3-LOG-MATRIX-RANK-BOUNDARY.md. This argument does not invoke
the stronger structural-rank or Matrix Coefficient conjectures. Multiplying
by the same nonzero a does not change the matrix rank.

## The exact NEW finite input

Let P be the kernel of the homogeneous map

    Q[X1,...,X5] -> Q[u,t], Xi -> u*T_i(t).

It is a homogeneous PRIME ideal. The formal scale u here is only a device
to define the homogeneous relation ideal, not an auxiliary logarithm in L.
The previous exact coefficient certificates give P1=P2=P3=0 and dim P4=9.
The NEW calculation computes ALL linear syzygies of this complete P4:

    S1(P4)=ker(P4 tensor span_Q(X1,...,X5) -> Q[X]_5).

In the old exact integer quartic basis, its multiplication matrix is
126-by-45, with EXACT rank43 and nullity2. All kernel vectors were checked
against the ORIGINAL integer multiplication matrix; their distinct positive
free coordinates prove independence. A43-by-43 minor has determinant673103
modulo the previously certified prime1000003, giving the rank lower bound.
Thus dim_Q S1(P4)=2, including after extension of scalars to Qbar.

check_log_curve_quartic_syzygies.py3935B/SHA
3cc7fd8d805177d84b05f27617d6d5804ab446cde81360fbea970e3ac0c15b2a
reuses the exact old curve/kernel constructors. The quartic basis is a
necessary input to this NEW multiplication question, not a new claim that
the earlier degree1--4 computations were missing. The executed result keeps
the entire multiplication matrix, monomial/column orders, old quartic basis,
two integer syzygies and complete minor indices, encrypted before persistence:

    [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]
    ciphertext da73b4f2d6a7d950278ea2358ebbcf14ab6f1fc2b59494e3308a3a172ce2d142.

Actual execution took0.662seconds. No full quintic relation ideal, numerical
log equality, determinant-matrix classification or G3 decision was run.

## Lemma: universal linear determinant identities span the field kernel

For any m-by-n matrix A over a characteristic-zero field K, rank A>=4,
consider one formal coordinate z_IJ for each4-by-4 minor. The evaluations
of UNIVERSAL linear identities among generic4-minors span, over K, the
entire kernel of the functional z_IJ -> det A_IJ.

Here "linear identity" means a coefficient homogeneous linear in the
generic matrix entries multiplying each degree4 minor. We need no general
minimal-resolution theorem. The following identities suffice after rank
normalization:

1. In a4-by-5 submatrix, expansion with one duplicated row gives a linear
   relation among its five4-minors, for each of its four rows.
2. The transposed5-by-4 duplicated-column identities.
3. In a5-by-5 submatrix, the difference of any two Laplace expansions of
   its determinant, along rows or columns, is such a linear identity.

The vector space of ALL universal linear identities is defined by rational
coefficient equations. It is stable under row/column changes and extension
of scalars: Cauchy--Binet linearly transforms the minor coordinates, and a
change of the generic matrix variables transforms degree1 coefficients.
Therefore it suffices to verify spanning at A=diag(I_s,0), s=rank A. Row/
column operations over K in this proof need not be rational constants; they
only prove a field-span statement about universal identities.

At that diagonal matrix, write I0,J0 for the portions of I,J in {1,...,s}.
If I0!=J0, a duplicated-row or duplicated-column relation forces z_IJ=0:
choose an unmatched pivot index and add its missing column/row. The selected
diagonal entry1 is the only surviving coefficient in that relation.

If I0=J0=P but |P|<4, both I and J contain an index outside {1,...,s}.
Choose a pivot index b outside P. In the5-by-5 submatrix with rows I+{b}
and columns J+{b}, expansion along row b is, up to sign, z_IJ; expansion
along a zero row is0. Identity3 therefore forces z_IJ=0.

Only coordinates z_PP with P a4-subset of {1,...,s} remain. If s=4 there
is just one. If s>4, Identity3 on each principal5-subset equates the
coordinates for its4-subsets. The graph of4-subsets joined when their
intersection has size3 is connected. Thus every remaining coordinate is
equal. These are exactly the actual minors, all1, up to a single common
scalar. The quotient by the universal linear relations has dimension1,
as asserted. This proves the lemma for all sizes, not by finite sampling.

## The span of L's quartic minors has dimension at most three

Work over K=Q(X1,...,X5). If the generic rank of L is>=4, let W be the
rational span of ALL its4-minors and let d=dim_Q W. Transcendence of r and
rank L(T(r))=3 imply every one of these minors vanishes IDENTICALLY on the
parametrized curve. Hence W is a subspace of the known complete P4.

Choose a rational basis F1,...,Fd of W. Expressing all minors in this
basis is a constant rational surjection C:Q^N -> W. The minor-evaluation
functional over K factors through the nonzero functional

    W tensor K -> K, Fi -> Fi(X).

Its kernel has dimension d-1. By the preceding lemma, universal linear
determinant identities span the full preimage kernel before applying C;
after C they therefore span this(d-1)-dimensional kernel. Each projected
identity has coefficients which are rational LINEAR forms in X, so is a
member of S1(W), embedded in S1(P4). Its K-span has dimension at most2
by the exact certificate. Therefore d-1<=2 and

    d<=3.                                           (3)

This uses all minors together, not only a particular4-by-5 block. Linear
dependencies among the minors cause no problem: quotienting by C's constant
kernel maps the full functional kernel SURJECTIVELY onto the kernel in W.

## Prime-ideal factorization excludes d=2 or d=3

If d=2, the field-span statement gives a nonzero linear syzygy
l1*F1+l2*F2=0. Independence of F1,F2 makes l1,l2 nonproportional nonzero
linear forms, hence coprime. The UFD property gives F1=h*l2,F2=-h*l1 with
h homogeneous of degree3. Primality and P1=P3=0 contradict Fi in P.

If d=3, it gives two K-independent linear syzygy vectors b,c in Q[X]_1^3.
Their nonzero cross product q=b cross c has degree2, and F=(F1,F2,F3) is
proportional to q over K. Divide q by the gcd g of its nonzero coordinates,
degree e<=2, to obtain a primitive vector q'. Primitivity and the UFD
property imply

    F=h*q', h in Q[X], deg h=2+e, deg q'=2-e.

If e=2, q' is constant, contradicting independence of the three Fi. If
e=0 or1, h has degree2 or3, so h is not in P. Primality then puts every
nonzero coordinate of q' in P, of degree2 or1, also impossible. This
excludes d=3. None of these UFD steps assumes independence of logarithms;
they concern the exact formal polynomial prime ideal.

Thus a generic-rank>=4 L must have d=1: all its4-minors are rational
multiples of one nonzero F in P4.

## d=1 forces generic rank4 and a constant four-dimensional block

If generic rank were>=5, choose an invertible5-by-5 submatrix B over K.
Its adjugate is F*D for a constant rational matrix D, since every cofactor
is a4-minor. D is invertible. Laplace expansion gives det B=F*l for a
nonzero homogeneous linear l. The adjugate identity yields

    B*D=l*I, hence B=l*D^{-1}.

Its nonzero4-minors are therefore constant multiples of l^4. Since one
is also a nonzero constant multiple of F, F is proportional to l^4.
Primality then gives l in P1, contradiction. Generic rank is exactly4.

Choose an invertible4-by-4 pivot block B. In the top four rows, Cramer's
rule expresses each other column as B times a vector of4-minor ratios.
All these ratios are rational CONSTANTS, because numerator/denominator
are constant multiples of F. The corresponding statement holds for other
rows. Generic rank4 then gives constant rational row/column relations
putting the whole L in one4-by-4 block, with all other rows/columns zero.

If m,n were both4, (1) would fail. Otherwise at least one zero full row or
column gives an identically zero rational rectangle satisfying (2). This
case therefore cannot provide a new arithmetic contradiction either.

## Generic rank3 and conclusion

If the generic rank was already3, choose a rational x0 of rank3 and put
L(x0) in rank normal form by rational operations. For every rational y,
all4-minors of L(x0)+h*L(y) vanish identically. The linear h coefficient
in each pivot3-plus-one minor is the corresponding bottom-right entry of
L(y). Hence that entire(m-3)-by-(n-3) rectangle is identically zero.
Its normalized size is2-3/m-3/n>1 by (1). This is exactly the elementary
maximal-rank tangent argument used earlier, now applied to generic rank3.

These cases exhaust the generic rank: it cannot be below the specialized
rank3; when it is above3, (3) and the prime-ideal argument reduce it to the
constant four-block case. The announced all-size rank-three screen follows.

## Scope and next real gate

The arithmetic purity/exact-zero implication remains OPEN. This new result
eliminates the earlier smallest rank3 shapes5-by-8,6-by-7,7-by-7 and ALL
larger homogeneous rational-linear rank3 attempts, not merely those samples.
No qualifying contradiction matrix was constructed. The next such route
would need rank>=4 and a genuinely new higher-degree structure. Combined
with the earlier width bound, possible first rank4 shapes include6-by-13,
7-by-10,8-by-9 and9-by-9; this is not an existence claim.

The new finite computation did NOT find zero linear syzygies: it found TWO.
The proof above explicitly uses that outcome; no failed zero-syzygy premise
is hidden. The universal-identity, prime-factorization and rational-block
arguments are HAND, uncompiled and not independently peer adopted here.
No complete quintic ideal or rank4 screen is claimed. Original source
construction, all-input attainment/word coverage and NO remain separate.

# Lower-endpoint curvature of paired-critical COMMON cells

22 October 2026 UTC. Existing G3 source owner. NEW RELATIVE HAND CANDIDATE;
self-audited, UNREVIEWED and UNCOMPILED. No mathematical program, solver,
old producer, source compiler, model/native job or peer task was run.

This is a supporting structural result, not a replacement for G3's total
all-input exact recognition/terminating-NO goal. It supplies no general
one-witness H, no exact logarithmic-zero test and no INDEPENDENT/BOTH theorem.

## 1. Exact claim, inherited suppliers and prior comparison

Let Lambda=(1,3,6,10,15,21). For 0<r<1 use the SAME uniquely normalized normal

    sum c_lambda=1, sum lambda*c_lambda=0,
    F_r(r)=F'_r(r)=F_r(r^2)=F'_r(r^2)=0,
    F_r(x)=sum c_lambda(r)*(1-x^lambda).

Set

    H_lambda(p,q)=-log(1-p+p*q^lambda),
    L_r(p,q)=sum c_lambda(r)*H_lambda(p,q).

Critical means BOTH L_p=L_q=0, with r and c(r) FIXED and 0<p,q<1.

**Relative hand claim.** Using the lower-endpoint supplier below, there is
a rational R>0 such that EVERY real strict critical cell with 0<r<R obeys

    L_pp(r,p,q)<0.                                      (1)

Thus none of those critical Hessians is positive semidefinite. The claim is
uniform over all real p,q; no algebraic-parameter premise, finite grid,
nondegenerate-critical-point promise or lower bound on 1-p is added.

All immutable source paths below are at Commons
8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6.

* Closest original provider: research/2026-10-02-codex-g3-parametric-critical-0330z/
  ALL-RESIDUE-CRITICAL-FINITENESS.md. Its complete body was read. It supplies
  the rational normal and finite critical set, not Hessian signs.
* Closest endpoint increment: handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-lower-endpoint-hand-increment-003/
  LOWER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-LOSS-05.md. Its complete body was read. Its HAND
  theorem says that some R0,eta>0 give p(1-q)>=eta on every critical cell
  with r<R0. This is REUSED, not rederived or silently promoted to independent
  acceptance. The present claim is RELATIVE to that unreviewed supplier.
  Its exact coefficient asymptotics, double-root estimates and uniform
  q-near-one exclusion are also reused below.
* Later full query: research/2026-10-16-g3-critical-psd-reduction-1950z/
  REDUCTION.md. Its complete body was read. It leaves the all-r predicate
  open and mentions L_pp<0 as an unproved sufficient statement.
* Later endpoint successor: handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-upper-endpoint-hand-increment-004/
  UPPER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-CLASSIFICATION-06.md. The complete body was read,
  including its unbalanced and probability-boundary sections. Its weak
  r->1 saddle/complementary loss floor is REUSED at HAND scope. It does not

The new implication compared with those bodies is the SIGN on all sufficiently
small-r critical cells, including the strong p->1,q->0 corner. Their existing
count finiteness, endpoint loss bounds and upper weak saddle are not new here.
This is a bounded predecessor/successor comparison, not a historical novelty
or whole-corpus absence claim.

Exact source identities verified by both raw SHA256 and Git blob, without
executing any retained producer:

| Source key | Bytes | SHA256 | Git blob |

| normal | 13664 | f108eb49332179e4ff34f791c36eee28d33adcf4ce24db9094cc029c567ebc95 | 8faa5ae863ae4518414582dd5d3f714d9ca3896b |

## 2. Exact critical equations in odds coordinates

Put z=p/(1-p), u_lambda=z*q^lambda/(1+z*q^lambda), and A=log z. Exactly,

    L=log(1+z)-sum c_lambda*log(1+z*q^lambda),
    L_z=1/(1+z)-sum c_lambda*q^lambda/(1+z*q^lambda).

At a critical cell the two equations are

    sum c_lambda*u_lambda=p,
    sum lambda*c_lambda*u_lambda=0.                    (2)

The second follows by multiplying L_q by -q. At such a cell,

    L_AA=-p^2+sum c_lambda*u_lambda^2.                  (3)

Indeed L_A=p-sum c*u and d u/dA=u(1-u). Also

    L_AA=[p(1-p)]^2*L_pp

when L_p=0. Thus a negative quantity in (3) proves (1), with no change in
the fixed-normal differentiation convention.

Another exact form of (2), with f_lambda=1-p+p*q^lambda, is

    sum c_lambda/f_lambda=1,
    sum lambda*c_lambda/f_lambda=0.                   (4)

For the second identity use sum lambda*c_lambda=0. No denominator in these
identities vanishes in the strict domain.

## 3. Inherited small-r data and the contradiction setup

Write nu=(2,6,9,13,13,13) in Lambda order. The exact scaled linear system in
note05 gives

    c_lambda(r)=k_lambda*r^(-nu_lambda)*(1+o(1)),
    k=(3/2,-1/2,7/8,-3/8,11/16,-5/16).               (5)

The coefficients are rational functions and the scaled coefficients are
analytic at r=0. The following limits, including derivatives on compact
positive t or v intervals, are inherited from that exact system:

    F_r(r^2*t) -> P2(t)=(t-1)^2*(t+2)/2,
    r^3*F_r(r*v) -> P1(v)=v^3*(4-7v^3+3v^7)/8.

Both displayed positive-variable functions vanish only at 1. The roots at
r^2 and r of the exact F_r are DOUBLE for every r. In particular, near v=1,

    F_r(r*v)=r^-3*O((v-1)^2),
    F'_r(r*v)=r^-4*(v-1)*(21/2+o(1)).                 (6)

The paired-normal Descartes argument also gives F_r(x)>=0 on (0,1).
This is an exact sign, not an unsigned-coefficient estimate.

If (1) fails arbitrarily close to r=0, the rational critical equations and
the rational inequality L_pp>=0 give a semialgebraic curve of counterexamples
with r->0. Curve selection and Puiseux parametrization may therefore be used.
Along this curve write limits p0,q0 in [0,1]. Note05 gives p(1-q)>=eta.
Consequently p0>0 and q0<1. Its separately established q-near-one exclusion
also applies. We now exhaust q0>0 and q0=0.

All curve-selection arguments concern this auxiliary derivative predicate,
not hidden parameter extraction from an original algebraic input.

## 4. A positive limiting q forces negative p curvature

Suppose q0 is in (0,1). Multiply L and its p derivatives by r^13. The limit is

    J(p,q)=(-6*H_10+11*H_15-5*H_21)/16.              (7)

If p->1, the limit of r^13 L_p is

    [-6*q0^-10+11*q0^-15-5*q0^-21]/16 < 0,

by strict convexity of x->q0^-x and 15=(6*10+5*21)/11. It cannot be critical.
The inherited loss floor excludes p->0. Hence p0 is strict.

For fixed strict q, J_p is a positive denominator times a LINEAR numerator
in p: the degree-two coefficient cancels because -6+11-5=0. Its numerator
is positive at p=0 and negative at p=1, again by strict convexity of
x->q^x and x->q^-x. The linear numerator therefore has negative slope.
At every zero of J_p, J_pp<0. Criticality of the actual curve passes to
J_p(p0,q0)=0, so r^13 L_pp tends to a strictly negative value. This
contradicts L_pp>=0.

This uses a three-term limiting identity; no assertion that signed c is
a probability measure or that the full six-term function is concave is made.

## 5. A vanishing q with p bounded away from both endpoints is impossible

Suppose q->0 and p->p0 in (0,1), so z->z0 in (0,infinity). Write
q=Q*r^a*(1+o(1)), Q,a>0. Note05's coefficient table has Newton orders

    min(0,a-2,3a-6,6a-9,10a-13,15a-13,21a-13).

For 0<a<2, the first critical equation can survive only at a=1,Q=1;
the a=2 case must be retained separately. Higher q powers in the rational
denominators have strictly higher order than the divergent leading term.
For a>2, L_z->1/(1+z0)>0.

At a=2 the q equation, after multiplying by r^2, forces P2'(Q)=0,
hence Q=1. The z equation then tends to -z0/(1+z0), which is nonzero.

At a=1 write q=r(1+h), h->0. The exact double roots give

    L_q/z=F'_r(q)-z*q*F'_r(q^2)+O(1),
    F'_r(q)=r^-4*h*(21/2+o(1)),
    q*F'_r(q^2)=O(r^-1*|h|).

The remainder is uniformly O(1) for bounded positive z; this follows by
summing the six absolute terms of order q^(3lambda-1). Thus h=O(r^4).
Using the exact roots again,

    L_z -> 1/(1+z0)-1+z0 = z0^2/(1+z0)>0.

There is no critical curve in this regime. A p0=0 limit was already
excluded by the inherited loss floor.

## 6. The strong corner: necessary exponent balances

It remains to treat p->1 and q->0. Along the selected semialgebraic curve,

    z=Z*r^-b*(1+o(1)), q=Q*r^a*(1+o(1)),
    Z,Q,a,b>0.                                         (8)

First, (4) forces b<10a. To see this, the orders of c_lambda/f_lambda are

    nu_lambda+min(b,a*lambda).

For 10a<=b<15a the largest terms are the upper three or the upper two.
At b=10a their mass coefficient is

    (6Z/16)*(1-1/(1+Z*Q^10))>0;

for 10a<b<15a it is 6Z/16>0. At b=15a only the 15 and 21 terms are
largest; two distinct nonzero terms cannot cancel both mass and lambda
moment in (4). For 15a<b and at or beyond 21a the 21 term is uniquely
largest. Thus every b>=10a is excluded. Lower coefficients have strictly
smaller orders in all these comparisons.

For b<10a use (2) instead. The orders of c_lambda*u_lambda are

    E_lambda=nu_lambda-max(a*lambda-b,0).               (9)

The 15 and 21 entries are strictly below the 10 entry, so only
lambda=1,3,6,10 can maximize (9).

A simultaneous leading cancellation in (2) needs at least THREE maximal
terms whenever the maximum order is positive. Two distinct nonzero terms
cannot cancel both their mass and lambda moment. The remaining possibility
of a nonpositive maximum gives no critical curve: it requires b<a and a>2,
where the lambda=1 term is uniquely largest and cannot satisfy the zero
lambda moment.

Here is the exhaustive finite comparison of the four affine orders. Boundary
equalities may occur in both adjacent rows; that harmless overlap is retained.

| Range | Three maximal entries can occur only as |
| --- | --- |
| 0<b<=a | a=1, entries 3,6,10, with 0<b<=1 |
| a<=b<=3a | a=1, entries 3,6,10, with 1<=b<=3 |
| 3a<=b<=6a | a=1,b=3, entries 3,6,10 |
| 6a<=b<10a | none |

For example, when the last three entries are unsaturated their mutual
equalities force a=1. If the 1 entry is saturated its order is 2, whereas
their common order at a=1 is 3+b>2. If the 3 entry is saturated, equality
of the 6 and 10 entries still forces a=1, then equality with the 3 entry
forces b=3. In the last range at least two saturated entries of any triple
have unequal orders. In the first range the 1--3 edge has slope 2 and
the 3--6--10 edges have slope 1, so no triple containing 1 is possible.

Therefore a=1 and 0<b<=3. If b<3, the two leading equations, after dividing
by the common nonzero factor, are

    -4Q^3+7Q^6-3Q^10=0,
    -12Q^3+42Q^6-30Q^10=0.

Subtracting three times the first gives Q^4=1, hence Q=1.
If b=3 the first terms become -4Q^3/(1+ZQ^3) and
-12Q^3/(1+ZQ^3), respectively. The same subtraction forces Q=1, but
the first equation then gives 4-4/(1+Z)=0, impossible for Z>0.

Every possible strong-corner critical curve consequently has

    q/r ->1,  z=Z*r^-b*(1+o(1)), 0<b<3.               (10)

The order analysis uses BOTH exact equations. It does not set the leading
mass to zero when its order is nonpositive, or infer a critical point from
a Newton diagram.

## 7. Finish all corner subregimes

### 7.1 0<b<1 is not critical

Here z*q->0. Expanding one exact denominator, with a finite six-term
absolute remainder, gives

    L_z=1/(1+z)-1+F_r(q)+z*(1-F_r(q^2))
           +O(z^2*sum |c_lambda|*q^(3lambda)).

For q/r->1, the sum in the remainder is O(r), F_r(q^2)->0 and F_r(q)>=0.
Since z*r->0,

    L_z >= z*(1-o(1))-1 >0.

This excludes criticality. No estimate of how quickly q/r approaches 1
is needed here.

### 7.2 b=1 forces Z=2 and negative curvature

Put h=q/r-1. From the exact q equation,

    0=L_q/z=F'_r(q)
             +z*sum lambda*c_lambda*q^(2lambda-1)/(1+z*q^lambda).

The second term is O(r^-2). Equation (6) thus gives h=O(r^2), and
F_r(q)=O(r). An exact rearrangement of the first equation is

    L_z=1/(1+z)-1+F_r(q)
             +z*sum c_lambda*q^(2lambda)/(1+z*q^lambda).

Multiplying by r and taking the limit yields

    0=Z*(3/[2(1+Z)]-1/2).

Thus Z=2. In (3), multiplication by r^2 now gives

    r^2*L_AA -> (3/2)*(Z/(1+Z))^2-Z^2/2
               = -4/3 <0.

Only the 1 and 3 entries survive this last limit; every other entry has
strictly higher order. Therefore L_pp<0 along the curve.

### 7.3 1<b<3 has a single negative leading square term

Now u_1->1 and u_3~Z*r^(3-b). In (3),

    r^(2b)*L_AA -> -Z^2/2 <0.

Indeed the positive 1 entry contributes O(r^(2b-2))->0, the 3 entry
gives the displayed negative limit, and entries 6,10,15,21 are smaller
by positive powers, beginning with r^3 and r^7. Again L_pp<0.

Sections 4--7 exhaust a selected counterexample curve. None can have
L_pp>=0, proving the relative claim (1).

## 8. Effective and original-source scope

Because c(r) is rational and its denominator is nonzero on (0,1), the
predicate "strict critical and L_pp>=0" is a rational semialgebraic
predicate after retaining denominators or clearing by positive squares.
Enumerating dyadic R and deciding its universal emptiness by RCF would
therefore terminate, IF this relative hand proof and its inherited note05
supplier are correct. No such elimination, search or certificate was run.
The argument supplies no numerical R and does not relabel a prepared query
as an executed UNSAT result.

The accepted negative-inertia source theorem could then bound retained
multiplicity by three on this LOWER-ENDPOINT branch, but only with its
actual positive drift/residue, zero killing, rank-five, untied COMMON
variation and nonattainment hypotheses. That count sharpening is optional:
the retained all-real fixed-input critical count is already solved.
Neither bound decides the at-most-one zero-head logarithmic equality.

The middle-r global Q13 predicate, possible strong upper-endpoint cells,
the full original shared-menu/caller problem and all-input H/complete NO
remain OPEN. No new original observation, independent row fit, physical
inverse, natural parameter endpoint or refreshed COMMON bit is admitted.
