# G3 lower-endpoint hand adoption

22 October 2026 UTC. Existing G3 source owner. This is an AUTHOR hand audit
and adoption, not independent review, a kernel check or a new mathematical
derivation. No mathematical program, solver, source producer or held job ran.
The original G3 all-input recognition/terminating-NO goal remains OPEN.

## Statement adopted at hand-proof scope

For the original normalized paired normal c(r), Lambda=(1,3,6,10,15,21),
there is R>0 such that EVERY real strict critical cell with 0<r<R has

    partial_pp [c(r).H(p,q)] < 0,
    H_lambda(p,q)=-log(1-p+p*q^lambda).

The normal and r are held FIXED when taking the p,q derivatives. Both
critical equations are required. No algebraic hidden-parameter promise or
restriction on how p or q approach their boundaries is added.

This adopts the auxiliary lower-endpoint loss-floor supplier and the new
corner proof together. The earlier conditional file stays byte-identical;
read it with this status note. External independent/formal review of the
combined argument remains unperformed.

## Exact proofs actually audited

1. Commons8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6,
   handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-lower-endpoint-hand-increment-003/
   LOWER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-LOSS-05.md,
   14737B/SHA256
   1e4b8624c42bdaf12abd9a7ecf364a619e75010f9b9e9cf637e36059a99ee4a8,
   Git blob3cf857ae6250042fbb54857c7626aa1bd6754107.
   Complete body read. The adoption needed here covers its scalar
   loss-floor theorem, Sections3--7, and the rational effectivity explanation.
   It does not independently certify every original-source corollary.
2. G3-LOWER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-CURVATURE.md,
   14270B/SHA256
   5f4ccdffd77f05f633188302502e3218cf44a283bd0b4c5d01319773e8e407b6.
   Complete new hand proof and its predecessor/successor comparison audited.
   Its four immutable source identities remain in that file.

The original all-r normal/finiteness theorem, later three-variable PSD query
and upper06 weak-endpoint successor were compared in that preflight.
Their finiteness, loss bounds and weak-saddle results are REUSED. This audit
does not claim the whole all-r Q13 predicate was previously solved.

## Decisive checks of the inherited loss floor

* The scaled six-equation system at r=0 is block triangular and invertible.
  Its successive two-by-two solves give b coefficients
  (-3/2,1/2,-7/8,3/8,-11/16,5/16), with the stated powers of r.
  The sign and order data used in the new proof agree with c=-b.
* The q-near-one derivative is divided by p(1-p)(q-1) BEFORE taking
  probability-endpoint limits. Its remaining value is 165/8>0.
  The claimed exclusion is therefore uniform even when p approaches 0 or 1.
* In the hypothetical vanishing-loss branch, an interior limiting q forces
  p->0. The r^13-scaled first equation then has the strictly positive P0
  limit. At q->0, the absolute six-term bounds preserve the Newton orders;
  they do not use cancellation in a remainder.
* At q/r^2->1 the exact double root gives
  t-1=O(z*r^2), z=p/(1-p)->0; the first equation divided by z tends to -1.
  At q/r->1 the two exact double roots give
  v-1=O(z^2*r^4); the first equation divided by z^2 tends to +1.
  The factor r^-3 in F_r(r*v) remains in the latter substitution.
  The geometric tails are uniformly bounded over all higher powers.
* These are all positive Puiseux scales of a semialgebraic counterexample
  curve. They exclude every vanishing-loss critical branch, which is the
  claimed floor. RCF is used only for a proposed terminating certificate
  search, not as an executed calculation or an exponential-zero oracle.

No new floor theorem is claimed: the complete old argument is being reused
and accepted by this source owner at mathematical hand-proof scope.

## Decisive checks of the new curvature argument

The odds equations are EXACT mass and lambda-moment equations, with
u_lambda=z*q^lambda/(1+z*q^lambda). At criticality,

    L_AA=-p^2+sum c_lambda*u_lambda^2,
    L_AA=[p(1-p)]^2*L_pp, A=log z.

Thus their negative sign transfers without varying the normal.

For positive limiting q, the scaled three-term limit has zero total
coefficient and a linear p-derivative numerator. Its endpoint signs are
strict by convexity, so its p-critical points have negative p curvature.
The finite-z,q->0 scales are excluded using BOTH critical equations.

In the strong corner z~Z*r^-b, q~Q*r^a, the reciprocal-f equations first
exclude b>=10a. The u equations then need at least three dominant entries;
two distinct entries cannot cancel both leading moments when the order is
positive. The nonpositive-order alternative has a unique leading entry
and is separately excluded. The four saturation ranges therefore force
a=1 and 0<b<=3. Their leading equations give Q=1; b=3 is impossible.

For b<1, F_r(q)>=0 and z*r->0 make L_z positive. For b=1 the q equation
gives q/r-1=O(r^2); the first equation forces Z=2 and
r^2 L_AA->-4/3. For 1<b<3 the single negative leading square gives
r^(2b)L_AA->-Z^2/2. All surviving corner cases have negative curvature.

The inherited loss floor rules out the remaining probability boundaries.
Semialgebraic curve selection therefore gives one uniform small-r interval.
The audit found no missing strict boundary, signed-Jensen substitution,
zero-denominator division or change from a fixed to a moving normal.

## Limits retained

No numerical R, RCF certificate, actual critical root, compiler receipt or
physical source witness was computed. The three-occurrence source consequence
still requires the OLD inertia theorem's actual positive drift/residue,
zero killing, rank-five, untied COMMON variation and nonattainment premises.
It is not an arbitrary joint-source count bound.

This closes the small-r scalar curvature statement at AUTHOR HAND scope
only. Middle-r and strong upper-endpoint Q13 remain open. The already solved
input-specific critical-count problem is not reopened. Most importantly,
neither this statement nor its review decides the zero-head logarithmic
equality or supplies total one-witness H for all original COMMON/I/BOTH inputs.

# A finite response quotient for marginal-quartet menus

Authored2026-10-22UTC. HAND extension of
G3-FOUR-TAXON-PAIRED-QUARTET-REDUCTION.md. It removes the four-original-taxa
and one-copy-per-taxon restrictions for this precise marginal observation
channel. General original G3, joint panels and formal source reflection
remain open. No independent proof review or native Lean pass is claimed.

## Input and inherited source boundary

Each authorized response row observes the unrooted quartet of FOUR DISTINCT
original sampled-copy IDs from ONE genealogy, or a declared coarsening of
that quartet. Original sources may have any finite number of taxa, and rows
may sample more copies before projecting to these four. Different rows
share ONE physical bank. Natural COMMON/INDEPENDENT mechanisms and finite
fixed/randomized protected original-ID parent controls are retained.

This statement concerns the vector of individual quartet marginals. A joint
distribution of two or more quartets is a different observation and is not
replaced by its marginals. There is no new synchronization of fresh private
bits across genealogies, no query inside the private word, no ranked/clock
readout and no label-dependent adaptive routing. All finite exposed sites,
uses and constraints stay in the protected template. Remaining eligible
private words have free strict rates/coins and fresh natural bits, as in
the inherited reduction; a declared nonfree constraint cannot be discarded.

Use the inherited source-faithful selected-current-root sampling consistency
and complete protected-template catalogue. The actual formal local-block/
opaque-forest/register adapter is still a supplier to finish, not a new
assumption claimed proved by the existing global-span theorem.

## The quotient theorem on a supplied original slot

For a private word W, let `C(W)` and `Q(W)` be its natural COMMON and
INDEPENDENT selected-pair no-merger survivals. Sampling consistency makes
them independent of unselected contemporaneous lineages. The exact paired
cap-two theorem gives

                             0<C(W)<=Q(W)<1.

For mechanism m, replace W in the response calculation by an ordinary
colocated Kingman edge of pair survival `s_m=C(W)` or `s_m=Q(W)`.
**HAND theorem:** this replacement preserves every permitted single-quartet
marginal, conditional on the actual entering selected forest and retained
old register. It holds simultaneously for all rows, with the same C,Q.

To prove it, project the original state to the row's four copy IDs, retaining
their current populations, opaque trees and old register. Let k be the
number of selected copies in this cut bridge's descendant component. This
component cannot acquire an outside selected lineage below its unique exit.

* k=0 or1: the selected word has no possible pair merger and is irrelevant.
* k=2: if already merged, the inside two-leaf clade fixes the quartet split;
  otherwise the complete selected two-root kernel is determined by s_m.
* k=3: with fewer than three current roots an inside two-leaf clade already
  fixes the split. With three singleton selected roots, the upper law is
  exchangeable in those three labels with the fourth fixed. Its quartet
  law is uniform, independent of the private forest kernel.
* k=4: with fewer than four selected roots a two-leaf clade already fixes
  the split. With four singletons the upper law is exchangeable in all four
  selected labels, so again the quartet law is uniform.

The ordinary replacement has the same symmetry/irreversibility properties.
Thus both programs give the same final readout in every case. The argument
does not cap the ORIGINAL live-copy population at three or ignore hidden
lineages; selection precedes the case split. It does not need the selected
quartet's least stable root to equal the original source root. At k=4 it
also bypasses the known noncommutativity of full cap-four private kernels:
only this readout quotient is being preserved.

## One coupled finite chart, with constructive source reconstruction

On every protected template T, introduce ONE pair `(C_s,Q_s)` for each
eligible private slot s and impose `0<C_s<=Q_s<1`. In a COMMON response row
the slot's ordinary response operator is E(C_s); in an INDEPENDENT row it
is E(Q_s). Protected original-ID/register operations and every other bank
coordinate stay in their original joint compiler. At fixed finite copy
cap the ordinary edge coordinates are finite polynomials in its survival,
as in the retained edge-polynomial implementation. Therefore this is a
fixed finite real-algebraic response chart whenever the inherited protected
chart D_T and its supplied feasibility interface have that scope:

    exists theta, (C_s,Q_s):
      D_T(theta) and all_s (0<C_s<=Q_s<1)
      and quartet_response_quotient_T(theta,(C_s,Q_s)) = input.

E(C_s),E(Q_s) are mode-dependent RESPONSE operators. They are not asserted
to be one physical ordinary edge with two unrelated rates. The strip is
exactly what couples their coordinates to ONE actual physical private word.
After a real-algebraic sampler returns a feasible joint point, the cap-two
constructor expands each pair into that finite strict word. Use the actual
eligible-slot graph/calendar/registry receiver and keep every outside old
parameter and original menu. The quotient theorem then preserves every
authorized row simultaneously. Counts need not be known before this finite
RCF calculation. Exact infeasibility over a SOURCE-COMPLETE finite catalogue
excludes this marginal-quartet source fragment; a supplied incomplete chart
cannot acquire that completeness from the quotient alone.

`PairedCap2WordCertificate.wl` supplies exact algebraic witness construction;
the rational version already returns values accepted by the retained
Source/calendar/Code pipeline. No algebraic certificate has thereby become
native BinaryValid/RegistryValid evidence or a checked whole-source compiler
equivalence. The literal old clock/bank and concurrent outside-root formal
transport obligations remain explicit.

## New exact original-source controls, including the joint-law guard

`g3_quartet_projection.py` is a small original-copy-ID-preserving pruning
readout using the retained tree constructor and quartet decoder. It changes
no transition law. `verify_g3_multitaxon_quartet_words.py` authenticates the
retained Source/forest objects and reuses the positive receiver/calendar/Code
adapter on a FIVE-taxon caterpillar.

On a three-descendant slot compare two one-cell words with ordinary bank1/4:

    cellA: (x,y,pParent0)=(1/2,1/2,3/4)
    cellB: (x,y,pParent0)=(11/32,13/16,2/3).

Their pair coordinates are identically `(C,Q)=(1/8,11/64)`, while their
COMMON/triple and INDEPENDENT/triple coordinates differ. Both mechanisms
gave exactly the same FIVE individual quartet marginals for these words,
but different full rooted laws AND different joint five-quartet panel laws.

On the four-descendant slot, compare cellA's word with a strict ordinary
edge E(1/2). Their pair coordinates differ; nevertheless all five individual
quartet marginals agreed in each mechanism. Again full rooted and joint
quartet laws differed. This is actual positive-source evidence for the
k=4 case and an actual guard against extending the result to joint panels.

Revision2 additionally replaced each of the four actual source variants by
the mode-dependent ordinary quotient above. All EIGHT comparisons matched
all five marginal readouts exactly. Four invalid-copy-ID inputs were refused.
No native Lean/model or old suite job was run. Full original data, source,
exact calendar, Code arrays and laws were encrypted before persistence:

* Revision1: [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately], cipher SHA256
  2b8d9c00ccd9b979945d2890d0487cfd768443fa414c6b4f8c2c182b875af1b1.
* Revision2 with ordinary-quotient checks:
  [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately], cipher SHA256
  8f8b429b2d5d397c72cafa1c6126457ab747159507417415abee85c975292c1f.

The fixtures are not an exhaustive catalogue execution or an independent
proof of the arbitrary-source case. The HAND derivation and inherited
sampling/source reflection supply the stated generality. Full original G3
still includes observation channels outside this quotient, such as rooted
and higher-copy full-tree laws and genuinely coupled quartet tensors.

  SHA256446727db5a89571342401147017198f57f848e39c4819486e9b57bef5af2210d:
  its fixed-intensity pure curve is already proved Zariski dense. That lemma
  and proof are REUSED. Its statement explicitly leaves classification on
  only encoded algebraic points open; real nonsemialgebraicity alone is not
  the additional rational-input conclusion below.
- [G3-PURITY-AS-TWO-BOUNDED-VOLUMES.md](G3-PURITY-AS-TWO-BOUNDED-VOLUMES.md),
  SHA256099c56eb95cabbb2ceb8f7e912b1ed0ddb871121be7680f5c67b9ebff89b50e5:
  exact two-volume reduction and one sign-changing-integrand control. It
  rejects that integrand as a zero-volume test, not every fixed alternative.
- The complete OLD NO-FIXED-SEMIALGEBRAIC-RATIONAL-CLASSIFIER.md and its
  complete INDEPENDENT-RATIONAL-CLASSIFIER-REVIEW.md, in
  research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-calibrated-original-recognition-1422z at that pin,
  SHA2563c89bb2d02f7166c8b9c8dc85c872ed348c95900ba8dc11404c7286f5879a0a6
  and85d7fbb2bd01211c599da559f087b00c21a616492d25b492c7282233042d23ab.
  They ALREADY exclude one fixed classifier on the original calibrated
  rational observation domain, without assuming invariance. The rational
  two-sided boundary method is REUSED. The14October copy at
  research/2026-10-14-dot-g3-coupled-effective-slice-0602z/primary/
  rational-classifier.md is byte-identical, not a new theorem.

The incremental use-site here is the arithmetic promise itself and the
single-volume receiver. It is not a new general fixed-classifier obstruction,
a reproof of the original all-core reduction, or a new undecidability result.

## Statement

Fix ANY j>=3. Put L={3,6,10,15,21}, J=[1/j,1-1/j], and

    D_n(r)=n-sum_(h=0)^(n-1) r^h,
    C=cone{D(r):r in J} subset R^5.

The promised input b is in Q^5, b_n>1, with log b in C minus{0}.
Call it pure if log b=w D(r) for some w>0,r in J.

There is NO semialgebraic set E subset R^5, even with arbitrary fixed real
coefficients, which accepts exactly the pure inputs on this rational promise
domain. A fixed finite RCF formula has the same limitation by elimination of
its real quantifiers. This concerns correctness only on promised rational
inputs; no correctness at irrational points is assumed.

## Rational labels force a whole curve onto the boundary

Let r0 be ANY point of the interior of J and put p=exp(D(r0)), coordinatewise.

Rational PURE inputs approach p. Choose rational r_k in J tending to r0.
Choose an integer A_k>=1 clearing all five denominators of D_n(r_k), so
e_n,k=A_k D_n(r_k) are positive integers. Choose rational t_k>1 such that
A_k log t_k tends to1; density of the rationals near exp(1/A_k) permits this,
with error less than1/k. Then

    b_n,k=t_k^(e_n,k)

is rational, its log vector is (A_k log t_k)D(r_k), and b_k tends to p.
Each is an actual promised pure input. No rationality of p is needed.

Rational NONPURE inputs also approach p. The five polynomials D_n have
distinct degrees2,5,9,14,20, hence their value vectors on rational nodes in J
span R^5. Select five independent such vectors. Their positive sum eta is
an interior point of their simplicial cone, hence of C. For every epsilon>0,

    D(r0)+epsilon*eta is in interior(C).

Indeed, add D(r0) to a suitably scaled open ball about eta inside C.
The old exposed-ray result implies that every pure ray is on the boundary
of this full-dimensional cone. Thus no interior point is pure.

Coordinatewise exp is a homeomorphism onto the positive orthant. The open
set exp(interior(C)) contains nonpure rational vectors arbitrarily close to
exp(D(r0)+epsilon*eta). Let epsilon decrease to zero and choose these rational
vectors closer still. They satisfy the SAME fixed-j, full-five promise and
tend to p. They are not approximate labels: every selected rational vector
lies in that open nonpure set.

If E classified the promised rational inputs, the pure sequence would be in
E and the nonpure sequence outside E. Therefore p is on the Euclidean
boundary of E. This holds for EVERY r0 in the interior of J.

## The reused Zariski-density contradiction

The old lemma says r -> exp(D(r)) on ANY nonempty open interval is Zariski
dense in R^5, including over real coefficients. Briefly, a polynomial in
these five coordinates becomes a finite sum of exp(P_alpha(r)). Differences
of the exponent polynomials are nonconstant: the D_n have distinct degrees
and all vanish at r=1. An identity on the interval extends analytically to
the real line. At positive infinity one exponent polynomial is eventually
strictly largest; division by its exponential contradicts its nonzero
coefficient. This is the retained proof, not a physical extension of J.

In a finite polynomial-sign description of a semialgebraic E, remove
identically zero atoms. At a boundary point some remaining nonzero atom
vanishes, since otherwise all signs are locally constant. The product of
these finitely many nonzero polynomials is nonzero and vanishes on the
entire curve exp(D(r0)). This contradicts that reused Zariski-density lemma.
The rational-input statement follows.

In particular there cannot be a fixed finite RCF certificate relation R(b,c),
with any fixed finite real-witness vector c, whose certificate exists exactly
for pure rational promised b. Projection over c would give such an E. This
permits arbitrary witness coefficients and does not require their selection
to be computable. A growing certificate language or a non-RCF verifier is
outside this fixed-checker conclusion.

## Consequence for the proposed volume certificate

Suppose K subset R^5 times R^k is ONE fixed semialgebraic family, k>=1,
and its fibre K_b has a nonnegative finite Lebesgue volume on promised inputs.
For a semialgebraic fibre, volume is positive exactly when it has nonempty
interior: lower-dimensional cells are null, and a full-dimensional cell
contains an open ball. The existence of a ball inside K_b is an RCF formula
in b. Thus

    {b:volume(K_b)=0}

is semialgebraic. It cannot agree with purity on all promised rational inputs.
In particular no such family can represent the nonnegative Phi(log b) with
the required exact zeros. The same obstruction applies to fixed semialgebraic
parameter changes or finitely many such zero tests combined by Boolean logic.

This rejects EVERY fixed SEMIALGEBRAIC-family version of the positive-volume
idea, rather than only the old direct integrand. The OLD two-volume adapter stays
valid: equality of two positive volumes is not the zero test just excluded.

## Limits and changed frontier

An arbitrary algorithm selecting a family from the encoded input is not
excluded. Its selection need not be semialgebraic in the input values, even
if the returned formulas have bounded size. Unbounded format complexity and
nonsemialgebraic parameter selection are BOTH outside this theorem's contract.
No individual rational pure input lacks a certificate by this proof; the known
rank-one cases remain decidable. No algebraic rank-five pure input is constructed
or excluded. The arithmetic promise is not dropped.

Remove fixed-family zero-volume/finite-RCF replacements from the arithmetic
receiver queue. A future period method must supply an actual exact equality
mechanism or a terminating input-dependent transformation whose zero case is
proved; positivity of Phi alone does not supply either. Original all-input
source H/complete NO, all mechanisms and original joint interfaces remain open.
All previous proofs and executed controls remain unchanged and unreplayed.

# Exact algebraic paired cap-two word certificates

Authored2026-10-22UTC. Implements the HAND strict-image theorem in
G3-PAIRED-CAP2-STRICT-IMAGE.md. This is a private-interface consumer, not
native source admission or unrestricted original G3 recognition.

Load `Cap3PrivateWordCertificate.wl` and then
`PairedCap2WordCertificate.wl`. The first supplies the reused exact algebraic
input and closed real-decision helpers; no independent model is substituted.

`Cap2PairedWordMember[C,Q]` decides `0<C<=Q<1` for exact real-algebraic
inputs. Inexact, transcendental and complex inputs return Failure. A genuine
unresolved decision also remains Failure. An outside exact target has no
finite strict fresh natural private cap-two word, by the HAND theorem.

`Cap2PairedWordWitness[C,Q]` returns a compact certificate. `C=Q` uses no
bigon and ordinary bank `C`. Otherwise it chooses `A=(1+Q)/2` and doubles
`N=1,2,4,...` until the positive algebraic roots of `C/A,Q/A` enter the
strict bare-cell image. The proof supplies an explicit finite sufficient
threshold; no supplied stopping oracle or count promise is needed. The
piecewise bare constructor produces ONE arm0/arm1/parent0 tuple. Its numeric
parameters are repeated at `N` DISTINCT fresh sites; their natural bits are
not tied or reused.

The certificate retains `Targets`, `OrdinaryBank`, `CellCount`,
`RepeatedCell`, `PassageCount` and `DistinctFreshSites`.
`Cap2PairedWordVerify` directly checks strict algebraic parameters and BOTH
physical products against the targets, normalizing algebraic differences.
It does not infer verification from a solver's status string.
`Cap2PairedWordPassage[certificate,j]` gives the telescoping strict ordinary
factor; `Cap2PairedWordExpand` returns the explicit passage/cell lists after
verification. Exact output can be large; the compact certificate is a
representation of a finite word, not an assumed continuous power of a
source signature.

Actual Wolfram execution of `VerifyPairedCap2WordCertificate.wl` passed all
fourteen controls, including the four bare construction branches, zero/one/
two-cell words, the expanded two-cell products, nontrivial algebraic input,
algebraic equality, strict boundary exclusion, a tampered target and refused
unsupported input. The five reported witness counts were `0,1,2,1,0`.
The hosted prevalidation undefined-symbol warnings are retained, not hidden.

Complete source/result is encrypted in
`[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]`, ciphertext SHA256
8bbc07461bd02fc2be118f5388ddf0a03db8fdc026cef762f35945c3fea652f7.
Module5722B/SHA256

control source2734B/SHA256

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. # Exact strict image of paired two-current-root private words

Authored2026-10-22UTC. HAND theorem and exact rational implementation; no
historical novelty or independent mathematical review is claimed. The
existing original two-root source algebra was inspected in full in
G4TwoRootSourceStopping (Commons1138a5, source SHA
b5dd33d135fcb9267ae3297229e51434b5cfd434e08ef89ecacf34affd5e541d).
It supplies INDEPENDENT routing/product/positivity and a conditional rival
envelope; it does not state the paired all-word image proved here.

The scope is one fresh unexposed natural private slot with at most TWO
entering current roots, free strict arm/ordinary survivals and natural coins.
One physical word serves the paired COMMON/INDEPENDENT forest tuple. This
does not determine arbitrary synchronized tensors or higher-cap kernels.

## Complete all-length image

For one cell, with `p=P(parent0)` and `h=1-p`, write

\[
 C=px+hy,\qquad Q=p^2x+h^2y+2ph,\qquad0<x,y,p<1.
\]

For a word of `N` cells and positive ordinary bank `A<1`, the complete
two-root paired kernels have survivals `C_word=A product C_i` and
`Q_word=A product Q_i`. A merged root is absorbing; empty/one-root kernels
are identities. Thus matching these two coordinates matches every forest
coordinate through two roots, with entering subtrees restored opaquely.

**HAND theorem.** The exact finite strict word image is

\[
                         0<C\le Q<1.
\]

Equality `C=Q` has an ordinary zero-cell witness. Every `C<Q` in the strip
has a finite positive witness, using the SAME tuple in both modes.
Well-formed exact targets outside it are excluded for EVERY finite private
length. In particular `C<1,Q=1` is an exact nonattainment NO, despite being
approached by strict finite words. This is private-interface NO, not an
exclusion over arbitrary original core/observation alternatives.

Necessity follows from `Q-C=ph(2-x-y)>0`, positivity and `Q<1` in each
strict cell, together with the same ordinary factor in both products.

## A bare cell's upper boundary and strict constructor

The exact strict bare-cell image is `0<c<1, c<q<U(c)`, where

\[
 U(c)=\begin{cases}(c+2)^2/8,&c\le2/3,\\2c-c^2,&c\ge2/3.\end{cases}
\]

For the upper bound let `d=1-c`, `a=1-x`, `b=1-y` and assume `p>=h` by
arm symmetry. Minimize `1-q=p^2a+h^2b` at fixed `d=pa+hb` on the closed
cube. Loss first fills the smaller-weight arm. If `h<=d`, take `b=1` and
`a=(d-h)/p`; then `q=c+h(2-c)-2h^2`, optimized at `h=(2-c)/4` when
`c<=2/3`, or at the boundary `h=d` otherwise. If `h>=d`, the optimum is
`a=0,b=d/h`, giving `q=1-hd`, again maximized at `h=d`. This proves `U`.
Every upper optimizer uses a closed arm endpoint, so strict cells are below
it. The lower `q>c` is strict and is approached by a rare natural coin.

There is also a direct strict constructor. If `c<q<=(c+1)/2`, choose

\[
 x=y=c,\quad t=(q-c)/[2(1-c)],\quad p=(1+\sqrt{1-4t})/2.
\]

If `q>(c+1)/2`, choose the closed upper point

\[
 (p_*,x_*,y_*)=\begin{cases}
 ((c+2)/4,4c/(c+2),0),&c\le2/3,\\
 (c,1,0),&c\ge2/3.
 \end{cases}
\]

At this fixed coin the equal-arm point has
`q0=c+2p_*(1-p_*)(1-c)<q`. Set `lambda=(q-q0)/(U(c)-q0)` and
`x=(1-lambda)c+lambda x_*`, `y=(1-lambda)c`. Here `0<lambda<1`, so every
physical parameter is strict and the two coordinates equal `c,q` exactly.
For rational input the upper construction is rational. In the lower branch,
rational coins near the equal-arm coin also give strict rational arms by
the two linear coordinate equations; exact dyadic bisection finds one.

Actual Wolfram checks proved the bare upper inequality by real quantifier
elimination and returned zero for the coordinate/interpolation identities.
Those are algebra checks; the arbitrary-length conclusion uses the proof
below and does not follow merely from a fixed-cell elimination.

## Constructing a word for every strict strip point

For `0<C<Q<1`, choose ordinary bank `A=(1+Q)/2`, and put `u=C/A`, `v=Q/A`.
They satisfy `0<u<v<1`. For sufficiently large integer `N`, the positive
roots `c_*=u^(1/N)`, `q_*=v^(1/N)` lie in the strict bare image. An explicit
sufficient choice is

\[
 N>\max\{1,\ 3(1-u)/u,\ (1-u)^2/[u^2(1-v)]\}.
\]

Indeed the geometric-sum identities give

\[
 1-c_*\le(1-u)/(Nu),\qquad1-q_*\ge(1-v)/N.
\]

Hence `c_*>2/3` and `(1-c_*)^2<1-q_*`, so
`c_*<q_*<1-(1-c_*)^2=U(c_*)`. Construct one strict cell for that pair and
use its numerical parameters at `N` DISTINCT fresh sites. Equal parameter
values do not synchronize their natural bits. Factor `A` into `N+1` strict
ordinary survivals using

\[
 a_j=(N+1-j+jA)/(N+2-j+(j-1)A),\quad j=1,\ldots,N+1.
\]

Then the two physical products are exactly the requested `C,Q`. All
coordinates are real algebraic for real-algebraic input, and the usual
positive calendar/rate realization supplies finite positive edge rates.

For rational input, `g3_paired_cap2_word.py` additionally constructs an
ALL-RATIONAL witness suitable for the existing Source engine. It brackets
the positive roots by exact dyadic powers. Once their strict bare-image
neighbourhood is certified, choose rational first-cell coordinates near the
roots and use the exact rational product remainders for the last cell.
Openness ensures both are strict after finite refinement. The same-tuple
bare constructor then supplies rational arms/coins. The final direct product
check is mandatory.

The implementation doubles candidate counts and uses root-interval width
below `(1-v)/(16N)`. The piecewise `U` is increasing and 1-Lipschitz on
`[0,1]`. For `N` above the displayed bound with its last term doubled,
`U(c_*)-q_* >= (1-v)/(2N)`, so this interval test must succeed. No infinite
equality test at an earlier frontier or unproved stopping oracle is used.

## Even this small interface can need exponentially many explicit cells

For a cell write `dc=p(1-x)+h(1-y)` and
`dq=p^2(1-x)+h^2(1-y)`. The exact identity

\[
 dq[(1-x)+(1-y)]-dc^2=(1-x)(1-y)(2p-1)^2\ge0
\]

gives `dc^2<=2dq`. The lumped ordinary bank obeys the same weak bound.
For all `N+1` factors, product telescoping and Cauchy give

\[
 (1-C)^2\le(\sum dc_i)^2\le2(N+1)\sum dq_i
       \le2(N+1)(1-Q)/Q.
\]

Thus every rival private word satisfies

\[
                     N+1\ge Q(1-C)^2/[2(1-Q)].
\]

For rational targets `C=1/2`, `Q=1-1/j`, `j>=3`, this gives
`N>=(j-9)/8`. The constructive root-margin procedure succeeds by a dyadic
count at most `8j`. Their private minimum is therefore `Theta(j)`, whereas
the input bit length is `Theta(log j)`. A constant or polynomial-in-input-
length bound does not hold at this private interface; a total computable
bound and the simple strip decider do hold. No all-core minimum claim follows.

These words have INDEPENDENT pair survival tending to one, so a positive
lower I-anchor alone cannot extend the cap-three FACE bound to arbitrary
unequal-arm paired words. The face assumption is essential there.

## Actual integrated checks and remaining original scope

`verify_g3_paired_cap2_word.py` passed four strict bare constructors, five
paired words, four high-minimum-family controls, four exact exclusions and
two unsupported-input refusals. It then sent three new returned words
through the authenticated original Source constructor, admission checker,
strict calendar, stable native Code layout and COMMON/INDEPENDENT compiler.
All six original readout rows matched exactly. Full actual data/source are
encrypted in `[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]`, ciphertext SHA256
a04c3642f38c92743c01a01a85340302b32e8d880e8fdd0875d2048b10681d03.
No old suite, native Lean or model job was replayed.

The exact original readouts included two-descendant-slot quartet
discordances `C/3,Q/3` and rooted-event probabilities `C/6,Q/6`. On the
three-descendant slot, quartet probabilities stayed fixed while rooted
events were `C/12,Q/12`. This demonstrates both a legal kernel-coordinate
readout and why that readout cannot be inferred from every coarsening.

The private image can now replace unbounded cap-two word quantification by
one semialgebraic predicate inside a supplied joint core chart. Full original
G3 still needs all higher-cap/paired/tensor interfaces, source-faithful formal
reflection and all-template coverage. Its goal remains open.

The exact universal bare-cell bound and coordinate identities are retained
in `[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]`. The pair-loss identity, derivative
bound and seven-state quartet projection identity are retained in
`[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]`, ciphertext SHA256
a847da9221276fb01ae8c5b43efa7e56db77461f6103a9fceca9b814da54478b.
These are symbolic calculations plus the separate HAND proofs above.

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# A universal paired cap-three inequality and its complete equality boundary

Authored2026-10-22UTC. HAND proof and exact algebraic consumer. This concerns
one fresh unexposed natural private bridge word, at most THREE current roots,
ONE physical tuple for COMMON/INDEPENDENT, free strict arm/ordinary rates and
natural coins. The complete cap-three forest kernels are the inherited M of
their pair/triple coordinates. No arbitrary synchronized tensor, higher-cap
source law, independent review, native proof or full G3 closure is claimed.

Write the supplied complete paired tuple as `(C,D,Q,R)`: COMMON pair/triple,
INDEPENDENT pair/triple. This is not restricted to D=C^3.

## Universal all-length lower inequality

Every finite strict word satisfies

                 R >= P(C,Q) = 3 C Q^2 - 3 C^2 Q + C^3.             (1)

For a bare cell with h=1-p, put

    c=px+hy,  q=p^2x+h^2y+2ph,
    r=p^3x^3+h^3y^3+3phc.

The exact polynomial identity is

    r-P(c,q) = 3phc [p(1-x)-h(1-y)]^2 >=0.                       (2)

This holds for arbitrary unequal arms, not only the COMMON ordinary face.
Normalize `v=q/c>=1`, `w=r/c^3`, and let `f(v)=3v^2-3v+1`. Equation(2)
gives w>=f(v). Every strict bigon has v>1. The identity

    f(s)f(t)-f(st)=3(s-1)(t-1)(2st-s-t)

is nonnegative for s,t>=1, and strictly positive when both exceed1.
Induction on the finite word, with its ordinary factor contributing v=w=1,
therefore proves(1). It also shows that a word with at least TWO strict
bigons has STRICT inequality in(1). No bound on its original length was
used. Positivity of f on v>=1 justifies multiplying the individual bounds.

Consequently R<P(C,Q) is an exact ALL-FINITE-LENGTH exclusion at this private
interface, even if the two mechanisms can each fit their own projections.
It does not exclude arbitrary alternative original cores/response fibres.

## Equal pair coordinates are rigid

Every strict bigon has q>c. Thus Q=C forces zero bigons and
`D=R=C^3`. Conversely those coordinates have a positive ordinary witness
when0<C<1. The same private pair-rigidity also forces the entire capped
ordinary kernel at higher arities; it is not a new observation of that kernel.

## Complete equality-boundary theorem

Suppose0<C<Q<1 and R=P(C,Q). Then a finite strict word exists EXACTLY when

    A=2Q-C <1,  C^3<=D,  D Q^2 < C^3 A^2.                       (3)

Its private minimum is exactly ONE bigon. Along with the zero-cell case
above, this is a complete semialgebraic boundary decision without H(p).

Necessity: strictness after two bigons forces N=1. The one cell in(2) must
have balanced weighted losses `p(1-x)=h(1-y)`. Write its common mean as
c=C/A and d=1-c. Then

    x=1-d/(2p), y=1-d/(2h), q=(1+c)/2,

so the physical ordinary product is necessarily A=2Q-C. The arm constraints
are p,h>d/2. With t=ph this is `(1-c^2)/4<t<=1/4`, and its COMMON triple is

    Phi(t)=1-3d+d^2(3+d)/(4t)-d^3/(8t^2).

Its derivative is `d^2[d-(3+d)t]/(4t^3)<0` on that interval. Indeed at its
left endpoint the numerator's bracket is
`-c(c-1)(c-3)/4<0` and it decreases with t. Endpoint values are

    Phi(1/4)=c^3,
    Phi((1-c^2)/4)=4c^3/(1+c)^2.

The latter endpoint is excluded by strict arm positivity. Multiplying this
range by A^3 gives exactly the two D conditions in(3).

Sufficiency: assume(3), put c=C/A,d=1-c and D0=D/A^3. The strict monotone
range just proved supplies a unique t in that interval with Phi(t)=D0.
It is real algebraic for algebraic input: solve the quadratic

    8(D0-1+3d)t^2 -2d^2(3+d)t +d^3 =0

on the specified interval. Choose `p=(1+sqrt(1-4t))/2`, then the above x,y.
The arms/coin are strict. Positive ordinary bookends
`z=(1+A)/2`, `a=2A/(1+A)` have product A. The same physical tuple gives
COMMON(C,D), INDEPENDENT(Q,R), and therefore both full cap-three forest
kernels. Direct substitution is the final implementation check.

For example C=8/25,D=26/625,Q=14/25,R=2528/15625 lies strictly OFF the
COMMON ordinary face and has A=4/5, p=3/5, x=1/2,y=1/4. The minimum is1.
The bare tuple C=2/5,D=13/160,Q=7/10,R=79/250 instead has A=1 and is
excluded for EVERY finite strict private length. So is equality at the
upper D boundary in(3). Extra bigons cannot repair these endpoints while

## Independent projection fits are insufficient, even off the COMMON face

Consider the exact tuple

    C=1/2, D=13/100, Q=117/200, R=85293/500000.

bookends7/8,6/7, coin1/2, arms `2/3 +/- 2sqrt(3)/45`.

coin1/2, arms1/5,2/5. It also satisfies0<C<Q<1 and D>C^3. Nevertheless

    R-P(C,Q) = -58003/2000000 <0.

Thus NO finite same-tuple paired private word realizes it. This rules out
using the intersection of separately feasible COMMON/I images and the

> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. # Rational paired cap-three kernels with arbitrarily large exact word minimum

21 October 2026. Authored HAND theorem and exact finite controls. No historical
novelty, independent review, Lean pass or complete G3 recognition is claimed.
This is a private-word kernel theorem; it does not add those coordinates to an
original observation menu, or exclude alternative original cores.

## A universal gain bound for one physical paired cell

For one strict natural bigon, write h=1-p and

    C=p*x+h*y,                       (COMMON pair no-merger)
    Q=p^2*x+h^2*y+2*p*h,             (INDEPENDENT pair)
    R=p^3*x^3+h^3*y^3+3*p^2*h*x+3*p*h^2*y. (INDEPENDENT triple)

The same physical x,y,p must occur in all three. Direct expansion gives

    3*C*Q-2*R
      = p^3*x^2*(3-2*x) + h^3*y^2*(3-2*y) + 3*p*h*x*y > 0.     (1)

All summands are positive for 0<x,y,p<1. Thus

    R/(C*Q) < 3/2.                                           (2)

NO equal-arm/ordinary-COMMON-face assumption is needed. The bound is sharp
as a supremum: at p=1/2 and x=y=s, its left side is

    rho(s)=(s^2+3)/(2*(1+s)) -> 3/2 as s->0+.

For any legal private word with L bigons and positive ordinary passage
product A<1, all three no-merger coordinates multiply on serial current-root
composition. An ordinary survival a contributes a,a,a^3 respectively. Hence
the entire paired word satisfies

    T := R_word/(C_word*Q_word)
       = A * product_i [R_i/(C_i*Q_i)] < (3/2)^L.             (3)

This includes L=0: T=A<1. Each multiplying scalar comes from the SAME word
and parameter tuple. No independent mode-by-mode refit is used. For any
supplied budget B, the exact comparison `T >= (3/2)^B` excludes EVERY word
of length at most B, even with unequal arms and freely chosen strict coins.
This is a LOWER bound on required length, never a stopping UPPER bound.

## Every positive integer occurs as an exact minimum

Given N>=1, choose N identical bigons with

    x=y=s=1/(10*N), p=1/2,

and give their N+1 ordinary passages product A=9/10. All can be rational
and strict: let M=10(N+1) and use passage survivals

    a_j=(M-j)/(M-j+1), j=1,...,N+1.

The telescoping product is 9/10. This is an actual legal positive word on
an eligible bridge, not a fractional cell or source mixture. Its coordinates
are the rational numbers

    C_N=A*s^N,
    Q_N=A*((1+s)/2)^N,
    R_N=A^3*(s*(s^2+3)/4)^N.

Its COMMON triple also equals C_N^3, but competitors do not need that extra
coordinate for the following lower bound. Its gain is

    T_N=A*rho(s)^N.

Because rho(s)>(3/2)/(1+s), and

    (1+1/(10N))^N
      = sum_(k=0)^N binom(N,k)/(10N)^k
      <= sum_(k=0)^N 10^(-k) < 10/9,

we have

    T_N > (81/100)*(3/2)^N
        = (243/200)*(3/2)^(N-1) > (3/2)^(N-1).               (4)

Every competing representation with L<=N-1 contradicts (3). The displayed
N-cell word attains the target, so its minimum number of bigons is EXACTLY N
among all strict paired private words. Full paired cap-three forest-kernel
agreement would in particular match the three coordinates used here.

## Consequence and limits for G3

There is no universal fixed bigon cap for paired cap-three private kernels,
even on four taxa with a fixed eligible bridge type and rational source
parameters. This rules out extending the I-only one-bigon theorem to any
input-independent constant for BOTH at this interface. The older scoped
minimum-two example remains valid; (1)--(4) give an unbounded exact family.

The bound is computable from SUPPLIED target coordinates and useful for
rejecting a supplied search budget. It does not give an input-effective
upper bound on ONE witness. Input encodings grow in this family. Nor does
it prove a lower bound over ALL original core templates under an arbitrary
coarsened topology menu. The inherited fixed-alphabet pair-budget upper
bound is consistent with this result: its positive pair target decreases
with N here. There is no undecidability inference.

The general G3 recognition/NO-termination goal remains OPEN. A complete
solver must retain the real same-source count issue for BOTH, while using
the separately scoped I-only cap-three branch where justified.

`paired-cap3-count-checks.wl` checks (1), the sharp limit, telescoping strict
passages and exact two-sided gain bounds for N=1,...,12. These are finite
controls; the arbitrary-N proof is the hand argument above.

# An all-length paired bound involving the COMMON triple

Authored2026-10-22UTC by the existing G3 owner. HAND finite-product proof,
executed exact polynomial identity and exact consumer controls. This concerns
ONE fresh natural paired private word through at most three current roots,
with free strict rates/bookends and the same physical tuple in both modes.
It is not an all-core topology-observation exclusion or original G3 closure.

Every such finite word satisfies the STRICT inequality

                           R > D Q,                         (1)

where (C,D,Q,R) are COMMON pair/triple, INDEPENDENT pair/triple coordinates.
This adds a genuinely D-dependent necessary condition to the earlier bound
R>=3CQ^2-3C^2Q+C^3. Passing these conditions is not sufficient for membership.

## Positive polynomial certificate and product proof

For a bare cell put h=1-p and

    d=p x^3+h y^3,
    q=p^2 x+h^2 y+2ph,
    r=p^3 x^3+h^3 y^3+3ph(p x+h y).

The exact identity is

    r-dq = p^3 x^3(1-x)+h^3 y^3(1-y)
      +ph[p x(3-2x^2-y^3)+h y(3-2y^2-x^3)].                 (2)

All summands are positive in the strict physical domain 0<x,y,p<1. In
particular 2x^2+y^3<3 and 2y^2+x^3<3. Hence each cell has r>dq.

For N cells and ordinary bank A in (0,1),

    R=A^3 product r_i,
    DQ=A^4 product(d_i q_i).

For N>=1 their ratio is A^-1 product[r_i/(d_i q_i)]>1. For N=0 the ratio
is simply A^-1>1. This proves(1) for EVERY finite length, including ordinary
words, without a word-length bound or a closure argument. Equality is also
excluded at every admitted finite length.

The consumer also retains the elementary all-word ranges

    0<C<=Q<1,        C^3<=D<C,        0<R<Q.

The COMMON lower range is Jensen on every cell; the upper range follows
from x^3<x and the ordinary factor. The INDEPENDENT pair/triple range follows
from the nested no-merger events under the retained full capped forest law,
with positive strict ordinary exposure. The previous polynomial lower bound
and(1) are checked alongside them. No extra legal observable is introduced.

## A new exclusion with separate strict rational witnesses

Take a COMMON-only word with ordinary bookends199/200,198/199, arm survivals
99/100,199/6600 and first-parent probability3/5. Its coordinates are

    C=3/5,
    D=2259594913797/4000000000000.

Take a different INDEPENDENT-only word with bookends19/20,18/19, arm
survivals9/10,1/10 and coin1/2. Its coordinates are

    Q=27/40,
    R=271917/800000.

Both separate witnesses are strictly physical and rational. Combining the
two projections into the candidate paired tuple passes the strict pair
strip, the COMMON moment range and the old coupled lower bound:

    R-P(C,Q)=26217/800000 >0.

But

    R-DQ = -6625662672519/160000000000000 <0.

Thus NO finite shared-tuple private word has those four coordinates. This
exclusion is not supplied by the old lower bound or by separately fitting
the two mechanisms. The same private exclusion holds on R=DQ.

These coordinates are not claimed to be a known all-core observable fibre.
Turning this into an original topology NO would require the actual legal
decoder and exclusion of every other protected template/source fibre.

## Failed stronger conjecture and actual controls

The tempting stronger inequality R^2>=D Q^3 is FALSE. Exact real elimination
returned a strict bare-cell counterexample; a simpler strict rational
control uses ordinary bookends19/20,18/19 and

    x=1/10000, y=1/2, p=1-1/1000000.

Its direct physical coordinates have R^2<D Q^3. This failed conjecture is
retained and is not a necessary-condition filter. More generally, the
bare family x=t^2,y=1/2,1-p=t^3 has q of order t^2, d of order t^3 and r of
order t^5; it explains why such stronger homogeneous powers can fail near
the coin/arm boundary. No endpoint cell is admitted into the actual word.

PairedCap3NecessaryConditions.wl returns a scoped ALL-FINITE-PRIVATE-WORD
NO only when a proved condition fails. Otherwise its status is
PASSES_PAIRED_CAP3_NECESSARY_CONDITIONS with MembershipEstablished->False.
Unsupported or unresolved arithmetic remains Failure. It never returns a
source witness, a general private membership YES or an original G3 NO.

The first software revision failed two exclusion controls: Return inside
Do was consumed by that iteration, so the filter fell through to the pass
record. A direct diagnostic reproduced the Wolfram control-flow behavior.
The repair evaluates the finite condition list, selects the first non-True
decision and returns OUTSIDE the iteration construct. The original failed
source/result/diagnostic are retained, rather than relabelled a pass.

After this repair VerifyPairedCap3NecessaryConditions.wl passed ALL10 exact
controls: the polynomial certificate, both separate rational witnesses,
new exclusion beyond the old bound, strict equality exclusion, ordinary and
actual one-/two-cell necessary passes, inexact refusal and the stronger
conjecture's strict counterexample. This was pure exact arithmetic, with no
Source compiler/native parser/Lean/Lake/model or old-suite replay. Hosted
undefined-symbol prevalidation warnings remain in the record.

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. # Exact paired cap-three one-cell quartic

Authored 2026-10-22 UTC by the existing G3 owner. HAND proof with executed
exact symbolic identities and exact algebraic controls. No new source-law,
Lean elaboration, original-source admission or all-word recognition claim.
This continues G3-PAIRED-CAP3-COUPLED-LOWER-BOUNDARY.md and reuses its full
cap-three paired-kernel boundary, rather than fitting the two modes separately.

## Statement and strict physical domain

Let (C,D,Q,R) be the COMMON pair/triple and INDEPENDENT pair/triple survival
coordinates of one fresh natural private word, on at most three entering
current roots. Each cell has a fresh original inheritance bit, common only
within that cell in COMMON mode. One physical arm/rate/coin tuple must supply
both modes. Ordinary passages have survival in (0,1), both arms have survival
in (0,1), and the first-parent probability p is in (0,1). The original compiler
uses parent1 probability gamma=1-p. No clock cost or fixed-source-rate menu is
being imposed in this scalar private-word interface.

For one cell, with h=1-p and ordinary-bank product A in (0,1), the coordinates
are

    C = A (p x+h y),             D = A^3 (p x^3+h y^3),
    Q = A (p^2 x+h^2 y+2ph),
    R = A^3 (p^3 x^3+h^3 y^3+3ph(p x+h y)).

These four coordinates identify the full capped forest kernels only through
the retained cap-three source/forest theorem and freshness/grafting premises.
The new theorem below is an exact algebraic equivalence for this physical
one-cell parameterization. It does not supply that source receiver.

Write

    P(C,Q) = 3 C Q^2-3 C^2 Q+C^3,
    Delta = R-P(C,Q).

The previous lower-boundary result already handles Q=C, Delta<0 and Delta=0
with their explicitly stated all-finite-private-word conclusions. Assume here

    0<C<Q<1,                 Delta>0.

Set the target-dependent constants

    S = 2Q-C,                g = 4 Delta/(3C)>0.

For one unknown ordinary bank A define

    Z = A-S,                 W = Z^2+g,                 T = S Z-g,
    N(A) = C^3 W(W+Z^2)-6 C^2 W T Z
           +3 C T^2(W+Z^2)-2 T^3 Z,
    F(A) = N(A)-D g^2.

There is a strict physical one-cell word with exactly the supplied FOUR
coordinates if and only if there is a real A such that

    0<A<1,
    4(Q-C)(A-Q)>g,
    C^2 W>T^2,
    F(A)=0.

F has degree exactly four: its leading coefficient is 16(C-Q)^3, which is
strictly negative in this branch. This is a one-variable real-algebraic test.
It is complete for at most one cell; no fixed-dimensional quantifier search
over unrelated COMMON and INDEPENDENT witnesses is used.

## Forward derivation

Start with a physical one-cell witness. Put c=C/A, q=Q/A,

    u=p(1-x),     v=h(1-y),     delta=u-v,     e=A delta.

The retained exact coupled identity is

    R-P(C,Q)=3ph C A^2 delta^2.

Delta>0 implies delta!=0. Exchanging the two fresh arms and their probabilities
preserves all four coordinates, so assume e>0. Direct expansion gives

    Z = (2p-1)e,
    g = 4ph e^2,
    W = e^2,
    T = e(Ap x-Ah y).

Hence

    p = (1+Z/e)/2,
    x = (C e+T)/(A(e+Z)),
    y = (C e-T)/(A(e-Z)).

As g>0, e>|Z|. Positivity of the two arms is exactly C^2 W>T^2. Their strict
upper bounds reduce to A-C>e. In the current domain this is equivalent to

    (A-C)^2-W = 4(Q-C)(A-Q)-g >0.

For the COMMON triple coordinate, substitution gives

    A^3(p x^3+h y^3)
      = [(C e+T)^3(e-Z)^2+(C e-T)^3(e+Z)^2]/(2e g^2)
      = N(A)/g^2.

Thus F(A)=0 and all the displayed strict constraints follow.

## Reverse construction and strictness

Conversely take a real A satisfying the four constraints. Let e=sqrt(W)>0
and use the same formulas for p,x,y. Since W=Z^2+g and g>0, both e+Z and e-Z
are positive, and 0<p<1. Since C>0 and C^2 W>T^2, both arm numerators are
positive. The linear strict constraint forces

    A>Q+g/[4(Q-C)]>Q>C,
    (A-C)^2>W,

so A-C>e. In the two upper-arm tests the numerator differences are
e(A-C+e) and e(A-C-e), respectively. Both are strictly positive; hence
0<x,y<1. No equality or limiting zero-length arm has been admitted.

The four coordinate formulas now reconstruct C and Q directly, reconstruct
R as P(C,Q)+3Cg/4, and reconstruct D as N(A)/g^2. They are the supplied
coordinates, on ONE shared tuple. Two strict bookends suffice:

    z=(1+A)/2,                a=2A/(1+A),                za=A.

Both z and a lie in (0,1). Since C<Q, an ordinary-only word cannot supply the
pair. Every successful one-cell witness therefore has minimum private count
exactly one, even if longer words can also realize the same tuple.

## Consumer, execution and bounds of the result

PairedCap3OneCell.wl reuses the exact input/decision helpers in
Cap3PrivateWordCertificate.wl and the physical four-coordinate verifier in
PairedCap3LowerBoundary.wl. It exposes the quartic polynomial/formula and an
exact algebraic witness constructor. Each successful witness is checked
again by direct evaluation of ALL FOUR physical coordinates and every strict
parameter. Inexact or nonalgebraic inputs are refused. Failure to resolve or
return a witness remains Failure.

The generic negative result is explicitly

    NO_AT_MOST_ONE_PAIRED_CAP3_PRIVATE_CELL,
    LongerWords -> OPEN_BY_THIS_TEST.

The earlier proved all-word lower-boundary exclusions retain their separate
status when delegated to that consumer. The generic quartic's empty feasible
set is not an unrestricted private-word NO, and none of these statuses is an
all-original-source G3 NO.

VerifyPairedCap3OneCell.wl actually passed 13 exact controls in the existing
Wolfram mathematical evaluator: three rational biased/unequal-arm witnesses,
one genuine real-algebraic witness, the degree/known-bank constraint, lower
boundary and ordinary delegation, the universal coupled exclusion and pair
rigidity, a genuine strict two-cell word rejected by the one-cell solver,
tampered-coordinate rejection, and inexact/nonalgebraic refusals. The four
new generic witness counts were 1,1,1,1. No original Source, native parser,
Lean/Lake or model suite was executed for these controls.

The reconstruction identities independently returned {0,0,0,0}. The leading
coefficient, strict-constraint polynomial identity and expanded COMMON triple
numerator were also checked exactly. New runtime records were encrypted with
the existing featurectl identity before first persistence:

    [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]
    ciphertext SHA256
    51070f60571f1ea382b42e70d96395019f7769e904d487a497f3f174be566cee

    [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately]
    ciphertext SHA256
    5690f2a6524d788baf056a19680f30b1b6377c9f4b6cd83a8cc64a931401d2e4

The evaluator's undefined-symbol prevalidation warning is retained in the
second record; the returned 13 named controls all passed. This is executed
exact algebra, alongside a HAND proof, and is not a Lean/kernel pass.

Remaining work: the generic strict interior can require two or more private
cells. This quartic supplies a small exact YES path and a bounded exclusion,
not a bound for those larger words. Higher entering-root caps, arbitrary
coupled panels, actual graph/reflection/readout suppliers and the original
all-input H/terminating-NO objective remain open.

   PHYSICAL-APPROXIMATION-COMPOSITION.md,6856B/SHA256
   ebb548e27e409a3752868afa3e8463fc9760856bad766d81f602e4f6c8dc71b1.
   The complete later source explicitly distinguishes separate-mode
   approximation from a same-tuple BOTH supplier and retains the changing

26854d63176a6dd5c91b45b2178143d24dc408eff625bdc1455c82f1f07bef1a.
It supplies computable B(m,eta) for POSITIVE rational error eta. One actual
finite strict private word approximates BOTH complete forest kernels through
cap m. Its leading ordinary edge may be retained exactly. No exposed private
bit, arbitrary new tie or exact source-size H is supplied by it.
R2 samples ONLY complete positive bigon/connector cells. This repairs R1's
literal-leading-edge proof detail without changing or rerunning its abstract
rounding control. R1 remains immutable with its original bytes and receipt.

**Classification:** integration of the OLD actual compiler with that new HAND
supplier, filling its inspected paired-effectivity use-site. No additional
matrix/source producer, generic Code factory or cap ladder is selected.
This is not an exhaustive prior-absence or historical-priority assertion.

## 2. Why the fresh slot is the right source object

Use the ORIGINAL finite explicit-ID topology/control/observation grammar.
One finite source and ONE tuple supply all rows. Protect every supplied ID,
fixed/read-only site, shared configuration use, box-template boundary and
endpoint of a supplied finite parameter relation BEFORE reducing the source.
Keep the root-containing blob and the actual source's cut-child/planarity/
labelled provenance. The inherited catalogue is finite for this input.

An unbounded remainder is then a fresh unmarked word on an ELIGIBLE original
bridge slot. It is not an arbitrary replaceable core arc. Its physical cells
have independent fresh parameters/IDs. A private COMMON bit is drawn once
for that whole cell and is marginalized after its one use; the independent
mode routes each surviving CURRENT root. Native gamma=1-p for original
parent0 weight p. Repeating numerical values never identifies the bit IDs.

No finite input row reads, forces or reuses these fresh bits: a site with
such a use would have been protected. Thus a slot's natural kernel is the
same complete labelled-forest kernel for every applicable entering state,
with old trees carried as opaque tokens. The finite original control bank
is retained outside that kernel and is summed ONCE by the joint compiler.
Its distribution can correlate entering forests and other populations; this
does not fit those marginals independently or freeze the exterior program.
Conditioning here is on the retained/used history, not on a fixed full
assignment of all FUTURE private bits. Their original once-drawn natural law
is marginalized at its correct use; it is not refreshed after exposure.

For a conditional boundary retain the old bank as a READ-ONLY index: the
fresh natural kernel acts on its entering forest and leaves that index
unchanged. This is a tensor with an identity on the old register, not a new
independent draw. The uniform full-forest error survives such conditioning,
opaque grafting and the original joint summation. Distinct mode blocks use
the SAME sampled physical private word. The old compiler still evaluates
every original observation map and shared randomized program as declared.

This paragraph uses the source grammar's actual protected/fresh boundary.
It does NOT extend the theorem to a different interface that exposes new
private bits, updates an exported register inside an unbounded slot, imposes
an additional relation on arbitrary fresh positions, or prescribes a new
metric/calendar law. A genuine coupled fresh-slot supplier, if such a
different interface is admitted, cannot be replaced by marginal products.

## 3. A finite compact algebraic approximation for the whole input

Let c run over the inherited finite complete core catalogue. Its bounded
semialgebraic strict parameter domain is D_c; keep all named original
equalities, weak controls and strict admission conditions. Its ACTUAL closure
cl(D_c) is computable by RCF. It is not obtained merely by replacing every
written strict sign by a weak sign. The usual quantified-neighborhood
formula defines it and RCF eliminates the quantifiers.

Let s=1,...,r_c be its independent fresh private slots. Retain the paired
forest kernel of every slot at a common computable cap m>=2, sufficient for
every physically sampled allocation in the menu. The old polynomial map

    F_c(theta,K_1,...,K_(r_c))

is the COMPLETE authorized response vector. Its coefficients are effectively
real-algebraic. Its JOINT state is not the product of separately averaged
lineage marginals. Every distinct slot contributes its full conditional
forest law at its single source occurrence.

All kernel coordinates and core survival/inheritance coordinates lie in
[0,1]. A rational L_c>=1 is effectively available such that, for the same
theta and any two slot tuples in that cube,

    ||F_c(theta,K)-F_c(theta,K')||_infinity
        <=L_c * max_s ||K_s-K'_s||_infinity.               (1)

For example, expand the finite polynomial compiler and bound each partial
derivative by its absolute coefficient sum; sum the bounds over all kernel
coordinates and take the largest response bound. Rational upper bounds on
the finitely many algebraic coefficients are computable. Set L>=1 to the
largest L_c. There is no inversion or unproved conditioning floor here.

Given rational0<epsilon<=1 choose eta=epsilon/(2L) and B=B(m,eta). The
paired supplier replaces EVERY actual private word, keeping one tuple and
leading ordinary edge, by one strict word of at most B bigons. Its maximum
row-sum error bounds each coordinate error by eta. Applying(1) gives whole
response error<epsilon/2, while keeping theta and its protected ties exactly.

For each c define A_(c,B) by using cl(D_c) and canonical B-cell words at
every fresh slot, with all fresh word coordinates in[0,1], SAME coordinates
for both mechanisms. Boundary identity padding includes fewer cells. If a
finite retained relation involves a leading ordinary edge, retain that edge
in the finite core/domain and use the supplier's unchanged leading factor.
No unrelated core or word coordinates are closed independently across a tie.

Each A_(c,B) is the compact semialgebraic RESPONSE IMAGE of this domain
under its one finite polynomial source map. Define

    A_B = union_c A_(c,B),   C = closure(actual original response image).

The OLD compactification and strict density give A_B subset C: every such
finite boundary tuple is a limit of admitted strict sources with the SAME
protected domain/word assignment. Conversely every actual response is
within epsilon/2 of A_B by the replacement above. Taking limits, using the
compactness of A_B, gives

    A_B subset C subset {p : dist_infinity(p,A_B)<=epsilon/2}.       (2)

This is one total construction for arbitrary finite menus/caps under this
source grammar. It is neither a list of cap-specific ranks nor an exact

## 4. Actual scope of the resulting NO certificate

    max(0,d_B-epsilon/2) <= d <= d_B.                      (3)

At epsilon=2^(-j), a certificate d_B>epsilon is sound original all-core NO.
It excludes every admitted finite source, of every private-word length,
using the paired approximation proof rather than an assumed count bound.
Equivalently the finite RCF test that p is within epsilon of A_B returns

If d>0, these tests eventually succeed: A_B subset C implies d_B>=d, and

Dovetailing this branch with the OLD finite-source RCF enumeration returns

> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. # A polynomial tube around the paired ordinary face

22 October2026. HAND candidate, self-audited, UNREVIEWED/UNCOMPILED.
Original G3 remains OPEN. This is a word-length-uniform necessary invariant
and a closure-face statement, not a complete recognition theorem.

## Exact question and predecessor/successor comparison

Use one fresh unexposed, untied private bridge word

    W=E(z) B(x1,y1,p1) E(a1) ... B(xN,yN,pN) E(aN),

with every parameter in(0,1). The SAME tuple supplies COMMON and natural
INDEPENDENT kernels. Each occurrence has its own original ID/bit. Current
roots carry their old trees opaquely. Here p is parent0 probability and the
native parent1 convention is gamma=1-p. No intermediate state is observed.

The exact finite-word implication C=Q => N=0 is ALREADY supplied by
G3-PAIRED-CAP2-STRICT-IMAGE.md and explicitly reused at all arities in
G3-PAIRED-CAP3-COUPLED-LOWER-BOUNDARY.md. It is NOT a new theorem here.
Both complete bodies were reread. The former's source hash is
b7d8bf1ab66d57a28acab6f5ea0186de81bf695e208d1176e7c7e3822dbbdc1b.

Older original-source predecessor ACTUALLY read COMPLETE at Commons
8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6:
research/2026-10-08-dot-g4-paired-natural-tree-certificate-2250z/
PAIRED-NATURAL-TREE-CERTIFICATE-AND-GENERAL-TARGET-GAP.md.
It already gives a finite ordinary-tree diagnostic in its declared BOTH
menu. Its zero-gap argument and positive-gap presentation counterfamily
are reused; neither is recounted as new.

Later sources actually compared at that same immutable pin:

* research/2026-10-13-codex-g4-renewed/whole-source/
  UNCALIBRATED-PAIR-GAP.md, COMPLETE: its proposed original crossed-cherry
  monotonicity/zero set is a different, stronger-observer transport question.
* Same project, chronology/continuation-1837z/
  PRIVATE-BOTH-FINITE-FORCING.md, COMPLETE: target-dependent semantic forcing
  for equal-arm targets, with COMMON clock and actual finite-persistence
  suppliers. No general effective stopping follows from it.
* general-algebra/continuation-2110z/GENERAL-PRIVATE-BOTH-LOCAL-EXCLUSION.md,
  selected Sections1,2,4,5: its local fixed-COMMON-fibre argument uses a
  full-kernel equal-arm estimate with a bounded target clock. Its intervening
  differential proof was not completely reread here.
* G3-SAME-TUPLE-PAIRED-APPROXIMATION-R2.md and
  G3-PAIRED-CLOSURE-ORIGINAL-COMPILER.md, COMPLETE: positive-error paired
  approximation is available, with exact boundary selection still open.

The proposed additional implication is an effective ALL-CAP polynomial tube,
valid for unequal arms and all word lengths, around the ordinary kernels
matched to EACH mode's own pair coordinate. Its positive-pair closure
consequence does not follow merely from strictness of each finite factor.
A bounded comparison of31 named paired/zero-score Markdown sources found
the suppliers above. This is not exhaustive absence or a novelty claim.

## Uniform statement

Fix any finite current-root cap m>=2. Use the OLD complete labelled-forest
polynomial kernels E_m(s), B_C,m(x,y,p), B_I,m(x,y,p), including opaque grafts.
Their retained algebra supplier is
research/2026-10-01-g4-admitted-testers-0819z/forest_algebra.py at Commons
07c9a510b594655a62c609a7e354ecfe5752e35f, Gitblob
edec614abba57800e220c3580549014335f0d1c4, SHA256
850589b346a6cc000e102c594a1ebc6342e9e1ba4604edace20fe5ecdc385884.
Its full source was read earlier in this conversation and is reused, not
run again. The same admitted-testers PROOF.md supplies the actual graphical
grammar/paired-current-root interpretation, SHA661696b322c1ee2f57ffeb45ada556808f945d698ef0187c1a32ec0d881e40a1.
Let ||.|| be the maximum absolute row-sum norm. Write C=d_C(W), Q=d_I(W).
There is a computable rational L_m>=1, generated from these polynomials,
such that EVERY actual strict W satisfies, for mu=C and mu=I,

    ||K_mu(W)-E_m(d_mu(W))|| <= L_m log(Q/C)
                              <= L_m (Q-C)/C.             (1)

In particular the following are closed semialgebraic necessary conditions:

    0<=C<=Q<=1,
    C ||K_C-E_m(C)|| <= L_m(Q-C),
    C ||K_I-E_m(Q)|| <= L_m(Q-C).                           (2)

One algorithm produces the rational constant for arbitrary finite m. No
sequence of fitted cap-specific constants or new forest engine is used.
The norm in(2) is a finite maximum of sums of absolute values, so its graph
and inequalities are semialgebraic. Entrywise versions are valid as well.

## Polynomial construction of L_m

For a bare cell put h=1-p and

    c=px+hy,  q=p^2 x+h^2 y+2ph,
    Delta=q-c=ph(2-x-y).

For each mode form the MATRIX polynomial

    F_mu(x,y,p)=B_mu,m(x,y,p)-E_m(d_mu(B)).

At p=0 both actual modes are E_m(y); at p=1 both are E_m(x).
Every entry of F_mu is therefore divisible by p(1-p) in Q[x,y,p].
Write F_mu=p(1-p)G_mu. At x=y=1 the actual cell and its pair-matched
ordinary kernel are both identity. Hence G_mu(1,1,p)=0 as a polynomial.
There are computable matrix polynomials H_mu,x,H_mu,y with

    G_mu=(1-x)H_mu,x+(1-y)H_mu,y.                           (3)

For example subtract G_mu(1,y,p) before division by1-x, and divide
G_mu(1,y,p)-G_mu(1,1,p) by1-y. These are exact polynomial divisions.
They do not fit an asymptotic normalized source direction.

For a rational polynomial H let |H|_coef be its absolute coefficient sum.
On the CLOSED unit cube, |H|<=|H|_coef. Choose L_m>=1 above the maximum of
the coefficient row-sum bounds, separately for each H matrix in each mode.
Then(3) gives

    ||B_mu,m-E_m(d_mu(B))|| <= L_m ph(2-x-y)=L_m Delta.     (4)

All boundary evaluations here are polynomial identities used for bounds;
endpoint inheritance or zero exposure is not admitted as a strict source.
Finite polynomial kernel generation, exact divisions and rational coefficient
arithmetic make L_m total computable. No RCF oracle or word bound is assumed.

## From cells to the whole ordered word

An ordinary connector has the SAME parameter in both modes. The old
semigroup identity E(s)E(t)=E(st) and stochastic contraction give

    ||B_mu E(a)-E(a*d_mu(B))|| <= L_m Delta.

Replace the cells in their ACTUAL order and telescope. Only after replacement
are all factors ordinary and combined. Thus

    ||K_mu(W)-E(d_mu(W))|| <= L_m sum_i Delta_i.            (5)

This preserves full matrices, all entering forests and opaque grafts; it is
not a diagonal-only calculation or permission to commute physical cells.
The positive leading edge and every connector cancel from the ratio:

    Q/C=product_i(q_i/c_i).

Since0<c_i<=q_i<=1,

    log(q_i/c_i)=-log(1-Delta_i/q_i)
                   >=Delta_i/q_i>=Delta_i.

Summation proves the first inequality in(1); log t<=t-1 proves the second.
There is no bound on N, no per-cell margin, no equal-arm hypothesis and no
COMMON/I clock equality. Static old registers are not refreshed.

## A directly inductive semialgebraic invariant

The tube(2), together with stochasticity, is closed under multiplying two
paired kernels that each satisfy it. Indeed stochastic telescoping and the
ordinary semigroup identity bound each product's deviation by the sum of
the two deviations. For pair coordinates(C,Q) and(c,q), multiplication by
Cc leaves the upper bound

    L_m[c(Q-C)+C(q-c)] <= L_m(Qq-Cc),

because the difference is L_m(Q-C)(q-c)>=0. This argument also works when
C or c is zero; its left side then vanishes where appropriate.
Each physical cell satisfies the tube by(4), since its c<=1, and ordinary
initializations satisfy it with zero error. Thus(2) is an explicit member
of the original reduction's semialgebraic invariant language. It can be
used in an actual finite core/word state without storing an unknown length.
No claim that this certificate language is complete is made.
Here C,Q are tracked multiplicative state coordinates; on actual source
states they are the retained two-current-root no-merger entries. This does
not assert multiplicativity for an arbitrary synthetic stochastic matrix's
unconstrained entry or admit such a matrix as a physical source.

## Positive-pair closure face, and protected leading fields

By continuity,(2) holds in the paired kernel closure. If a closure point has
C=Q=s>0, it necessarily has BOTH complete kernels equal to E_m(s).
This is the new quantitative closure consequence. The exact finite-word
rigidity used to decide this face is OLD: every strict cell has q>c, so
an actual finite word on that face has N=0.

If z is FREE, an ordinary E(s) is a zero-cell witness for0<s<1.
If z is a PROTECTED static field, N=0 instead forces s=z. A replacement
E(s) is not permitted merely because it has the same total kernel.
An explicit nonclosed inductive set in that canonical fixed-z grammar is

    {C=Q=z, K_C=K_I=E(z)}
      UNION {0<C<Q<z, stochastic paired K satisfying(2)}.  (6)

A strict append enters or remains in the second branch. The zero-cell
initialization is the first. This gives a finite exact exclusion on this
private interface when an equal-pair target disagrees with the protected
leading field. It reuses the old scalar strictness, not a new all-core NO.

For example z=1/2 and paired target(E(1/4),E(1/4)) is NO in that fixed-z
canonical grammar, but lies in its actual paired closure at EVERY finite cap.
Use ONE cell with x=2/3,y=1/3,a=3/4 and p_n=1-1/n, n>=2. Each tuple is strict,
uses distinct original occurrence/bit semantics, and has

    C_n=1/4-1/(8n),
    Q_n=1/4+1/(4n)-3/(8n^2).

Polynomial continuity gives both full kernels ->E(1/4). The limiting p=1
is not an admitted natural coin. This is a protected-field binding of the
old equal-pair rigidity. It does not exclude other original cores or new
ordinary fields outside that declared grammar.

## Why absolute pair gap without a positive anchor is insufficient

At C=Q=0 the polynomial tube intentionally gives no restriction.
There is a concrete physical closure guard. Take z=1/2,p=1/2 and let both
arm survivals x=y=e and the connector a=e tend to zero. Every e in(0,1)
gives a strict one-cell word. Its pair coordinates are

    C=z e^2,   Q=z e(1+e)/2,

so Q-C->0 and both tend to zero. COMMON tends to ordinary completion E(0).
For four singleton tokens the limiting I cell completes each routed colour
group, then its two groups merge in the upper ordinary completion.
Six of the sixteen equally likely routings split2+2 and produce a balanced
tree; two put all four in one group, with ordinary balanced probability1/3;
the other eight give a comb. Its balanced probability is therefore5/12,
against1/3 for ordinary completion. After the leading E(z), the difference
is z^6/12=1/768: on all smaller current-root states the completed first-pair
extension is already the ordinary one, and the four-root no-merger mass is z^6.

Thus a uniform bound tending to zero with Q-C alone would be false.
The ratio in(1), or the positive C anchor for its closed-face consequence,
is essential. This boundary guard is not an admitted zero-exposure target
or a full original-source compiler execution.

## Original G3 use and unresolved endpoint

The old source/path grammar supplies the finite templates and correct fresh
slot state. Apply(2) to such a slot, or tensor its full kernel with the
identity on a genuinely read-only old bank, then use the actual joint
compiler. A finite RCF contradiction with these necessary constraints is a
sound NO on that supplied template. Every alternative template must still
be excluded before returning original all-core NO. A legal decoder must
actually bind any pair/kernel coordinates used from observations.

An exported private bit, cross-slot synchronization, updated external
register, changed clock interface or arbitrary graph core does not acquire
this private supplier by notation. Earlier all-source ordinary-tree forcing
retains its own stronger source proof and menu. It is not reproved here.

The remaining original G3 task is exact strict-fibre recognition at ALL
inputs. Neither(1),(2),(6), the old equal-pair corollary nor the new closure
estimate supplies a total H, completeness of invariants, the rank-five
log-purity zero test or general positive-gap finite attainment. No G4
I-only/full-panel endpoint or cap-independent exact-return budget follows.

## Actual new control and its limits

check_pair_gap_tube.py was executed ONCE and passed. It uses only exact
Fraction polynomial/scalar arithmetic and a sixteen-case categorical sum.
It does not import or execute the retained forest/source producer.

For the old seven-state cap-three formulas it verifies BOTH complete formal
defect decompositions(3), normalization and the row coefficient factor3.
It constructs one conservative bound L_3=312. It also checks the multiplicative
excess identity, four strict pair-coordinate members of the fixed-z closure
family, its protected-field mismatch, and the zero-anchor balanced-tree guard
5/12-1/3=1/12 (leading factor gives1/768).

Full source/result encrypted before first runtime persistence:
[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately], ciphertext SHA256
f7807982d3ff301de70f3de9781ac8ac865c06628cb2bbef73d22df2868f99ee.
These are finite algebra/categorical controls. They do not independently
accept the arbitrary-m proof, new Code/Calendar/Originated instance,
original observation decoder, RCF invariant check, full-source integration
or G3 closure. No compiler, model/native/Lake job, old suite, peer dispatch,
new worker or local Git action was performed. The proof remains HAND.

> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution.
