# Positive original word receiver with fresh IDs and one calendar

21 October 2026. Authored HAND construction plus actual specified graph/compiler
controls. The prototype reuses the immutable admitted-testers source. Native
Lean construction, full-calendar exterior factorization and general G3 closure
remain separate. Fresh populations here have freely chosen positive per-edge
rates; additional ties involving new rates are outside this receiver.

## Reused implementation and concrete new interface

g3_source_word_receiver.py wraps the existing source_checks.Source and insert_chain
at Commons07c9a510b594655a62c609a7e354ecfe5752e35f,
research/2026-10-01-g4-admitted-testers-0819z/source_checks.py.
Source SHA25679be4b179572c18acee354b44be4d31aa7d6449bb07579e04f08e56c91077a1b;
Git blob64602b8eeb7e1dcc40708e1e98889dd7bc22bf68.
The retained checker tests binary degrees, DAG, hybrid cut children, retained
least stable root, outer-labelled planarity and strict edge/coin parameters.
The retained compile_source integrates the joint current-forest source law.

The new adapter takes the existing source, an unexposed eligible bridge ID,
strict rational lead/cells, a rational original calendar and the protected edge
control set. It refuses a protected selected edge. It allocates a namespace
disjoint from ALL original vertex/edge names before invoking the old constructor,
then preserves every original vertex/label/hybrid control and every outside edge
field. It supplies exact new ages, original parent occurrence IDs, native
P(parent1)=1-P(parent0), and only the new positive-rate recipes. Existing outside
rates are carried by their original edge IDs without a parameter refit.

The retained rational Source stores survivals, not an explicit physical old
rate bank. Given an old bank compatible with those survivals and the supplied
calendar, the outside rates are retained literally by ID. The adapter does not
test that pre-existing exponential compatibility. In the concrete controls a
compatible baseline bank exists by the same `-log(survival)/duration` formula.

The preserved exterior graph fields are checked directly, including namespace
collisions. The caller still supplies the actual eligible-menu contract: a
bridge test alone does not derive that an observed edge/control may be replaced.
The underlying retained Source representation uses rational survivals; the
separate algebraic private-word prototype is not silently narrowed by this tool.

## Calendar/rate construction

Let the original slot be u->v with D=C(u)-C(v)>0. For N bigons, put

    C(H_j)=C(v)+(2j-1)D/(2N+1),
    C(U_j)=C(v)+2jD/(2N+1),             j=1,...,N.

The literal rootward sequence is the positive lower connector, first bigon,
positive connector, next bigon, ..., positive final connector to old u. Every
connector and each arm interval has duration d=D/(2N+1)>0. Parallel arms share
the SAME actual interval. Every old age stays unchanged, including the retained
root and arbitrarily serial/negative old tip ages if the supplied calendar has
them. Each new survival z in(0,1) is realized exactly by

    rate(z)=-log(z)/d > 0,
    exp(-rate(z)*d)=z.

All new rates are finite and positive. The N=0 receiver keeps one ordinary slot
with its old duration D and the requested strict new survival. No zero passage,

# Exact log-purity as equality of two bounded volumes

22 October2026. HAND/unreviewed adapter and one exact arithmetic control.
Original all-input G3 remains OPEN. No period equality algorithm, new
rank-five example, source/compiler/model/native run or independent acceptance.

Prior comparison: the COMPLETE retained THREE-LOG-PURITY-REDUCTION.md at
Commons8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6,
research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-three-log-purity-1210z,
SHA c99623631f972c3911f3dceba9f1b376ed2b135fd2dbc04aeae268633fcb33a9,
supplies Phi and every source-facing implication. Its first-three Jensen
test is REUSED. The later G3-WITNESS-BOUND-ROUTE.md,
SHA446727db5a89571342401147017198f57f848e39c4819486e9b57bef5af2210d,
already screens fixed semialgebraic real exceptional-set shortcuts; that
argument is reused, not rederived. The bounded targeted G3 Markdown search
located no prior period/volume adapter; this is not an absence/priority claim.

## The explicit finite construction

Retain the FULL five-coordinate logarithmic-cone promise of the old reduction.
It implies b_3,b_6,b_10>1. Write b=(b_3,b_6,b_10), alpha_i=b_i-1, and

    L_i(t)=alpha_i/(1+alpha_i*t),  0<=t<=1.

Then integral_0^1 L_i(t)dt=log b_i. Write the REUSED homogeneous Phi as
sum_(a+b+c=8) h_abc*u^a*v^b*z^c, with its25 nonzero integer coefficients.
For each term choose an eight-slot label list rho containing a labels3,
b labels6 and c labels10, and define

    F_b(t_1,...,t_8)=sum h_abc product_(j=1)^8 L_rho(j)(t_j).

Fubini and absolute convergence on the compact cube give EXACTLY

    integral_[0,1]^8 F_b = Phi(log b_3,log b_6,log b_10).             (1)

This uses eight INDEPENDENT integration variables. Integrating the diagonal
function Phi(L_3(t),L_6(t),L_10(t)) would be a different integral.

An explicit positive denominator is

    D_b(t)=product_(j=1)^8 product_(i=3,6,10)(1+alpha_i*t_j).

Let N_b=D_b*F_b. Clearing each term cancels one denominator per slot, so
N_b is a polynomial of degree<=2 in each t_j, total degree<=16. D_b has
total degree24. All coefficients are effectively real-algebraic. Set

    M_b=sum |h_abc|*alpha_3^a*alpha_6^b*alpha_10^c.

Since 0<L_i<=alpha_i, |F_b|<=M_b. Define two COMPACT semialgebraic sets
in nine integration variables (t_1,...,t_8,s):

    K_+/- = {0<=t_j<=1, 0<=s<=M_b, s*D_b(t)<= +/-N_b(t)}.

Their defining polynomials have degree<=25 in those nine variables, with
the input b treated as algebraic coefficients. Vertical integration proves

    vol_9(K_+)-vol_9(K_-)=Phi(log b_3,log b_6,log b_10).            (2)

Thus this is a TOTAL explicit construction of a fixed-dimensional,
fixed-degree TWO-volume equality instance from every promised algebraic input.
Purity iff those volumes are equal, with their original SAME input and full
cone promise. The inherited small-loss/all-core transformation still supplies
the original COMMON source consequence. It is not rerun or replaced here.

## A zero whose two volumes are both strictly positive

Take the OLD rational-node pure family with r=1/2 and a=256*log2:
b_n=2^(256*T_n(1/2)) for n=3,6,10,15,21. This is an algebraic promised input,
with j=3 allowed; w=512*log2 gives ell=w*D(r). Its first three entries are

    b_3=2^640, b_6=2^2064, b_10=2^4097.

The other exponents are 6656+1/32 and9728+1/2048. No new arithmetic NO family
is claimed: rational-node purity and the original source transform are OLD.
The reused polynomial identity gives Phi(640,2064,4097)=0, hence (1) is zero.

The NEW direct-integrand control evaluates the SAME coefficient list exactly:

    F_b(0,...,0)>0,
    F_b(2^-3488,...,2^-3488)<0.

Continuity gives full-dimensional positive and negative regions inside the
cube, including a one-sided neighbourhood of the origin. Both K_+ and K_-
therefore have strictly POSITIVE nine-volume, although their volumes are equal.
The promise Phi>=0 does not make this direct rational integrand nonnegative.
An RCF dimension/emptiness test for either set cannot detect this cancellation.
Both displayed diagonal values are independent of each term's slot ordering;
averaging those orderings to symmetrize F leaves this counterexample intact.

5c8604214e7dcb7088caa3605c9d095803cea8648ea48e85b50b6a8484aa5617,
ran ONCE, exit0/PASS. It retains all three exact rational values in hexadecimal
numerator/denominator form, encrypted before first persistence:
[encrypted runtime receipt retained privately], ciphertext SHA
705a92c81402f8c52e3a0a1f4bd1d7d254582cc6c5193beef0d4d7337be5cf7d.

control checks this receiver counterexample, not the universal reduction proof.

## Exact stopping point

The period-to-single-volume theorem is REUSED: Viu-Sos, Theorem1.1, assumes
a NONZERO real period. Its v4 Section5 zero-detection paragraph and Algorithm4
were actually read; the latter needs a strict volume inequality to terminate.
It does not decide equality in (2):
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.01097v4

The earlier v3 introduction was also read, with its version kept separate.
Neither version is a new G3 supplier of exact cancellation. A different
input-dependent positive-integrand construction is not ruled out by the
specific counterexample above, but must actually terminate on zero inputs.
No general period-conjecture equivalence, hardness theorem or impossibility
of an original G3 recognizer is established. This adapter exposes rather than
solves the remaining exact-zero operation; fixed domain degree is not a
physical source-length bound or a complete NO certificate.

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# A terminating repetition bound from algebraic multiplicative rank

22 October2026 UTC, existing G3 owner. HAND/self-audited, UNREVIEWED and
UNCOMPILED. This is a count bound for repetitions of ONE supplied block
family, with a supplied exact algebraic diagonal target. It is not the full
G3 witness bound. No RCF, PARI, compiler, source/model/native job or new
mathematical program was run; the example below is hand arithmetic.

The distinction from unrestricted words is essential: the block's numerical
parameters are the SAME in every repetition. Fresh physical sites and bits
are distinct. This is a search family, not an extra constraint imposed on
the original G3 problem or on every possible rival source.

## Exact claim and reused suppliers

Supply a semialgebraic parameter domain Omega over real algebraic constants
and a rational map

    f:Omega subset R^d -> R_(>0)^s,

with denominators nonzero on Omega. Supply positive effectively algebraic
b=(b_1,...,b_s). Let r be their multiplicative rank: the rank of the subgroup
they generate. Assume r>d. Then there is a TOTAL computable integer H(f,b)
such that, for every positive integer N and every theta in Omega,

    f_i(theta)^N=b_i for all i  =>  N<=H(f,b).                 (1)

H is computed without assuming that any solution exists, including on NO
inputs. Once it is computed, exact fixed-N polynomial feasibility for
N=1,...,H decides this repeated-block family. A full fixed-N source compiler
may impose additional joint equations; the same necessary bound still
applies. H=0 means there is no positive repetition count.

The closest retained count statements, variable-N construction and later
parametric review were inspected before this argument at Commons
8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6:

- research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-real-critical-finiteness-1446z/
  ALL-REAL-CRITICAL-PRESENTATION-FINITENESS.md bounds the retained count in
  its specified paired-critical positive-residue predicate. It expressly
  does not bound arbitrary actual words. No criticality or Poisson residue
  is assumed in (1). Its accepted/current SHA256 is
  52b4b1cba30ebd792b3c8b47c81e071d232c18491c67be634decd79018fa4688;
  the complete later INDEPENDENT-ALL-REAL-CRITICAL-FINITENESS-REVIEW.md,
  SHA25689edb2ef58d6c37758e22b57c6536fec5eab1fbd9873bb98cae0b61dfb98119a,
  was also read. Its scoped acceptance does not acquire the count in (1).
- research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-variable-count-exact-slice-1300z/
  VARIABLE-COUNT-EXACT-SLICE.md and the later parametric-certificate review
  supply a different, already solved variable-count construction: an N-cell
  primary group plus a retained head and secondary correction. Those other
  factors cannot be divided out as known target coordinates. Their forcing,
  rank and tail-certificate hypotheses remain; none is supplied here anew.
- The old source/path REDUCTION.md at9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1,
  research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-global-source-reachability-0019z, already supplies
  fixed-shape RCF feasibility and actual-source reconstruction. These are
  REUSED, not a new solver or graph constructor.
- The retained integer-power/root-descent audit remains in force. Here a
  positive root is a NECESSARY algebraic signature of a supposed repeated
  witness. It is not declared a physical operation; actual feasibility is
  checked separately at each of the finitely many N.

The arithmetic supplier is the main theorem on printedp626 of
[Mordell1953](https://msp.org/pjm/1953/3-3/pjm-v3-n3-p10-s.pdf).
For a real number field K and real radicals x_j with x_j^N in K, it gives
K-linear independence of the monomials with exponents0,...,N-1, provided
no monomial in the x_j lies in K unless each exponent is divisible by N.
The publisher text's statement, lemma and proof were read. Its prime-radical
special case is the older Besicovitch theorem, restated on printedp625.
These are REUSED arithmetic, not new independence theorems or novelty claims.

The incremental interface is (1) for a supplied rational signature family.
A bounded Markdown prior search is navigation, not a worldwide absence claim.

## Effective saturated coordinates, without a logarithmic zero oracle

Take a real number field K containing b and every coefficient of the supplied
family. Let S consist of the prime ideals supporting the principal fractional
ideals (b_i). Compute a basis epsilon_1,...,epsilon_t of its POSITIVE S-units,
positive at the selected real embedding. This group is free: a field embedded
in R has only the roots of unity+/-1, and its positive torsion is trivial.

This is standard effective algebraic number theory, not a transcendence
premise. For clarity, an unconditional acquisition argument is as follows.
Dirichlet's known unit rank lets one enumerate integral units and rational
enclosures of their logarithmic embeddings until a full-rank tuple is
certified. Only a NONZERO determinant has to be found; zero determinants
need not be decided. Its log parallelepiped bounds representatives modulo
the generated finite-index subgroup. A computable rational bound on all
Archimedean absolute values bounds their coordinates in an integral basis.
Enumerating that finite integer box supplies the remaining ordinary units.

For each prime ideal P in S, dovetail powers P^h and algebraic integers until
a generator is found; finiteness of the ideal class group guarantees success.
Their valuation vectors give independent multiples of every S-coordinate.
Reduce S-valuations to finite residue ranges using those generators, then
reduce Archimedean logs using the ordinary-unit tuple. The norm is bounded
on those valuation ranges. By the product formula the remaining log coordinate
transverse to the ordinary-unit hyperplane is bounded too. Thus another finite
integral-basis box contains
representatives for the remaining positive S-unit quotient. This obtains a
finite generating set. Its rank is the ordinary-unit rank plus |S|.

Enumerate exact algebraic multiplicative relations between these generators
until the required number of independent relations is found. Saturating that
relation lattice gives the entire kernel, since the positive group is
torsion-free. Smith normal form then extracts a basis. All equality tests
here are algebraic product tests; no nonlinear logarithmic equality is used.

As a practical implementation caution, the official PARI documentation marks
uncertified bnf data as GRH-dependent and requires full certification before
unconditional uses, including S-units. An attempted online full-page read
failed; its indexed official contract was inspected, not a complete current
manual or an execution. No PARI call or installation is selected here. The
termination argument above does not assume a provisional class-group result
or termination of a certification call on incorrect data.

Write the b_i as products of the epsilon_j, obtaining an integer t-by-s
matrix W. Those coordinates can be found by exact product enumeration since
membership is already known. Let U be an integer basis for

    span_Q(columns W) intersect Z^t.

This lattice is primitive. Compute D with W=U D. It has r rows and full row
rank. Define C_j=product_l epsilon_l^(U_lj). Thus

    b_i=product_j C_j^(D_ji).                                (2)

If g=product_j C_j^(v_j/N) lies in K, it is a positive S-unit: its Nth power
is an S-unit, so every valuation outside S is zero. Write its integer
S-unit coordinates as z. Then N z=U v. Primitivity of U supplies an integer
left inverse, and hence every v_j is divisible by N. Mordell's precise
hypothesis is therefore acquired for x_j=C_j^(1/N), for EVERY N.

## Choose one polynomial and compute the bound

Let T be the algebraic subtorus parametrized by

    X_i=product_j Y_j^(D_ji).

Its dimension is r. The Zariski closure V of f(Omega) has dimension at most d.
Thus T is not contained in V. There exists a polynomial P over K which
vanishes on f(Omega) but whose restriction to T is nonzero.

This P is effectively obtainable: enumerate finite polynomials over K;
RCF decides their universal identity on the supplied rational map/domain,
and substitution of the displayed monomials decides whether their restriction
to T is zero. The dimension inequality proves that this search terminates.
An empty Omega can instead be rejected immediately. This is a mathematical
algorithm using the OLD fixed-formula RCF procedure, not a newly run search.

Expand P=sum_alpha c_alpha X^alpha. On T collect terms with the same
integer vector e=D alpha and discard zero summed coefficients. Let E be
the finite remaining support. It is nonempty. Define

    H=max_j [max_(e in E) e_j - min_(e in E) e_j].             (3)

For N>H, factor product_j x_j^(min_E e_j) out of
P(b_1^(1/N),...,b_s^(1/N)). The remaining NONZERO polynomial in the x_j has
degree at most H<N in each variable. Mordell's theorem makes its value
nonzero. But any solution of f(theta)^N=b has
f(theta)=b^(1/N), using positive roots, and would make that P vanish.
This contradiction proves (1). No sign test at a limiting logarithmic value,
positive distance to a boundary, or effective source-loss floor was assumed.

## A fully explicit prime-power specialization

If P has rational coefficients and b_i=p_i^(A_i/B_i), with distinct rational
primes p_i, nonzero integers A_i, positive integers B_i, and reduced fractions,
put d_i=degree_(X_i) P. Then an immediate alternative to (3) is

    H_prime=max_i floor(d_i*|A_i|/B_i).                       (4)

Indeed set z_i=p_i^(1/(B_i N)). After substituting and removing a nonzero
common Laurent monomial, exponents in z_i range over at most d_i|A_i|.
For N>H_prime this is strictly less than B_i N. Distinct monomials remain
distinct because every A_i is nonzero. Besicovitch/Mordell independence then
prevents cancellation. Negative A_i are handled by the common monomial,
not by treating a negative physical survival as allowed. The given prime/
exponent representation is exactly checkable by algebraic-number arithmetic.

## An actual repeated-bigon use-site

For k entering CURRENT roots let lambda_k=k(k-1)/2. A fresh strict natural
bigon with arm survivals x,y, parent0 probability p and ordinary survival s
has no-merger coordinates

    C_k=s^lambda_k [p*x^lambda_k+(1-p)*y^lambda_k],
    I_k=s^lambda_k sum_(j=0)^k binom(k,j)*p^j*(1-p)^(k-j)
                              *x^(j(j-1)/2)*y^((k-j)(k-j-1)/2).

Here 0<p,x,y,s<1 and original native gamma=1-p. COMMON averages one original
bit inside its cell; I routes by current root. BOTH retains the SAME p,x,y,s.
The six coordinates k=2,...,7, or the twelve paired coordinates, are rational
polynomial maps of FOUR parameters. Therefore target multiplicative rank>=5
meets r>d and gives a terminating count bound for this repetition family.

On no-merger states the block returns the same root count to its common exit,
and fresh copied sites have not been read. This is the actual constant-
continuation/freshness contract needed for product diagonals. N repetitions
give the Nth power in every displayed coordinate, even though the COMPLETE
forest kernel has off-diagonal mergers and is not replaced by that diagonal.
Same numeric p across cells does not reuse their bits; distinct original IDs
remain distinct. Opaque entering trees are not rerouted by their old leaves.

Extra ordinary prefix/inter-cell factors can be allowed for this necessary
bound: their PRODUCT survival A contributes A^lambda_k and is absorbed into
s=A^(1/N) in the diagonal equation. This asserts no reordering or equality
of the full chronological forest operators. At each bounded N the actual
source compiler must still use all the original factors and joint equations.

The high-rank case is not vacuous. At p=x=s=1/2,y=1/3 the COMMON coordinate is

    C_lambda=(3^lambda+2^lambda)/(2^(2lambda+1)*3^lambda).

For lambda=1,3,6,10,15 the numerators are respectively
5,35,793=13*61,60073=13*4621, and14381675.
The last is divisible by11; none of the previous four is. Any prime divisor
of4621 is new relative to2,3,5,7,13,61, as direct division verifies. Thus these
five coordinates are multiplicatively independent by their successive new
prime valuations. Every fixed positive repetition count gives rational
targets of rank at least5. This is hand nonvacuity arithmetic, not a new
executed source fixture, checked calendar, or claim about minimum count.

## Original-goal boundary

The target diagonals must actually be supplied, or recovered by a licensed
observation decoder such as the retained identifying COMMON calibration.
Selecting one latent diagonal from a general coupled fibre does not suffice.
The finite-N search must enforce the full declared data, source admission,
IDs, freshness, strictness, calendars and SAME physical tuple.

Failure of every N<=H rejects only this supplied repetition family. General
G3 permits unrelated parameters and heterogeneous words; it does not force
them to repeat one block. High multiplicative rank is not itself a purity
or nonpurity test. The old variable-N slice also has other unknown
head/correction factors, so its inner block is not a known root of the whole
target. Neither scope is silently replaced here. No complete original NO,
input-effective bound over all words, or goal closure follows. The acquired
result is a usable total count bound on the stated high-rank family, not
another conditional consumer with an unproved count premise.

# Restoring the actual private bank before the actual original future

Authored22October2026UTC, existing G3 owner. This is a HAND source-specific
construction and an UNCOMPILED Lean candidate. No compiler, kernel, native,
model or held-job execution is claimed. Original G3 remains open.

## Exact new supplier

[G3ActualUnusedBankRestore.lean](G3ActualUnusedBankRestore.lean),13260B,
SHA2569ce716f032af7b649e4b7416abe9b47b420cc267b5b0722f292e5f2b06064ebb,
constructs a SAME-graph source-valid restoration, derives its inverse on
ACTUAL prefix support, and composes it with the actual original future.
It imports ActualStoredRegister, reusing the complete authenticated sources
recorded in [the whole-bank recovery](G3-ACTUAL-FRONTIER-WHOLE-UNUSED-BANK.md).
It does not change that already delivered frontier candidate or its hash.

Let N be the supplied original RootedBinary, P a finite set of original
nodes and S=PrivateHybrid N P. Let e(c)=erasePrivateCode N P c. For an
original private bank xi:S->Bool and an erased Code z, define R(xi,z) by
keeping EVERY snapshot field except register, and setting its register at v:

    v in P and hybrid: xi at that SAME original hybrid v;
    v in P and nonhybrid: false;
    v outside P: z.register(v).

PrivateRegisterErasure already proves source validity ignores these register
fields: all five validity obligations are the same forest/descendant
obligations. The new constructor rebuilds those literal obligations, with
all live roots, ancestor owners, opaque genealogy, populations and locations
unchanged. No new graph, parent registry, ID enumeration or fresh rate bank
is constructed.

The nonhybrid case matters. The inherited private bank only indexes original
HYBRIDS, while e clears all nodes in P. R is consequently not advertised as
an inverse on an arbitrary Code whose erased nonhybrid slot could be true.
It is an inverse on the actual initialized source support, where the
originalRegister initializer puts false at every nonhybrid node.

## Derived inverse on the actual original prefix

For an original complete hybrid assignment coin, the natural initializer is
initialCode N sample (originalRegister N coin); xi is its restriction to S.
ActualStoredRegister.actual_program_register_support proves that every d
in the ACTUAL finite prefix sourceProgram support has exactly that original

then gives

    R(xi,e(d))=d.                                       (1)

All other fields are definitionally the same and the Code proof fields are

the new candidate derives. No desired kernel equality, original-register
posterior or independent-entering-law premise is assumed. The support
inverse itself does not need no-read; no-read is needed for the product law.

## Actual endpoint product and restoration

Use the existing naturalInitialJoint, which draws ONE original hybrid bank
and retains its original private restriction together with its SAME valid
initial Code. Run the literal original prefix ops, retaining that bank label;
call the joint endpoint PMF J_ops. Let

    O_ops = outsideInitialCodeLaw.bind(sourceProgram N r ops),
    U = privateSeedPMF N P p.

Under literal NoPrivateWordRead N P ops, the existing actual source program
erasure and actual natural initial product give

    J_ops.map((xi,d)->(xi,e(d))) = independentPMF U O_ops. (2)

The candidate proves this directly at the endpoint; it does not assume a
missing history-endpoint extractor. All outside roots and their actual
source operations evolve inside O_ops. No frozen-exterior claim is used.

Mapping (2) by (xi,z)->(xi,R(xi,z)), and using (1) on actual support, yields

    (independentPMF U O_ops).map((xi,z)->(xi,R(xi,z)))
      = J_ops.                                         (3)

Thus the whole-bank product can reconstruct the ACTUAL full prefix law.
The independent product description is a disintegration of the original
once-drawn-bank law. It does not authorize resampling bits at cells or
discarding original private register coordinates before the future uses them.

## The stochastic continuation is now the literal source future

For ANY supplied original operation word future, on the SAME N/sample/rates,
and any final stochastic kernel finish from the SAME Code, (3), the natural
Code marginal, and finite-word bind associativity give

    naturalInitialCodeLaw.bind(sourceProgram(ops++future)).bind(finish)
      = U.bind(xi => O_ops.bind(z =>
          sourceProgram(future,R(xi,z)).bind(finish))).   (4)

This is actual_natural_word_after_restore_kernel in the candidate.
The future has no no-read requirement: its actual COMMON operations can
read the restored original bits. The same xi is carried through every
operation, and the source primitive invariant retains it. The rates and
ordered operators are literally the original supplied ones.

Equation(4) supplies the concrete post-prefix future binder missing from
the earlier arbitrary-internal-K interface. A deterministic endpoint readout
is its pure-kernel case. An actual ancestral completion can be supplied as
finish once its caller identifies that kernel. The equation itself does not
grant legality to an arbitrary finish map or prove a marked-clock record.

## Actual-frontier use and remaining boundaries

Instantiate ops with the literal actualFrontierProgram, which includes all
tied exits and stops BEFORE node entry. The previous UNCOMPILED
G3ActualFrontierUnusedBank.lean derives its NoPrivateWordRead from strict
private-node ages above that cut. The original closing-cohort/calendar
suppliers give the same physical prefix/closing/future order for an existing
Originated source. They are not replaced with a different calendar prefix.

The new candidate is source-level and has NOT elaborated. No selected full
type/axiom receipt, native object or kernel acceptance follows. Its exact
PMF API proof steps remain subject to a real future check in an admitted
lane; there is no selected compile request here.

Still separate: fresh N'/Code/BinaryValid/RegistryValid and protected
old-ID/menu/calendar/rate/Originated diagrams; SAME natural-p/compiler-gamma
bank in a physical BOTH application; actual first node entry and own-edge
clock/pulse/exit identification with numerical M/Phi; current-root canonical
labels, opaque grafting and actual future/readout reassembly. This candidate
is one original Code/operation-word endpoint law. Joint cross-genealogy or
marked-clock mechanisms retain their actual coupling and observation contracts.

In particular, (4) does not make an arbitrary exterior independent of private
bits. Replacing a conditional kernel by averaged M still needs its precise
eligible decoder/context equation; the law now retains every private bit and
executes its actual future instead of guessing that equation. No source-size

documents.body:
> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# Effective finite approximation by ONE paired physical word

22 October2026. Revision2 HAND candidate, unreviewed/uncompiled. No original G3 endpoint.
This is an approximation theorem, not an exact physical witness bound.
Historical novelty is unassessed. No retained source producer is replayed.

R1 remains immutable at G3-SAME-TUPLE-PAIRED-APPROXIMATION.md,
14516B/SHA2568d8d249f5ca0d2bcfe1df46c0991e7573a78f477dee1d0354f7b4eeffe1c2ecb.
This revision restricts the sampled alphabet to complete positive cells. R1
also admitted standalone ordinary representatives; merging one at the front
could change a literal leading-edge parameter. The same rounding proof on
the cell-only alphabet now preserves that leading edge in canonical syntax.
This is a proof/caller correction, not a new theorem or a repeated check.

## 1. Actual source and the prior difference

Fix any finite cap m>=2 of CURRENT roots, carrying their original opaque
trees. Use the literal fresh, unexposed, untied private bridge grammar

    E(z) B(x_1,y_1,p_1) E(a_1) ... B(x_N,y_N,p_N) E(a_N),

all parameters strictly between0 and1. One tuple supplies BOTH complete
COMMON and INDEPENDENT labelled-forest kernels through that cap. Each new
hybrid occurrence has its own fresh ID/bit, even when numerical parameters
are repeated. Here p is original parent0 probability; native gamma=1-p.
No exported register, cross-slot tie or newly legal hidden observation is
added. The kernels are internal compiler coordinates.

Earlier complete sources read at Commons8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6:

- research/2026-10-01-sol61-g3-interior-2025z/UNIFORM-CLOSURE-BOUND.md:
  effective COMMON approximation, not exact factor compression.
- research/2026-10-05-dot-g3-recovered-provenance-0206z/g3-package/
  compactification/MASTER-COMPACTIFICATION-MAP.md: the compact joint image
  formula; explicitly says SAME-parameter paired approximation needs its
  own theorem, rather than two separate marginal approximants.
- research/2026-10-16-g3-g4-obligation-audit-1930z/
  PHYSICAL-APPROXIMATION-COMPOSITION.md: complete later comparison, explicitly
  retaining that separate-mode G6 approximation is not automatic BOTH
  approximation. Its changing-chart exact-correction gap remains.

Projectivity, ordinary/current-root kernels, clipping and the finite
polynomial source compiler are REUSED. The proposed addition is the
bounded-clock rounding argument below and its two-clock paired composition.
It does not claim separate-mode robust closure exclusion as new.

Exact identities of those complete bodies, respectively:

    13150B/SHA25624c2a156fe6d817a1f097c8ec964b6a4f3a95bae63ca4e47d6774babddfbfd2d
    9561B/SHA2562842f84c6d89fc082aae74a9036985eb5df527e966d63b941b6eb1bf611e0e37
    6856B/SHA256ebb548e27e409a3752868afa3e8463fc9760856bad766d81f602e4f6c8dc71b1

Classification: a STRICTLY STRONGER claim than these inspected suppliers,
whose explicit missing implication is a joint physical approximant. This
bounded predecessor/successor comparison is not a corpus-wide priority claim.

**Candidate theorem.** There is a TOTAL computable B(m,epsilon), for rational
0<epsilon<=1, such that EVERY finite strict private word has ONE strict
replacement with at most B(m,epsilon) bigons and paired full-kernel error
less than epsilon. The original leading E(z) can be retained exactly.
Error is maximum absolute row-sum norm, over both modes and every entering
forest through m. Hence the statement includes contextual opaque grafting.

## 2. Reused source estimates

Use stochastic matrices on the finite forest carrier; disjoint arity/mode
blocks may be combined by direct sum. Their absolute row-sum norm is1,
and multiplication contracts errors. Set C=m(m-1).

For either mode write d(K)=b_2(K), its pair no-merger probability. On any
entering forest there are at most binom(m,2) token pairs. Projectivity and
the fact that a changed forest requires a merger give

    ||K-I|| <= C(1-d(K)).                                    (3)

For any physical prefix P and physical suffix Q, a change after P requires
at least two remaining current roots. The pair union bound gives

    ||P Q-P|| <= C d(P).                                    (4)

These are row-sum versions of the inherited full-forest TV bounds, with
the factor2 included in C. Already formed opaque trees never change.

For the SAME physical letter B(x,y,p)E(a),

    d_C=a[p*x+(1-p)*y],
    d_I=a[p^2*x+(1-p)^2*y+2p(1-p)],
    d_I-d_C=a*p*(1-p)*(2-x-y)>0.                            (5)

Ordinary letters have equal diagonals. These diagonals multiply, so d_C<=d_I
on every paired prefix. The paired block therefore satisfies (3) with
h=1-d_C; the I block satisfies it with h=1-d_I.

## 3. A general bounded-clock rounding lemma

Let A be a fixed effectively semialgebraic family of actual stochastic
matrices of dimension D, with polynomial/rational algebraic parameterization
and decidable algebraic sampling. A finite union of letter types is allowed.
Take rational C>=1. Suppose a semialgebraic scalar h(M)>0 satisfies

    ||M-I|| <= C h(M),    h(M)<=1.                           (6)

For supplied rational T>=1 and 0<rho<=1, a computable N(A,T,rho) has this
property: every product M_1...M_n with sum h(M_i)<=T is within rho of a
product of at most N ACTUAL letters from A. No commutativity is assumed.
The representative alphabet is finite, physical and algebraic.

Here is a complete construction of that bound. Choose rational

    delta=rho/(4T).

Cover [-C,C]^(D^2) by finitely many rational closed coordinate boxes of
width<=delta/D. Let K be a computable upper bound on their number. Any
two matrices in one box differ in row-sum norm by at most delta. Choose

    eta=min(1/2, rho/[4(C^2*T+K*C*(1+2*C*T))]).

For each box test, by RCF, whether there is a strict physical M in A with
0<h(M)<=eta and (M-I)/h(M) in that box. If so, select an ALGEBRAIC such M_j.
Write u_j=h(M_j) and A_j=(M_j-I)/u_j. Every actual weak letter M_i with
h_i<=eta can be assigned to a selected j with

    ||(M_i-I)/h_i-A_j||<=delta.

All selected u_j are strictly positive and at most eta. A rational
u_*>0 below their minimum is computable. In the application there are
arbitrarily weak complete positive cells, so this list is nonempty. If a general
family has no weak letters, omit this part and use only its strong net.

Keep every strong letter h_i>eta in its original place for now. For each
weak type j maintain a real residual r_j, initially0. At an old weak
letter assigned to j, add h_i, emit

    n_i=floor((r_j+h_i)/u_j)

copies of ACTUAL M_j, and replace r_j by r_j+h_i-n_i*u_j. Other residuals
do not change. Thus 0<=r_j<u_j. Each emitted occurrence gets a fresh source
ID when A is a physical cell alphabet; repeated values do not reuse a bit.

Let Z_i be this emitted power, or the original strong M_i. Total emitted
weak clock is at most the old weak clock, and each weak step emits clock
n_i*u_j<=h_i+u_j<=2eta. By stochastic telescoping,

    E_i=Z_i-I-n_i*u_j*A_j,
    ||E_i|| <= (C^2/2)(n_i*u_j)^2.

Consequently sum ||E_i||<=C^2*eta*T. Put

    R_i=sum_j r_j(after i)*A_j,   ||R_i||<=K*C*eta.

At a weak position,

    M_i-Z_i = h_i[(M_i-I)/h_i-A_j]+(R_i-R_(i-1))-E_i.     (7)

At strong positions the first and last terms are0 and R_i=R_(i-1).
Use the EXACT product telescoping identity with

    alpha_i=Z_1...Z_(i-1), beta_i=M_(i+1)...M_n.

Both contexts have norm<=1. Discrete summation by parts bounds the
contribution of R_i-R_(i-1) by

    K*C*eta * [1+sum ||alpha_(i+1)-alpha_i||
                 +sum ||beta_(i+1)-beta_i||]
      <= K*C*eta*(1+2*C*T).                                (8)

Indeed the old clock sum is<=T. The new emitted weak clock plus the retained
strong clock is also<=T, so (6) bounds each of the two total variations by
C*T. The boundary R_0 is0; R_n need not vanish and is included in the1.
This is why rounding residues may cross strong letters without charging
an error for every intervening position.

Combining (7),(8) gives the FULL noncommutative product error

    ||product M_i-product Z_i||
      <= delta*T+C^2*eta*T+K*C*eta*(1+2*C*T) <=rho/2.        (9)

Finally set gamma=rho*eta/(4T). Cover the strong-letter image by finite
rational boxes of row-sum diameter<=gamma. RCF selects one ACTUAL algebraic
strong letter in each nonempty box. There are at most T/eta old strong
occurrences. Replacing them in place adds at most rho/4 error, by stochastic
contraction. The weak and strong selected alphabets are physical; no
normalized direction, convex mixture or negative-time operation is used as
an actual replacement letter.

The number of emitted weak occurrences is<=T/u_*, since each has clock
at least u_*. A sufficient computable bound is therefore

    N(A,T,rho)=ceil(T/eta)+ceil(T/u_*).                     (10)

Omit the second term if there are no weak letters.
The resulting error is<=3rho/4<rho. All finite box-existence/sample problems
are RCF: h>0 allows denominator clearing, and actual letter parameters stay
strict. This proves both existence and total computability of the bound.
For arbitrary real original parameters, existence is the assertion; no exact
floor algorithm for a black-box computable real input is being assumed.

## 4. Why the actual paired alphabet meets the lemma

# G3 continuation: a direct rank-one transcendence route fails its hypotheses

21 October 2026. Authored hand derivation in the user's independent G3 chat.
No sub-agents, publication, external review or historical novelty claim. This
workspace is outside local Git; no Git addition or commit is authorized.

This note screens a proposed way to decide an inherited arithmetic gate. It
does not solve that gate, prove undecidability, or close the original G3.

## Original target and reused work

Original G3 asks for a terminating decision on every admitted finite rational
or effectively real-algebraic joint observation input: either construct one
finite strictly positive original source with one shared physical parameter
tuple, or exclude every such finite source. All original cores, labels, site
IDs, chronology, COMMON/INDEPENDENT distinctions and authorized response rows
remain. No extra observation or source-size promise is supplied.

The [source-faithful reachability reduction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-global-source-reachability-0019z/REDUCTION.md)
already gives fixed-length real-algebraic feasibility and YES enumeration.
It does not bound the number of legal appends. The
[October 16 obligation audit](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/4a082a70ef5d604ffb2db89f988d88b6159f569d/research/2026-10-16-g3-g4-obligation-audit-1930z/OBLIGATION-AUDIT.md)
and [decision-theorem reassessment](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/8ede964c050a23972dd7de620357f9bac7e0fc05/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G3-DECISION-THEOREM-REASSESSMENT-0900.md)
retain the complete-attainment/NO-termination gap. Their results and earlier
contributors' attribution are inherited here.

The [five-coordinate cone-promise refinement](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-three-log-purity-1210z/THREE-LOG-PURITY-REDUCTION.md)
uses positive algebraic inputs b_n at n in {3,6,10,15,21}, with the full stated
cone promise on ell_n=log b_n. In its pure branch,

    ell_n = w D_n(r),  w>0,
    D_n(r) = (1-r) T_n(r),
    T_n(r) = sum[k=0..n-2] (n-1-k) r^k.

The possible transcendental-node/rank-five branch remains unexhibited and
unexcluded in the retained sources. A generic moment fit, continuous powers
of a physical signature, or tangent-space deletion is not a substitute:
[exact finite flat completion failure](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/38276bf90114506b0460e34251b8ffeaec12408b/research/2026-10-19-dot-g3-flat-completion-1825z/FAILED-ROUTE.md),

and [scoped local-deformation audit](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/85f5772a5726bb03fa06a12dc539624db3e0aeac/research/2026-10-18-dot-new-attacks-0419z/g3-deformation/README.md).
These failures are prior results, not discoveries of this continuation.

## Candidate bypass checked

The strong six-exponentials theorem forbids a rank-one 2-by-3 matrix of the
appropriate algebraic linear combinations of logarithms when its two rows
and three columns have the required algebraic linear independence. See
Waldschmidt, [Variations on the Six Exponentials Theorem, Theorem 2.1](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/Hyderabad.pdf).
The paper's field of algebraic numbers is essential; its PDF text extraction
can lose the overline. No assertion of a newer comprehensive literature audit
or a nonlinear-logarithm equality algorithm is made.

A tempting route is to use the pure parameter r to construct just such a
rank-one matrix from the five supplied logarithms. The needed multiplicative
rectangle does not follow from this curve. The following elementary argument
rules out the direct homogeneous construction even before number theory.

## Polynomial-space lemma

Let K be any characteristic-zero field and

    V = span_K {T_3(t),T_6(t),T_10(t),T_15(t),T_21(t)}.

The basis degrees are 1,4,8,13,19. Their positive differences, each occurring
once, are

    3,4,5,6,7,9,11,12,15,18.

For every nonconstant h in K(t), the vector space

    U_h = {f in V : h*f in V}

has dimension at most one over K.

Proof. Every nonzero element of V has one of the five displayed degrees,
because the basis degrees are distinct. Any two-dimensional subspace has
two elements of different degrees: cancel leading coefficients if necessary.
Write deg h = deg numerator minus deg denominator. If deg h=d is nonzero,
two independent elements of U_h would supply two different pairs of degrees
in the displayed set with the same nonzero difference d. This contradicts
the difference list, also for negative d by reversing the pairs.

If deg h=0, let c in K be its leading-coefficient ratio. Since h is not
constant, h-c is nonzero of negative degree. For f in U_h, both h*f and c*f
belong to V, so (h-c)*f belongs to V. Thus U_h is contained in U_(h-c), and
the preceding nonzero-degree argument again bounds its dimension by one.
This proves the lemma.

## Application to the inherited transcendental-node branch

Take K=Qbar and suppose r is transcendental. Polynomial evaluation at r is
injective over K. Write a=w(1-r), so the five logs span a*V(r). If a rank-one
2-by-3 matrix with entries in this span had independent rows and columns,
choose a nonzero pivot. The ratio of the second-row entry to the first-row
entry in that column defines a rational function h(r). The first-row
polynomial entries f,g in two independent columns are independent in V.
Rank one requires h*f,h*g in V after
evaluation, hence as polynomial identities by transcendence of r. Row
independence makes h nonconstant. The lemma gives a contradiction.

Zero entries do not evade the argument: in a rank-one matrix with two
independent rows and at least two independent columns, neither row is zero;
the outer-product description supplies a nonzero pivot and two independent
column factors. A constant algebraic row ratio violates precisely the
required row independence.

Thus a direct rank-one matrix formed by algebraic homogeneous linear
recombination of these five logs cannot meet the strong theorem's hypotheses
on the proposed pure transcendental branch. This does not exclude adding
further independently justified arithmetic information, a different theorem,
or a nonhomogeneous construction involving 1. Those require actual new
premises; none is supplied here. In particular, the result does not assert
that the strong six-exponentials theorem is useless in every reformulation.

## Exact finite calculation and limits

The pairwise degree sums are also all distinct. Consequently the fifteen
products T_i*T_j, i<=j, have distinct leading degrees and are independent.
There is no homogeneous quadratic polynomial identity on this curve.

The accompanying calculation constructs integer coefficient columns for all
homogeneous monomials of degrees one, two and three and provides square
minors nonzero modulo the trial-division-certified prime 1,000,003. Such a
minor is a nonzero integer determinant, and remains nonzero over Qbar.
This supplies a finite certificate of cubic independence as well. The
script calculates all row selections and determinants rather than relying
on numerical rank tolerance. Its actual run receipt is kept encrypted in
the existing shared featurectl store; no plaintext runtime log is written.

Encrypted execution/setup receipt:
`[owner-local path omitted]`.
It binds the actual checker source hash, command, exit status and original
stdout/stderr. The receipt also distinguishes the observed peer goals from
unverified peer live model/permission settings. Decrypt only to an explicit
authorized local consumer; do not dump it to a cloud tool or conversation.

Exploratory modular ranks in degrees four and five are lower bounds only;
rank deficiency modulo one prime is not proof of a rational relation. No
quartic relation, complete ideal, positivity characterization or smaller
purity test is claimed.

All these statements concern the inherited promised arithmetic subfamily.
They produce no new source, NO certificate, global witness bound or
termination proof. The next full-master work must still acquire an effective
all-input source/NO mechanism, while preserving this arithmetic stress test.

## Continuation: allowing the constant 1 still does not supply a rank-one contradiction

This section is a further authored hand proof, not independent acceptance.
It resolves the explicitly retained nonhomogeneous route check. It does not
claim to exclude applications using additional auxiliary logarithms or other
rank theorems.

Set K=Qbar. In the putative pure branch with transcendental r, write
ell_i=a*T_i(r), where a=w(1-r) is nonzero. The five ell_i are independent
over K because evaluation of the five different-degree polynomials at r is
injective. They are therefore independent over Q. Baker's theorem implies
that 1,ell_1,...,ell_5 are independent over K. In particular,

    1 is not in a*V(r).                                      (B)

The accompanying finite minor certificate proves that the degree-three
monomials in the T_i are independent over K. Consequently a homogeneous
cubic identity in their evaluations forces the corresponding polynomial in
five formal variables to be identically zero. The same holds in degree two.

**Claim.** A rank-one 2-by-3 matrix with entries in
K + span_K{ell_i} cannot simultaneously have two independent rows and three
independent columns over K, using just these premises. Hence adding the
known constant 1 does not produce the hoped-for contradiction to strong
six-exponentials on this branch.

Write the matrix as C+a*B(r), with C a constant K-matrix and each entry of
B(t) in V. Constant invertible row and column operations over K preserve
the required independence and this form. We may put C in its rank normal
form. There are precisely three cases.

### Constant rank two

The matrix is

    [1+a*u,   a*v,   a*w]
    [  a*x, 1+a*y,  a*z],       u,v,w,x,y,z in V(r).

Rank one forces, after division by the nonzero a,

    z+a*(u*z-w*x)=0,    -w+a*(v*z-w*y)=0.

Multiplying these equations by w and z respectively and adding eliminates
the terms without a, giving

    v*z^2 + (u-y)*w*z - x*w^2 = 0.                           (C)

Replace each V-entry by its linear form in five formal variables. Cubic
independence makes (C) a polynomial identity in those variables.

If w and z were dependent linear forms over K, the third column would either
vanish or fix an algebraic ratio between the two rows of a rank-one matrix.
The required row or column independence would fail. They must therefore be
independent, coprime linear forms. Reducing (C) modulo w shows w divides v;
reducing it modulo z shows z divides x. Since the entries are linear forms,

    v=c*w, x=d*z, u-y=d*w-c*z        for some c,d in K.

Substitution in the second displayed minor yields

    a*(c*z-y)=1,

contradicting (B), since c*z-y belongs to V(r). The argument uses the
polynomial identity before evaluation; it does not factor polynomials at
an unknown transcendental numerical point.

### Constant rank one

The matrix is

    [1+a*u, a*v, a*w]
    [  a*x, a*y, a*z].

The last two columns give v*z-w*y=0. Quadratic independence makes this a
formal polynomial identity. If v,w are independent linear forms, their
coprimality gives y=c*v,z=c*w for one c in K. The other two minors become

    v*[c+a*(c*u-x)]=0,  w*[c+a*(c*u-x)]=0.

For c nonzero, either equation contradicts (B). For c=0 the equations force
x=0, and the second row vanishes, violating row independence.

If v,w are dependent but not both zero, write (v,w)=(v0*t,w0*t) for constants
v0,w0 and a nonzero linear form t. The formal identity implies
(y,z)=(v0*s,w0*s) for a linear form s. The second and third columns are then
dependent over K, which violates the required three-column independence.
Finally, if v=w=0, a nonzero y or z forces 1+a*u=0, contradicting (B). If
both are zero, the required column independence already fails. This exhausts
constant rank one, including all zero-entry cases.

### Constant rank zero

This is precisely the homogeneous case proved above by the polynomial-space
lemma. No application of strong six-exponentials is needed in any case.

### Scope and actual verification

The new checker section verifies seven exact polynomial identities used in
the elimination and substitutions. It does not automate Baker's theorem,
the UFD divisibility arguments, independence of evaluated entries, or the
original source transport. Those are the hand proof just given. The first
encrypted receipt above predates this checker extension. The first extended
run failed before the calculation because SymPy was unavailable in this
phone's Python environment. Its original stdout/stderr and source hash are
preserved, encrypted, at
`[owner-local path omitted]`.
The corrected calculation removes that dependency and uses sparse integer
coefficient expansion. It passed, with a separate source-bound encrypted
receipt at
`[owner-local path omitted]`.
No dependency was installed, and no plaintext runtime log was written.

The result screens ALL affine-linear 2-by-3 constructions from these five
logs and 1 at the inherited transcendental-node branch. It does not show
that the branch exists, that it is impossible, that all uses of the linear
subgroup theorem fail, or that a nonlinear expression known independently
to belong to the logarithm span cannot help. Asserting such membership is
exactly the kind of missing extra premise this check was meant to expose.

## Continuation: actual point supply for a natural linear-subgroup construction

This section answers the retained point-dimension question for a specified
family of hyperplanes. It is a new authored hand derivation with finite
representative controls, not independent acceptance or general G3 closure.

Waldschmidt's Theorem 3.1 bounds the K-dimension of H intersect Le^d by
d(d-1) when H contains no nonzero vector from K^d. Here K=Qbar and Le is the
algebraic-linear span of 1 and logarithms of nonzero algebraic numbers. To
exclude a proposed pure input by this theorem, one must actually provide
MORE than that many independent qualifying points in one such hyperplane.
Theorem 2.11 and Corollary 3.2 derive useful consequences from that bound;
they do not grant missing points or closure under products.

Continue with ell_i=a*T_i(r), r transcendental, a nonzero. Set

    V = span_K{T_3,T_6,T_10,T_15,T_21},
    W = K + a*V(r).

Baker's theorem makes W a six-dimensional K-space, with the sum direct.
It is a known subspace of Le. Let E be ANY d-dimensional subspace of V,
with basis e_1,...,e_d, where 1<=d<=5. Consider the hyperplane

    H_E = {z : sum_i e_i(r)*z_i = 0}.

Its coefficients are independent over K by transcendence of r, so its
intersection with K^d is zero, as the primary theorem requires. This family
includes every hyperplane whose independent normal coefficients are
algebraic linear combinations of the five supplied logarithms: their common
nonzero scale a cancels from the hyperplane equation.

The points supplied using ONLY known W-entries form H_E intersect W^d.
The goal is to count this space without assuming a generic value of a.

### Product-space dimension

The fifteen quadratic products of the five basis polynomials are independent.
Therefore multiplication Sym^2(V) -> K[t] is injective. Extending a basis of
E to one of V shows that E*V has dimension

    dim_K(E*V) = 5d - binom(d,2).                             (D)

Indeed the distinct symmetric products with at least one factor in E number
d*(5-d)+d*(d+1)/2. Their only tensor redundancies are the binom(d,2)
antisymmetric pairs within E. This is uniform over all subspaces E, not just
the first d displayed basis elements.

### Special scale values are included

In coordinates z_i=c_i+a*f_i(r), the hyperplane map has image

    E(r) + a*(E*V)(r).

Let s be the dimension of the intersection of these two summands. The first
summand has dimension d, so s<=d, including any nongeneric rational-function
value of a. Using (D), rank-nullity on the six-dimension-per-coordinate
domain gives EXACTLY

    dim_K(H_E intersect W^d) = binom(d,2) + s
                             <= d*(d+1)/2.                  (E)

If a is not in K(r), the intersection is zero: any nonzero common element
would express a as a quotient of two rational functions of r. For an
independent formal scale this gives exactly binom(d,2) points. The upper
bound (E) does not assume this stronger condition on the actual input.

For d=3,4,5 the upper bounds are 6,10,15, whereas a contradiction to the
primary theorem would require at least 7,13,21 independent points. No value
of a, including a special one, can make this construction cross the bound.
For d=2, the previous affine 2-by-3 argument already bounds the qualifying
point space by two, also at the theorem's bound. For d=1 the hyperplane is
zero. Thus every possible independent normal drawn from the supplied log
span is covered.

### Meaning and verification scope

The checker now constructs the formal map in independent variables a,t for
the first d basis elements, d=1,...,5. Its modular ranks are compared with
the hand-derived upper bound, while the explicit antisymmetric relations
give the opposite dimension bound. This is a finite check of representative
formal matrices. The proof of (D) and the intersection argument establish
the arbitrary-subspace and nongeneric-scale cases; those universal statements
are not claimed as a finite enumeration or a numerical experiment.

This rules out the specified point-supply construction, not the linear
subgroup theorem itself. Normals outside the original log span, or additional
points whose entries are independently proved to lie in Le, are not covered.
No such successful supplier is asserted here. The entire original
source-recognition problem remains separate and open.

The source-bound successor check passed and was encrypted before runtime
file persistence at

This receipt includes the complete authored checker and proof version at

# G3: exact forms of the missing effective termination information

21 October 2026. Authored hand proof using the inherited fixed-budget source
compiler and the construction in G3-WITNESS-BOUND-ROUTE.md. No independent
review, Lean verification, RCF execution or mathematical novelty claim.
General G3 remains OPEN. No local Git change or sub-agent is involved.

## Source contract

Inputs p are the finite exact rational/effectively real-algebraic original
joint observations with their finite legal menus, original IDs and controls.
The inherited protected template and source-word grammar is effective and
finite except for the natural number of private appends. The same physical
assignment supplies every row and paired/register component. Let Y(p) mean
existence of ONE actual finite strictly positive original realizing source.

The source/path equivalence and its limits are in sections 2--5 of the
[pinned full-source reduction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-global-source-reachability-0019z/REDUCTION.md).
The decider/one-witness-bound equivalence below is already explicitly
inherited from G3.2 of the [October 16 obligation audit](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/1138a5b1a281caa00b38e0976db95b586938754b/research/2026-10-16-g3-g4-obligation-audit-1930z/OBLIGATION-AUDIT.md),
which was reread in full. Its proof is restated to connect it to the new
weighted-score/height audit, not claimed as a new source result.
For a natural N, let B(p,N) mean existence with at most N total private
appends over the protected templates. RCF and finite grammar enumeration
decide B, including N=0, and return an exact algebraic physical witness when
positive. An admitted real witness can be replaced by a real-algebraic one
for this finite formula over algebraic coefficients. This does not impose
extra algebraicity on the original source class.

Thus B is monotone in N and

    Y(p) iff exists N, B(p,N).

This inherited equivalence preserves all cores and original joint rows.
It does not assert a bound on N or closure attainment.

## A computable one-witness count bound is also necessary for a decider

The following statements are equivalent under this contract:

1. A total algorithm decides Y on every admitted encoded input.
2. A total computable natural-valued H(p) satisfies
   Y(p) implies B(p,H(p)).
3. The minimum realizing append count, with an explicit NO sentinel, is
   a total computable function.

For 2 implies 1, compute H(p) and decide the one finite formula B(p,H(p)).
The implication in 2 prevents a YES from hiding at a larger count. For
1 implies 2, first run the total decider. Return H=0 on NO. On YES, test
B(p,0), B(p,1), ... until the first success and return that N. The promised
YES supplies termination; nothing is searched on NO. This also proves 3.
Conversely a computable minimum with a NO sentinel immediately decides Y.

H need not bound all presentations. It need not vary continuously or be
locally bounded as response values approach one another. It may depend on
the entire exact encoding. The accepted high-minimum examples therefore
do not refute statement 2; they refute stronger numerical-only bounds.

If valid input syntax is decidable and finitely many strings have length at
most L, a total input-length bound H_len(L) exists effectively if and only
if the decider exists: maximize H(p) over that finite decidable list. The
mere set-theoretic existence of a maximum over finite YES descriptions is
not an algorithm to compute it.

## The canonical attained score has exactly the same effective gate

Use the entire architecture enumeration and quality maxima M_i(p) from
G3-WITNESS-BOUND-ROUTE.md, including all original strict admission slacks.
If a domain uses a finite Boolean combination of polynomial signs, split it
effectively into finitely many basic semialgebraic branches first. Each
closed relaxation then has its own continuous normalized slack product;
no disjunction is silently replaced by a conjunction or by its boundary.
Keep legal fixed intervention endpoints weak/fixed as originally specified.

Set

    S(p) = sup_i 2^(-i-1) M_i(p),
    S_N(p) = max(0, 2^(-i-1) M_i(p) for i<N).

Each M_i and S_N has an exact effective algebraic code. The tail is bounded
by 2^(-N-1); S>0 iff Y. Every S is algebraic and the exact prefix maxima
eventually stabilize, but no uniform stabilization index has been proved.

The following additional statements are equivalent to a total Y decider:

4. A total algorithm returns an exact algebraic-number code for S(p).
5. A total computable T(p) satisfies S(p)=S_T(p)(p).
6. A total computable rational g(p)>0 satisfies
   S(p)>0 implies S(p)>=g(p).
7. A total computable integer H_S(p)>=1 bounds the coefficient height of
   some nonzero integer polynomial annihilating S(p).

For 4 implies a decider, compare the coded algebraic S with zero. Conversely,
use a total Y decider: return the algebraic number zero on NO; on YES,
enumerate until one weighted term l>0 is found. Choose N whose tail bound
is strictly less than l and compute the exact S_N. No omitted term can
exceed the known l, so S=S_N. This also constructs T, setting T=0 on NO.
Computing an S_T code proves that 5 implies 4.

For 6 implies a decider, choose N with 2^(-N-1)<g(p) and compute exact S_N.
If S_N>0 return YES. If S_N=0 then S is below g, which excludes a positive
S by the promised implication, so return NO. Conversely an exact algebraic
code for S gives a positive rational lower bound when S>0; use any positive
rational, for example 1, when S=0. Thus 4 supplies 6.

For 7 implies 6, the elementary root bound is enough; no degree bound is
needed. Remove any power of x from the annihilating polynomial, so its
integer constant coefficient is nonzero if S is nonzero. Write its height
bound as H>=1. For a positive root 0<s<1,

    1 <= |a_0| = |sum_(j>=1) a_j s^j|
                <= H*s/(1-s).

Therefore s>=1/(H+1). A root s>=1 already satisfies that bound. In particular
g(p)=1/(H_S(p)+1) works for S. Conversely an exact algebraic code from 4
provides an integer annihilating polynomial and hence a computable H_S.

These equivalences do not construct any of the functions in 1--7. They
identify why finite attainment, algebraicity, approximation rates and
post-hoc algebraic heights have not supplied a simpler completion route.
An algorithm that computes S only on YES still has precisely the inherited
NO-termination gap. The classical countermodel in the companion note does
not embed halting computations into the actual G3 source class.

## Real-coefficient semialgebraic NO certificates can be searched exactly

The reduction's invariant conditions are sound by finite path induction:
for each c, Init_c is included in I_c, I_c is Trans_c-closed, and I_c avoids
the original joint target. One valid finite family excludes EVERY size.

For a FIXED finite Boolean/polynomial formula shape for each I_c, regard all
its polynomial coefficients as finitely many unknown real variables.
The three conditions, with their universal state/path-variable quantifiers,
are a first-order RCF sentence over the algebraic input constants. Existence
of real coefficients is therefore decidable. If coefficients exist, the
same finite formula has real-algebraic coefficients: the real-algebraic
field is an elementary real-closed subfield for this sentence. Algebraic
sampling gives an effective finite coefficient encoding. No rational-only
density argument is used, since strict and exact constraints may forbid
rational coefficient replacements.

Enumerating finite formula shapes and running these terminating RCF tests
therefore enumerates all NO inputs admitting finite semialgebraic invariant
families, even if their originally exhibited coefficients were arbitrary
reals. Dovetail this branch with the actual-source YES enumeration.

If EVERY original NO has such a family, the dovetailed recognizer is total.
This source-specific completeness statement is still unproved. It is only
a SUFFICIENT route to the equivalent gates above: a total decider need not
imply completeness of this PARTICULAR invariant language. Soundness and
coefficient synthesis alone do not justify that reverse implication.

## Formal and practical use

The useful conditional interface is bounded source feasibility plus witness
extraction, followed by a total-recognizer theorem that takes H and its
coverage proof as explicit parameters. Its missing premise has the full
logical strength just established. An independent optional NO-certificate
branch has all-size soundness; its completeness must be a separately named
assumption until proved for the actual source grammar.

Neither interface is a general G3 endpoint without the missing theorem.
The corresponding source/path correspondence, exact compiler refinement,
actual kernel checking and a runnable solver remain distinct deliverables.

# G3: reuse of Roy's all-size three-coordinate matrix screen

Authored22October2026UTC in the existing G3 workspace. This is a HAND,
UNREVIEWED use-site application of an existing theorem, not a new matrix-rank
theorem, a computation, or original G3 closure. No local Git action occurred.

## Prior-solution comparison

The exact proposed claim concerns EVERY finite matrix size and EVERY rank,
with entries homogeneous RATIONAL linear combinations of only the three
original logarithms ell_3,ell_6,ell_10 on the putative transcendental-node
pure branch. It asks whether the strict Waldschmidt–Masser rank condition
can contradict that branch through absence of a rational zero rectangle.

The complete earlier G3-LOG-MATRIX-RANK-BOUNDARY.md was inspected,
SHA25615d070bb81f52d3e6951fa0f011e911dabdc219c71c251d351dc3ac08d7b647a.
Its low-rank screen concerns ALL FIVE coordinates. The retained rank-three
successor is G3-LOG-RANK-THREE-SYZYGY-OBSTRUCTION.md,
SHA2563192d7a8698d0623ba72c78beabadfe0d3dd0f16519128ae73393976e63bbc4a.
Neither statement supplies an all-rank screen for the whole five-log span.

The later immutable source actually inspected is Commons
8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6,
research/2026-10-22-dot-g3-transcendence-admission-0557z/
METHOD-ADMISSION-UNREVIEWED.md,18072B,
SHA2566eaf35d5af52cf7b86b0e24d02c32bd3d999a6c24d2080f091ca42f37bddee13,
Gitblobc8955fb76337bc8e9783464aa0f28499e0306f7e. Its section6 already
screens square determinant-power representations of the three-log equation;
its remaining desired pencil explicitly allows all FIVE logarithms.

The stronger THREE-coordinate screen below is REUSE of Roy1995, not a new
rank-by-rank derivation. It supersedes further searches restricted to those
three entries. It does not supersede the all-five-coordinate question.

## Existing supplier and field convention

Use Damien Roy, [Points whose coordinates are logarithms of algebraic
numbers on algebraic varieties](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/117/6518-11511_2006_Article_BF02392486.pdf),
Acta Math.175(1995),49–73, section3.2, Theorem3.4, printedpage66.
The inspected proof gives the following algebraically closed constant-field
form: if k is algebraically closed, L is a three-dimensional k-subspace of
an extension field F, and an m-by-n matrix in L has k-independent rows and
k-independent columns, its F-rank r obeys

    4r >= m+n.                                             (1)

The PDF text extraction suppresses overbars. Here k=Qbar is explicit;
no assertion with merely Q-independent arbitrary scalar coordinates is
being substituted. The proof's scalar-stabilizer step is valid over k:
a multiplier preserving a nonzero finite-dimensional k-space is algebraic
over k, hence lies in k. This is the relevant constant-field condition.
The primary theorem is reused; no new rank theorem or formal check occurred.

## Application and rational descent

Let lambda_1,lambda_2,lambda_3 be Qbar-linearly independent complex numbers,
let A_1,A_2,A_3 be rational m-by-n matrices, and set

    M = lambda_1*A_1 + lambda_2*A_2 + lambda_3*A_3.

Suppose there is no nonzero common rational left null vector of the A_i
and no nonzero common rational right null vector. Then the rows and
columns of M are Qbar-linearly independent. Indeed a Qbar row relation
u^T*M=0, expanded entry by entry, gives u^T*A_i=0 for every i by the stated
independence of the lambdas. This is a rational linear system. A nonzero
solution over Qbar implies a nonzero solution over Q by ordinary rank
invariance under field extension, contrary to the supposition. The right
relation is identical.

Apply (1). Since (m+n)^2>=4mn,

    rank(M) >= (m+n)/4 >= mn/(m+n).

Consequently the strict Waldschmidt–Masser hypothesis

    rank(M) < mn/(m+n)

FORCES a common rational left or right null vector of ALL THREE A_i.
Rational invertible row or column operations put that vector in a basis.
They produce an identically zero full row or full column of the coefficient
pencil, before any lambda is inserted. Its normalized rectangle size is
1/m+1>1 or 1+1/n>1. The required rational zero-rectangle alternative is
therefore already present and cannot supply the desired contradiction.
Zero matrices and one-row/one-column cases are included.

## Original G3 binding and changed queue

For a hypothetical pure point ell_n=a*T_n(r) with transcendental r,
the three distinct-degree polynomials T_3,T_6,T_10 make these three logs
Q-linearly independent. They are logarithms of the supplied positive
algebraic numbers, so Baker gives Qbar-LINEAR independence. Algebraic
independence is NOT inferred; the retained degree-eight relation is exactly
the issue under study.

Thus all homogeneous three-log pencils, rectangular or square and of
arbitrary finite size/rank, are removed from the direct rank-contradiction
queue at once. No size search, determinant producer or old checker was run.
