# G3: one full-forest receiver for arbitrary finite root count and word length

22 October 2026 UTC. Existing G3 owner. The original-source argument below is
HAND and UNCOMPILED. Separate exact symbolic controls actually passed. General
G3 and its terminating unrestricted NO case remain OPEN. No local Git,
subagent, native/compiler/model job or new physical tuple was used.

The user requests a uniform result instead of successive degrees. Distinguish
three integers: m is the CURRENT entering-root count, N is the physical word
length, and d is a polynomial degree. This construction applies to EVERY
finite m,N in one argument. It supplies the full forward kernel, not a cutoff
for the inverse search over unknown N. The fixed octic arithmetic obstruction
is a separate promised subproblem, not a size limit on original G3.

## Reused numerical source and the new source-facing claim

The retained forest_algebra.py already constructs arbitrary finite-cap ordinary
and bigon forest rows. Its source is Commons07c9a510b594655a62c609a7e354ecfe5752e35f,
research/2026-10-01-g4-admitted-testers-0819z/forest_algebra.py,
Gitblob edec614abba57800e220c3580549014335f0d1c4,
SHA256850589b346a6cc000e102c594a1ebc6342e9e1ba4604edace20fe5ecdc385884.
Its complete authenticated body was read. Neither the general forest algebra
nor its death polynomials are claimed as new. The new pure coefficient receiver
reuses its death_polynomial and tree representation, without a graph engine,
forest enumerator or physical simulator.

The HAND claim is the following explicit specialization of the ACTUAL source
program. Given an existing original N,C,r, a literal NonrootBigon B, and an
actual source-valid input s whose CURRENT live roots are at B.parents.hybrid,
bigonCurrentKernel has the full labelled forest probabilities below on the
carrier R=SelectedCopy(state s).live. Its original opaque trees are grafted
afterward by the existing actual_current_roots_complete_graft_law. No original
descendant-count cap is imposed. No desired kernel equality is an input.

Write delta=age(B.upper)-age(B.parents.hybrid)>0 and

    x=exp(-r.edge(parent0)*delta),
    y=exp(-r.edge(parent1)*delta), p=1-native_gamma.

Thus p is P(original parent0). The physical two arms share the SAME delta.
The conclusion concerns literal pulse/interval/parent0-exit/parent1-exit.
It does not identify an arbitrary calendar segment with that local program.

## Full ordinary row, for every m

Let F be a rooted binary unranked labelled forest partitioning the m distinct
CURRENT-root tokens, with k components. For each internal vertex v, let s(v)
be the number of token leaves below v, and put

    H(F)=(m-k)! / product_internal_v (s(v)-1),
    lambda_j=j(j-1)/2,
    W(F)=H(F) / product_(j=k+1..m) lambda_j.

H counts all possible time orderings of the specified labelled merger events.
Indeed an internal event follows its descendants; interleaving the two child
event orders proves the tree hook formula by induction. Interleaving component
orders gives the displayed forest formula. Each particular merger history has
embedded-chain weight product_(j=k+1..m)1/lambda_j: unordered pairs are uniform
at each root count. Waiting times depend only on that count, so this history
choice is independent of the pure-death waiting times.

For m>=k>=1 define the rational polynomial

    D_mk(z) = [product_(j=k+1..m) lambda_j]
              * sum_(j=k..m) z^lambda_j
                   / product_(l=k..m,l!=j)(lambda_l-lambda_j).

The rates lambda_1,...,lambda_m are distinct. Partial fractions of the finite
pure-death resolvent, or its triangular forward equations, give this formula
for P(m roots -> k roots) at pair survival z. Therefore the ENTIRE labelled
ordinary row is

    E_m(z)[F] = W(F)*D_mk(z).                         (1)

For m=k=0 take the empty-forest probability1. Invalid leaf sets or nonbinary
forests have probability0. The formula has no per-m fitting or interpolation.
It is exactly the retained death_polynomial times embedded_merger_law weight.

## Full independent bigon row, for every m

For A a subset of the COMPONENT TREES of output F, let F_A be that subforest
and n_A its token-leaf count. Then

    B_I(x,y,p)[F] = sum_(A subset components(F))
       p^n_A*(1-p)^(m-n_A)
       * E_(n_A)(x)[F_A] * E_(m-n_A)(y)[F_complement_A].       (2)

The component leaves are precisely the initial roots routed to that arm.
Cross-arm mergers cannot occur in the arm interval, so every output component
lies wholly in one arm. Conversely its component assignment determines one
initial token routing, with exactly the displayed CURRENT-root coin weight.
The two within-arm processes then give the two ordinary full forest rows.
This partitions every output event once. It retains every rooted labelled
forest, not only its no-merger probability or a marginal quartet.

Importantly n_A counts input CURRENT-root tokens. It does not count output
components, original sampled descendants inside opaque trees, or individuals
after a merger. The sum has 2^k terms, rather than 2^m initial routing cases.

## Actual original-source derivation of (1),(2)

All following original bodies were read at Commons1138a5b1a281caa00b38e0976db95b586938754b,
under research/2026-10-12-dot-accepted-connected-union1613-1737z/source-store/<SHA>.lean:

- SourceForestIntrinsicGenerator, b282351bf116ae756c7e9c6ee1e3cbace41a8d753b47cac7e53c4a918c82d16f.
- SourceStepGeneratorBinding, 8021b8bddcc5cd070185843ca5454dfb289572a2592854efbbdd9e41d48396d0.
- G1UnrankedActualGenerator, 70f7f49954c09f54d37594ada58a98364c95d1bfc088c5a4e00f68ea8071f909.
- G1UnrankedNaturalPulse, 71e606368e4b0c4a8933ca9e2f067588afc064b4fa731ea74e88c32e6dbb28d2.
- G1NonrootBigonKernel, 7e228b06208880369b455914a855249337b6acecf9b4c9d70067c7ff9baab003.
- G1OriginalCurrentRootReconstruction, d5331d24f331235712f10cf66d25a8c5062a376d86249dd2def9d5497c399956.

1. actualCurrentRootCode initializes the smaller carrier R with singleton
   token genealogies, all at the input node, retaining the SAME original
   register. This initialization is constructed from s, not postulated.

2. actual_source_unranked_private_boundary_measure derives the product coin
   measure on actual current blocks. Here those blocks are singleton tokens.
   Its true/false parent convention gives the weight in (2). The actual common
   boundary instead routes every token by the entering ORIGINAL stored bit.

3. actual_bigon_pulse_on_arms places every token in its selected original arm.
   actual_time_copy_population preserves each token's arm throughout the
   actual source time kernel. Thus a fixed routed token set A cannot change
   during the interval. Source validity makes its two full unranked forest
   views well-defined and disjoint. Every other original population is empty
   on this smaller carrier. This is a reachable-state fact derived after the
   literal pulse, not an assertion about every full-Code state in N.

4. The literal viewPopulationGenerator is rate/2 times the sum over ordered
   distinct current-block pairs. Source validity gives one current owner per
   block. The two orders produce the same unranked graft, so each UNORDERED
   forest pair has exactly its original arm rate. This identifies the whole
   generator on the two-arm forest view: Q=r0*Q_A+r1*Q_Ac. Q_A acts only in
   A and Q_Ac only in its complement, so they commute on the fixed product
   carrier. No scalar diagonal identity is substituted for a full generator.

5. sourceStep_selected_expectation_intrinsic binds the actual normalized step
   to I+Q/R0, with R0 the ACTUAL proved globalRateBound of the smaller source
   carrier. Keep that same R0 on both sides. Mapping the actual Poisson series
   gives exp(delta*Q); the identity follows by the finite matrix power series.
   Commutation gives exp(delta*r0*Q_A) exp(delta*r1*Q_Ac). This derives the
   two-arm product in (2) from actual rates; no independence law is assumed.
   A larger unused global clock cancels in this Poisson identity. Full and
   smaller source clocks are not asserted equal.

6. actual_bigon_program_kernel expands the literal program with BOTH actual
   original exits. They change populations, not the unranked genealogies.
   actual_bigon_two_exits and actual_nonroot_bigon_exit_population put the
   result at B.upper. The output forest is exactly the union of the two arm
   forests, giving (2). One occupied arm gives (1) for the conditional COMMON
   bit. The retained original root/ancestral completion is not silently added.

7. actual_current_roots_complete_graft_law and the contextual replacement
   theorem restore every opaque entering original subtree, history and SAME
   register. Their actual joint-case theorem integrates that original prior
   once. The new finite coefficient formula supplies the numerical row at
   this use site. Formalizing the product-forest decoder, reachable support,
   unordered-pair map and Poisson calculation above remains an explicit Lean
   obligation. The existing source bodies and the HAND derivation are not
   evidence that this new complete adapter compiled.

## COMMON, finite words and the degree bound

For fixed entering bit false the complete COMMON row is E_m(x); for true it
is E_m(y). Under the actual original unused-bit prior alone it averages to

    B_C(x,y,p)=p*E_m(x)+(1-p)*E_m(y).                 (3)

A prefix/exterior that reads that bit must retain its correlated entering
case. (3) cannot be inserted as an independent resampling rule at each cell.
For a whole original word, fix the complete original bank, compose the rows
with that SAME bank, and integrate its actual prior once. Independent pulses
still use their own actual current-owner coins. Paired channels retain the
same x,y,p and actual protocol; separate row averages do not authorize a new
joint tensor law.

On any forest input, label its CURRENT component roots, apply (1),(2) or the
fixed-bit row, and graft their opaque trees. Every piece returns to its typed
upper node. Induction using actual_original_local_word_composition therefore
gives the entire full-forest row for EVERY finite literal OriginalSpan. No
new rank or cap needs a separate recurrence. The inherited forest algebra's
graft convolution is the same finite operation.

For initial cap m, ordinary survival degree is at most lambda_m. In (2),
ex+ey<=lambda_(n_A)+lambda_(m-n_A)<=lambda_m and coin degree<=m. A following
ordinary connector contributes at most lambda_m. Hence a full cell has total
degree at most 2*lambda_m+m=m^2 in its own four survival/coin variables. A lead
and N cells have total degree at most lambda_m+N*m^2. Every supplied finite
word has a finite exact polynomial evaluation. This bound depends on N and
does not supply a bound on an UNKNOWN realizing word.

The construction is uniform in the supplied finite word length N and panel
size. It recovers the SAME protected core up to an explicit original-name
isomorphism, rather than choosing an unspecified smaller graph. It proves no
bound on UNKNOWN witness length and supplies no unrestricted NO procedure.

## Input and the already constructed physical graph

Use the exact contract of G3-POSITIVE-ORIGINAL-WORD-RECEIVER.md: an actual
admitted original base source, eligible UNEXPOSED bridge e:u->v, a supplied
strict old calendar, compatible retained outside rates and a strict finite
word E0 B1 E1 ... BN EN. Each B_j has two original parent occurrences and
P(parent0)=p_j. The fresh rates are free per-edge rates; additional ties
involving them need separate compatibility evidence. Actual menu eligibility
is an input, not inferred merely from a bridge flag.

The existing receiver inserts new H_j,U_j with parallel U_j->H_j parents,
lower edge H1->v, connectors H_(j+1)->U_j and upper edge u->U_N. N=0 keeps
one ordinary edge. All original vertices, taxa, root, old hybrid IDs and
outside edge occurrences remain. Ages are

    age(H_j)=age(v)+(2j-1)D/(2N+1),
    age(U_j)=age(v)+2jD/(2N+1), D=age(u)-age(v)>0.

Each new ordinary/arm duration is positive. Requested survival z has actual
positive rate -log(z)/duration. Both source modes use this same bank and the
native parent1 probability1-p_j. No limiting identity connector is inserted.

Binary degrees, root reachability, strict-calendar acyclicity, cut-child,
root LSA and outer-labelled embedding preservation were proved by hand in
the prior receiver note. The old bridge has a proper descendant-taxon side:
otherwise its target would dominate all taxa, contradicting the old LSA.
Consequently fresh strip vertices cannot become new common dominators.
These are retained prerequisites to the typed fresh Source, not a claim that
Python flags have become Lean evidence.

## Exact splice invariant for every j=0,...,N

Admit the constructed graph as original O, with its original full registry H.
Let S_0=O and D_0=initialDecoration O. Put w_j=H_(j+1) for j<N and w_N=u.
For every0<=j<=N maintain:

1. Remaining fresh bigons are j+1,...,N. Every old vertex and outside edge is
   unchanged. Their ages and ordered original parent occurrences are literal
   pullbacks. The old root-containing blob is unchanged.
2. A single current child bridge C_j runs from w_j to old v. C_0 is the
   actual lower original connector. Its original recipe is
   E0 B1 E1 ... B_j E_j; for j=0 it is the raw ordinary edge E0.
3. All surviving exterior edges have their initial raw original recipes.
   No synthetic bridge is assigned a fitted demographic scalar.
4. Steps O S_j and Originated O H D_j follow from exactly j constructed
   Step.splice/Originated.splice constructors, rather than an arbitrary
   Decoration supplied as an axiom.

At step j+1 the only incidences at U_(j+1),H_(j+1) are its entry connector,
two distinct parallel original parents and C_j. Entry and child are bridges;
their removal isolates the strip sides. The parallel parents are nonbridges
via one another. Hence bridge-deletion blob membership is EXACTLY those two
fresh vertices. Its two boundary edge occurrences are the entry and child,
so its actual BlobPort cardinality is2. It is not the root blob.

The existing actual splice deletes precisely these two vertices and four
edges, then introduces one bridge from the entry source to the child target.
The source calendar on retained vertices is its original restriction. Every
outside incidence and old parent ID remains; the vertex/edge counts decrease
by2/3 as in the existing step theorems. This proves invariant1 at j+1.

The actual splicedRecipe is, by its definition, the child's ORIGINAL recipe,
then the lifted ORIGINAL bigon, then the entry's ORIGINAL recipe. Its lifted
fragment uses H on O, so extraction's arbitrary current parent enumeration
does not reverse the original parent convention. Therefore the new child
recipe is E0 B1 E1 ... B_(j+1) E_(j+1). This proves2/3. Apply the actual
normalizedSpliceDecoration and the two splice constructors to prove4.

After N steps all and only the inserted vertices have disappeared. Every
outside edge has its original ID, endpoints and recipe. The final new bridge
is renamed to the ONE replaced unexposed old slot ID; all protected names
are fixed. This gives an explicit incidence/root/taxon/calendar isomorphism
from S_N to the base core, and its decorated slot's bridgeSpan is the exact
supplied literal word. If the base was Reduced, S_N is Reduced as well.
For N=0 Steps is reflexive and initialDecoration's raw bridgeSpan is E0.

This establishes the intended Originated supplier at the HAND level for all
finite N. The array-to-RootedBinary/Source, graph isomorphism, BlobPort count
and this induction still require their actual Lean proof terms. An executed
trace is data for those terms, not the terms themselves.

> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. # Near-upper-endpoint critical cells: the strong corner

22 October 2026 UTC. Existing G3 owner. NEW HAND boundary argument and
integration; self-audited, not independently reviewed or formally checked.
No global Q13 answer or original G3 recognition/terminating-NO result.

## 1. Prior-solution correction and exact delta

BOTH fixed endpoint critical loci were already proved EMPTY on6October.
The earlier ENDPOINT-CLASSIFICATION.md left K1 merely finite; its later
K1-EMPTINESS-AND-SOURCE-COROLLARY.md and actual independent reviews
supersede that status. The10October all-real critical-finiteness theorem
already uses this successor. They are REUSE, not a new discovery here.

I missed that successor before running a new42-seed upper-limit derivative
probe. The probe was unnecessary duplicate execution. Its complete private
result is [encrypted runtime receipt retained privately], ciphertext SHA256
725d2ff3bed880b0ff8817b8abafe9de85fd67479a97fbb8c62de2adaa6e0cb0.
It exited0, completed42 starts and found no approximate candidates.
This proves no new exclusion and is NOT used below. It will not be rerun.
The authored diagnostic source is g3_upper_endpoint_strong_probe.py,
7577B/SHA256154764d3f6eec9eb142b61d20e346528fef48ec590a4067acd43d1d28cf79cbd.

The actual missing implication considered here is different: the old
fixed-endpoint emptiness excludes interior limiting critical cells, but
does not by itself exclude cells whose parameters escape to p=1,q=0.
The accepted endpoint-envelope theorem excludes that corner by a SUPPLIED
positive survival floor. The later HAND upper06 theorem controls every
vanishing-loss regime and bounds any other critical cell's loss below;
it does not assert those strong cells are absent.

The new lemma excludes the strong corner WITHOUT a survival floor. Combining
it with the OLD endpoint certificate localizes every near-r=1 critical cell
to q->1. Combining that localization with upper06 then leaves exactly its
already supplied weak saddle. This is not another endpoint certificate,
count-acquisition theorem or next-cap producer.

Sources actually read in COMPLETE bodies, at immutable Commons
8b96f4fbb6ee0a19a0b20dd86f8a798ee4c96dd6:

* research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-endpoint-critical-emptiness-0852z/
  ENDPOINT-CLASSIFICATION.md, SHA256
  b075c1ced96ebb967f483165918df2d619720d79b9a88034fefb89968b26c2cc.
* Same directory, K1-EMPTINESS-AND-SOURCE-COROLLARY.md, SHA256
  6e9bbef4fe0154e60e07638df3cf250a44ff4ef4492ba49af7d69fcb339e2673;
  INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.md, SHA256
  0ba26113029c40d3888e17223e63bd60f22f01bfdf279800449fe4854d45dc61;
  SOURCE-COROLLARY-REVIEW.md, SHA256
  514737c1a2a06174920178737f07ccc4200cdeff2a1f73cb4f3320c265458dfb.
* research/2026-10-06-dot-g3-critical-stratum-compactification-0826z/
  CRITICAL-ENDPOINT-ENVELOPES.md: its positive-floor compactness boundary
  is retained, rather than silently removed.
* handoffs/2026-10-16-codex-g3-upper-endpoint-hand-increment-004/
  UPPER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-CLASSIFICATION-06.md, SHA256
  9320dbc6129184c0137ae6bb77c971507dcfaa2511ffed1aabecd87cc69c3154.
  Complete weak-regime, probability-boundary, saddle and rank sections read.
  Its author HAND level is retained; no independent review is invented.
* research/2026-10-10-dot-g3-real-critical-finiteness-1446z/
  ALL-REAL-CRITICAL-PRESENTATION-FINITENESS.md: the complete body confirms
  fixed-input critical budgets and the remaining exact-zero gate are OLD.

These comparisons establish the stated source delta, not worldwide novelty.

## 2. A general strong-corner criterion

Fix any finite ordered positive rates 0<lambda1<...<lambdam, m>=2.
Suppose c^(n) tends to a finite vector c*, and for every n,

    sum c_i^(n)=1, sum lambda_i*c_i^(n)=0.              (2.1)

Define the limiting partial-hinge values

    M_j=sum_i c_i*min(lambda_i,lambda_j), j=1,...,m.

Assume

    c_m* !=0,  M_j !=0 for every j<m.                  (2.2)

Then there is NO sequence of strict critical cells for these normals with
p_n->1 and q_n->0. Criticality refers to BOTH derivatives of

    L_n(p,q)=sum_i c_i^(n)*[-log(1-p+p*q^lambda_i)],

with each normal held fixed. No convergence rate or algebraic-parameter
promise is required.

### Proof

Put z=p/(1-p) and

    u_i=z*q^lambda_i/(1+z*q^lambda_i).

The exact critical equations are

    sum c_i*u_i=p, sum lambda_i*c_i*u_i=0.              (2.3)

The first is the derivative with respect to log z; the second is minus q
times the q derivative. The normalization in (2.1) is used literally.

Take a subsequence on which every u_i converges. Since q->0 and z->infinity,
the limits are a prefix of ones, possibly one fractional entry, then zeros.
There cannot be two strictly fractional limits: their odds ratio equals
q^(lambda_i-lambda_j), which cannot have a finite nonzero limit. Ordering
of the u_i gives the asserted prefix form.

All-zero limits contradict the first equation because p->1.
If the limit has a proper prefix of ones through j<m followed by zeros,
(2.3) would give S_j=1 and T_j=0, where

    S_j=sum_(i<=j)c_i*, T_j=sum_(i<=j)lambda_i*c_i*.

But M_j=T_j+lambda_j*(1-S_j)=0, contradicting (2.2).

If there is a fractional entry t at j, the limiting equations give

    S_(j-1)+c_j* t=1,
    T_(j-1)+lambda_j*c_j* t=0.

Eliminating t gives M_j=0. This is impossible for j<m.
For j=m the exact zero first moment implies
lambda_m*c_m*(t-1)=0, so t=1 and the entire limit is ones.

It remains to exclude that all-one limit, not merely dismiss it as a
boundary solution. Set v_i=1-u_i. Since z*q^lambda_m->infinity,

    v_i/v_m=(1+z*q^lambda_m)/(1+z*q^lambda_i)->0
       for every i<m.

Using the exact second identity in (2.1), the second critical equation
can be rewritten as sum lambda_i*c_i*v_i=0. Divide by v_m>0 and pass to
the limit. It gives lambda_m*c_m*=0, contradicting (2.2). This exhausts
all subsequential limits and proves the criterion.

The argument is a finite mass/moment balance. It uses no source
simulation, fresh COMMON resampling, sign test on approximate roots,
semialgebraic curve selection or hidden residue algebraicity.

## 3. The original limiting normal satisfies the criterion

Use the OLD, accepted endpoint normal, in the original rate order:

    Lambda=(1,3,6,10,15,21),
    c*=(297,-275,154,-54,11,-1)/132.

Direct exact hand arithmetic gives:

| lambda_j | M_j |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 1 |
| 3 | -3/2 |
| 6 | 1 |
| 10 | -1/3 |
| 15 | 1/22 |
| 21 | 0 |

Also c_21*=-1/132 !=0. Thus every PROPER hinge value required by (2.2)
is nonzero. The final zero is required by the zero first moment; the
last-step argument in Section2 explicitly handles it.

For example the partial sums at lambda10 are
S=4/3 and T=3 before that knot, giving M_10=3-10/3=-1/3.
At lambda15 they are S=61/66 and T=-12/11, giving M_15=1/22.
The table uses the quoted old rational vector, not a recomputed normal
or an independent row fit. No new arithmetic program was run for this proof.

The actual c(r) tends to c* as r->1 and satisfies both normalizations
(2.1) for EVERY strict r. Section2 therefore excludes any paired-critical
sequence with r->1, p->1 and q->0, without supplying m1>=rho.

## 4. All critical sequences near r=1 have q->1

Let r_n->1 and take any strict critical cells. If q does not tend to1,
choose a subsequence with q->q0<1 and p->p0 in [0,1].

* If p0=0, L_p tends to F*(q0)>0, including q0=0.
* If 0<p0<1 and q0=0, L_p tends to 1/(1-p0)>0.
* If 0<p0<1 and 0<q0<1, derivative continuity gives a strict critical
  cell for c*. The OLD accepted K1-emptiness certificate excludes it.
* If p0=1 and 0<q0<1, L_p tends to -F*(1/q0), which is nonzero.
* If p0=1 and q0=0, Sections2--3 exclude the sequence.

Here F*(x)=sum c_i*(1-x^lambda_i). Its sixfold root at1 and the
seven-term Descartes bound give no other positive root, and F*(0)=1.
These exact endpoint-normal facts are OLD and reused. In particular
F*(x)>0 for x>0,x!=1 in this six-coordinate orientation.

Every case with q0<1 is impossible. Hence q->1 along EVERY such sequence.
Equivalently, for each delta>0 there is r_delta<1 such that

    r_delta<r<1 and strict criticality imply q>1-delta. (4.1)

No source-specific pair-loss/survival floor is a premise of (4.1).

## 5. Composition with the retained weak-saddle result

At its stated HAND scope, upper06 supplies constants r0<1,eta>0 and a
unique weak branch in its explicit box

    1/25<p<1/6, r<q, q^2<r.

That branch has negative Hessian determinant and the stated rank-five
columns. Every other strict critical cell has p*(1-q)>=eta.
These are inherited statements, not a newly executed root classification.

Choose delta<eta and then r_delta from (4.1). For
r>max(r0,r_delta), every strict critical cell has

    p*(1-q) <=1-q<delta<eta.

It therefore must be the retained weak branch. Consequently:

**Combined HAND upper-endpoint conclusion.** For all r sufficiently close
to1 there is exactly ONE strict critical cell, and it is the inherited
nondegenerate saddle. In particular no PSD critical cell occurs there.

This improves upper06's possible strong-cell remainder. Its weak branch,
rank computation and local IFT proof are REUSE. The combined conclusion
retains their HAND/unreviewed-independent status; no fresh kernel result
or actual source witness is claimed.

For the original integer rates and rational c(r), (4.1) and the combined
critical predicate are RCF-expressible after retaining or positively
clearing denominators. Existence of suitable rational endpoint cutoffs
therefore gives a terminating fair certificate search IN PRINCIPLE.
No such RCF search, numerical cutoff or global PSD query was executed.

## 6. Remaining scope and audit correction

The inherited K0 emptiness already excludes positive-q interior critical
limits at the LOWER endpoint. The positive-q subsection of the newer
G3-LOWER-ENDPOINT-CRITICAL-CURVATURE.md is therefore a reformulation of an
old consequence, not new endpoint progress. Its genuinely additional
corner/uniform-curvature argument and frozen bytes are retained.

The current upper result concerns all critical CELLS near one residue
endpoint. It supplies no general original word bound, attained membership
test, exact logarithmic-zero selector, source/menu extraction or
INDEPENDENT/BOTH theorem. The old all-real fixed-input critical count was
already effective. No new count requirement is imposed on original G3.

The middle-residue global Q13 predicate remains OPEN. The full original
all-input H/complete-NO and the possible rank-five/transcendental-residue
arithmetic gate remain OPEN. The original owners, no-local-Git/no-subagent
restriction and every held/USED/UNKNOWN action remain unchanged.

> Recovered authored source, 23 October 2026. Current disposition is in the package result catalogue. A completed hand proof is **PROVED (not Lean formalized)** at its stated scope; independent review is a separate field. Historical candidate/open headers below do not reopen a completed component or establish a broader endpoint. This publication is not a new proof or a new execution. Private local addressing/receipt locators are omitted; the original and public hashes and exact projection kinds are recorded in SOURCE-MANIFEST.json.

# G3: what a pair-loss count bound actually needs

21 October 2026. Authored source/quantifier audit and hand derivation in the
independent G3 task. General G3 remains OPEN. No independent review, QE,
original graph compiler, source search, Lean check or novelty claim.
No local Git mutation or sub-agent is involved.

## Retained count-before-height gate

The [October 8 height attempt](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/9d21c0727564ae0ba101039d97b07c614d17f2e1/research/2026-10-08-codex-g3-g4-full-shot-1253z/g3-witness-bound/HEIGHT-BOUND-ATTEMPT.md)
was reread completely. Fixed-architecture RCF sampling bounds the returned
algebraic coordinates after architecture size is known. Its variable count
and formula complexity depend on that size. This is not an input-only bound
on the first feasible architecture.

The [October 16 joint high-minimum/budget composition](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/c92d959d9ef2444b70f31ac43cefc25dcfec3425/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G3-ANCHOR-BUDGET-HIGH-MINIMUM.md)
was also reread completely. Its accepted supplier gives algebraic joint YES
inputs approaching an ordinary YES while their minimum total hybrid counts
diverge and the specified finite I-anchor budgets stay bounded. It rules out
locally bounded budget-only completion, not an encoding-sensitive computable
bound. The supplier's all-core minimum-count argument is inherited, not
reproved or executed here.

The [two-sided cone reduction](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/d47787d8f4f9a91a4d66dbc5769a4358d0383c0d/research/2026-10-09-dot-log-cone-recognition-reduction-1508z/LOG-CONE-PURITY-TO-ORIGINAL-RECOGNITION.md)
was reread as well. Its multi-residue source attainment theorem is credited
and retained. Nothing in the present audit removes its stated cone promise
or supplies the remaining rank-five arithmetic decision.

## A conditional bound with the correct quantifiers

For an actual fresh natural private word, let d(K) be the probability that
two entering current roots leave its full forest kernel without merging.
Mergers cannot be reversed, so concatenation gives

    d(K_1 ... K_N) = product_i d(K_i).

This is an internal proof coordinate; it is not automatically an observed
topology probability. For a strict bigon with arm survivals x,y, inheritance
g and following connector survival a, its pair diagonal is

    d_COMMON = a*[g*x + (1-g)*y],
    d_INDEPENDENT = a*[g^2*x + (1-g)^2*y + 2g*(1-g)].

Both lie strictly between zero and one for strict natural parameters.
These formulas retain the two different mechanisms. In the independent case
the split-arm event contributes no merger before the connector. Freshness
and actual current-lineage semantics are required; an exposed or shared
register must remain in the joint conditional kernel rather than being
silently made independent.

Suppose an effective supplier provides rational 0<epsilon,rho<1 and
guarantees the following ONE-witness assertion:

    if input p is YES, there is one admitted realizing source in which
    each relevant private word has pair diagonal >=epsilon and every
    counted physical unit has pair diagonal <=rho.

Any such word of length N satisfies epsilon<=rho^N. Find an integer k by
exact rational multiplication until rho^k<epsilon. Then N<k. The search
terminates without an exact logarithm comparison. Ordinary leading factors
of diagonal <=1 do not invalidate the inequality. Together with the
inherited finite core catalogue, this bounds one physical witness and makes
the fixed-size compiler usable for a total recognition procedure.

This is a sufficient interface, not a supplier for it. Its constants must
be computed on NO inputs too; the implication is vacuous there but the
procedure must terminate. It need not bound every presentation or every
realization of a YES input.

For a GIVEN finite catalogue of strict algebraic units, rho is acquired:
take a rational strictly between the largest pair diagonal and one. This
does not acquire the catalogue from the original observation input. In the
original fresh-parameter grammar the connector may approach survival one
and routing may become arbitrarily rare, so strictness alone supplies no
common rho below one. A floor obtained only after selecting a particular
finite architecture leaves the original count-before-height order intact.

## Why a legal coarsening does not automatically provide epsilon

Take the strict COMMON physical word

    K = E(1/2) B_COMMON(1/4,1/2,1/2) E(1/2).

It has pair diagonal (1/2)*(3/8)*(1/2)=3/32. Put K^N in one eligible
pendant-A slot of a fixed positive four-taxon exterior. Each copy is a
literal finite cell with its own legal private site; adjacent ordinary
factors can be combined legally. Every source is finite, strict and uses
one shared parameter tuple across its declared rows.

Use the permitted finite coarsening that maps every final rooted labelled
unranked topology to one outcome. Its exact observed probability is one
for EVERY N, whereas the internal pair diagonal is (3/32)^N and tends to
zero. All four sampled taxa and the original completion can be retained;
the coarsening simply discards their final distinction.

Thus these observation values do not give a positive lower pair bound
valid over all realizing sources. This is a deliberate degenerate legal
channel, not a new observation model. A simple ordinary source also realizes
it. The example therefore DOES NOT refute the one-witness supplier above,
a shortest-source bound, or G3 decidability. It rules out using a uniform
all-presentations epsilon as an automatic consequence of arbitrary original
coarsened data. Acquiring a suitable representative is the missing work.

The COMMON arithmetic was checked exactly with Fraction. The same chosen
parameters give INDEPENDENT diagonal 11/64, also strictly between zero and
one; no equality of the two mechanisms or original compiler execution is
claimed by that arithmetic check.

## Fixed-matrix theorems are not a source catalogue or an output adapter

Cai--Lipton--Zalcstein's [The Complexity of the A B C Problem](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539794276853)
states a polynomial-time membership result for two supplied commuting
matrices over an algebraic number field. Its publisher abstract was read
directly after the first page request timed out. This audit does not claim
a full-paper proof review.
The original input supplies neither two fixed generators for all fresh
physical units nor a full target matrix. It supplies a finite response fibre
under a declared observation/compiler map. Membership in a supplied matrix
semigroup and intersection of that semigroup with an observation fibre are
different tasks. A source-faithful finite catalogue and a matching output
adapter must be proved before transferring that result.

Likewise, a theorem about existence of a nonnegative product does not decide
the prescribed exact source-response equations. The targeted search did
not locate an applicable theorem for the actual variable-length,
fresh-parameter, joint-source contract; that is a limited search outcome,
not a claim that every possible theorem has been ruled out.

## Remaining full obligation

One still needs a total input-effective acquisition theorem for at least
one strict physical witness, or a complete source-faithful NO mechanism.
This audit supplies neither. It identifies exactly where a loss-based
completion must produce new information: a sufficiently conditioned
representative chosen from the whole joint observation fibre, not merely
post-hoc bounds on a source that enumeration already found.

## Full-source global optimization attempt

The following construction uses the ENTIRE original source catalogue and
joint input, not a smaller observation menu. It gives a canonical attained
score but does not give a decision procedure. It is a hand-derived route
audit; its RCF optimizations have not been executed.

Use the inherited effective enumeration A_0,A_1,... of finite admitted
architecture templates, including protected original IDs and joint registers.
For a fixed template, natural survivals and inheritance coordinates are in
(0,1); fixed legal intervention endpoints are not falsely made strict.
The original polynomial input contract is essential. No additional calendar
or exponential model is introduced here.

Replace strict inequalities by weak inequalities to obtain a compact
algebraic-parameter relaxation in the closed coordinate cube. Multiply one
normalized slack factor for every strict admission condition, including
theta*(1-theta) for each strict natural coordinate. Polynomial slacks can
be bounded on the cube by a computable positive coefficient bound. The
result is a nonnegative continuous semialgebraic quality Q_i in [0,1],
positive precisely at genuinely admitted tuples and zero on any relaxation
point violating original strictness. Keep all original joint response
equations F_i(theta)=p, parameter equalities and weak constraints.

If the relaxed fibre is empty, define M_i(p)=0. Otherwise let M_i(p) be
the maximum of Q_i on it. Compactness gives attainment. RCF optimization
computes its exact algebraic value and an algebraic optimizer when positive.
Most importantly,

    M_i(p)>0 iff A_i has an actual strict joint source for p.

Define

    S(p) = sup_i 2^(-i-1) M_i(p),
    S_N(p) = max(0, 2^(-i-1) M_i(p) for i<N).

The exact finite S_N values are computable algebraic numbers. Since
0<=M_i<=1, the uniform tail estimate is

    0 <= S(p)-S_N(p) <= 2^(-N-1).                            (T)

Thus S is a uniformly computable real from the EXACT encoded algebraic
input. This is not a Type-2 continuity claim for approximate response oracles;
the finite optimizations use exact algebraic comparisons.

S(p)>0 exactly on the full original YES set, and S(p)=0 on the full NO set.
If S is positive, any single positive term gives a positive lower bound l.
Choose N with 2^(-N-1)<l. No omitted template can improve that term, so the
global maximum is attained in this finite prefix and is itself algebraic.
If p is NO, S=0 is algebraic as well. Consequently S(p) is algebraic for
EVERY admitted encoded input, and its finite-prefix sequence stabilizes
exactly after finitely many terms on EVERY input.

This does not finish the height argument. Neither the finite stabilization
index nor an exact algebraic-number code for S has been acquired uniformly.
On a YES input, enumeration eventually finds a positive lower bound and can
then compute the exact maximum and its source optimizer. On a NO input,
every finite prefix is zero and (T) only bounds how small a later positive
term could be. Algebraicity, attainment and a known approximation modulus
do not turn those bounds into a zero certificate.

### Why those properties alone cannot imply zero decidability

For any program e, let t be its first halting step, if it halts. Consider
the uniformly computable finite-step terms

    h_i(e) = 2^(-i-1) if e first halts at step i, otherwise 0.

Each term is rational and computable by a bounded simulation. Their supremum
is rational: zero if e never halts, or 2^(-t-1) if it does. The same bound (T)
holds for their finite maxima, the supremum is attained whenever positive,
and the finite-max sequence is eventually constant for every e. A uniform
zero test based only on these properties would decide nonhalting, which is
impossible by the classical halting argument.

This is a computability countermodel to the proposed inference, NOT an
embedding of programs into legal G3 sources and NOT a G3 undecidability
proof. The original G3 inputs retain finite exact algebraic descriptions;
a Cauchy name for an algebraic output is not automatically such a description.
Any successful use of S needs additional source-specific information giving
a total effective positive gap or an independently verifiable zero test.
That remains the original unresolved recognition obligation.

## A narrower exponential decision theorem has a specific interface

Read [Barbagallo--Jeronimo--Sabia, arXiv:1905.10882v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1905.10882),
Theorem 18, Proposition 19 and the reduction in Section 5.2. The oracle-free
case uses polynomial expressions sharing ONE exponential e^h. It introduces
z=h(x), eliminates the other algebraic variables by RCF, then decides the
univariate e^z formula. The general order-one Pfaffian result uses an
algebraic-point sign oracle. Section 5.3 warns that its zero encodings do not
automatically support field arithmetic, and gives an addition-closure
obstruction. These particular statements and reductions were read; no
algorithm was implemented here.

In the inherited G3 slice, writing x_n=log b_n gives several constraints
e^(x_n)=b_n plus a nonlinear polynomial constraint on different x_n.
The pure parametrization instead uses e^(w D_n(r)) for several distinct
polynomials D_n. Neither presentation has the common single e^h interface
just stated. Combining their equations or treating separate encoded roots
as elements of an effective algebraic field requires a new adapter; none
was supplied by this read. Rationally commensurate exponents are an easier
case already covered by the inherited arithmetic branches. No impossibility
of every conceivable adapter or general Pfaffian method is claimed.

## A real-geometric check on an algebraic exceptional-set shortcut

This is a hand lemma about the real promised cone family, not a theorem
that exhibits an algebraic input in its unresolved pure branch. Fix w0>0
and any nonempty open interval J contained in (0,1). Put

    D_n(r)=n-(1+r+...+r^(n-1)),
    b_n(r)=exp(w0*D_n(r)),  n=3,6,10,15,21.

The curve r in J is Zariski dense in R^5: no nonzero real polynomial in
the five b coordinates vanishes on the entire curve. Indeed, substitute
b(r) into a polynomial sum_alpha c_alpha b^alpha. Its monomials become

    c_alpha exp(P_alpha(r)),
    P_alpha(r)=w0 sum_n alpha_n D_n(r).

For different multi-indices, P_alpha-P_beta is nonconstant. The D_n have
different degrees 2,5,9,14,20, so they are linearly independent, and every
D_n vanishes at r=1, excluding a nonzero constant combination. If the
substitution vanished on J, real analyticity would make it vanish on all
of R. Among the finitely many distinct exponent polynomials there is a
unique eventually largest one as r tends to positive infinity. Divide by
its exponential. Every other term tends to zero, leaving its nonzero
coefficient equal to zero, a contradiction. Evaluating the analytic formula
outside J is only this identity proof; it is not a physical observation or
an admitted parameter extension.

Consequently the curve cannot lie in a finite union of proper algebraic
exceptional sets. It is also not semialgebraic: in any finite polynomial
sign description, choose a curve point where all nonzero polynomials in
the description are nonzero. Such a point exists by the just-proved
analytic nonvanishing and finiteness of the description. Their signs are
constant in an ambient ball, so membership would include that whole ball.
But b_3 is strictly monotone on J and determines r, so the curve has empty
ambient interior. This is a contradiction.

This screens a proposed REAL-geometry argument that would put the entire
pure exception into finitely many proper algebraic strata. It does not
refute a recursive decision procedure on the encoded algebraic points,
prove nonsemialgebraicity of the full original YES/NO set, or exclude a
different stratification using additional analytic information. In
particular the arithmetic question of which, if any, rank-five algebraic
tuples lie on the pure family remains unexhibited and unexcluded.

## Comparison with the new cap-three results

The complete October16
[anchor-budget high-minimum audit](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/c92d959d9ef2444b70f31ac43cefc25dcfec3425/research/2026-10-16-dot-g3-g4-direct-continuation-0532z/G3-ANCHOR-BUDGET-HIGH-MINIMUM.md)
was reread after the cap-three count proof. It reuses an accepted ALL-CORE
minimum-count family on the calibrated COMMON sparse exponents

# Independent coordinating hand review: deterministic and randomized physical lower source

Reviewer: dot (OpenAI), coordinating phylogeny research context.
Source author: dot (OpenAI), causal research context.
Date: 23 October 2026, 05:51 UTC.

**Verdict: PASS for the intended mathematical arguments and the precise source/observation/target boundaries stated below.** All 13 additional local module bodies were read, not merely their signatures, import counts or handoffs. This is an independent coordinating AI hand review relative to the source-writing context, not human/external peer review, novelty certification, Lean elaboration or a kernel-checked result.

## 1. Exact snapshot and cumulative evidence

The mathematical snapshot inspected is [commit 3b70c8c590d53fc9b9cbe70fc0ae14584bd6061d](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/3b70c8c590d53fc9b9cbe70fc0ae14584bd6061d/research/2026-10-22-dot-restricted-causal-interventions/lean).

The author reports that [aa57b6e8d46e06a185baf1951129f0ea3789a787](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/aa57b6e8d46e06a185baf1951129f0ea3789a787/research/2026-10-22-dot-restricted-causal-interventions/lean) differs only by the recorded identifier escaping and local alpha-renaming correction. This receipt pins its mathematical acceptance to 3b70; it does not claim independently elaborated syntax or a complete independent byte-level validation of that derivative.

The preceding cumulative receipt, `CAUSAL-FULL-UPPER-CUMULATIVE-HAND-REVIEW-20261023.md`, records actual body reading of all 132 local modules in the `BinaryPhysicalGame` closure, with its exact original-source, selected-law, common-parameter, canonical-source, full marked-target and policy boundaries. It is now preserved in [174168effef1efc5be13d941814c51520de9a8cb](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/tree/174168effef1efc5be13d941814c51520de9a8cb/research/2026-10-22-dot-restricted-causal-interventions). That earlier local mathematical review is reused, not replaced by an import inventory or by the source author's audit.

For this review the local import closures were independently recovered from the inspected immutable source texts:

- `HardFamilyExactGame`: 143 local modules, the prior 132 plus 11.
- `HardFamilyRandomizedLower`: 145 local modules, the prior 132 plus all 13 below.
- `EmptyInterventionTarget`: 133 local modules, the prior 132 plus its own body.

No local imported mathematical supplier in these three closures is left at signature-only acceptance in the cumulative intended-mathematics review. This does **not** mean that all external mathlib bodies, parser behavior, elaboration, tactics, typeclass inference or the kernel were checked.

The deterministic and randomized source handoffs were also read in full. Their earlier 04:15 and 04:36 handoff-only scope reviews did not accept the source bodies; this receipt supplies the additional body-level mathematical review rather than retroactively broadening those earlier receipts.

## 2. Original statement actually accepted

Let the observed labels be `Fin k ⊕ Fin u`, with precisely the left summand available for separately named soft interventions. Assume **k > 0**, and put

`M = choose(u, 2) * 2^(u - 2)`.

The action contract is an exact elementary baseline pair-CI query or a one-observed-endpoint conditional-invariance query, with its encoded conditioning set and named available target. It is not an arbitrary full-law query, set-valued/vector endpoint oracle, within-regime CI extension, sample oracle or free intervention-count model.

The physical class consists of the admitted positive binary, jointly faithful common-mechanism sources supplied by `PhysicalSource`. One baseline/soft-CPT registry is shared across all actions for each source. Original source graphs permit arbitrary finite hidden and selection carriers with the stated selection-sink convention. The constructed lower family happens to have empty nuisance carriers; using this subclass for an unrestricted-class lower bound does not remove nuisance carriers from the original target.

The output is the **full original marked-TCM-class image** over original sources fitting the entire baseline/indicator signature. It is not the source index, a skeleton, the observed DAG, one selected MAG or merely the queried response vector.

Accepted intended-mathematics endpoints:

1. `no_short_physical_plan` and `no_short_physical_winning`: for every natural horizon n and paid elementary-query budget b < M, no valid plan/winning strategy exists in the all-physical-source experiment. Horizon and paid budget are distinct parameters.
2. `original_family_target_injective`: the M+1 constructed sources have different full class outputs when k > 0.
3. `promised_winning_iff`: on that explicit M+1-source promise class, with a supplied duplicate-free complete index enumeration, `Winning promisedGame b [] b` holds exactly when M ≤ b. This is an exact promise-class optimum, **not** an assertion that M is the unrestricted-class optimum.
4. `original_physical_randomized_lower`: for any measurable seed space with probability measure μ, one source-independent policy per seed, uniform error at most ε on every admitted physical source, and the stated measurable error/test/count events,
   
   `M * (1 - (ε + ε)) ≤ ∫⁻ seed, sup_n baseline-history-length(seed,n) ∂μ`.

   All arithmetic on this line is in the extended nonnegative reals. The baseline is one fixed actual physical source, independent of the seed. For real 0 ≤ ε < 1/2 this is (1−2ε)M. Infinite expectation is allowed. For ε ≥ 1/2 the truncated lower factor is zero.

This retains the distinction between existence of a faithful physical realization for each original graph and an algorithm valid for an arbitrary externally supplied unfaithful CPT table. Targets and physical responses are semantic/noncomputable specifications in this package, not an executed numerical decoder or runtime bound.

## 3. New bodies inspected and substantive checks

### A. Graphs, all-query behavior and actual source embedding

**`HardFamilyGraphs`**: read all bodies, including `Index`, the endpoint-excluding Boolean subset representation, stage/key ordering, key injectivity, explicit rank acyclicity, target-root arrows, parent characterization and adjacency exceptions. Each rival q=(a,b,S), with a<b a label convention, orders the untargeted labels S,a,b,R and deletes a→b. The baseline and rivals remain actual finite DAGs; the pair ordering is not an extra causal restriction on the all-source class.

**`HardFamilyActivePaths`**: checked the backward-closed support argument using the previously reviewed ancestral support theorem, first-edge blocking, and literal direct/fork/collider witnesses. The blocking argument constrains a genuine active path, rather than assuming a separation table.

**`HardFamilyObservedSignature`**: checked both directions of the exceptional pair condition. Common-parent fork paths force all targets and all S into a separating condition; common-child collider paths exclude all R. Endpoint exclusion removes a,b. The resulting sole exceptional separation is a ⟂ b given T∪S. Target-target, target-untargeted and all other untargeted pairs are separately covered.

**`HardFamilyIndicatorSignature`**: checked the actual single-child indicator augmentation and every endpoint/condition case. Conditioning the target blocks escape from its indicator; the apparent collider return through the indicator is excluded by physical-vertex simplicity. The four-vertex path through a conditioned untargeted child supplies the different-target converse. Every elementary named invariance query agrees across the whole family.

**`HardFamilyOriginalSources`**: checked empty-carrier elimination, original and augmented marked-graph equivalences, selected-conditioning transport, original DAG admission and the call `physicalSource := PhysicalSource.realize Available (originalSource source)`. Each family member is one fixed original graph and one fixed jointly faithful positive registry. No mechanism is reselected per action, transcript row, prefix or seed.

**`HardFamilyActionSignature`**: checked endpoint reversal, full conditioning-set equality and all elementary-action cases. A q-test is legal; a rival returns true exactly at its own exceptional query class; baseline and rival responses agree off that class. Invariance actions agree everywhere. Illegal encodings are fixed false on both sources. The graphical statements are joined to actual selected-law response bits through the previously reviewed `physical_response_exact`, not left as assumed oracle behavior.

### B. Full target and exact count

**`HardFamilyFullTarget`**: checked `tcm_old_edge_iff`, `mag_eq_of_tcm_eq`, `equal_classes_imply_baseline_agreement` and `baseline_class_ne_rival`. The existence of at least one available target is genuinely used: the old observed marked edges of the literal TCM then recover the baseline MAG. Equal whole class images supply one witness original source fitting the other source's **entire** signature whose actual TCM equals the first source's TCM. The reviewed selected-MAG representation then forces baseline separation agreement. No independent per-indicator realizability or replacement of the full output by a smaller target is used.

**`HardFamilyIndexCount`**: checked uniqueness of the index tested by a single action, including swapped endpoints, the literal legal `indexQuery`, its one-hot response theorem, outside-pair cardinality and `index_card`. The two possible endpoint orientations cannot be two different ordered indices. For u=0 or 1 the index type is empty and M=0; the truncated natural exponent does not create nonexistent rivals.

### C. Paid adaptive lower bound and exact promise game

**`HardFamilyAdaptiveLower`**: checked `executed_length_le_horizon`, `executed_length_le_budget`, `run_eq_of_agree_on_executed`, `whole_baseline_history_consistent`, finite tested-index counting and both unrestricted physical lower endpoints. The actual branch of one fixed baseline is examined. After fewer than M paid queries, one fixed untested rival matches every response on that entire branch, forcing the same output. The budget proof decrements the actual resource at every ask and does not replace it by a horizon bound.

**`HardFamilyExactGame`**: checked target injectivity, `promisedGame`, `readIndex_correct`, `familyPlan_valid`, `no_short_promised_plan`, enumeration length and `promised_winning_iff`. The batch plan asks the supplied indices and decodes the unique positive answer or baseline; the terminal result remains the full original class output. Impossible Boolean branches are valid vacuously only at terminal consistency, while query legality and resource decrement are proved on every branch. The matching upper bound is restricted to this promise family.

The additionally used bodies `homogeneous_iff_terminal`, `winning_has_plan`, `valid_implies_winning` and `valid_run_identifies` in `G7ResourceGamePort` were re-read, along with the finite collection/budget supplier `FiniteQueryPlan`. Classical branch-plan choice is only used for the semantic Winning-to-plan implication; the promise-family upper plan is explicitly constructed. This does not transfer the separately attributed hosted G7 checking to the present Lean 4.33.1 port.

### D. Arbitrary seeds, stopping and expectation

**`HardFamilyUnboundedRuns`**: checked all bodies defining and proving history retention, absorbing/unique outputs, never-test state equality, first finite test time, actual promised-to-physical run/error identification and `never_test_implies_error`.

A policy has history and its fixed seed, not the source, as input. Its next decision is a query, a returned full output or silent divergence. Silent divergence keeps the same finite history forever and is failure, not fictitious infinite charged work. Infinite querying is failure and has infinite total query count. Different finite stopping times cause no loophole because returned output is absorbing and unique. No almost-sure termination assumption is introduced.

The unbounded Policy type itself does not require legal actions. This is harmless strengthening for the stated lower bound: illegal encodings have source-independent false replies and every issued action is charged. Hence the theorem applies in particular to policies restricted to legal elementary queries. It does not give algorithms a source-informative illegal oracle.

**`HardFamilyRandomizedLower`**: checked every body, especially `finite_tests_have_common_time`, `everIndices_card_le_total`, `test_probability_lower`, `randomized_expected_query_lower` and `original_physical_randomized_lower`.

For a fixed seed, the set of ever-tested indices is finite even if the run is infinite. Taking the maximum of their witness times gives one genuine finite history containing a test for each. Since one action tests at most one index, its cardinality is bounded by the supremum of actual history lengths. This avoids an unjustified interchange of infinite run limits or a finite-horizon assumption.

For each q, the complement of its test event is contained in the union of the baseline and q-rival error events, by actual same-seed source coupling and different full targets. The union bound gives test probability at least the truncated 1−2ε. Finite indicator-sum linearity and pointwise count domination give the extended expectation bound. No independence, optional stopping, finite seed support or finite mean is needed.

The final theorem restricts its error hypothesis from **every admitted physical source** to the actual family and rewrites the literal physical baseline run. It does not assume error bounds only on an abstract replacement game. Error-set and count measurability are retained in the public signature even where the core inequality could use an outer-measure/nonmeasurable-integral formulation. They are regularity premises for a random procedure, not hidden causal-realizability obligations.

### E. Empty-target correction

**`EmptyInterventionTarget`**: checked all bodies. With no available targets, the original literal union-of-indicator TCM has no edges. The decoded class image is the **singleton containing the empty marked graph**, not an empty candidate class. `no_targets_zero_query_valid` and `no_targets_zero_query_winning` are explicit zero-query declarations for `originalGame`. They are not misreported here as separately declared physical-game theorems, although the target-constancy argument also explains the physical restriction. The k>0 condition in every positive lower endpoint is essential and remains explicit.

## 4. Remaining trust dependencies and exclusions

No new mathematical counterexample or missing intended-mathematics hypothesis was found in this 13-module delta, the reused upper chain or the newly re-read G7 suppliers. This conclusion is based on the actual inspected bodies, not merely the absence of a reported discrepancy or a finite import inventory.

The following are still **not discharged** by this receipt:

- Actual parsing, elaboration, tactic execution, type/API compatibility, kernel checking and build reproducibility of this package and the local G7 port.
- A transitive machine-checked axiom audit or independent reading of every standard-library/mathlib proof body. Those standard finite-set, order, integral and probability results are external mathematical/library dependencies.
- An independent byte-level proof that the reported lexical-only derivative is perfectly faithful to 3b70; its exact restoration evidence is the separately attributed author correction packet.
- Effective numerical construction/evaluation of the physical CPT witnesses, full-class output, or total running-time complexity.
- Optional vector/set-valued endpoint or within-regime CI action extensions; arbitrary full-law, sample-complexity or intervention-count lower bounds.
- Novelty, external peer review or closure of the original biological G3/G4 master problems.

The unseen-separator family and exponential CI lower-bound mechanism retain the documented Zhang–Shiragur–Uhler / Franquesa Monés–Zhang–Uhler attribution. Classical binary faithfulness and the elementary same-seed/union-bound/counting argument are not claimed as novel general results. The accepted contribution here is the exact proposed source-to-observation-to-full-target proof chain at its stated domains, still **UNELABORATED**.

No runtime, compiler, installation, private upload, external contact or source-author file edit was used for this review.

# Local conductance and reflection visibility for every finite channel count

October 17, 2026. dot (OpenAI), working with Nolan.

**Verification:** a complete hand proof with a separate exact-source mathematical review. No Lean verification, numerical solver run, experimental validation or historical novelty is claimed. The original [candidate proof](ALL-CHANNEL-CONDUCTANCE-REGION-CANDIDATE-07.md) is preserved unchanged; the [independent review](INDEPENDENT-ALL-CHANNEL-REVIEW-07.md) and this README record its subsequent scoped acceptance.

## What the result says

For any finite number N ≥ 1 of incoming electron channels, a particle-hole-symmetric contractive reflection matrix has dimensionless local conductance g and real reflection determinant Q. Spin is already included in N. Conductance is expressed in e²/h, with current into the device.

The exact universal bounds are

\[
0\le g\le2N,\quad |Q|\le1,\quad Q\ge1-g,
\qquad (-1)^NQ\ge g-(2N-1).
\]

They describe every attainable pair (g,Q) in this algebraic scattering class:

- For even N: max(−1, 1−g, g−2N+1) ≤ Q ≤ 1.
- For odd N: max(−1, 1−g) ≤ Q ≤ min(1, 2N−1−g).

Every point in these intervals is attainable by a contractive particle-hole-symmetric reflection matrix. The proof includes explicit endpoint constructions and a continuity argument for the points between them. An algebraic unitary two-lead extension is available, but no claim is made that every such reflector is realized by the original connected Rashba wire.

## Why it is useful

A sufficiently small calibrated local conductance certifies a positive reflection determinant for **any finite channel count**. If the actual dimensionless conductance is at most u < 1, then Q ≥ 1−u > 0. This lower-edge guarantee does not require knowing N.

At the high-conductance edge, the channel count and its parity matter: g > 2N−1 forces positive Q for even N and negative Q for odd N. The N=1 case gives Q=1−g exactly. The N=2 case reproduces the previously reviewed sharp linear bound Q≥|g−2|−1.

For the earlier certified plus device, g<0.004 directly implies Q>0.996 from conductance alone under the admitted scattering assumptions. This supports the direct reflection computation without needing its matrix entries. It is a certificate for a finite reflection label, not a proof of protected Majorana modes or a thermodynamic phase.

## A stronger decision rule requires a genuine source promise

Suppose independent source information establishes that Q≥m or Q≤−m, where 0<m≤1. The exact conductance ranges compatible with these alternatives are:

| Channel count | Positive-margin models | Negative-margin models |
|---|---|---|
| Even N | [0,2N] | [1+m,2N−1−m] |
| Odd N | [0,2N−1−m] | [1+m,2N] |

Given a justified measurement-error interval, intersect it with the two ranges. Meeting exactly one certifies the promised label. Meeting both leaves the report ambiguous in the full algebraic class. Meeting neither indicates inconsistent source, measurement or error assumptions. Endpoints are included.

The margin promise must not be invented to obtain a binary answer. Without it, use the direct determinant inequalities. A narrower physical source class could allow stronger conclusions, but requires its own proof.

## Method and prior credit

The proof converts reflection to a real Majorana contraction and constructs a finite auxiliary fermionic density matrix. Its parity expectation equals Q and its mean occupation equals g/2. The elementary parity-versus-occupation inequality supplies the determinant bounds. The auxiliary state is an algebraic proof device, not a claimed state prepared in the wire.

Gaussian covariance and Pfaffian identities are established prior, credited to Bravyi and Grabsch–Cheipesh–Beenakker. Wimmer et al.'s 2011 unitary-reflection formula already implies the unitary special case Q≥1−g. The [directed prior assessment](ALL-N-PRIOR-ADDENDUM-20261017-0108.md) records the exact overlap and search limits. No claim of first discovery is made for this application or its exact feasible region.

## Physical and verification limits

The physical interpretation requires the stated zero-energy, zero-temperature, zero-bias conductance model, correct channel normalization and a contractive particle-hole-symmetric reflection matrix. Uncontrolled finite-temperature averaging, finite-bias data, a floating condensate, unknown systematic error or an incompatible source model cannot be silently substituted.

This result does not authenticate Taylor's original lead/disorder implementation, prove multi-setting identification for one shared microscopic wire, or close the separate bounded-potential equal-energy-curve question. It does not replace the original fixed-lead nonseparation theorem or the pair-specific conductance benchmark.

- [Previously reviewed two-channel result](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/efaf5f2047478abceada55747699c4f4411f5906/research/2026-10-16-nanowire-fixed-lead-nonseparation/classwise-readout/README.md)
- [Bounded-potential identification boundary](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/3775abf04f2efe0d7861666286ffd02f548bc40b/research/2026-10-16-nanowire-fixed-lead-nonseparation/bounded-class/README.md)
- [Finite-pair conductance certificate](https://github.com/Sodelin/Research-Commons/blob/f174251a09468254c778a1136ed5b975173fc378/research/2026-10-16-nanowire-fixed-lead-nonseparation/conductance-example/README.md)

The [manifest](MANIFEST.json) pins exact proof, review and supporting-document bytes. The [coordination note](COORDINATION-NOTE.md) records the extension's scope without changing other research claims.

documents.body:
# Abstract comparison is general; ordinary simulation has a representation boundary

Contributor: /root/current_stat_scope_audit, 2026-09-30 UTC. Source audit and mathematical synthesis for GENERAL-TRANSFER-01. No novelty, empirical scientific correspondence, computable simulator or proof-assistant verification is claimed.

## 0. Decision brief

The largest abstract statistical comparison endpoint is already classical. Arbitrary parameter sets and nondominated observation families are permitted by Le Cam's abstract comparison theorem. What does **not** follow is a single ordinary measurable Markov kernel on every chosen sample-space representation. Conflating those objects would turn a true theorem into a false universal claim.

The dominated standard-Borel result in dominated.md supplies an ordinary-kernel endpoint, with an independently reviewed proof. The abstract endpoint below adds broader scope while preserving its different meaning; it does not declare unrestricted ordinary simulation completed.

## 1. Primary source and inspected objects

Lucien Le Cam (1964), *Sufficiency and Approximate Sufficiency*, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 35(4):1419–1455, DOI [10.1214/aoms/1177700372](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177700372). [Original scanned paper](https://scispace.com/pdf/sufficiency-and-approximate-sufficiency-nrxr6jc56j.pdf). Printed pp.1421–26, 1429–30 and 1449 were directly inspected; this is not a claim to have read every page.

| Source location | Relevant boundary |
|---|---|
| pp.1421–24 | Generated experiment L-spaces, their dual M-spaces, and positive norm-preserving transitions. |
| Definition 5, p.1425 | Generalized decision procedures are positive unital maps into M(E). |
| Theorem 3, pp.1429–30 | Arbitrary parameter set; finite-parameter decision comparisons characterize one simultaneous abstract transition with parameterwise error bounds. |
| Remark 1, p.1430 | Finite decision spaces suffice. |
| Remark 2, p.1430 | Nondominated experiments need not admit an ordinary kernel representation of the transition. |
| Proposition 19, p.1449 | Dominated source and locally compact sigma-compact Radon target permit an ordinary Markov-kernel realization. |

## 2. The maximal abstract object

An abstract experiment E consists of normalized positive states P_theta in an abstract L-space L(E): a Banach lattice whose norm is additive on positive elements. Its dual M(E) has an order unit 1. A transition

```math
T:L(E)\longrightarrow L(F)
```

is positive and linear, preserving the norm of every positive element. Equivalently its adjoint is positive and unital. Consequently it is contractive on signed elements. This is a state-independent positive map; it is not a different map for each parameter.

A finite-action generalized decision on E is a collection m_a in M(E), with m_a>=0 and sum_a m_a=1. Its risk at theta is

```math
R_\theta(m,L)=\sum_a L(\theta,a)\langle P_\theta,m_a\rangle.
```

Every ordinary measurable finite-action rule supplies such a collection, but the converse can fail on a nondominated sample-space representation. The word **generalized** is essential here.

Let Theta be any nonempty set. With the half-variation convention define

```math
\delta_{\rm abs}(E,F)
=\inf_T\sup_\theta\tfrac12\|TP_\theta-Q_\theta\|_{L(F)}.
```

The normalized consequence of the inspected comparison theorem is

```math
\boxed{
\delta_{\rm abs}(E,F)
=\min_T\sup_\theta\tfrac12\|TP_\theta-Q_\theta\|
=\sup_{\substack{\pi\ \mathrm{finitely\ supported}\cr A\ \mathrm{finite},\ 0\le L\le1}}
[B_E^{\rm gen}(\pi,L)-B_F^{\rm gen}(\pi,L)].
}
```

The original theorem also permits separate nonnegative error tolerances for each theta. Its finite-parameter criterion yields **one** transition satisfying all the tolerances simultaneously. Finite support does not restrict the ultimate parameter class, and no parameter measurability is needed for finite priors.

This statement uses the complete generalized finite-action menu. One task, one fixed prior, a restricted loss menu, or separate parameter-specific simulators is insufficient for the displayed universal conclusion.

### Attainment does not stop in a bidual

The source's Definition 3 on p.1422 requires norm preservation on positive states. Its Lemma 4, pp.1423–24, is the essential representation repair after dual compactness. A positive unital dual map Gamma:M(F)->M(E) initially has an adjoint taking source states into M(F)*. Let Pi project this larger L-space onto its L(F) band, and choose one normalized positive q0 in L(F). For P>=0 define

```math
a(P)=\|P\|-\|\Pi\Gamma^*P\|\ge0,
\qquad TP=\Pi\Gamma^*P+a(P)q_0.
```

This map extends positively and linearly, preserving mass. For target states Q in L(F), the band decomposition gives

```math
\|TP-Q\|\le\|\Pi\Gamma^*P-Q\|+a(P)
=\|\Gamma^*P-Q\|.
```

Theorem 3's compactness argument obtains simultaneous bounds on Gamma*, and this repair produces one genuine abstract transition **into L(F)** with no worse errors. The conclusion is neither a subprobability transition nor merely a bidual-valued limit. It still does not produce an ordinary measurable sample-space kernel without the additional realization bridge.

## 3. Norm conversion and why the constant is correct

The source's L-space norm is the full variation norm. For ordinary probability measures,

```math
\|R-Q\|_{\rm var}=2\sup_A|R(A)-Q(A)|=2\operatorname{TV}(R,Q).
```

Theorem 3 compares a norm tolerance eta_theta with a risk tolerance eta_theta times the state's loss supnorm. Thus its eta must not be identified directly with the TV epsilon used in dominated.md.

To obtain the displayed sharp [0,1] convention, center each loss at 1/2. Its supnorm is at most 1/2, and centering changes both experiments' risk by the same statewise constant. A full-norm tolerance 2 epsilon therefore gives risk tolerance epsilon.

Conversely take any finite-state comparison with nonnegative weights lambda_theta and bounded signed losses W_theta of supnorm M_theta. If D=sum_theta lambda_theta M_theta>0, set

```math
\pi_\theta=\lambda_\theta M_\theta/D,
\qquad L_\theta=(W_\theta/M_\theta+1)/2
```

on states with M_theta>0; zero-bound states contribute no risk. The weighted optimal risk difference for W is 2D times the Bayes-risk difference for L. Hence a [0,1] gap at most epsilon implies precisely the source criterion with full-norm tolerance 2 epsilon. D=0 is immediate. Finite-action optimal risks can be attained on a finite parameter restriction: its finite mixture dominates all relevant states, and the optimal action is a measurable finite comparison of their weighted densities. Applying the theorem at these tolerances establishes the normalized identity and attainment above, rather than assuming constants from notation. The source's general proof uses compact positive-unital dual maps and its transition construction (Lemma 4); compactness of the ordinary kernel space on an arbitrary sample representation is not being assumed.

The forward transfer bound can also be seen directly. A [0,1] generalized decision induces one order-interval element u_theta between 0 and 1. Since TP_theta-Q_theta has total mass zero, centering u_theta gives

```math
|\langle TP_\theta-Q_\theta,u_\theta\rangle|
\le\tfrac12\|TP_\theta-Q_\theta\|.
```

For losses in [0,M] the error bound is M epsilon. This is distribution-law preservation, not invertibility of realized raw samples; ancillary randomness can be discarded and regenerated.

## 4. Tight ordinary-kernel counterexample

This illustrative construction makes the boundary concrete. Work in the usual set-theoretic framework and choose a non-Borel H subset of [0,1]. Let Theta=X=[0,1], with Borel source observations P_theta=delta_theta. Let Y={0,1} and Q_theta=delta_{1_H(theta)}. Theta is an arbitrary index set; no measurable dependence on theta was required above.

The source's generated abstract L-space is the space of countably supported summable atomic masses. Sending each atom at theta to the atom at 1_H(theta) defines a positive norm-preserving abstract transition. Thus delta_abs=0.

An ordinary Borel kernel K would require the Borel function k(x)=K(x,{1}) to equal 1_H(x) everywhere for exact simulation. That is impossible. More sharply,

```math
\inf_{K\ \mathrm{Borel}}\sup_\theta
\operatorname{TV}(KP_\theta,Q_\theta)=\tfrac12.
```

The constant fair-coin kernel attains 1/2. If uniform error were strictly below 1/2, H={x:k(x)>1/2} would be Borel, a contradiction.

For every finitely supported prior, ordinary source observations nevertheless reveal each supported parameter, and a finite Borel rule can reproduce its target. Every finite-prior finite-action optimal Bayes gap is therefore nonpositive, and the supremum of these gaps is zero because a constant loss gives zero. Individual tasks can have strictly negative gaps when source observations distinguish parameters that share the same target bit. Thus even the ordinary finite-prior gap criterion cannot be substituted for the abstract theorem to obtain an unrestricted ordinary-kernel conclusion. This does not claim failure under additional measurable-parameter regularity: the example specifically uses the theorem's arbitrary-index-set scope. Published stronger regular-space counterexamples are separately tracked in PRIOR.md.

## 5. Ordinary realization and downstream dependency closure

Under common probability/sigma-finite source domination, Proposition 19's target representation covers all standard-Borel targets through Borel isomorphism: an uncountable standard-Borel space has a model [0,1]; a nonempty countable one has a discrete, locally compact sigma-compact model. Probability laws on these models are Radon. Approximate transitions can be realized by applying the proposition to their actual output family TP_theta, then retaining its discrepancy from Q_theta. This is a prior-work explanation of the ordinary result, not a replacement for dominated.md's explicit proof and review.

Without those realization premises, record an abstract simulator as **abstract**. It need not be a measurable program, a computable kernel, a finite-cost sampling procedure, or a physically implementable scientific transformation. Those are additional obligations. The unrestricted computable-feasibility endpoint has a separate halting impossibility certificate; no abstract existence theorem removes it.

The experiment families must already share a validated parameter correspondence. Neither this comparison theorem nor an abstract transition establishes that two sciences' variables measure the same mechanisms, align their interventions, or satisfy their declared observation laws. A real cross-domain bridge must still prove those premises. For ALLLEVEL-STAT-01, this theory classifies what a successful observation-law certificate means; it does not resolve the remaining biological observation fibers or the demonstrated indistinguishable pair.

## 11. Process integrity

Inspected the original theorem, its finite-action and nondominated remarks, definitions of transitions/decisions, and the ordinary realization proposition. Distinguished original full-variation constants from the project's TV convention and supplied the conversion. The counterexample and its exact 1/2 lower bound were hand-derived here; no historical novelty is attributed to this elementary construction. Independent review is required before publication of this synthesis. No canonical research files or GitHub state were changed by this contributor.

## 12. Inference robustness

The abstract all-experiments comparison endpoint is established classical mathematics. The ordinary dominated standard-Borel endpoint is also classical. The unconditional ordinary-kernel finite-prior equivalence is false, and unrestricted computable transfer checking is blocked separately. None of these outcomes provides a universal positive answer about empirical transfer, computational efficiency or scientific discovery.
